papers.abstract_en: Cornelia de Lange syndrome (CdLS) is a rare congenital disorder characterised by craniofacial features, growth retardation, limb anomalies, and intellectual disability. The condition arises from pathogenic variants in genes encoding cohesin complex components or regulators, most frequently NIPBL. Despite advances in genomic testing, approximately 30% of clinically diagnosed cases remain unresolved, suggesting the presence of non-coding variants. We investigated 10 classical CdLS patients negative for pathogenic variants in NIPBL, SMC1A, SMC3, RAD21, and HDAC8. Genome-wide methylation profiling was performed to identify CdLS-specific epigenetic signatures. Episignature-positive cases underwent trio-based deep sequencing of the entire NIPBL locus while targeted NIPBL RNA sequencing was used to assess splicing. Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed in episignature-negative individuals. Five of ten patients exhibited a positive CdLS episignature in blood, saliva, or skin. Deep sequencing identified de novo deep intronic NIPBL variants in all cases, and two additional variants in episignature-negative patients. Seven distinct intronic variants were identified across introns 4, 10, 21, and 32. In silico tools predicted the creation or activation of cryptic splice sites in six variants. RNA sequencing confirmed pseudoexon inclusion in three patients, leading to premature termination codons and predicted nonsense-mediated decay. Tissue-specific variation in aberrant transcript expression was observed between blood and fibroblasts. We conclude that deep intronic NIPBL variants represent an under-recognised cause of CdLS, frequently escaping detection by conventional exome analysis. Integration of methylation episignatures, deep intronic sequencing, and RNA analysis enhances diagnostic yield and provides insight into the regulatory architecture of cohesinopathies.

papers.abstract_en: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is a complex three-dimensional (3D) spinal deformity. Although standing full-spine radiography remains the cornerstone of clinical diagnosis and longitudinal follow-up, two-dimensional projections cannot fully characterize vertebral rotation, local osseous geometry, or global spatial alignment. In recent years, computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), conventional radiography, EOS/biplanar radiography, 3D ultrasound, and surface imaging have increasingly been integrated with deep learning, statistical shape modeling, and generative approaches, substantially expanding the technical pathways for patient-specific 3D reconstruction in AIS. However, substantial heterogeneity remains across studies with respect to input constraints, target populations, reference standards, and validation endpoints, and the evidentiary boundaries between technical performance, AIS-specific validity, and clinical validity have not been systematically clarified. This review adopted a structured methodological framework and systematically searched the Web of Science Core Collection, PubMed/MEDLINE, and IEEE Xplore, supplemented by forward and backward citation tracking. Study-level evidence was synthesized across imaging inputs, reconstruction tasks, algorithmic paradigms, and validation designs. A total of 115 core studies were included, comprising 32 AIS-specific studies (27.8%), 21 scoliosis-specific or mixed-population studies (18.3%), and 62 studies based on general spinal-image-analysis evidence (53.9%). Based on the reference standards and validation endpoints used, we established a five-level validation framework ranging from image/segmentation-level validation (L1), anatomical-structure-level validation (L2), and clinical-parameter-level validation (L3), to workflow/generalization-level validation (L4) and clinical-translation-level validation (L5). An evidence-gap matrix based on "imaging modality × methodological task" was also constructed. Among the 115 studies, 28 (24.3%) reached a maximum of L1, 49 (42.6%) reached L2, 34 (29.6%) reached L3, and only 4 (3.5%) reached L4; no study met the L5 criteria, and no explicit AIS-specific external validation was identified. Current evidence indicates that CT provides a strong basis for high-fidelity osseous reconstruction, EOS has accumulated relatively continuous AIS-specific evidence for weight-bearing 3D parameter assessment, and 3D ultrasound offers advantages for repeated radiation-free parameter measurement, whereas MRI-based reconstruction and limited-projection 3D recovery remain rapidly evolving fields. The principal challenge has therefore shifted from whether a 3D structure can be generated to whether structural fidelity can be translated into reliable clinical parameters and whether models can generalize consistently across independent AIS populations, imaging systems, and acquisition protocols. Future work should prioritize AIS-specific multicenter validation resources, task-matched 3D reference standards, and a continuous evidence chain linking structural fidelity, clinical-parameter validity, external generalization, and clinical impact, thereby advancing AIS 3D reconstruction from technical feasibility toward trustworthy clinical application.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lymph node metastasis identification has important clinical implications for treatment decision-making in rectal cancer (RC). To evaluate the diagnostic performance of the CT-based Node Reporting and Data System 1.0 (Node-RADS) for lymph node metastasis risk in treatment-naive RC patients, and to investigate the correlation between the Node-RADS score and clinicopathological factors. Lymph node status was assessed using Node-RADS score ranging from 1 to 5. Sensitivity, specificity, and Youden's index were calculated for different Node-RADS cut-off values. The overall diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves and the area under the curve (AUC). The associations between Node-RADS score and clinicopathological parameters were analyzed. RESULTS: A total of 459 RC patients were evaluated, including 174 pN + and 285 pN-. Node-RADS scores ≥ 3 and ≥ 4 have the satisfactory diagnostic performance, with sensitivity/ specificity/Youden's index of 87.36 %/58.25 %/0.46 for Node-RADS scores ≥ 3 by Reader 1, 89.08 %/54.04 %/0.43 for Node-RADS scores ≥ 3 by Reader 2, 74.14 %/78.95 %/0.53 for Node-RADS scores ≥ 4 by Reader 1, and 72.99 %/75.44 %/0.48 for Node-RADS scores ≥ 4 by Reader 2, respectively. The AUC of Node-RADS scores were 0.831(95 %CI:0.793-0.864) and 0.806(95 %CI:0.767-0.841) by Reader 1 and Reader 2, respectively. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) is among the most devastating modes of progression in EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although dose escalation of third-generation EGFR-TKIs has been an important central nervous system (CNS)-directed salvage strategy, therapeutic options after progression on this intensification approach remain limited. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients treated between September 2024 and December 2025. Eligible patients were adults (≥18 years) with histologically confirmed lung adenocarcinoma, a documented EGFR mutation, and LM diagnosed by gadolinium-enhanced MRI or positive cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytology. Patients received ivonescimab plus chemotherapy after documented intracranial or extracranial progression on a dose-escalated third-generation EGFR-TKI regimen used for LM management, with or without concurrent CSF-directed therapy. Ivonescimab was given intravenously at 20 mg/kg every 3 weeks with chemotherapy selected according to prior treatment and clinical status. The primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and LM progression-free survival (LM-PFS). RESULTS: Of 517 screened patients, 33 initiated ivonescimab plus chemotherapy and comprised the overall treated cohort. Concurrent intrathecal or intraventricular chemotherapy was administered to 29 of 33 patients (87.9%). The median age was 61 years (IQR 56-62); 24 (72.7%) were female; 24 (72.7%) had baseline ECOG performance status of 2-3. The median number of prior therapy lines was 4 (IQR 3-6). At a median follow-up of 8.28 months, median OS was 8.54 months (95% CI 5.75-14.32), median LM-PFS was 6.54 months (95% CI 3.42-11.86), and median systemic PFS was 4.83 months (95% CI 2.79-7.56). Three-month treatment persistence was 64.4% (95% CI 44.9-78.6). Among 29 patients evaluable for LM response, 6 achieved a response, yielding an LM response rate of 20.7% (95% CI 8.0-39.7) and an LM disease control rate of 82.8% (95% CI 64.2-94.2). Among 31 patients with evaluable safety documentation, grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 14 (45.2%), most commonly hematologic toxicities. No permanent ivonescimab discontinuation due to toxicity was documented. CONCLUSIONS: This cohort provides real-world outcome data for patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC and LM receiving multimodality salvage treatment incorporating ivonescimab plus chemotherapy after dose-escalated third-generation EGFR-TKI failure.

papers.abstract_en: Filamin C (FLNC) is an essential cytoskeletal protein required for cardiomyocyte structural integrity and mechanotransduction. Truncating FLNC variants cause haploinsufficiency associated with dilated and arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathies, yet no therapies currently address the underlying defect of FLNC deficiency. Gene replacement is challenging because the approximately 8.2-kb FLNC coding sequence exceeds the packaging capacity of conventional adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors. Here, we engineered a triple-AAV strategy optimized for full-length FLNC reconstitution in the heart. Screening in HEK293 cells identified GP41-1 and IMPDH as a compatible orthogonal pair for efficient full-length FLNC reconstitution. In tamoxifen-inducible, cardiomyocyte-specific Flnc knockout mice, systemic delivery of optimized MyoAAV2A vectors restored full-length FLNC expression and re-established sarcomeric localization following cardiomyocyte FLNC depletion. A total vector dose of 1 × 10¹³ genome copies/kg restored FLNC to approximately endogenous abundance, preserved systolic function and ventricular dimensions, limited cardiac enlargement, attenuated fibrotic remodeling and prevented premature death. FLNC replacement also attenuated pathological transcriptional remodeling and compensatory changes in cytoskeletal and junction-associated proteins. These findings demonstrate that systemic split-intein-mediated reconstitution of full-length FLNC can preserve cardiac structure and function in vivo, providing preclinical support for a mutation-independent therapeutic strategy for FLNC-associated cardiomyopathy.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Although cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy for patients with localized muscle-invasive blader cancer (MIBC) is associated with improved survival, nearly half of these patients are ineligible for cisplatin-based chemotherapy and historically proceed to radical cystectomy (RC) without neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Perioperative enfortumab vedotin (EV) plus pembrolizumab with RC is an alternative option, but little is known about its cost-effectiveness compared with surgery alone. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab for cisplatin-ineligible patients with localized MIBC. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This economic evaluation developed a decision-analytic Markov model that compared neoadjuvant EV plus pembrolizumab followed by RC and adjuvant EV plus pembrolizumab (intervention arm) vs RC alone (control arm). The sample consisted of simulated patients with MIBC who were ineligible for or declined cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The model was informed by efficacy and safety data from the KEYNOTE-905/EV-303 trial, which had a median (range) follow-up of 25.6 (11.8-53.7) months. Analyses were performed between October 2025 and August 2026. INTERVENTION: The 2 treatment strategies were (1) neoadjuvant EV plus pembrolizumab followed by RC and adjuvant EV plus pembrolizumab and (2) RC alone. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Outcomes included life-years, quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), and direct medical costs estimated from a Medicare payer perspective over a 10-year horizon. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) was assessed against a willingness-to-pay threshold of $100 000 per QALY. Scenario, 1-way, and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were conducted. RESULTS: The model consisted of 10 000 patients (age at baseline, 73 years; 77 900 males [77.9%]). Over 10 years, adding perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab to treatment was associated with increased projected survival from 4.12 to 5.63 life-years per patient, quality-adjusted survival from 3.20 to 4.51 QALYs per patient, and total costs from $317 513 to $412 160. Higher upfront perioperative therapy costs were partially offset by lower postprogression treatment costs ($12 578 per patient for the intervention arm vs $238 729 per patient for the control arm). Perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab with RC achieved an ICER of $72 460 per QALY vs RC alone and therefore represented a cost-effective treatment approach. In 1-way and scenario sensitivity analyses, the cost-effectiveness result was sensitive to alternative assumptions for key factors, including time horizon length, adjuvant therapy utilization rates, patient age, postprogression treatment mix, drug costs, and health utility before disease progression. In the probabilistic sensitivity analysis, perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab with RC had a 53% probability of being cost-effective vs RC alone at the prespecified willingness-to-pay threshold of $100 000 per QALY. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this economic evaluation of a simulated cohort of patients with cisplatin-ineligible MIBC, clinical trial-informed modeling suggested that adopting the perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab intervention extends overall survival and quality-adjusted survival and is likely cost-effective in the US.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Perioperative 5-fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin, and docetaxel (FLOT) is a guideline-recommended standard for patients with resectable gastric cancer or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma globally. Guidance is limited on patient selection, nutritional optimization, and toxicity management within existing guidelines. This study aimed to develop an international consensus to address these management gaps. METHODS: A modified Delphi methodology, informed by the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method, was conducted virtually between March and August 2025. A multidisciplinary panel of 16 experts independently rated draft clinical statements across multiple domains. Responses were anonymized, with structured, iterative rounds of feedback and re-rating. Consensus was defined a priori as a median score of 7-9 (appropriate) or 1-3 (inappropriate) with a disagreement index ≤1.0. RESULTS: Consensus was reached on 66.3% of the statements. Experts agreed that patients aged >70 years should not be routinely excluded from perioperative FLOT but require comprehensive assessment; inclusion of Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG PS) 0-1 is appropriate, and ECOG PS 0-2 may be considered on a case-by-case basis. Adequate organ function, correction of baseline conditions, hepatitis B screening, and dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase testing are appropriate before FLOT initiation. Universal baseline nutritional screening and support, proactive intervention for malnourished patients, and structured physical activity were endorsed. Surgical planning was supported through multidisciplinary input, with defined perioperative windows, individualized dosing, and flexibility in pre-/postoperative cycles. For toxicity management, the panel supported dose modification over drug omission, where possible. CONCLUSION: This Delphi consensus provides expert-driven, practice-oriented advisories codifying fitness-based selection, nutrition-forward optimization, and pragmatic toxicity management. The resulting guidance builds on current standards and provides internationally applicable consensus statements to ultimately enhance patient care.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: This work reports on the proof-of-concept testing for a suite of educational modules designed to improve oncology clinician sexual health (SH) communication with adolescent and young adult (AYA) patients. METHODS: Pediatric oncology clinicians completed four interactive SH education modules. Intervention feasibility was evaluated through rates of intervention completion and study retention, with benchmarks of 60% and 70%, respectively. Acceptability and perceived usefulness were assessed through standardized self-report measures, using a benchmark of 70% of participants rating the intervention favorably. Pre- and postsurveys evaluated knowledge, attitudes and beliefs, SH communication practices, and perceived self-efficacy. Open-ended feedback and key takeaways from each module were analyzed qualitatively. RESULTS: A total of 45 clinicians enrolled, with 39 completing the intervention and study surveys. Completion and retention rates (86.6% and 100%, respectively) exceeded the preset feasibility benchmarks. Positive endorsement of self-report measures demonstrated acceptability (100%) and perceived usefulness (94.9%). Pre- and postintervention surveys signaled increases in clinician knowledge, beliefs, and self-efficacy. Key qualitative insights from participants were received pertaining to AYA concerns, needs, and preferences and clinician responsibilities. CONCLUSION: This innovative approach to clinician education on SH demonstrates potential to improve clinician knowledge and engagement in SH conversations with AYAs, a key first step in improving AYA SH during and after cancer. Next steps must focus on a larger trial to assess intervention effectiveness.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lack of health insurance limits access to health care, leading to potentially preventable inequities in health outcomes. This modelling study estimates the impact of providing insurance to currently uninsured individuals on colorectal cancer (CRC) outcomes in the US. METHODS: The MISCAN-Colon model was adapted to an uninsured population aged 40-100 during 2025-2055, using age-specific estimates from national data sources for screening, stage distribution, survival and all-cause mortality by insurance status (ages 40-64: privately insured vs. uninsured; ages 65-100: Medicare and private coverage vs. Medicare only). The effects of this uninsured population gaining health insurance coverage in 2025 were compared with the same population remaining uninsured for CRC incidence, mortality, and costs. Both groups were assumed age-eligible for Medicare coverage at 65 years. RESULTS: In an uninsured population, the model predicted 170 CRC cases and 73 deaths per 100,000 in 2055. If this population gained private insurance, up to 15 (8.9%) cases and 22 (30.7%) deaths per 100,000 could be averted by 2055. Although insurance gains would decrease treatment costs by $1.37 million per 100,000 (-4.8%) through prevention and earlier diagnoses, total CRC-related costs would increase by $1.29 million per 100,000 (+3.7%) due to increased screening costs ($2.66 million per 100,000, +41.7%). CONCLUSION: If the previously uninsured population gained health insurance, CRC incidence and CRC mortality could be reduced substantially because of improved access to care. Assuming analogous improvements for other cancers, this case study provides an example for the potential benefits of gaining health insurance on mitigating health disparities.

Median time from radiotherapy completion to study participation was 41 (IQR, 22-61) months. The mean fatigue score was 44.7 (SD, 28.0), exceeding the fatigue levels in the age- and sex-adjusted German general population (29.7); 51.3% of patients showed clinically relevant fatigue (≥ 39 points). Fatigue was inversely associated with HRQoL (ρ = - 0.59, p < 0.001), and positively with distress (ρ = 0.54, p < 0.001) and fear of cancer recurrence (ρ = 0.41, p < 0.001). Higher fatigue was found in patients with impaired performance status and in those with laryngeal and hypopharyngeal cancers. Neither cerebral OAR radiation doses nor skeletal muscle mass index was associated with fatigue, and VBA revealed no relevant subregions. CONCLUSIONS: Clinically relevant fatigue affects about half of head and neck cancer survivors. IMPLICATIONS FOR CANCER SURVIVORS: The absence of a correlation with cerebral OAR doses suggests that other, probably multifactorial somatic, psychological and lifestyle-related factors play a more central role in the genesis of fatigue than the radiation-related brain exposures investigated.

papers.abstract_en: Epigenetic modifications are critical determinants governing the proper initiation and progression of gametogenesis. Accumulating evidence has indicated that epigenetic dysregulation underlies the pathogenesis of infertility. However, detailed information on the individual powerful roles of these epigenetic enzymes in facilitating programmed meiosis remains elusive. This study indicates that lysine-specific demethylase 1 (LSD1) plays critical roles during meiotic prophase I in mouse spermatogenesis. Germ cell-specific deletion of the Lsd1 gene in male mice caused meiotic arrest at the pachytene stage, ultimately leading to infertility. In primary spermatocytes of Lsd1-deficient mice, compromised homologous chromosome synapsis and DNA double-strand break repair activated the DNA damage checkpoint pathway, triggering spermatocyte apoptosis. Mechanistically, LSD1 directly binds to the promoters of meiotic genes, including Prdm9 and Rpa2, to regulate their expression during meiosis. PRDM9 and RPA2 are upregulated upon LSD1 loss and are essential for homologous recombination and DNA double-strand break repair. The promoters of Prdm9 and Rpa2 are also occupied by H3K4me2, whose levels increase upon LSD1 loss. Collectively, this study highlights the crucial role of LSD1 in orchestrating meiotic genes, possibly through its demethylase activity during spermatogenesis, and may help explain the pathology of non-obstructive azoospermia in humans.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) rupture remains the leading cause of AAA-related mortality, while current clinical management relies primarily on aneurysm diameter, which inadequately predicts rupture risk. Increasing evidence suggests that stromal cell heterogeneity critically shapes vascular remodeling; however, the specific fibroblast states associated with AAA rupture predisposition remain poorly defined. METHODS: We integrated cross-species single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets spanning the full spectrum of AAA progression to systematically characterize fibroblast heterogeneity and state transitions. Pseudotime trajectory analysis, transcriptional regulatory network inference, and ligand-receptor interaction modeling were applied to delineate fibroblast-associated microenvironmental programs. Based on these findings, a fibroblast-derived molecular signature was constructed and validated in an independent human AAA cohort. RESULTS: Single-cell analysis revealed a progressive transition from homeostatic IGFBP6+ fibroblasts to a disease-associated COL10A1+ fibroblast state during AAA progression. COL10A1+ fibroblasts were selectively enriched in rupture-prone lesions and exhibited transcriptional programs linked to extracellular matrix remodeling and osteogenic-like activation. Intercellular communication analysis indicated that COL10A1+ fibroblasts were predicted to engage macrophage populations through coordinated ligand-receptor signaling pathways, including MDK, CSF1, and CXCL12, collectively delineating a rupture-associated vascular microenvironment. Translationally, leveraging this fibroblast state enabled the development of a minimal two-gene risk score (COL10A1-IGFBP6), which stratified AAA patients by molecular rupture risk independently of aneurysm diameter in the validation cohort. CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies a COL10A1+ fibroblast-associated transcriptional state that defines a rupture-prone vascular microenvironment in abdominal aortic aneurysm. The derived COL10A1-IGFBP6 signature establishes a biologically informed framework for molecular risk stratification, complementing anatomical size-based assessment and providing a foundation for future development of mechanism-guided strategies to refine AAA risk evaluation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Breast cancer has the highest incidence and second-highest mortality burden of all cancers in women. Breast density, the extent of fibroglandular tissue within the breast, is strongly associated with breast cancer risk, and is visually graded on a four-level ordinal scale on imaging studies including chest CT. However, current automated methods for CT breast density assessment are limited, relying on semi-automated breast segmentation followed by intensity thresholding, and excluding higher-order image features. In this work, we train and evaluate a 3-D convolutional neural net (3D-CNN) to predict breast density grade on CT. METHODS: IRB-approved chart review identified female patients from 2010 to 19 with both mammography and chest CT acquired within 1 year. CT breast density was visually assessed following the BI-RADS density criteria by a subspecialist faculty radiologist. CT scans were downsampled to isotropic 2.5 mm resolution, and volumes of interest (VOIs) of size 80 × 80 × 80 voxels were extracted for each imaged breast. Our 3D-CNN model consists of consecutive 3-D convolutional layers with ReLU activation, convolutional block attention modules (CBAM), and batch normalization and pooling operations. Rank-consistent ordinal regression was applied to the final layer to predict the density grade of each VOI, with models optimized to minimize ordinal cross-entropy. Patient-level predictions were generated on test cases by averaging over the right- and left-breast VOIs. RESULTS: 503 scans matched our inclusion criteria; 86 (17.1%) were assigned breast density grade 1 (i.e. mostly fatty), 244 (48.5%) were grade 2 (scattered dense), 131 (26.0%) were grade 3 (heterogeneously dense), and 42 (8.3%) were grade 4 (extremely dense). Our optimized 3D-CNN model achieved ROC AUC of 0.935, and Cohen kappa of 0.787, for classification of high (grades 3-4) versus low breast density, comparable to literature-reported inter-radiologist agreement. Both ordinal regression and attention mechanisms improved model performance over standard architectures. In test cases where both breasts were within the CT image, ROC AUC and Cohen kappa improved to 0.955 and 0.873, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: We have developed a 3-D CNN model for prediction of breast density grade on chest CT which achieves test-set performance comparable to prior literature reports of inter-radiologist agreement on CT breast density.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Non thrombotic iliac vein lesions (NIVL) are thought to be associated with deep vein thrombosis (DVT), yet most individuals with NIVL never develop thrombotic complications. This study assessed whether ultrasound-derived hemodynamic measurements differ between NIVL patients with and without a history of DVT, and whether these hemodynamic measurements better discriminate DVT history than percent stenosis alone. METHODS: We performed a retrospective case-control study of patients evaluated at a tertiary academic referral center between 2022 and 2025 who underwent pelvic venous duplex ultrasound imaging. Patients with left common iliac vein stenoses greater than 20 percent were included and categorized by history of left lower extremity DVT. Exclusion criteria included concurrent DVT or prior venous stenting. Ultrasound images were digitized to obtain vessel diameters and spectral Doppler velocities in the iliac veins. Mean velocity, peak velocity, flow rate, shear rate, and ipsilateral and contralateral ratios were calculated. Continuous variables were compared using Welch t tests, with statistical significance defined as p<0.05. RESULTS: 45 patients were included, comprising 9 with prior DVT and 36 without. Amongst all metrics, velocity-based metrics at the compressed left common iliac vein showed the strongest associations with a history of prior DVT, including ipsilateral velocity ratio (log2 fold change -1.539, p=0.007), peak velocity (log2 fold change -0.999, p=0.002), and mean velocity (log2 fold change -0.989, p=0.002). Differences in percent stenosis were statistically significant but less discriminative than velocity-based metrics (log2 fold change 0.363, p=0.033). Composite metrics such as flow rate and shear rate demonstrated weaker discrimination. Dimensionality reduction analysis revealed distinct clustering based on multivariate hemodynamic features between patients with and without a history of DVT. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with NIVL, decreased velocity through the left common iliac vein at the compression point was the strongest predictor of prior DVT whereas percent stenosis was less discriminative. papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) is driven primarily by venous reflux and affects nearly one-third of adults. While superficial reflux is effectively treated with ablation, therapeutic options for deep venous reflux (DVR) remain limited. Despite decades of innovation, no prosthetic or bioprosthetic venous valve has achieved U.S. regulatory approval. We systematically reviewed device strategies, clinical and hemodynamic outcomes, complications, and barriers to translation for devices designed to treat DVR. METHODS: We conducted a PROSPERO-registered systematic review (CRD420251101761) of six databases from inception through February 2026, including in vivo animal and human studies evaluating prosthetic or bioprosthetic devices for DVR. Studies of native valve repair or autotransplantation were excluded. The primary outcome for human studies was clinical improvement, and secondary outcomes included patency, procedural complications, valvular function, and thrombosis. RESULTS: Of 516 records identified, 15 met inclusion criteria: 8 human and 7 animal studies. Two principal strategies were identified: intraluminal valve restoration (VR) and external compression (EC), with approximately 40% of devices delivered percutaneously or endovenously. In human studies, technical success ranged from 87.7%-100%, patency from 67%-100%, and perioperative complication rates from 0%-44%, consisting primarily of bleeding, wound infection, and valve thrombosis. Valve occlusion occurred in up to 28% of animal implants and 18%-22% of select human cohorts. Two perioperative deaths occurred in animal studies; none were reported in human studies. Among human studies, valve competency assessment methods varied substantially. Reported competency ranged from 0%-92%, reflecting heterogeneity in imaging modalities and definitions. Discordance between anatomic patency, duplex-derived reflux reduction, and clinical improvement was frequently observed. In contemporary multicenter trial data, fewer than half of patients met predefined reflux-reduction endpoints despite high device patency and substantial clinical improvement, highlighting discordance between anatomic, hemodynamic, and patient-centered outcomes. By one year, pain had improved in 75%-97% of patients; rVCSS decreased by 37%-81%, with clinically meaningful (≥3-point) improvement in up to 84.6%; and ulcer healing ranged from 67%-100%. Longer follow-up extended to 2 years in animal studies and up to 11 years in human series with various outcomes reported. CONCLUSION: Several devices developed for DVR have demonstrated technical feasibility and symptom improvement. However, the risk of thrombosis, the marginal impact on valvular function, and the lack of standardization and selection of adequate endpoints in the measurement of results remain major barriers to regulatory approval. Standardized composite endpoints integrating objective hemodynamic measures with patient-centered outcomes are essential to advance durable DVR device development and clinical translation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Facial appearance offers a non-invasive window into health. We built Foundation Artificial Intelligence for Health Recognition-Face (FAHR-Face), a foundation model trained on more than 40 million facial photographs and fine-tuned it for two distinct tasks: biological age estimation (FAHR-FaceAge) and survival prediction (FAHR-FaceSurvival). METHODS: FAHR-FaceAge underwent two-stage, age-balanced fine-tuning on ten public image datasets; FAHR-FaceSurvival was fine-tuned on 34 363 photographs of patients with cancer. Model robustness (cosmetic surgery, make-up, pose, and lighting) and independence (attention mapping) were tested. Both models were clinically tested in two independent cancer patient datasets with survival analysed by multivariate Cox models and adjusted for clinical prognostic factors. FINDINGS: For age estimation, FAHR-FaceAge had the lowest mean absolute error of 5·1 years on public datasets, outperforming benchmark models and maintaining accuracy across the full human lifespan. In patients with cancer, FAHR-FaceAge outperformed a previous age estimation model in survival prognostication. FAHR-FaceSurvival showed robust prediction of mortality, and the highest-risk quartile had more than triple the mortality of the lowest (adjusted hazard ratio 3·23; p<0·0001). These findings were validated in the independent cohort and both models showed generalisability across age, sex, race, and cancer subgroups. The two algorithms provided distinct, complementary prognostic information; attention mapping revealed that each model relied on distinct facial regions. The combination of FAHR-FaceAge and FAHR-FaceSurvival improved prognostic accuracy. INTERPRETATION: A single foundation model can generate inexpensive, scalable facial biomarkers that capture both biological ageing and disease-related mortality risk. The foundation model enabled effective training by use of relatively small clinical datasets. Routine quantitative facial analysis could enhance risk stratification when traditional biomarkers are unavailable. FUNDING: EU European Research Council.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The growing threat to health systems posed by extreme weather events (EWEs) disproportionately affects people living with HIV and tuberculosis disease in high-burden, low-resource settings. In Zimbabwe, for example, the 2023-24 El Niño-induced drought intensified food insecurity and reduced access to clinics and medication for such vulnerable populations. We aimed to conduct a formative evaluation to assess the perceived impact of climate change and EWEs on HIV and tuberculosis determinants and service delivery and identify potential climate-adaptive health-service strategies. METHODS: In this survey-based multicentre cross-sectional observational study with a formative evaluation supplemented by qualitative data, we surveyed people living with HIV from Sept 19 to Dec 19, 2024, across 321 clinics in Zimbabwe to describe their perceived impact of EWEs on their health. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling. The inclusion criteria were being diagnosed with HIV, being older than 18 years, and receiving HIV care at Organization for Public Health Interventions and Development (OPHID) clinics during the study period. Individuals who were not receiving HIV care at an OPHID clinic or who were younger than 18 years were excluded. A client satisfaction survey was used to collect data from in-person surveys. The survey included questions related to the general effects of EWEs, such as drought, extreme heat, and flooding; how EWEs had affected HIV or tuberculosis care; and what, if any, services were currently available or should be made available to mitigate climate impacts on health. We also conducted six focus group discussions (FGDs; five to eight participants per group) between March 12 and May 12, 2024, across the Bulilima, Mangwe, and Matobo districts. We used a convenience sampling approach to select patients who had visited the health facility for medical check-ups, medication resupply, or viral load testing, as recorded in clinical registers and verified by clinical staff. Eligible participants for the FGDs were adults (≥18 years) with HIV, or with current or previous tuberculosis treatment, receiving care at the study facility during the recruitment period; those under 18 years or not receiving care at the facility were excluded. Participants' sex was self-reported at enrolment. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively, whereas FGD data were analysed using a modified framework approach. The main outcomes were the perceived impact of climate change and EWEs on HIV and tuberculosis determinants and service delivery outcomes, as reported by affected communities, and community-prioritised mitigation strategies to feasibly address climate-sensitive determinants and barriers to care. FINDINGS: Among 1804 eligible participants approached across 15 districts, all completed the survey and were included in the analysis. Most survey participants (1363 [75·6%] of 1804 participants) reported noticing changes in climate over the past 5 years; of these 1363 participants, 900 (66·0%) were female and 1024 (75·1%) participants reported disruptions to their HIV care during the time they noticed changes in climate. Survey respondents reported that climate-related disruptions were associated with increased food insecurity (reported by 877 [85·6%] of 1024 participants) and water shortage (667 [65·1%] of 1024 participants). Qualitative analysis confirmed that the barriers to HIV and tuberculosis care from EWEs included widespread food insecurity, crop failures, and livestock deaths, with consequent effects on income leading to challenges in paying for food and transportation to clinics. Participants highlighted the need for expanded services that facilitate social and economic wellbeing, including nutrition support, water access, transportation, and income-generating activities, and decentralised models of health-care delivery. INTERPRETATION: Extreme heat and drought affect food and water security and have financial implications, creating challenges for patients to access care in Zimbabwe. Our findings underscore the urgent need for integrated, climate-adaptive strategies to maintain HIV and tuberculosis care in such climate-vulnerable regions. FUNDING: Nina Ireland Program in Lung Health.

papers.abstract_en: Bladder cancer is a major malignancy worldwide. Although cigarette smoking is the leading modifiable risk factor, the contribution of waterpipe smoking (WPS), which is increasingly popular globally and often misperceived as safer, remains unclear. In 2019, Lebanese males had the highest bladder cancer incidence in the Arab world (five times the global average), prompting investigation of WPS as a potential carcinogen. We performed a cross-sectional genomic analysis of patients with exclusive WPS and urothelial carcinoma treated at the American University of Beirut Medical Center (n=250 screened; 14 exclusively WPS), integrating targeted sequencing (MSK-IMPACT®) and whole-exome sequencing (TEMPO pipeline). Tumor mutational burden (TMB), microsatellite instability, mutational signatures, and oncogenic alterations were assessed. Previously profiled bladder cancer tumors from cigarette smokers and non-smokers at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (n=751) served as comparators. MSK-IMPACT® successfully profiled 13 tumors. WPS-associated tumors exhibited a numerically higher median TMB than cigarette (20 vs. 10 mut/Mb; p=0.10, q=0.2), with 38.5% classified as MSS-hypermutated, a phenotype associated with elevated mutational load despite microsatellite stability. Common mutations included TERT promoter (62%), TP53 and FGFR3 (46%), and PIK3CA (38%). APOBEC mutational signatures predominated across all cohorts, suggesting shared mutagenic processes, while chromatin-modifying gene alterations were less frequent. PD-L1 expression was generally low. Implications: Exclusive WPS induces bladder tumors with overall genomic features resembling cigarette-associated disease, yet with numerically higher TMB and enrichment of MSS-hypermutated phenotypes. These findings provide novel mechanistic evidence of tobacco-related carcinogenesis beyond cigarettes and highlight potential biomarker relevance for immunotherapy in a globally rising exposure group.

papers.abstract_en: Metastasis is the primary cause of mortality in cancer including lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Preferentially expressed antigen of melanoma (PRAME), a cancer-testis antigen, displays context-dependent functions across malignancies, but its biological role in LUAD metastasis has not been clearly defined. Here, we demonstrate that the significantly upregulated PRAME in metastatic LUAD directly interacts with the m6A methyltransferase METTL3 and promotes its K63-linked non-proteolytic ubiquitination. This modification occurs at lysine 235 of METTL3, increases its protein stability and facilitates METTL3 interaction with METTL14 and WTAP. Consequently, m6A modification of TGFB2 mRNA and activation of the TGF-β signaling pathway are enhanced, which is essential for PRAME-driven pro-metastatic effects both in vitro and in vivo. Clinically, PRAME expression positively correlates with METTL3 protein abundance and TGF-β pathway activation, and is robustly associated with poor clinical outcomes. Taken together, our findings identify K63-linked ubiquitination as a previously unrecognized post-translational modification of METTL3 and underscore the importance of the PRAME/METTL3/TGF-β axis in LUAD metastasis, providing mechanistic insights and potential therapeutic targets for this malignancy.

papers.abstract_en: H2AK119ub (H2Aub) and H3K27me3, which are deposited by the Polycomb group (PcG) complexes PRC1 and PRC2, respectively, cooperatively repress developmental genes. Loss of H2Aub abolishes H3K27me3 reestablishment at PcG targets causing moderate derepression, accompanied by ectopic H3K27me3 deposition and impaired embryonic development. Finally, H2Aub and DNA methylation cooperatively maintain H3K27me3 patterning in human embryonic stem cells. Therefore, H2Aub-dependent H3K27me3 deposition underlies the earliest establishment of Polycomb repression in humans.

papers.abstract_en: Light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) enables gentle, rapid and efficient volumetric imaging of biological specimens. Despite its potential, LSFM has fragmented into multiple variants, each narrowly optimized for specific samples or imaging regimes, limiting its broad applicability. Here we introduce the multi-immersion oblique plane microscope (miOPM), an adaptable LSFM platform for high-resolution imaging ranging from subcellular dynamics to whole organisms and cleared tissues. miOPM supports seamless interchangeability of oil, water and air objectives and maintains diffraction-limited performance across a refractive index range of 1.33 to 1.51. By expanding the adaptability and ease of use of LSFM, miOPM is poised to democratize advanced 3D imaging.

Twenty-six completed conservative treatment, and 54 underwent surgery. In practice, conservative treatment was used for clinically stable patients without peritonitis or CT signs suggesting ischaemia, perforation or closed-loop obstruction, provided that close clinical monitoring was possible. Conservative treatment included bowel rest, intravenous fluids, electrolyte correction, symptom-directed medication and nasogastric decompression when needed. Failure was defined by clinical deterioration, persistent or worsening obstruction, inability to tolerate oral intake, or new radiological concern. The primary outcome was clinical resolution during the index admission. Secondary outcomes were hospitalisation, in-hospital mortality, postoperative complications and readmission after discharge. RESULTS: The treatment groups were not equivalent at baseline. Patients treated surgically more often had gastric bezoars (18/54, 33.3% vs. 0/26, p = 0.002), multiple bezoars (18/54, 33.3% vs. 1/26, 3.8%, p = 0.009) and greater small-bowel dilatation (median 4.0 cm vs. 3.4 cm, p = 0.014). All 26 patients in the conservative pathway completed the index admission without operation, although routine radiological confirmation of resolution was not performed. Median hospitalisation was 4 days (IQR 4-5) in the surgical group and 7 days (6-8) in the conservative group (p < 0.001); this difference should be interpreted in the context of clinical selection and local practice. Postoperative complications occurred in 11/54 surgical patients (20.4%), including two deaths from pulmonary embolism. Among discharged patients, readmission did not differ significantly between groups (13/52, 25.0% after surgery vs. 5/26, 19.2% after conservative treatment; p = 0.776). Exploratory regression findings were treated as hypothesis-generating only. CONCLUSIONS: Conservative treatment may be feasible in selected stable patients with bezoar ileus after previous abdominal surgery. Surgery remains appropriate for patients with peritonitis, suspected ischaemia, perforation or closed-loop obstruction, clinical deterioration, or failure of conservative management. Because treatment was not protocolised and the groups differed at baseline, the findings should be read as observational and hypothesis-generating, not as evidence that either strategy is superior.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To explore needs among persons with advanced COPD and informal caregivers, and to explore how palliative care can address those needs. BACKGROUND: COPD is a common, progressive disease affecting lung function and represents a leading cause of death. Advanced COPD is associated with a high symptom burden and poor quality of life. Persons with advanced COPD may benefit from palliative care, but its use among persons with COPD remains limited, also in Germany. METHODS: A qualitative, multi-perspective interview study was conducted with persons suffering from advanced COPD, informal caregivers, and formal caregivers (general practitioners, pulmonologists, and palliative care physicians). A total of 53 interviews were analysed following structuring (Kuckartz') as well as latent content analysis methods using MAXQDA. RESULTS: Key needs were identified in the following domains (1) management of dyspnoea and anxiety, (2) home-based healthcare, (3) emergency planning and support, (4) psychosocial care, (5) organisational support, and (6) timely information about COPD and palliative care. Persons who had previously received PC reported various needs met in the first five areas. CONCLUSIONS: Persons with advanced COPD and their informal caregivers reported numerous needs. Persons receiving palliative care reported relief from various needs. Timely information about COPD's progression and palliative care could increase acceptance and thus use of palliative care among these persons and could consequently reduce or curtail the burden of living with advanced COPD.

papers.abstract_en: AIMS: Using more than five decades of national data, we examine how age, period and cohort factors influence lung cancer mortality in Switzerland, and forecast future death counts to the early 2040s. METHODS: Lung cancer deaths were extracted from Swiss vital statistics. We applied age-period-cohort (APC) modelling to lung cancer mortality rates using substantiated assumptions about the age-mortality relationship as model constraints. To account for the uncertainty in the age-mortality relationship, boundary constraints were applied to the line of APC solutions, yielding a range of plausible results. In an alternative model, we replaced the cohort terms with smoking prevalence estimates from Swiss health surveys, enabling unconstrained modelling of age and period effects. Predictions are based on modelled age trends, and linearly extrapolated period and cohort trends. RESULTS: Plausible age, period and cohort effects indicated that age-specific mortality risks decline at the oldest ages, that period effects were minimal, while cohort effects showed distinct peak risks for men born around 1909 and women born around 1954. Among women, birth cohorts with the highest mortality closely aligned with those exhibiting the highest smoking prevalence. The models predicted a decline in the number of lung cancer deaths among men beginning in the mid-2020s, and among women from the mid-2030s onwards. CONCLUSIONS: This population-based analysis of lung cancer mortality not only highlights declining mortality rates in men of all ages, but reveals an emerging downward trend among younger women. We predict that the total number of lung cancer deaths in women will begin to decrease by the mid-2030s.

papers.abstract_en: Medical image segmentation is essential for computer-aided diagnosis and precision medicine, yet conventional supervised models depend heavily on high-quality annotations and often generalize poorly across domains. The Segment Anything Model (SAM) family offers a transferable, interactive, and extensible foundation for segmentation, but direct medical transfer remains limited by domain gaps, insufficient modeling of medical semantics and anatomy, and mismatches in high-dimensional volumetric and sequential imaging scenarios. This review critically examines the evolution and native capability boundaries of SAM, SAM 2, and SAM 3. Across generations, native capabilities expand from spatial prompting to sequential propagation and concept-level target specification, without automatically conferring medical expertise. We organize medical adaptation from three connected perspectives: model adaptation and strategy selection, task knowledge organization and utilization, and application-oriented adaptation. Cross-method analysis shows that no strategy is universally optimal; effectiveness depends on the gap between foundation-model capabilities and target-task requirements, together with data scale, domain discrepancy, imaging dimensionality, computational resources, and clinical constraints. We further identify four priorities for clinical translation: standardized evaluation for cross-study comparability, controlled continual adaptation under clinical domain drift, dynamic resource scheduling for high-dimensional and real-time workflows, and uncertainty stratification and clinical reliability control. Overall, further progress depends on accurate capability assessment, condition-matched adaptation, and explicit control of computational and prediction risks.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Esophageal variceal (EV) bleeding is a lethal complication in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Current risk stratification relies on invasive endoscopy or systemic surrogates of liver cirrhosis. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model utilizing EV-specific CT radiomics to identify high-risk esophageal varices, as defined by endoscopic criteria, in patients with HCC. METHODS: 151 HCC patients were enrolled and divided into a training cohort (n = 101; 75 high-risk; January 2017 - December 2022) and an independent temporal validation cohort (n = 50; 29 high-risk; January 2023 - December 2024). Endoscopic stigmata were used as an endpoint, including active bleeding or varices with high-risk features. Radiomic features were extracted from contrast-enhanced CT images acquired within six months prior to endoscopy. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC) of receiver operating characteristic (ROC), Brier score, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). RESULTS: In the training cohort, the varix-specific radiomics signature developed via the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) demonstrated excellent discriminative power (cross-validated AUC: 0.956; 95% CI 0.872-1.000). In the temporal validation cohort, this model maintained high generalizability, yielding an AUC of 0.926 (95% CI 0.846-0.984, sensitivity: 93.1%, specificity: 71.4%) as well as a Brier score of 0.1186 and good calibration (intercept = -0.157, slope = 1.354). Surface-to-Volume Ratio (SVR) and NGTDM Coarseness are feasible radiomics. CONCLUSION: The varix-specific radiomics model provides highly sensitive and mathematically stable non-invasive risk stratification for EV bleeding in patients with HCC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The role of hilar lymph node metastasis (LNM) in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) was investigated and a simple postoperative risk-stratification system combining LNM and preoperative anemia was established to predict the outcome of patients with ICC after curative resection. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 384 patients who underwent hepatectomy for ICC. Both postoperative clinical outcomes and long-term oncological outcomes were systematically evaluated. Subsequently, predictive models were developed to assess the risks of tumor recurrence, overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS). RESULTS: The primary cohort demonstrated 65.2% recurrence and 13.1-month median RFS (1-/3-/5-year rates: 51.9%/37.6%/25.0%), with median OS of 31.1 months (1-/3-/5-year rates: 81.8%/63.3%/54.1%). The external validation cohort showed 79.4% recurrence, 11.7-month median RFS (1-/3-/5-year rates: 49.5%/11.8%/5.9%), and 16.2-month median OS (1-/3-/5-year rates: 98.1%/10.4%/6.4%). We developed nomograms for recurrence, OS, and RFS incorporating LNM and preoperative anemia, yielding C-indices of 0.881, 0.802, and 0.758, respectively. Risk-stratified analysis revealed significant prognostic discrimination: high-risk patients demonstrated substantially inferior 5-year OS compared to low-risk patients (19.6% vs. 86.6%, P < 0.001), with median OS of 16.7 months versus not reached. Similarly, median RFS declined from not reached in low-risk patients to 6.1 months in high-risk patients. These results were confirmed in the external validation cohort, where high-risk status corresponded to a median OS of 14.4 months and median RFS of 8.1 months (both P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: The integration of LNM status and preoperative anemia emerges as a novel and clinically valuable prognostic indicator, effectively predicting outcomes in patients with ICC following curative resection, thereby providing tailored clinical guidance for postoperative adjuvant therapy selection and intensive surveillance planning.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) can exacerbate myocardial fibrosis, which may further impair microvascular function. However, the relationship between CMD and the extracellular volume fraction (ECV) in patients with ischemia with no obstructive coronary artery disease (INOCA) who are late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)-negative remains undetermined. We used T1 mapping and ECV to assess diffuse myocardial tissue abnormalities and extracellular compartment expansion in LGE-negative patients with CMD. We then investigated how these markers correlate with global myocardial flow reserve (MFR). METHODS: Between August 2024 and May 2026, we prospectively enrolled 86 LGE-negative patients with INOCA from a single center who underwent a positron emission tomography-magnetic resonance imaging (PET-MRI) protocol. Patients with significant epicardial stenosis (stenosis on coronary angiogram or computed tomography ≥ 50%), prior history of revascularization, known myocardial infarction, or heart failure were excluded. MFR and ECV were derived from PET perfusion imaging and pre- and post-T1 mapping, respectively. CMD was defined as PET-derived MFR of < 2.0 in at least one major coronary artery territory. RESULTS: Among the 86 patients included, 39 (45.3%) were diagnosed with CMD. ECV was substantially higher in the CMD group (31.22 [29.93, 33.25]% vs. 26.66 [25.85, 27.55]%, P < 0.001), with a more modest but statistically significant elevation in native T1 (1225 ± 25 ms vs. 1212 ± 21 ms, P = 0.012). Multivariable linear regression revealed that only global MFR (β [95% confidence interval] = - 1.905 [- 2.489, - 1.321], P < 0.001) was an independent predictor of ECV in LGE-negative CMD patients. In the overall cohort, resting myocardial blood flow (MBF) (r = 0.539, P < 0.001) and global MFR (r = - 0.741, P < 0.001) were positively and negatively correlated with ECV, respectively. When participants were stratified into ECV tertiles, global MFR showed a progressive decrease (2.92 vs. 2.48 vs. 1.78; P < 0.001 for trend) with increasing ECV values. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with INOCA with CMD, prolonged native T1 and elevated ECV indicate diffuse interstitial expansion, consistent with early tissue remodeling, even when LGE is absent on CMR. These findings suggest that native T1 and ECV may hold promise as adjunctive tissue markers to support risk stratification, though their role in clinical management requires further validation in larger cohorts.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) are associated with substantial short term mortality and healthcare utilization, yet the prognostic utility of the immunonutrition based hemoglobin, albumin, lymphocyte, and platelet (HALP) score in this setting remains unclear, particularly in comparison with the well validated dyspnoea, eosinopenia, consolidation, acidaemia, atrial fibrillation (DECAF) score. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, single centre observational cohort study of adults presenting to the emergency department (ED) with AECOPD between June 2022 and June 2025. DECAF and HALP scores were calculated at admission using routinely collected clinical and laboratory data, and the primary outcome was 30 day in hospital mortality. Discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, with Youden-derived, data-driven cut-off values, and we further evaluated previously validated DECAF thresholds and a categorical DECAF model. Associations with 30 day mortality were examined using univariable and multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for baseline clinical variables. Model calibration was evaluated using Brier scores and the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and 30 day survival was analysed with Kaplan-Meier. RESULTS: A total of 499 patients were included in the study, 63 (12.6%) died within 30 days, and 76% of the cohort were male. The HALP score showed acceptable predictive performance (area under the curve (AUC) 0.724), at a cut-off of 16.84, sensitivity was 57.1%, specificity 75.0% and negative predictive value (NPV) 92.4% for 30 day in hospital mortality. The DECAF score demonstrated excellent discrimination for 30 day in hospital mortality (AUC 0.932), and showed significantly better discrimination than HALP (DeLong p < 0.001), using a cut-off of ≥ 4, sensitivity was 76.2%, specificity 95.6% and NPV 96.5%. CONCLUSION: In ED patients with AECOPD, the HALP score provides only limited prognostic information for 30 day in hospital mortality, whereas the DECAF score exhibits excellent discriminative performance and retains its value as a robust, clinically applicable predictor of short term outcomes in acute care.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The impact of different inguinal hernia repair techniques on testicular perfusion remains a subject of clinical interest. While open and laparoscopic approaches demonstrate comparable outcomes in terms of recurrence and complications, their effects on testicular microcirculation are not fully elucidated. METHODS: This retrospective comparative cohort study included 180 male patients who underwent unilateral primary inguinal hernia repair using open Lichtenstein, total extraperitoneal (TEP), or transabdominal preperitoneal (TAPP) techniques between January 2015 and December 2025 at a tertiary referral center. Doppler ultrasonography parameters, including resistive index (RI), peak systolic velocity (PSV), end-diastolic velocity (EDV), and testicular volume, were evaluated preoperatively, at postoperative day 7, and at 1 month. Changes over time and between groups were analyzed using multivariable regression and linear mixed-effects models. Subclinical testicular ischemia was defined based on predefined Doppler criteria. RESULTS: Early postoperative changes in testicular perfusion parameters differed significantly between surgical techniques. At postoperative day 7, RI values were higher and EDV values were lower in the Lichtenstein group compared to TEP and TAPP (p < 0.001 and p = 0.002, respectively). These differences decreased at 1 month but remained statistically significant for RI (p = 0.003). Multivariable analysis demonstrated that surgical technique, operative time, and hernia sac size were independently associated with changes in RI. Subclinical testicular ischemia was more frequent in the Lichtenstein group, while laparoscopic approaches were associated with lower odds (TEP: OR 0.34, p = 0.002; TAPP: OR 0.41, p = 0.006). Longitudinal analysis confirmed a significant time-by-technique interaction for RI (p < 0.001), indicating partial recovery over time. CONCLUSION: Surgical technique is associated with transient alterations in testicular perfusion following inguinal hernia repair. Open Lichtenstein repair demonstrated more pronounced early microvascular changes, whereas laparoscopic techniques exhibited a more stable perfusion profile. These findings highlight the importance of surgical technique and intraoperative handling in preserving testicular microcirculation.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To evaluate the nationwide adoption of genicular artery embolization (GAE) in Germany and to describe patient selection, technique, safety and radiation dose. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed procedures recorded in the quality-assurance registry of the German Society for Interventional Radiology and Minimally Invasive Therapy (DeGIR), from January 2024 to December 2025. Technical success, entered per procedure, was defined as subjective adequate devascularization of the synovial blush. Complications were graded using the modified CIRSE classification, and radiation exposure was expressed as dose-area product (DAP) and fluoroscopy time. The analysis was primarily descriptive. RESULTS: Overall, 2335 procedures in 2209 patients across 109 centers in 15 federal states were recorded (median age 67 years, IQR 59-77; 57% female; prior total knee arthroplasty (TKA) in 300, 13%). Annual volume rose from 579 procedures in 2024 to 1,756 in 2025, and the embolic agent shifted from permanent (40-21%) toward temporary microspheres (4-29%). Center-reported technical success was 93% (87% in 2024, 94% in 2025). Eleven complications were recorded (0.5%), all CIRSE grade 1-3, with no permanent sequelae; none were recorded in 2024. Median DAP was 1536 cGy cm2 (IQR 731-3048) and median fluoroscopy time 24 min (IQR 16-34). CONCLUSION: During rapid nationwide adoption, GAE was performed for osteoarthritis-related and post-TKA pain with low radiation dose and high center-reported technical success across centers of all volumes, supporting its feasibility in routine practice. The complication rate is a lower limit, as the registry is not designed for complication surveillance.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To compare the costs of percutaneous segmentectomy, a single-session combination of transarterial embolisation and microwave ablation, against chemoembolisation and radioembolisation for hepatocellular carcinoma. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective cost analysis of 66 patients treated with percutaneous segmentectomy at five Italian centres, using bottom-up micro-costing. Comparator costs were derived from published Italian per-session costs multiplied by mean sessions per patient, and survival from published curves. A partitioned survival model estimated life-years and incremental net monetary benefit at 50,000 euros per life-year. RESULTS: Procedural cost per treated patient was 6331 euros for percutaneous segmentectomy, 9792 euros for chemoembolisation (mean 2.94 sessions), and 21,673 euros for radioembolisation (1.52 sessions). At 24 months, percutaneous segmentectomy had lower total cost and a small life-year deficit (incremental cost-effectiveness ratio approximately 70,800 euros per life-year versus chemoembolisation and 57,500 versus radioembolisation, both above threshold). This life-year-adjusted advantage reversed versus chemoembolisation, and became neutral versus radioembolisation, in a worst-case sensitivity analysis, and reversed against both when transplantation costs for the eight transplanted patients (19%) were attributed to percutaneous segmentectomy alone. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory analysis, percutaneous segmentectomy appeared to have a lower procedural cost per treated patient than chemoembolisation and radioembolisation, mainly because it is delivered in a single session. However, because costing routes, cohorts, and survival sources were not equivalent and the life-year-adjusted comparison was not robust, no formal cost superiority can be established. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in prospective, matched studies. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4, Retrospective Cohort Study with Historical Comparators.

papers.abstract_en: Fetal cerebral ventriculomegalies are brain anomalies with potentially poor neurodevelopmental prognosis. They are amenable to prenatal imaging, isolated or associated with other cerebral and/or extra-cerebral abnormalities. Most are obstructive due to a focal or diffuse dysgenesis of the ventricular system, disturbing the cerebro-spinal fluid outflow. Triventricular dilatation is the most common, predicting a lesion at the level of the aqueduct of Sylvius (AS). Although variants in several genes have recently been linked to ventriculomegaly, their role remains unclear, compromising our ability to predict the impact of such variations when detected prenatally. To go further, we report here a monocentric cohort of 51 fetuses with cerebral ventriculomegaly linked to dysgenetic AS and discuss phenotype/genotype correlations after neuropathological study. A genetic cause has been identified in 15 cases (29.4%) using different genetic methods available between 1992 and 2021: standard karyotyping, targeted mutation screening (Sanger sequencing), and Next Generation Sequencing. Dysgeneses of the AS are still controversial in their nosology and etiology; most are discussed on the basis of brain imaging findings alone. In this series, complete fetal and neuropathological examination allowed detection of key clinical and histopathological clues, allowing the orientation of molecular screenings and the identification of cellular mechanisms involved in triventricular dilatations.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Tissue biomarkers may improve risk stratification in locally advanced cervical cancer before definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT). We evaluated pretreatment expression of chromobox 4 (CBX4), NADPH oxidase 4 (NOX4), specificity protein 1 (SP1), and copper transporter 1 (CTR1) in relation to CCRT response and overall survival. METHODS: In this retrospective 1:1 matched case-control study, pretreatment biopsies from 40 patients with locally advanced cervical squamous cell carcinoma (20 CCRT-resistant, 20 CCRT-sensitive) were quantified by AI-assisted digital pathology using H-scores. A parsimonious CBX4 + NOX4 logistic model was evaluated by apparent ROC, leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV), repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation, and bootstrap optimism correction. Overall survival analyses were exploratory. RESULTS: CBX4 and NOX4 expression was lower in CCRT-resistant tumors (median H-score: CBX4, 40.47 vs. 79.62; NOX4, 7.00 vs. 53.93; both p < 0.001), whereas SP1 and CTR1 did not differ. Apparent AUCs were 0.840 for CBX4 and 0.843 for NOX4. The two-marker model had an apparent AUC of 0.903, LOOCV AUC 0.845, repeated 5-fold CV AUC 0.854 ± 0.022, and bootstrap-corrected AUC 0.883. High CBX4 and NOX4 expression was associated with better 5-year overall survival; in joint Cox models, hazard ratios per 1-SD increase were 0.31 (95% CI 0.13-0.74) for CBX4 and 0.48 (0.26-0.90) for NOX4. No histochemically detectable copper deposits were observed. CONCLUSIONS: Lower pretreatment CBX4 and NOX4 expression was associated with a CCRT-resistant phenotype and poorer overall survival in this small, response-enriched cohort. Internal resampling suggested discrimination, but same-dataset marker selection may introduce residual optimism and does not establish generalizability. Independent validation in a consecutively recruited cohort is required before clinical application. No mechanisms involving DNA repair, ROS, or chemoradiotherapy sensitivity were established.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: New-onset diabetes (NOD) potentially associated with pancreatic cancer (PC) requires further investigation to assess its potential as a tool for PC screening. MATERIAL AND METHODS: In this longitudinal nationwide register study, which includes 14,712 PC patients and 18 years of follow-up time (2000-2018), we aimed to assess the prevalence of diabetes by using a large national registry. Survival was analyzed according to diabetes status and duration (long-term diabetes, i.e., DM diagnosed > 3 years prior to PC, NOD, i.e., DM diagnosed 0-3 years prior to PC, or DM diagnosed after PC diagnosis) and treatment status (curative intent vs. palliative) using multivariable Cox regression analysis. RESULTS: Overall, 18% of PC patients had diabetes. The median time interval between DM and PC diagnoses was 4.8 months. In the multivariable Cox regression analysis, only DM diagnosed after PC was associated with worse survival, both in the palliative intent treatment group (HR 1.12, 95% CI 1.03-1.23, p = 0.011) and in the curative intent treatment group (HR 1.44, 95% CI 1.14-1.81, p = 0.002). Among patients diagnosed with diabetes prior to PC, neither long-term nor NOD significantly affected survival. CONCLUSIONS: Most of the diabetic PC-patients have been diagnosed with DM within a close proximity of cancer diagnosis. The progression from diabetes to clinically detectable cancer seems to be rapid-less than 6 months. Given the aggressive nature of PC and the fact that NOD can be an early sign, screening may need to begin at the time of diabetes diagnosis. The fact that a DM diagnosis made after a PC diagnosis is associated with worse survival may suggest that pancreatic tumors that cause hyperglycemia are particularly aggressive.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Non-invasive tests (NITs) accurately detect fibrosis and may reduce the need for liver biopsy (LB). Detection of advanced fibrosis (≥F3) is clinically important for prognosis, but few studies have explored the use of NITs in patients with Wilson Disease (WD). METHODS: In this multicentre observational study, adult and pediatric WD patients from seven international expert centers with histologic fibrosis staging were included. NITs (Transient elastography (TE), Fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4), AST to platelet-ratio (APRI), Steatosis-associated fibrosis estimator (SAFE), and NAFLD fibrosis score (NFS)) and clinical data were collected. NITs were compared with liver biopsy (LB) to detect advanced fibrosis (≥F3). RESULTS: In total, 123 patients were included: median age was 30 years (IQR 17.4, 43.1); time from WD diagnosis to LB was 6.7 months (0.7, 144.1); 30.9% had advanced fibrosis (≥F3), while concomitant metabolic risk factors (obesity and diabetes) were rare. Overall, 64 patients had NITs measured within 1 year of the LB and constituted the primary analysis group. All NITs, except FIB-4, were significantly elevated in patients with ≥F3. TE had the best overall accuracy (AUC=0.79), and performed well at an optimized cut-off of ≥8.35 kPa (sens=0.88, spec=0.85). APRI had lower accuracy, but effectively ruled out ≥F3 at the optimized cut-off of ≥1.3 (AUC=0.71, sens=0.38, spec=1.00). Combining those into a score (APRITE) achieved an AUC of 0.88. DISCUSSION: TE demonstrated good diagnostic performance for identifying advanced fibrosis in WD. APRI showed high specificity, while the exploratory APRITE score showed encouraging performance.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cognitive impairment is a substantial comorbidity in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); however, the neural mechanisms underlying this association remain poorly understood. This study aimed to assess alterations in effective connectivity (EC) in patients with COPD and investigate their relationships with clinical measures. METHODS: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (RS-fMRI) was performed in 38 patients with COPD and 30 healthy controls. EC was estimated using vector autoregressive (VAR) modelling combined with Granger causality analysis across 26 prespecified brain regions of interest derived from our previous functional connectivity study of the same cohort. Between-group differences in directed connectivity were assessed using Welch's t-tests. Associations between EC measures showing between-group differences and clinical measures were evaluated using age-adjusted partial Pearson correlations. RESULTS: At the nominal two-sided p < 0.05 level, 37 directed connections showed between-group differences in effective connectivity, and the mean vector autoregressive coefficients for 35 of these connections lay on opposite sides of zero between the COPD and control groups. Among the connections showing between-group differences, age-adjusted associations in patients with COPD involved pulmonary function, systemic oxygenation, cognition, affect, and health status. These associations involved distributed cortical, subcortical, and cerebellar regions, with several directed connections showing convergence across multiple clinical domains. CONCLUSION: Resting-state VAR-based EC revealed distributed between-group differences in direction-sensitive BOLD temporal organization in COPD. Several of these EC measures were associated with pulmonary function, SpO2, respiratory and COPD symptom burden, cognition, affect, and health status after age adjustment. These findings extend the functional connectivity profile of COPD by linking directed temporal relationships to its multidimensional clinical burden.

papers.abstract_en: Benchmarks labelled by panels of human readers underpin most medical image analysis. We ask whether such a dataset has a single attainable ceiling. All 1319 annotation files of the Lung Image Database Consortium image collection (LIDC-IDRI) were parsed into 7034 reader-level ratings. Modelling each nodule by a latent malignancy propensity of which the four reader verdicts are conditionally independent draws, we prove that no image-based model can exceed, against a reader-derived label, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of the propensity itself; we derive how that bound depends on the labelling policy, test the independence assumption against a prediction the fit does not use, simulate its failures, and audit a purposive sample of 22 published studies against the rules they declare. Among 905 nodules read by all four radiologists, all four agreed exactly for 11.7% and 58.0% carried ratings spanning two or more points. Across three latent families, retaining every nodule the ceiling is 0.898-0.913; discarding the 19.6% the readers split two-two lifts it to 0.946-0.954; retaining only unanimous nodules discards 57.7% and lifts it to 0.991-0.994. On the binary scale, no family predicted more reader agreement than observed; simulated reader heterogeneity would make these ceilings slightly low. Of 27 reported figures, 11 lie above the bound implied by the study's own declared rule, four beyond sampling error and two if modest heterogeneity is also allowed for. The ceiling is set by the label, not by the images.

Three datasets were used: an abdominal CT dataset of 300 subjects with adipose-tissue labels, a lower-limb Dixon MRI dataset of 25 subjects with 13 thigh and 9 calf muscles, and an independent cohort of 66 subjects for external testing. Network architecture, encoder pretraining, a Dixon-derived fat-fraction input, and a shared CT-MRI encoder were compared. A 2.5D model, subject-level cross-validation, zero-shot transfer, label-free domain adaptation, and few-shot adaptation were also evaluated. The best models reached Dice 0.947 ± 0.017  for CT adipose tissue and 0.925 ± 0.010  for thigh muscle; the best 2.5D model reached 0.928, while a reported 3D Attention-Res-V-Net reached 0.857 under a different protocol. Encoder pretraining helped most at the smallest budgets, with ImageNet performing best and comparably to CT-based pretraining at eight subjects. A shared CT-MRI encoder retained accuracy with 44 %  fewer parameters, and thigh-muscle volumes agreed closely with reference measurements (ICC ( 2 , 1 ) = 0.998  ). On the external cohort, fine-tuning raised Dice from 0.11 zero-shot to 0.61, 0.76, and 0.88 with four, eight, and 46 labelled target subjects. The fat-fraction input improved segmentation only when very few subjects (two or four) were labelled. Encoder pretraining and efficient model sharing help when annotated MRI data are scarce. A small amount of target-domain annotation substantially improves cross-cohort transfer, and repeated subject-level validation is important for reliable evaluation.

papers.abstract_en: Automatic colorectal polyp segmentation in retrospective still colonoscopy images remains challenging for small, low-contrast, partially occluded, or irregular lesions. We propose SVF-Net, a heterogeneous dual-encoder network combining a frozen SAM2 Hiera-L image trunk with a trainable MaxViT-RMLP-Small specialist branch. At four feature scales, the two streams are projected to a common width, spatially aligned, and reconciled by complementary channel-spatial gating before progressive decoding. Across five public benchmarks, three-run mean mDice is 0.922 on CVC-ClinicDB, 0.898 on Kvasir-SEG, 0.805 on CVC-ColonDB, 0.770 on ETIS-LaribPolypDB, and 0.896 on CVC-300. Matched projected-concatenation and fixed-weight ( G = 0.5  ) controls retain the surrounding fusion path while removing input-dependent weighting; across ten matched training runs, adaptive gating gives higher mean mDice than both controls on all five datasets. Dataset-wide gate diagnostics on all 380 CVC-ColonDB and 196 ETIS cases indicate non-collapsed, scale- and region-dependent activations, while targeted one-factor sensitivity checks cover the MaxViT learning-rate multiplier, gate initialization, and auxiliary-loss weight. Matched per-case analyses further show that cross-domain gains are heterogeneous across lesion size, brightness, and an image-derived specular-reflection proxy. SVF-Net requires 92.8 ms per image (10.8 FPS) and 8.5 GB peak GPU memory on an NVIDIA RTX 3090 under the reported profiling protocol. The study evaluates retrospective static images only and does not establish real-time colonoscopy performance, prospective clinical effectiveness, or clinician benefit.
