papers.abstract_en: The da Vinci Xi replaced the Si with a boom-mounted architecture intended to remove the re-docking and multiquadrant limits on pelvic access. Whether it changes outcomes in rectal cancer surgery is unresolved: existing syntheses pooled rectal with colonic resection. Five databases, Google Scholar and citation graphs were searched to August 2026, without language or design restriction, for comparative studies reporting outcomes separately by platform in rectal cancer resection. Screening, extraction and risk-of-bias assessment were done in duplicate. Random-effects models with a Hartung-Knapp adjustment were used; certainty was rated with GRADE. Eight non-randomised cohorts (843 patients; 380 Xi, 463 Si) were included. Pooling all five cohorts reporting operative time, the mean difference was - 27.7 min (95% confidence interval - 80.4 to + 25.0; I² 95%); restricted to the four reporting means with standard deviations, thus conditional on excluding the largest cohort, it was - 50.6 min (- 69.4 to - 31.7). Docking time was shorter with the Xi in all three reporting cohorts, which defined it differently or not at all. The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of platform on anastomotic leak (risk ratio 0.53, 0.24 to 1.14), complications, conversion, reoperation, margin involvement and specimen quality; certainty was very low throughout. The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of the da Vinci Xi compared with the Si on perioperative and oncological outcomes in rectal cancer, and functional outcomes have not been compared. Because the platforms were compared across periods, centres and levels of experience, no estimate isolates the platform.PROSPERO registration CRD420261480007, registered 18 August 2026, before data extraction.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) is associated with high mortality and morbidity. Antenatal counselling enables parents to prepare for the postnatal outcomes and relies on effective prognostic tools. Ultrasound (USS) predictors including observed/expected lung head ratio (o/e LHR) and liver position, are used independently, or combined into severity classifications. The aim was to evaluate the association between USS predictors, and severity classifications with survival to discharge and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) requirement in prenatally diagnosed CDH at Birmingham Women's and Children's Hospital (BWC). METHODS: CDH patients from BWC with dates of birth between 1st December 2013-1st December 2023 were retrospectively collected. Study inclusion required o/e LHR measurement between 22- and 32-weeks gestational age (GA.) Comparisons between groups was assessed by Fisher exact test and Mann-Whitney U test. Logistic regression was performed to determine prognostic ability, with area under curve (AUC) calculated. RESULTS: 91 eligible patients were identified, which included 82 left-sided, and 9 right-sided CDH. Overall, 55% survived to discharge and 13% required ECMO. In the left CDH cohort, 57% of infants survived to discharge, and 15% required ECMO. O/e LHR, liver position and the combined predictive model including o/e LHR and liver position were predictive of survival to discharge with good prognostic ability (AUC 0.769, AUC 0.703, and AUC 0.823, respectively). O/e LHR, liver position, and the combined predictive model were not predictive of ECMO requirement. In the right CDH patients, 33% survived to discharge, O/e LHR and liver position were not predictive of survival to discharge. CONCLUSION: O/e LHR, liver position and the combination of these predictors, predicted survival to discharge in prenatally diagnosed left CDH with the combined model, the most predictive particularly in the isolated left CDH sub-group. Further analysis into effective predictors for ECMO requirement, and for right and complex left CDH is required.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cancer treatment-induced bone loss (CTIBL) is well-recognized in hormone-sensitive malignancies such as breast and prostate cancer but is less consistently implemented in patients with other solid tumors and hematologic malignancies. Furthermore, the long-term skeletal effects of newer systemic therapies, including immune checkpoint inhibitors and targeted agents, remain incompletely characterized. Although bone mineral density (BMD) assessment by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) is recommended for patients at increased skeletal risk, real-world utilization patterns remain poorly characterized. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate DXA utilization, timing, BMD results, and associated clinical characteristics following a new cancer diagnosis in a large real-world cohort. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the MDClone platform, including adults with a first cancer diagnosis between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2024, treated at Assuta Medical Centers in Israel. DXA completion, timing, BMD and T-scores, and prevalence of osteopenia and osteoporosis were analyzed. RESULTS: Among 21,112 patients with newly diagnosed cancer (77.0% women; mean age 60.2 ± 13.1 years), 7496 (35.5%) underwent DXA at any time following diagnosis. DXA utilization was significantly lower in men than in women (15.0% vs. 41.7%). Early DXA assessment within 6 months of diagnosis was uncommon (1550 patients; 7.3% of the total cohort), and only 14.1% underwent DXA within the first 12 months. Median time from cancer diagnosis to DXA was 14.8 months. DXA utilization varied by cancer type and was highest in breast cancer (42.2%) and prostate cancer (30.0%), with substantially lower utilization among patients with other malignancies. Among patients with complete evaluable measurements, 40.2% had normal BMD, 45.2% had osteopenia, and 14.5% met criteria for osteoporosis. CONCLUSIONS: In our real-world experience within a large private healthcare network, DXA assessment after cancer diagnosis is infrequently performed and often delayed, with marked disparities by sex and cancer type. A substantial burden of low bone mass is already present at the time of evaluation, highlighting missed opportunities for early skeletal risk identification.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Brain metastases (BM) are frequent in EGFR-mutated (EGFRm) non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and remain challenging after prior EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. This exploratory study evaluated high-dose fimmonertinib and explored subtype-specific spatial biology. METHODS: iFORCE was a prospective, single-center, single-arm study. Eligible patients had advanced NSCLC harboring EGFR mutations with previously treated BM following EGFR-TKI therapy, or intracranial disease progression. Patients received 160 mg firmonertinib once daily. The primary endpoint was intracranial progression-free survival (iPFS). Archival paired primary tumors and BM specimens from an independent retrospective cohort underwent exploratory digital spatial profiling (DSP). RESULTS: Twenty-three patients were enrolled. At a median follow-up of 19.7 months (95% CI, 14.5-25.3), median iPFS was 14.6 months (95% CI, 4.2-not estimable [NE]), with 12- and 18-month iPFS rates of 53.8% and 46.1%, respectively. Based on the best intracranial overall response, intracranial objective response and disease control rates were 34.8% (95% CI, 16.4-57.3) and 91.3% (95% CI, 72.0-98.9). Median systemic PFS was 10.7 months (95% CI, 3.9-NE). Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 13 (56.5%) patients, mostly grade 1; one patient (4.3%) developed grade 3 stomatitis. No treatment discontinuations or treatment-related deaths were observed. DSP revealed distinct EGFR subtype-specific BM ecosystems: exon 19 deletion tumors retained immune-enriched inflammatory programs, whereas L858R-mutated tumors showed tumor-intrinsic cell-cycle, DNA-repair, RNA-splicing, apoptosis-resistance, and immune-evasion features. CONCLUSIONS: Fimonertinib 160 mg showed promising intracranial activity with a manageable safety profile in EGFR-TKI-treated EGFRm NSCLC with BM. L858R BM displayed tumor-intrinsic, microenvironment-independent biology, suggesting preferential sensitivity to high-dose firmonertinib.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Marijuana (cannabis) use has become increasingly prevalent worldwide, raising concerns about its potential long-term health effects, particularly on the respiratory system. While tobacco smoking is a well-established risk factor for lung cancer,the association between cannabis use and lung cancer risk remains unclear and controversial. This systematic review and meta-analysis of existing observational studies aimed to evaluate the potential relationship between marijuana use and the risk ofdeveloping lung cancer. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus to identify cohort and case-controlstudies up to September 2025. Studies were selected, relevant data were extracted, and statistically analyzed using effect sizes (ES)and 95% confidence intervals (CI). All analyses were conducted using STATA software. FINDINGS: This meta-analysis included six observational studies, comprising 16 effect sizes, consisting of two cohort studies andfour case-control studies. The pooled analysis of the cohort studies (7 effect sizes) indicated a statistically significant associationbetween marijuana (cannabis) smoking and increased lung cancer risk (ES: 2.06; 95% CI: [1.04-4.07]; P=0.038; I2=75%). Incontrast, the meta-analysis of the case-control studies (9 effect sizes) showed a non-significant increase in risk (ES: 1.16; 95% CI:[0.71-1.88]; P=0.542; I2=82%). CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis indicates that marijuana smoking may increase lung cancer risk, with cohort studies showing asignificant twofold association. Although case-control studies were not statistically significant, the upward trend highlights theimportance of considering cannabis use in lung cancer risk assessments and patient counseling.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Entosis is an actomyosin-dependent cell-in-cell process that may culminate in lysosome-mediated entotic cell death and is implicated in tumor evolution. Its clinical relevance in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains unclear. METHODS: To construct an Entosis-related Prognostic Prediction Index (EPPI), this study integrated TCGA-LUAD transcriptomic, clinical, and somatic mutation data. Three independent GEO cohorts provided external validation. The initial candidate gene set covered components driving cell-in-cell formation and the intracellular degradation of internalized cells. For subgroup comparison, the analytical approach incorporated survival analysis, functional enrichment, tumor microenvironment profiling, mutation analysis, immunotherapy assessment, and drug-sensitivity prediction. Tissue and cellular distributions of the EPPI genes were mapped using spatial transcriptomics and single-cell RNA sequencing. Molecular docking assessed predicted drug-target interactions. Finally, in vitro RAC1 knockdown experiments evaluated the cellular function of a representative EPPI gene. RESULTS: Comprising RND3, RAC1, KRAS, CTNNA1, AURKA, and ACTB, the final EPPI consistently stratified overall survival across all cohorts and showed moderate prognostic discrimination. The high-EPPI group had greater tumor purity and mutational burden, with enhanced cell-cycle, DNA-repair, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and NF-κB programs, whereas the low-EPPI group showed greater immune and stromal infiltration. TIDE and immunophenoscores also differed between subgroups. Drug-response models predicted greater sensitivity to cisplatin and paclitaxel in the high-EPPI group and to several targeted agents in the low-EPPI group. Molecular docking predicted RAC1-EHT-1864 and AURKA-alisertib interactions. Spatial and single-cell analyses showed heterogeneous EPPI-gene expression, with ACTB and RAC1 broadly distributed and AURKA restricted to selected populations. RAC1 depletion suppressed LUAD-cell proliferation, DNA synthesis, migration, and invasion. CONCLUSION: The EPPI is an entosis-informed prognostic index for survival stratification in LUAD. Based on this index, patients can be separated into subgroups with distinct proliferative features, genomic alterations, tissue compositions, and predicted drug sensitivities. These findings associate entosis-related molecular features with distinct cellular and clinical characteristics of LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: Acquired resistance to osimertinib remains a critical clinical challenge in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), with 40%-60% of progressing patients lacking an identifiable genetic resistance driver. Through quantitative secretomic profiling of paired osimertinib-sensitive and -resistant NSCLC cell lines, we identified laminin subunit γ2 (LAMC2) as markedly enriched in resistant cell secretomes. Single-cell RNA sequencing reanalysis revealed a LAMC2-high drug-tolerant persister subpopulation that expanded under osimertinib pressure, with pseudotime analysis suggesting progressive co-upregulation of LAMC2 and matrix metalloproteinase 14 (MMP14) along the treatment-to-resistance trajectory. Across four independent cohorts, MMP14 exhibited the strongest co-expression with LAMC2 among all metalloproteinases; the two proteins also physically interacted, and their concurrent high expression predicted the worst overall survival. Mechanistically, MMP14 cleaved LAMC2 to release a bioactive Domain III (DIII) fragment harboring EGF-like repeats, which reactivated EGFR/AKT/ERK signaling despite continued osimertinib exposure. Exogenous DIII conferred resistance in sensitive cells, whereas an anti-DIII blocking antibody reversed MMP14-driven resistance in cell lines and patient-derived organoids. The selective MMP14 inhibitor NSC405020 restored osimertinib sensitivity in vitro and suppressed xenograft growth. In residual tumor tissues from neoadjuvant osimertinib-treated patients, non-responders exhibited higher LAMC2/MMP14 co-expression and more prominent spatial exclusion of CD8⁺ T-cells from the tumor core compared with major pathological responders. These findings identify the MMP14-LAMC2-DIII proteolytic axis as a non-genetic resistance mechanism and suggest that MMP14 inhibition or DIII neutralization may represent a rational strategy to overcome acquired osimertinib resistance.

papers.abstract_en: PD-L1-mediated immunosuppression is a key mechanism underlying tumor immune evasion, whereas PD-1/PD-L1 blockade therapies remain limited by low response rates and acquired resistance. Through small-molecule screening, we identify isobavachalcone (IBC), a naturally derived compound that modulates PD-L1 homeostasis by targeting the deubiquitinase OTUB1. Mechanistically, IBC targets OTUB1 at the His217 residue and suppresses its deubiquitinase activity, thereby promoting K48-linked polyubiquitination of PD-L1 and its proteasome-dependent degradation. Functionally, IBC reduces tumor cell PD-L1 expression and enhances CD8+ T cell-mediated cytotoxicity. In PD-L1-deficient tumor models, IBC fails to further enhance antitumor activity, indicating that PD-L1 is required for IBC-mediated immune regulation. Moreover, IBC combined with anti-CTLA-4 therapy further enhanced antitumor efficacy. Together, these findings highlight IBC as a potential drug candidate that promotes PD-L1 degradation and demonstrate the therapeutic potential of targeting the OTUB1-PD-L1 axis to improve immune checkpoint therapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Transanal surgery has advanced significantly since the introduction of transanal endoscopic microsurgery (TEM) in 1983. The single-port (SP) robotic system marks the latest technological advancement in minimally invasive transanal surgery, combining single-site access with full robotic articulation through a single 25 mm port. This is the first video dynamic manuscript and 2nd document of a four-part SAGES Colorectal Committee series outlining the foundational application of SP technology in colorectal surgery, specifically transanal minimally invasive surgery (SP-TAMIS). METHODS: The SAGES Colorectal Committee SP Task Force performed a structured review of the da Vinci SP system, assessing platform features, instrumentation, and workflow considerations for transanal surgery. Task force members (subject matter experts with early experience with single-port robotic platforms) analyzed technical details, patient selection, operative workflows, and early outcomes. Representative procedural video-based techniques were detailed with emphasis on instrumentation, docking, and key operative steps specific to the SP transanal procedure. RESULTS: The SP platform appears to offer several technological advantages for transanal surgery: (1) natural hand-eye coordination in an inverted field, (2) enhanced visualization with an articulating cobra camera, and (3) a third arm for retraction and exposure. These features appear to improve precision, reduce collision risk and fatigue, and shorten operative time. Published early clinical data suggest low positive margin rates (≈ 4-5%) and acceptable morbidity for multiport robotic TAMIS/SP-TAMIS in selected patients. However, direct comparative evidence versus conventional TAMIS remains limited, and many comparisons are indirect across heterogeneous cohorts. Current limitations include high cost, limited distal reach, lack of dedicated energy devices, and learning curve. The learning curve appears to be shorter than for laparoscopic TAMIS. Peritoneal entry during full-thickness excision of upper rectal and anterior lesions is a recognized event in transanal surgery; the SP platform offers several features that may facilitate its management, though SP-specific incidence data are not yet available. CONCLUSIONS: SME early experience with SP-TAMIS suggests that it can provide a safe, effective, and ergonomically superior method for local rectal excision. Mastery of this foundational application builds the skills needed for more complex SP colorectal procedures, with the potential for single-port robotics expansion into minimally invasive colorectal surgery through enhanced precision, reduced invasiveness, and improved surgeon ergonomics.

papers.abstract_en: Accumulating evidence has shown that the dysfunction of mitochondria, the multifunctional organelles in various cellular processes, is a pivotal event in the development of various diseases, including human cancers. The molecular alterations in tumors that promote metabolic diversity and distinct targetable dependencies remain poorly defined. The mitochondrial transporter SLC25A20, also known as carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase (CACT), is crucial for fatty acid β-oxidation (FAO) by importing acylcarnitines into the mitochondrial matrix. Here, we demonstrate that SLC25A20 is significantly upregulated in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) tissues and cells, and its expression correlates with poor patient survival. Gain- and loss-of-function experiments reveal that SLC25A20 promotes tumor cell proliferation, survival, migration, and invasion by enhancing FAO-associated mitochondrial bioenergetics and suppressing apoptosis. Mechanistically, SLC25A20-mediated FAO maintains mitochondrial function and supports oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), thereby sustaining tumor bioenergetics and redox homeostasis. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic silencing of SLC25A20 impairs tumor growth in vivo. These findings establish SLC25A20 as a key metabolic driver in LUAD and suggest it may be a therapeutic target.

papers.abstract_en: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) is a common severe complication of advanced lung cancer and significantly worsens prognosis. Physical targeted therapies, represented by piezocatalytic therapy, sonodynamic therapy, photodynamic therapy, hyperthermic intrathoracic chemotherapy, radiofrequency ablation and thermosensitive in situ hydrogel drug delivery system, induce reactive oxygen species generation via light, ultrasound, or piezocatalytic energy, or achieve tumor killing through local hyperthermia and temperature-controlled drug release, offering new strategies for MPE. However, existing reviews mostly focus on single modalities, lacking systematic classification and suitability comparison based on the pleural microenvironment and respiratory mechanics. This review summarizes their mechanisms, biological effects, and translational status in the context of pleural anatomy and pathological microenvironment, and highlights multi-field combination, microenvironment remodeling, and precise energy regulation as future directions for MPE therapy. .

papers.abstract_en: Medical Vision Foundation Models (MVFMs) mark a shift from task-specific artificial intelligence (AI) toward general-purpose visual intelligence in medical imaging. However, clinical deployment remains constrained by tensions among data availability, technological development, and integration into clinical workflows. To address these issues, this review provides a systematic analysis of the field's evolution from 2019 to 2025. We introduce the Data-Technology-Translation Triad as a unifying conceptual framework to structure the progress, key factors, and challenges of MVFMs. Our analysis traces the field's development and identifies a convergence toward Transformer-based and hybrid architectures, alongside hybrid pre-training paradigms. We present a unified technical framework that covers pre-training strategies, including generative, contrastive, and hybrid learning, as well as adaptation mechanisms such as full fine-tuning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and prompt learning. Furthermore, we examine how data scarcity, heterogeneity, and privacy constraints in medical imaging drive the adoption of self-supervised learning and highlight domain generalization as a critical research direction. Although MVFMs demonstrate strong performance in data-efficient and multi-task settings, their clinical translation is hindered by limited generalization, insufficient interpretability, misalignment with clinical workflows, and regulatory uncertainty. In response, we propose practical directions for developing reliable general-purpose medical vision systems, with emphasis on causal reasoning, dynamic data learning, interactive human-AI collaboration, and coordinated efforts among researchers, clinicians, and regulators. This review provides a structured reference to guide MVFMs from technical validation to clinically effective, reliable, and ethically sound deployment. An updated collection of MVFM papers and related resources is available at our website https://github.com/ice-TuoShui/MVFM-Review.

papers.abstract_en: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) have advanced the study of complex lung diseases by resolving cellular heterogeneity, tissue architecture, and intercellular communication. These technologies are particularly informative in chronic respiratory disorders, where pathological remodeling involves coordinated alterations across epithelial, stromal, immune, and endothelial compartments. Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), a rare fatal fibrotic disorder, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), a prevalent heterogeneous respiratory condition, represent distinct chronic lung diseases shaped by persistent injury, maladaptive repair, and progressive tissue remodeling. However, current understanding of their pathogenesis remains incomplete, and conventional approaches lack the resolution to define disease-associated cell states, spatially restricted niches, or compartment-specific interactions. This review synthesizes recent scRNA-seq and ST studies in IPF and COPD, emphasizing how high-resolution atlases refine established pathobiological frameworks and reveal shared and disease-specific cellular programs. We highlight epithelial dysfunction and impaired progenitor repair as shared mechanistic features of IPF and COPD, while emphasizing alveolar regenerative failure, fibroblast activation, and profibrotic niche formation as central features of IPF, and compartment-specific airway remodeling, inflammatory epithelial states, and emphysema-associated parenchymal injury as prominent features of COPD. We further discuss stromal and immune remodeling, hypoxia-associated vascular remodeling, and the translational implications of these findings for molecular stratification, target prioritization, and mechanism-informed therapeutic development, while noting limitations related to end-stage tissue sampling, platform constraints, and mouse-human correspondence. This review provides an integrated framework for understanding the cellular and spatial mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis and translational relevance of IPF and COPD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Neonatal gastric perforation (NGP) is a rare but life-threatening surgical emergency of the newborn. We systematically reviewed its clinical characteristics, risk factors, surgical management and outcomes. METHODS: Five databases were searched from inception to 31 December 2025 for observational studies reporting at least five neonates (≤ 28 days) with confirmed gastric perforation. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data and appraised quality. Proportions were pooled using random-effects models; predictors of mortality were summarised as odds ratios (OR). The review followed PRISMA 2020 and was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO). RESULTS: Twenty studies (410 neonates) were included. Pooled prevalences were prematurity 58.3%, low birth weight 63.5% and male sex 59.0%; abdominal distension (90.5%) and pneumoperitoneum (80.9%) were the commonest features. Primary repair was performed in 78.4% of operated neonates. Pooled in-hospital mortality was 28.6% (95% CI 22.0-36.3%). Sepsis at presentation (OR 4.10) and delay to surgery beyond 24 h (OR 3.55) were the strongest predictors of death. CONCLUSIONS: NGP mainly affects premature, low-birth-weight neonates, and still carries approximately 28% mortality. Early recognition, prompt treatment of sepsis and timely surgery offer the clearest route to improved survival. PROSPERO ID: CRD420261436438.

papers.abstract_en: As one of the malignant tumors with high incidence and mortality worldwide, lung cancer features high heterogeneity and therapeutic resistance, which severely impair the prognosis of patients with lung cancer. In recent years, novel cell death modes such as ferroptosis, cuproptosis, disulfidptosis and necrosis by sodium overload have become research hotspots in oncology. Focusing on these four forms of cell death, this review systematically clarifies their roles in lung cancer initiation and progression, regulation of the tumor microenvironment, and therapeutic resistance; summarizes related prognostic biomarkers and representative prognostic models; and discusses the crosstalk among multiple cell death pathways and advances in clinical translation. This review aims to provide a reference for improving prognostic assessment in lung cancer, elucidating mechanisms of therapeutic resistance, and developing novel antitumor strategies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Relapses, need for further treatment lines and significant treatment attrition are typical for multiple myeloma (MM). This retrospective study investigates attrition and outcomes among MM patients in Finland. Patient, material and methods: Study included all adult MM patients (n = 1733) diagnosed and treated in four hospital districts in Finland in 2013-2022. Data were collected from hospital data lakes, Statistics Finland and Social Insurance Institution. Treatment attrition was defined as death before next treatment line. RESULTS: By the end of follow-up 31% of patients without stem cell transplantation (non-SCT) had died before initiation of second line treatment (2L), compared with 5% of stem-cell transplant (SCT) patients. The factors associating with this early attrition in the non-SCT cohort were older age (over 75 years), higher comorbidity burden, International Staging System (ISS), and (R)-ISS scores (p < 0.001). Furthermore, non-SCT patients were more likely administered less intensive therapy during 1L (p < 0.001). During the first 6 months post diagnosis in the non-SCT cohort, the most common immediate cause of death was MM. Also, during later stages MM was responsible for 54% of deaths in the non-SCT and 68% in the SCT cohorts whereas infections were linked principally with early deaths before 2L treatment. INTERPRETATION: This study highlights significant treatment attrition across disease course and also early mortality especially in the non-SCT cohort resulting primarily from progressive MM or infections. The findings underscore the need for more tolerable and effective anti-myeloma treatments in earlier course of the disease to enhance patient survival.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Approximately 30% of sinonasal and nasopharyngeal carcinoma cases are HPV-associated, yet studies investigating circulating tumor HPV-DNA (ctHPV-DNA) among these patients are scarce. The aim of this study was to investigate the sensitivity of ctHPV-DNA in pretreatment blood samples from patients with HPV-positive (HPV+) sinonasal and nasopharyngeal carcinoma. METHODS: Patients with a confirmed HPV+ sinonasal or nasopharyngeal carcinoma treated at the Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery and Audiology at Rigshospitalet, Copenhagen, Denmark in the period 2017-2025 were included in this study. Blood samples were drawn in Streck tubes before treatment initiation and analysed for the presence of ctHPV-DNA by Droplet digital PCR (ddPCR). RESULTS: Fifteen patients with primary HPV+ sinonasal or nasopharyngeal carcinoma were included. Except for two cases of HPV-related multiphenotypic carcinoma, all cases were squamous cell carcinoma. HPV16 was most prevalent and found in 6 patients (40%). HPV18 (n = 2), HPV33 (n = 1), HPV35 (n = 3), HPV45 (n = 1), and HPV56 (n = 2) were also represented. The sensitivity of detecting ctHPV-DNA in the pretreatment blood samples of the included patients was 80%. The level of ctHPV-DNA increased significantly with increasing T-category. CONCLUSION: ctHPV-DNA was detected in pretreatment blood samples in 80% of patients with HPV+ sinonasal and nasopharyngeal carcinoma. This supports further investigation of ctHPV-DNA as a biomarker for post-treatment surveillance in these patients.

papers.abstract_en: Biallelic pathogenic variants in UBR7, encoding ubiquitin protein ligase E3 component n-recognin 7, cause Li-Campeau syndrome (LICAS; OMIM #619189), which is characterized by developmental delay/intellectual disability, epilepsy, hypothyroidism, ptosis, genital anomalies, and cardiac anomalies. LICAS is an ultrarare disorder, and to date, only nine patients from eight unrelated families have been reported with detailed clinical phenotypes. Here, we report an 18-year-old female patient with dysmorphic facial features, ptosis, congenital hypothyroidism, intellectual disability, stereotypic hand movements, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, hepatosplenomegaly, and toenail hypoplasia. In contrast to previously reported patients, all of whom presented with global developmental delay, our patient achieved age-appropriate early motor and language milestones, representing the mildest early developmental course reported in LICAS to date. Exome sequencing revealed a homozygous deletion encompassing Exon 7 of UBR7, representing the first single-exon deletion reported in this gene. This report expands both the phenotypic and genotypic spectrum of LICAS and underscores the clinical utility of Next generation sequencing-based copy-number variant analysis in the diagnostic workup of rare diseases.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Recurrent cervical cancer within previously irradiated fields remains a major therapeutic challenge. This study aimed to evaluate clinical outcomes and safety of image-guided re-irradiation and to identify prognostic factors associated with tumor control and treatment-related toxicity. METHODS: All consecutive patients who underwent image-guided re-irradiation between March 2020 and December 2024 were retrospectively analyzed. Re-irradiation was delivered using image-guided external beam radiotherapy and/or image-guided brachytherapy. Concurrent chemotherapy or immunotherapy was administered when clinically indicated. Organ at risk doses were recorded from re-irradiation plans. Logistic models were applied to evaluate tumor control probability and normal tissue complication probability. RESULTS: A total of 102 patients were included. At recurrence, 45.1% had central relapse, 14.7% pelvic relapse, 17.6% combined central and pelvic relapse, and 22.5% had distant metastasis. The median re-irradiation dose was 56.8 Gy (a/β = 10). With a median follow-up of 13.7 months, the 1- and 2-year LC were 67.6% and 59.2%, and the 1- and 2-year PFS were 52.7% and 42.6%. Higher re-irradiation prescription EQD2 was associated with improved tumor control. A progression-free interval > 2 years after initial radiotherapy predicted better progression-free survival and local control, whereas distant metastasis was associated with inferior progression-free survival. Higher rectal and bladder D2cc values were significantly associated with increased late toxicity. The risk of grade ≥ 2 late complications rose substantially when the rectal or bladder D2cc exceeded approximately 50 Gy (a/β = 3). No grade 4 or 5 toxicities were observed in this study. CONCLUSION: Re-irradiation is a feasible and effective salvage option for patients with recurrent cervical cancer and provides moderate local control with acceptable toxicity.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Multi-cancer detection (MCD) tests currently being tested in clinical trials may be a scalable, convenient means to improve cancer screening, yet little is known about the potential clinical and psychosocial consequences of doing so in underserved communities. OBJECTIVE: To summarize the current literature examining potential clinical and psychosocial outcomes and consequences for MCD testing in underserved populations. METHODS: We searched and then reviewed articles from five databases: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane. For inclusion, studies had to primarily focus on MCD testing within underserved populations. Out of 376 articles identified, 29 met inclusion criteria. RESULTS: Financial constraints were the most frequently cited barrier (n = 23). 24 articles mentioned clinical consequences and nine mentioned psychosocial consequences, with the most common being lower rates of cancer screening with proven existing recommended tests (n = 10) and emotional stress, worry, and anxiety (n = 11), respectively. Many expressed concerns about underrepresentation in clinical trials. CONCLUSIONS: The review highlights common potential clinical consequences as well as important factors underserved populations may face if/when MCD testing is implemented in their healthcare. Future prospective studies, experimental and observational, should intentionally include underrepresented patient populations to better understand and address these challenges.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Lung transplantation (LT) improves survival in patients with end-stage lung disease; however, recovery of physical function after transplantation remains insufficiently characterized, particularly in critically ill recipients bridged with extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Understanding longitudinal functional recovery and potential differences between ECMO and non-ECMO recipients is essential for optimizing post-transplant rehabilitation strategies. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 84 adult patients who underwent lung or heart-lung transplantation between 2018 and 2023. Physical function was assessed at 6 and 12 months using the 6-minute walk test, gait speed, and strength measures. Changes over time and group differences were evaluated using longitudinal statistical models. RESULTS: Fifty patients (59.5%) required ECMO support. Overall physical function significantly improved from 6 to 12 months, with 93.4% achieving independent ambulation by 12 months. ECMO recipients had a lower proportion of independent ambulation at 6 months compared with non-ECMO recipients. At 12 months, no statistically significant between-group difference was observed in the proportion of patients achieving independent ambulation. CONCLUSIONS: LT recipients showed significant improvement in physical function between 6 and 12 months after transplantation. ECMO-bridged recipients had lower independent ambulation rates at 6 months, while no statistically significant between-group difference was observed at 12 months. Further studies incorporating pretransplant and early postoperative assessments are needed to better characterize functional recovery after lung transplantation.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study is to evaluate the early postoperative morbidity rates with a particular focus on surgical site infection rates, in patients undergoing resection for retrorectal tumors with the modified Kraske Procedure. METHODS: This descriptive observational case series study included patients who underwent resection for retrorectal tumors performing the modified Kraske Procedure between August 2006 and August 2025. Patients with recurrent disease or a history of pelvic radiotherapy or chemotherapy were excluded. The primary outcome was early postoperative morbidity, especially in terms of surgical site infections, which was defined as complications occurring within the first 30 days after surgery. RESULTS: Among 35 patients operated for retrorectal tumors, 23 (65.7%) patients underwent a resection performing the modified Kraske Procedure and were included in the analysis. The majority of patients were female (82.6%), with a mean age of 40.3 ± 15.8 years. The mean tumor size was 42.5 ± 10.0 mm, and most lesions were benign (87%). Postoperative complications occurred in three (13%) patients, with surgical site infection observed in only one (4.3%) patient. The mean length of hospital stay was 3.8 ± 1.9 days. CONCLUSION: The modified Kraske Procedure was associated with a low surgical site infection rate and acceptable early postoperative morbidity in this series. This technique may represent a feasible surgical modification for selected retrorectal tumors and warrants further evaluation in comparative studies.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the access vessel patency after endovascular therapy performed via tibiopedal access. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a retrospective, single-center, observational study. Patients who underwent endovascular therapy via tibiopedal access with sheath insertion were enrolled. The primary outcome was loss of access vessel patency defined as access vessel occlusion or stenosis with a peak systolic velocity ratio > 2.4 on duplex ultrasound at 6 months. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed to identify the predictors of access vessel patency loss, with hemodialysis, severely calcified access vessel and sheath-to-artery ratio included as covariates. RESULTS: A total of 95 limbs in 91 patients were included in this study, and loss of access vessel patency was observed in 22 limbs (23.1%). Multivariate logistic regression analysis demonstrated that sheath-to-artery ratio was the only independent predictor (odds ratio: 1.493, 95% confidence interval: 1.130-1.976; p = 0.005). The receiver operating characteristic curve analysis revealed that the optimal cutoff value of sheath-to-artery ratio for predicting loss of access vessel patency was 1.08, with an area under the curve of 0.723. In this cohort, the 2-year freedom from major adverse limb events were 98.6% (95% CI: 90.8-99.8%), and no major amputation occurred. CONCLUSION: The present study demonstrated a relatively high incidence of loss of access vessel patency after endovascular therapy via tibiopedal access, although this was not associated with an increase in major adverse limb events. A larger sheath-to-artery ratio was identified as an independent predictor of loss of access vessel patency.

papers.abstract_en: Young breast cancer (YBC), defined as diagnosis at or before the age of 40 years, is characterized by an aggressive phenotype and poor prognosis. The tumor microenvironment (TME), comprising immune and stromal cells, plays a critical role in tumor initiation and progression and is closely associated with clinical outcomes. However, alterations in cell states and the organization of multicellular ecosystems within the YBC microenvironment remain poorly understood. We analyzed 7379 bulk transcriptome samples and spatial transcriptomic data from eight samples using EcoTyper and complementary spatial analyses. The abundance of CD4+ T cells (S07), fibroblasts (S05), monocytes/macrophages (S09), and epithelial cells (S05) was significantly lower in young than in older patients with breast cancer. CD4+ T cells (S07), fibroblasts (S05), and monocytes/macrophages (S09) formed a spatially organized multicellular ecosystem with putative interactions involving CDH1-PTPRF/ERBB3. Lower ecosystem abundance was associated with poorer prognosis, including among patients who did not achieve a pathological complete response after neoadjuvant therapy. These findings identify a distinct multicellular ecosystem within the YBC microenvironment, providing insights into the microenvironmental features associated with disease progression.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) frequently disseminates within the lipid-rich peritoneal cavity, where tumor progression is accompanied by metabolic adaptations involving lipid utilization and mitochondrial function. Although these metabolic alterations are increasingly recognized as important features of EOC progression and peritoneal metastasis, the molecular factors linking mitochondrial-lipid metabolic remodeling with aggressive tumor behavior remain incompletely characterized. We therefore integrated mitochondrial- and lipid metabolism-related transcriptomic analyses to identify candidate regulators and further investigated the clinical and biological features associated with CDS2. RESULTS: Seven key genes associated with mitochondrial and lipid metabolism were identified in EOC through comprehensive bioinformatic analyses and were used to construct the MALRS prognostic model. Further integration of FIGO stage, histologic grade, and MALRS scores yielded a nomogram whose calibration plots showed good agreement between predicted and observed 1-, 3-, and 5-year survival probabilities. Subsequent screening of these candidate genes in chemotherapy-resistant datasets identified CDP-diacylglycerol synthase 2 (CDS2) as the most consistently upregulated candidate gene. Clinical validation confirmed that CDS2 was significantly overexpressed in tumor tissues and was associated with advanced disease stage, and survival analysis showed that higher CDS2 expression was associated with shorter progression-free survival (PFS) in stage III/IV patients. Functional characterization demonstrated that CDS2 overexpression promoted both lipid droplet accumulation and migratory capacity in ovarian cancer cells. Pathway analysis identified significant enrichment of PI3K/AKT signaling, and experimental validation confirmed CDS2-mediated hyperactivation of PI3K/AKT phosphorylation. Computational immune-deconvolution analyses further identified exploratory associations between CDS2 expression, estimated T-cell abundance, and immune-checkpoint transcripts. CONCLUSION: CDS2 is a lipid metabolism-associated candidate biomarker linked to aggressive clinicopathological features in EOC. Our findings associate CDS2 with disease progression, PI3K/AKT-related signaling, and immune-related transcriptomic features, supporting its further evaluation as a candidate prognostic marker.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Systemic metastasis remains the leading cause of mortality in patients with advanced prostate cancer, particularly in castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC), for which effective systemic therapeutic options are limited. Gene therapy is a potential strategy for achieving selective tumor targeting and systemic disease control in metastatic settings. This study aimed to establish a systemic metastasis animal model for CRPC and evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of JC polyomavirus (JCPyV) virus-like particle (VLPs)-based gene therapy against metastatic disease. METHODS: A near-infrared fluorescent protein (iRFP)-expressing CRPC cell line was used to establish a systemic metastasis model by tail-vein injection in mice. The therapeutic efficacy of JCPyV VLPs carrying a prostate-specific antigen (PSA) promoter-driven suicide gene (PSAtk-VLPs), administered in combination with ganciclovir (GCV), was evaluated longitudinally by fluorescence molecular tomography (FMT), with enzalutamide/leuprorelin acetate (ENZ/LEU) included as a clinical treatment comparator. RESULTS: CRPC metastases in the lungs, liver, spleen, kidneys, and bones were detected by FMT in real time. Control mice exhibited exponential CRPC growth, whereas ENZ/LEU treatment delayed CRPC progression. PSAtk-VLPs/GCV significantly inhibited the growth of metastatic CRPC. However, no significant differences in survival were observed among the MOCK, ENZ/LEU, and PSAtk-VLP/GCV groups (log-rank test, p = 0.7351). CONCLUSION: These findings support that JCPyV-derived virus-like particles constitute a promising therapeutic approach for metastatic CRPC, enabling systemic delivery of suicide gene therapy with selective inhibition of tumor growth and translational relevance.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) frequently occur during combination immune checkpoint inhibition. However, their prognostic impact may vary according to organ involvement and severity. In this study, we exploratorily evaluated whether severe non-endocrine irAEs represent a temporally distinct and prognostically unfavorable clinical phenotype in patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC) treated with ipilimumab plus nivolumab. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analyzed 63 patients with mRCC treated with ipilimumab plus nivolumab who were followed for at least 5 years. Patients were categorized into non-irAE, non-severe + severe endocrine irAE, and severe non-endocrine irAE groups. Overall survival (OS) was assessed. Multistate modeling was used to evaluate the transitions between treatment, irAE occurrence, and death. Landmark analyses were performed at 8 and 12 weeks to address immortal time bias. RESULTS: The severe non-endocrine irAE group was associated with inferior OS. The multistate analysis revealed a potentially increased risk of direct transition from ipilimumab plus nivolumab to death in the severe non-endocrine irAE group. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Skin cancer is the most common type of cancer worldwide, categorized into melanoma and non-melanoma types. While genetics play a crucial role in the development of skin cancer, recent developments in metabolomics have revealed that circulating metabolites influence genetic risk profiles. METHODS: In this study, we utilized a bidirectional two-sample Mendelian Randomization (MR) approach, analyzing metabolite datasets from the Canadian Longitudinal Study of Aging (CLSA) and skin cancer datasets from the UK Biobank. Replication analyses were performed with the 10th round of the FinnGen project. Instrumental variables (IVs) were chosen according to established MR criteria and assessed through the Wald ratio, IVW, MR-Egger, and weighted median methods. Various sensitivity analyses were conducted utilizing Cochrane's Q, Egger's intercept, MR-PRESSO, and leave-one-out (LOO) techniques. RESULTS: After meticulous analysis, we identified causal relationships between circulating metabolites and skin cancer risks. Specifically, levels of 1,2-dilinoleoyl-GPE (18:2/18:2), 1-palmitoyl-2-linoleoyl-gpc (16:0/18:2), 1-stearoyl-2-arachidonoyl-gpc (18:0/20:4), 1-stearoyl-2-linoleoyl-gpc (18:0/18:2), and Docosapentaenoate n3 DPA, the ratio of Arachidonate (20:4n6) to oleate to vaccenate (18:1), and Oleoyl-linoleoyl-glycerol (18:1 to 18:2) to linoleoyl-arachidonoyl-glycerol (18:2 to 20:4) were linked to non-melanoma skin cancer, whereas levels of trans-urocanate were causally linked to melanoma of skin, and S-adenosylhomocysteine (SAH) showed a putative association. It should be noted that docosapentaenoate n3 DPA and SAH were each supported by a single SNP and should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than definitive causal evidence. Reverse MR analysis highlighted robust causal relationships with 18 and 10 metabolites and non-melanoma skin cancer and melanoma of skin, respectively. CONCLUSION: These findings enhance our understanding of skin cancer etiology and risk factors, providing genetic evidence for hypothesis-generating associations that support the development of targeted therapies and aid in the identification of potential biomarkers.

papers.abstract_en: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is projected to become the second-leading cause of US cancer death by 2030, and survival is dominated by stage at diagnosis: roughly 44% at five years for localized disease versus about 3% with distant metastases. Only about 15% of cases are detected while localized, surgery reaches a minority of patients, and no validated screening test exists for average-risk adults. This topical review examines the biologic, clinical, economic, psychological, equity, and therapeutic evidence bearing on where scarce resources should be directed. The long interval between initiating mutation and invasive disease provides a mechanistic rationale for prevention and interception, and the modifiable exposures of obesity, tobacco, type 2 diabetes, and alcohol act largely within that window. We consider innovations that extend prevention beyond lifestyle advice-incretin-based weight management, risk stratification anchored in new-onset diabetes and biomarkers, and immunoprevention-together with early-onset disease, implementation and policy, and the barriers and evidentiary limits that temper these arguments. We propose a three-tier framework of primary prevention, early detection in high-risk groups, and therapy, and argue that research, policy, and clinical investment should be weighted upstream, because every case prevented spares the cost, capacity, and suffering that the downstream tiers must otherwise absorb.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) was approved in Japan in June 2020 as a curative option for unresectable, locally advanced, or recurrent head and neck cancers. The cumulative incidence of grade ≥ 3 late adverse events was 14.0% at 2 years, with grade 5 adverse events occurring in 2.1% of patients. No significant differences were observed in LC or PFS among histological type subgroups; however, OS was significantly worse in patients with squamous cell carcinoma (SqCC) than in patients with non-SqCC. Regarding TNM stage at irradiation, radiation therapy at an early disease stage was significantly associated with improved LC. CONCLUSIONS: BNCT should be administered during the early disease stages when no other effective treatment options are available. Further studies should determine the factors contributing to treatment efficacy and safety, thereby optimizing multimodal treatment strategies involving BNCT.

papers.abstract_en: Radiation dose to the heart is associated with various cardiac side effects. However, the specific cardiac and pulmonary structures that contribute to these toxicities remain incompletely understood. Moreover, although multiple factors contribute to reduced survival after radiotherapy, the role of radiation-induced cardiac toxicity remains underrecognized. This scoping review aimed to evaluate the associations between radiation dose to specific cardiac and pulmonary structures, cardiac side effects, and survival. A total of 137 clinical studies were analysed in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. Associations between radiation dose and cardiac side effects were identified not only for the whole heart but also for specific cardiac substructures, including myocardial segments, coronary arteries, and the pericardium. Notably, radiation dose to the lungs was also associated with decline in cardiac function, suggesting that minimizing cardiac toxicity may require consideration of both local cardiac irradiation and non-local irradiation of adjacent organs, particularly the lungs. Direct evidence linking cardiac side effects to survival was limited. Nevertheless, the observed associations between higher radiation doses, increased cardiac toxicity, and poorer survival suggest a potential relationship that warrants further investigation. These findings support the hypothesis that reducing specific cardiac side effects may benefit from targeted sparing of the relevant cardiac and pulmonary substructures. While many radiation-related cardiac side effects are now recognized, further research is needed to identify and characterize previously unrecognized manifestations and to clarify their contribution to long-term survival.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: High-risk human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cervical carcinogenesis involves oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and altered non-apoptotic cell-death programs. The score was benchmarked against ssGSEA, GSVA, and PLAGE and evaluated in controlled simulations. For feature prioritization, score-defining genes were excluded from predictors and Elastic Net feature selection, XGBoost tuning, and model fitting were performed strictly within repeated nested cross-validation. External validation used GSE138080, GSE63514, GSE223804, and GSE151666. RESULTS: CombinedNet showed moderate-to-high concordance with ssGSEA, GSVA, and PLAGE (Spearman rho = 0.735, 0.882, and 0.943, respectively), while 1,300 controlled simulations showed strong recovery of the latent promoter-minus-inhibitor balance across scenarios and effect sizes (mean rho = 0.944; mean sign-recovery accuracy = 0.902; mean standardized RMSE = 0.305). Stability-weighted SHAP and perturbation prioritized CKMT1B and KLK13, whereas GNA13, PANX2, and all five sterol genes were not selected in any of 25 outer-fold models. The sterol genes retained modest score correlations but showed no model sensitivity. Across three lesion-progression cohorts, no pathway score remained associated with stage after FDR correction; in the cancer-only GSE151666 RNA-seq cohort, CombinedNet also showed no FIGO-stage trend. CONCLUSION: This study supports directionality-aware transcriptomic scoring and a leakage-resistant feature-prioritization framework, but does not support GNA13/PANX2 or cholesterol-biosynthesis signals as stable model drivers or the composite score as a validated lesion-stage biomarker. papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To characterize the burden, temporal trends, geographic heterogeneity, demographic components, pandemic-era deviations, and projected age-standardized rates of bladder cancer across Africa. METHODS: We conducted an ecological secondary analysis of modeled Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 estimates for the GBD aggregate labeled "African Union" and 54 African country locations from 2010 to 2023. Incidence, prevalence, deaths, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) were assessed as counts and age-standardized rates (ASRs) per 100,000 population for both sexes combined. Trends were summarized using estimated annual percentage changes. Incidence trajectories were descriptively grouped using dynamic time warping, and changes in counts were partitioned into population-size, age-structure, and age-specific rate components using Das Gupta decomposition. Exploratory autoregressive integrated moving average models compared GBD-estimated rates in 2020-2023 with trajectories extrapolated from 2010 to 2019. Country-specific ASRs were projected through 2030 using log-linear models. RESULTS: For the GBD aggregate labeled "African Union," incident cases increased from 16,357 in 2010 to 31,503 in 2023, prevalent cases from 73,806 to 147,599, deaths from 9,261 to 16,467, and DALYs from 232,414 to 415,746. Corresponding ASRs increased from 3.5 to 4.4 for incidence, 13.9 to 18.3 for prevalence, 2.2 to 2.6 for deaths, and 48.1 to 56.1 for DALYs. The highest estimated incidence ASRs in 2023 occurred in Tunisia, Malawi, Libya, Egypt, and Mali, while several countries with low estimated baseline rates had rapid relative increases. Population-size change was the largest decomposition component, accounting for 39.8%-58.8% of the increase across outcomes, with additional contributions from age structure and age-specific rates. GBD-estimated incidence, mortality, and DALY rates during 2020-2023 were above the extrapolated point forecasts; however, this exploratory analysis did not establish a causal pandemic effect. The primary projection models yielded higher fitted 2030 ASRs in a majority of countries, although results varied across training windows. CONCLUSION: GBD 2023 estimates indicate an increasing but geographically heterogeneous bladder cancer burden across Africa. Population growth was the largest contributor to increasing counts, while age-structure and age-specific rate changes also contributed. Regionally tailored prevention, diagnostic and treatment capacity, and improved cancer surveillance are needed. Pandemic-era deviations and 2030 projections should be interpreted as model-dependent rather than causal or definitive forecasts.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a heterogeneous disease with distinct inflammatory profiles that may be associated with key pathological features, including emphysema and airway wall remodeling. Cluster 1 (Severe-low inflammation) was characterized by the lowest circulating inflammatory cytokine levels, the greatest symptom burden, the most severe airflow limitation, an increased exacerbation frequency, and the most extensive emphysema. Cluster 2 (Mild-low inflammation) exhibited low levels of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines, mild symptoms, relatively preserved lung function, and a low frequency of annual exacerbations. Cluster 3 (Moderate-elevated inflammation) had moderately elevated levels of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines, with intermediate mMRC and CAT scores, pulmonary function impairment and exacerbation frequency. Cluster 4 (Extremely high inflammation) was characterized by markedly elevated levels of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines, intermediate symptom burden, relatively preserved pulmonary function, pronounced airway wall thickening and a high frequency of moderate-to-severe exacerbations. Further cytokine ratio analysis revealed an IL-6-related shift in Clusters 3 and 4 and an IL-17-related shift predominantly in Cluster 3. CONCLUSION: Integrating cytokine profiles with airflow limitation identified four exploratory COPD phenotypes, highlighting a potential dissociation between systemic inflammation and disease severity. External and longitudinal validation is needed to confirm their reproducibility and clinical relevance.

PEF may serve as a simple bedside indicator for early risk stratification and targeted clinical evaluation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are at an elevated risk of fungal infections, yet reliable tools for early risk stratification are lacking. This study aimed to analyze the risk factors associated with fungal infections in patients with COPD and to develop a predictive model. METHODS: This study retrospectively analyzed patients with COPD who were admitted to Shanghai Pulmonary Hospital, between June 2021 and June 2023. Demographic and clinical data were extracted from electronic medical records. The risk factors were explored by univariate logistic regression and stepwise multivariate logistic regressions. Model performance was assessed using the receiver operating characteristic curve and area under the curve (AUC), along with calibration and decision curve analyses. The internal validation was performed using Bootstrap (n=1000) method. RESULTS: A total of 498 patients with COPD were enrolled, with 78 patients in the fungal infection group. Multivariable logistic regression analysis revealed that PaO2 within the normal range (OR=2.04, 95% CI: 1.12-3.71, P=0.02) and mold mix specific IgE above the normal threshold (OR=2.37, 95% CI: 1.04-5.36, P=0.04) were independently associated with an increased risk of fungal infections, whereas lymphocyte counts within the normal range (OR=0.37, 95% CI: 0.21-0.63, P<0.01) were associated with a reduced risk. Procalcitonin, albumin, and medical history of COPD duration were also included in predictive model based on the regression analysis. The AUC was 0.74 (95% CI: 0.68-0.79), and the Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test and decision curves indicated good differentiation and calibration. CONCLUSION: This study identifies elevated PaO2, mold mix specific IgE and lymphocyte counts as risk factors for fungal infections. The predictive model incorporating PaO2, mold mix specific IgE, lymphocyte counts, procalcitonin, albumin, and medical history of COPD duration demonstrated good predictive performance, offering a potential tool for early identification of high-risk patients in clinical practice.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) shows marked clinical heterogeneity and poor long-term survival, highlighting the need for simple and reliable risk stratification tools beyond the limited usability of existing complex prognostic models. In this study, we developed and validated PROGRESS (Prostate Cancer Global Risk Evaluation and Stratification Score), a simplified prognostic score derived through machine learning‑guided feature selection distilled into a simple laboratory-based tool. METHODS: Baseline data from 2,035 patients with mCRPC (training set) were embedded into synthetic representations, reduced with UMAP, and clustered with DBSCAN to discover outcome-related subpopulations. Feature contribution analysis informed a multivariable model that yielded three independent predictors (prostate specific antigen [PSA], alkaline phosphatase [ALP], and AST) composing PROGRESS. External validation used two independent data sets (n = 1,239) across different therapeutic settings. Overall survival (OS) was analyzed with Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression; discrimination was assessed by ROC-AUC, AUC(t), and Harrel C-index. RESULTS: Unsupervised modeling identified two patient risk subpopulations with significantly different OS rates (median 27.4 v 17.7 months; hazard ratio [HR], 2.20 [95% CI, 1.91 to 2.54]; P < .00001). The three retained predictors (PSA, ALP, and AST) were combined into a composite score (PROGRESS) that showed strong discrimination in the training cohort (ROC-AUC 0.89; AUC(t) 0.60; Harrel C-index 0.69). Using a prespecified cutoff, patients classified by PROGRESS as increased risk had significantly shorter survival than low-risk patients (median 18.3 v 25.6 months; HR, 1.72 [95% CI, 1.50 to 1.97]; P < .0001). PROGRESS prognostic performance was consistent across all validation cohorts (all P < .0001). CONCLUSION: By combining ML-based pattern discovery with classical modeling, PROGRESS provides a simple, objective, and readily implementable prognostic tool using three inexpensive routine laboratory measures. Its consistent performance across independent data sets supports clinical utility for individual risk stratification, trial enrichment, and early decision making. Prospective real-world validation is warranted.

papers.abstract_en: The purpose of this study is to determine the smallest tested fraction of manually labeled training data required for a multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) classifier to achieve satisfactory MRI series classification performance (macro-F1 ≥ 0.80) across five heterogeneous public MRI datasets using digital imaging and communications in medicine (DICOM) metadata, image data, or both. This retrospective study included 3804 examinations and 14,054 MRI series from five public DICOM datasets spanning brain, knee, lumbar spine, liver, and breast MRI, accessed February-April 2026. AI classification models included a random forest classifier using DICOM header metadata, a deep convolutional neural network classifier using the geometric center slice of each MRI series, and decision-fusion models. Models were trained with 5%-40% of studies manually labeled in 5-percentage-point increments, with additional 1%-4% fractions for the knee and lumbar spine. Model performance was evaluated on the remaining studies using study-level splits across five random seeds. Results were summarized as mean ± standard deviation. Zero-label unsupervised clustering results were evaluated separately on the full dataset. The macro-F1 target was reached at the smallest tested training fraction of 1% in the lumbar spine (0.945 ± 0.013), at 2% in the knee (0.818 ± 0.006), at 10% in the brain (0.872 ± 0.027), and at 20% in the liver (0.827 ± 0.016) and the breast (0.847 ± 0.012). The best-performing model differed by dataset, reflecting different contributions from metadata versus image data. Across five separately evaluated public MRI datasets, at least one header-based, image-based, or combined model achieved macro-F1 ≥ 0.80 using no more than 20% manually labeled studies.

papers.abstract_en: Mandibular odontogenic cysts can complicate surgical planning if located near the mandibular canal. Accurate delineation of both structures is therefore clinically important. This study presents a deep learning-based method for simultaneously segmenting mandibular odontogenic cysts and the mandibular canal in cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images. The developed method relies on a hybrid deep learning architecture integrating a ConvNeXt-Base encoder, a Dilated Context Block, a U-Net-based decoder, and a Deep Supervision mechanism. This framework simultaneously segments the mandibular canal and odontogenic cyst regions within the same architecture, promoting multi-scale contextual feature learning. We evaluated the performance of the proposed method using fivefold cross-validation experiments on a real-world clinical CBCT dataset comprising 103 patient images. We assessed segmentation performance using overlap-based metrics together with boundary-aware HD95 and ASSD metrics. The experimental results demonstrated that the model achieved a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 76.28% ± 1.83%. Excluding the background class yielded macro IoU and macro F1-score values of 64.46% ± 2.74% and 77.00% ± 1.89%, respectively. Meanwhile, the weighted IoU and weighted F1-score values were 78.71% ± 4.25% and 87.63% ± 2.63%, respectively. In boundary-based evaluations, the mandibular canal had an HD95 of 2.44 ± 2.98 mm and an ASSD of 0.45 ± 0.30 mm. The corresponding values for odontogenic cysts were 5.59 ± 3.65 mm and 1.43 ± 0.88 mm, respectively. These results suggest that the mandibular canal is more consistently delineated, while cyst segmentation remains more challenging, particularly at irregular and low-contrast boundaries. The proposed framework allows for the simultaneous and objective segmentation of mandibular odontogenic cysts and the mandibular canal within a unified, multi-class CBCT analysis framework. By providing reproducible delineation of both structures, this method could serve as a technical foundation for future quantitative analyses of lesion-canal relationships. However, further validation using larger, multicenter, volumetric CBCT datasets is required before clinical translation.

papers.abstract_en: The radiology report is essential for directing the course of treatment for a patient. However, writing radiology reports is a huge burden for radiologists. Manual reporting faces challenges due to intra-labeler and inter-labeler variability, causing inconsistent patient treatment and diagnostic results, and complicating matters due to alertness and changing judgment. To address these challenges, we propose an automated radiology report generation model tailored for chest X-ray imaging. We introduce BLIX-Ray, a vision-language model (VLM) designed to generate radiology reports using a transfer learning approach. BLIX-Ray fine-tunes the pre-trained BLIP model to extract and align rich visual and textual representations suited to the medical imaging domain. We use reinforcement learning (RL) to directly optimize report generation based on language evaluation metrics in order to further enhance performance. We evaluate BLIX-Ray on two publicly available datasets: IU-Xray and CheXpert Plus. Experimental results demonstrate that our model achieves the highest CIDEr and BERTScore on both datasets, while n-gram-oriented baselines retain an advantage on BLEU. BLIX-Ray integrates reinforcement learning and transfer learning to improve medical report generation under limited and heterogeneous data conditions. The results highlight the potential of vision-language models to support automated and standardized radiology reporting. Notably, BLIX-Ray achieves the best reported CIDEr (0.6534) and BERTScore (0.8765) among the compared methods on IU-Xray and leads on CIDEr, METEOR, and BERTScore on CheXpert Plus (BERTScore 0.8407), demonstrating strong report-level consensus and semantic similarity with the reference reports.

papers.abstract_en: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) is the most common cause of vestibular vertigo, yet accurate diagnosis remains challenging without specialist expertise. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an artificial intelligence (AI)-based diagnostic algorithm for BPPV using video-nystagmography (VNG) recordings. A total of 1352 VNG recordings were collected from patients with posterior semicircular canal (PSCC) BPPV (n = 234), lateral semicircular canal (LSCC) BPPV (canalolithiasis, n = 188; cupulolithiasis, n = 58), and healthy controls (n = 224) at a single tertiary referral hospital, yielding 1738 signal segments (1312 nystagmus segments annotated by two otolaryngologists and 426 normal segments). Eye trajectory signals were extracted using a deep learning-based VNG eye-tracking algorithm, transformed into two-dimensional (2D) scalogram representations via continuous wavelet transform (CWT), and classified using task-specific backbone architectures selected through systematic comparison under a patient-level data split. Ablation analysis showed that CWT-based 2D representations significantly outperformed raw one-dimensional (1D) time-series baselines. The final models achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) values of 0.974 for horizontal and 0.961 for torsional nystagmus classification. For BPPV subtype diagnosis, recording-level accuracy was 0.935 for the PSCC and 0.938 for the LSCC evaluation; F1-scores exceeded 0.84 for all PSCC classes and ranged from 0.59 to 0.98 for LSCC classes, with canalolithiasis variants outperforming cupulolithiasis variants. These findings suggest the feasibility of AI-assisted BPPV diagnosis from VNG recordings.

papers.abstract_en: Major histocompatibility complex class Ia (MHC-Ia)-restricted CD8⁺ T cell responses play a central role in the host defense against HIV-1, with certain MHC-Ia alleles known to be associated with cytotoxic T lymphocyte responses having an increased potential for viral control. However, the impact of immune aging on the effectiveness of such protective alleles remains unclear. In this study, we assessed SIVmac239 replication in aged (17-23 yr old) rhesus macaques (RMs) exhibiting low frequencies of naïve T cells and expanded effector memory T cells, that were further stratified by the presence (MHC⁺) or absence (MHC-) of 3 known "protective MHC-Ia alleles" (Mamu-A*01, Mamu-B*08, or Mamu-B*17). All RMs were infected with SIVmac239 and viral dynamics monitored longitudinally. MHC⁺ RMs demonstrated significantly lower plasma viral loads (PVLs) through 70 d postinfection compared with MHC- RMs. At 70 d postinfection, half of the RMs from each group initiated suppressive triple antiretroviral therapy comprising dolutegravir, emtricitabine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) for 15 wk, followed by suboptimal TDF monotherapy for an additional 21 wk. While antiretroviral therapy substantially reduced PVL in both groups, viral decline was accelerated in MHC⁺ RMs relative to MHC- RMs. Moreover, upon switching to TDF monotherapy, PVL rebounded by almost 3 logs in MHC- RMs, while MHC⁺ RMs maintained viral suppression. Collectively, these findings indicate that protective MHC-Ia alleles can mediate viral control in aged hosts, even under suboptimal treatment conditions, and highlight the potential role of optimized CD8+ T cell responses in strategies targeting viral persistence in aging populations.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To characterize cardiac effort and heart rate (HR) responses during the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) early after cardiac surgery, compare HR patterns between walking and cycle ergometry, and evaluate differences by sex, frailty, and atrial fibrillation status. METHODS: We analyzed a publicly available PhysioNet dataset of adults ≥65 years with pre-frailty/frailty undergoing cardiac surgery who completed a 6MWT and symptom-limited cycle ergometry with continuous single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring (Polar H10). Cardiac effort was defined as total 6MWT heartbeats divided by distance walked (beats/m). Associations with cycle-ergometry performance were assessed using Spearman correlations with bootstrap CI; paired t tests compared HR responses between modalities; subgroup differences were evaluated using Welch t tests and multivariable linear regression. RESULTS: Of 80 enrolled participants, 66 (83%) had analyzable 6MWT ECG recordings (mean age 73 ± 5 years; 67% male; 18 ± 8 days post-surgery). Mean 6-minute walking distance (6MWD) was 300 ± 79 m, and mean cardiac effort was 1.62 ± 0.52 beats/m. In 38 participants with paired cycle-ergometry data, HR responses were similar between walking and cycling. Greater 6MWD was associated with better cycle-ergometry performance, while higher cardiac effort was associated with lower cycle-ergometry performance. In multivariable analysis, female sex was independently associated with higher cardiac effort (β = .34 beats/m; P = .042), atrial fibrillation with lower average and end-of-test HR (P ≤ .035), and greater frailty with shorter 6MWD (P = .036). CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac effort is a feasible ECG-derived metric that complements 6MWD by integrating heart rate response with functional performance early after cardiac surgery. In this frail, predominantly beta-blocked cohort, HR responses during walking closely mirrored cycle ergometry.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Despite normalization of left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), symptoms and impaired exercise capacity can persist ~1 year after Takotsubo syndrome (TTS). Rates of major adverse cardiovascular events were similar between groups (P > .05). CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac rehabilitation did not enhance cardiac structural or functional recovery but did improve functional exercise capacity and HRQoL in patients with TTS.

papers.abstract_en: Uterus transplantation (UTx) has emerged as a promising treatment for women with absolute uterine factor infertility (AUFI), enabling pregnancy and live birth with their own genetic offspring. Living-donor uterus procurement remains the most technically demanding component of the procedure. Robotic-assisted donor hysterectomy has been introduced to improve surgical precision, reduce donor morbidity, and preserve graft quality, while recipient implantation is performed via laparotomy. This systematic review evaluated current evidence on robotic-assisted living-donor hysterectomy for UTx, focusing on surgical techniques, donor safety, recipient outcomes, and reproductive success. Databases and trial registries were searched from inception through June 2026. Six studies reporting 29 unique robotic-assisted living-donor hysterectomies across five countries met the inclusion criteria. All procedures used the da Vinci Xi robotic platform. Operative time and estimated blood loss decreased with increasing surgical experience, while major donor complications (Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher) were less frequent in later series. Among cases with reported follow-up, no graft loss was observed; restoration of menstruation, embryo transfer, clinical pregnancy, and live birth were achieved, including ten live births in the largest programme. Robotic-assisted living-donor hysterectomy for uterus transplantation appears technically feasible and has been associated with viable grafts and successful pregnancies in highly selected cases. However, major donor complications, including ureteric injury requiring reimplantation and bilateral oophorectomy, were observed, and the true incidence of donor morbidity remains uncertain. Current evidence remains limited to small observational studies, and these findings support careful evaluation within structured, multidisciplinary programmes and international registries rather than widespread expansion.

papers.abstract_en: Robotic surgical platforms are diversifying, and clinical outcomes are increasingly comparable across systems, yet the console surgeon's subjective experience remains poorly characterized. We developed a surgeon-reported questionnaire on robotic surgical systems and performed a preliminary psychometric evaluation in robotic radical prostatectomy. The Surgeons' Perception Questionnaire on Robotics (SPQR) includes 31 five-point items in six domains: technical and operational aspects, key surgical tasks, ergonomics and physical comfort, communication and workflow integration, learning curve, and overall evaluation. In a cross-sectional web-based survey, surgeons rated the platform they primarily used for robotic radical prostatectomy. Internal consistency was assessed with polychoric-based Cronbach's alpha and McDonald's omega; exploratory (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) were performed in the same sample. Fifty-nine surgeons participated (response rate 42%); 81% evaluated the da Vinci Xi. Overall internal consistency was high (alpha 0.96; omega 0.97). Alpha and omega were ≥ 0.84 in five domains but below 0.70 for ergonomics and physical comfort (0.64 and 0.67). EFA suggested three factors (system performance and satisfaction; learning curve and training; ergonomics). CFA showed high incremental fit (comparative fit index 0.985) but inadequate absolute fit (root mean square error of approximation 0.097; standardized root mean square residual 0.135), and the ergonomics factor was weakly defined. The SPQR showed high internal consistency in most domains and a provisional multidimensional structure. Because the sample was small, highly experienced, predominantly male, and dominated by one platform, these findings require confirmation in larger independent cohorts before the SPQR is used for platform comparisons.
