papers.abstract_en: Respirable crystalline silica (RCS) is a major occupational health hazard associated with silicosis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), lung cancer, autoimmune diseases, and other systemic disorders. Saudi Arabia is undergoing rapid industrial expansion in sectors with substantial potential for RCS exposure, including mining, construction, cement production, glass manufacturing, oil and gas, engineered stone fabrication, and photovoltaic manufacturing. This review evaluates the potential risk of occupational RCS exposure in Saudi Arabia by integrating evidence from the scientific literature, government reports, labor and mining statistics, mineralogical data, and regulatory documents. The novel silica Hazard triangle framework was applied to assess three principal determinants of occupational exposure: workforce distribution, silica-containing materials, and high-risk industrial activities. Saudi Arabia possesses extensive reserves of high-purity silica sand, and continued expansion of mining and downstream silica-based industries may increase occupational exposure potential. The kingdom's arid climate may also contribute to dust generation and increase the occupational exposure of RCS. Although documented cases of silicosis confirm that silica-related disease exists in Saudi Arabia, published evidence on occupational exposure assessment, epidemiology, and health surveillance remains limited. International regulatory developments demonstrate the importance of health-based occupational exposure limits (OELs), exposure monitoring, engineering controls, and medical surveillance. Current Saudi labor law, National Council for occupational safety and health (NCOSH) policies, and General Organization for Social Insurance (GOSI) occupational disease frameworks provide an important legal and institutional foundation for the future development of silica-specific occupational health regulations. This review identifies important knowledge gaps and highlights the need for comprehensive exposure assessment, strengthened industrial hygiene capacity, and evidence-based regulatory strategies to reduce the future burden of silica-related diseases while supporting sustainable industrial development in Saudi Arabia.

papers.abstract_en: Proton boron capture therapy (PBCT), based on proton-boron fusion reactions (11B + p →3α + 8.7 MeV), has the potential to enhance the biological effectiveness of proton therapy. To achieve this potential, the efficient delivery of enough 11B to cancer cells will be paramount. This study demonstrates a newly developed method of poor solvent-mediated spontaneous assembly of polymeric micelles with entrapped o-carborane, in which ethanol is a good solvent for the payload o-carborane but a poor solvent for the hydrophobic segment poly(ε-caprolactone) in this amphiphilic block copolymer. This method provided smaller polymeric micelles compared to use of tetrahydrofuran, a good solvent for the amphiphilic block copolymer, as the sole solvent for both payload and copolymer. The prepared nanoscale formulation enabled the boron-rich cage compound o-carborane to be effectively delivered to tumor cells, and its enhancement of the biological effectiveness of proton therapy was preliminarily validated in a pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cell line, MiaPaCa-2, by survival assays and DNA damage assessment. The 111In-labeled congener was also successfully prepared and used in biodistribution assays in normal mice, opening the way to further studies on image-guided PBCT in preclinical animal models.

papers.title_zh: 星形胶质细胞在神经系统疾病炎症反应中的作用：叙述性综述
papers.title_en: The Role of Astrocytes in the Inflammatory Response in Neurodiseases.
papers.authors: Peng S, Wang L, Ouyang J, Liu R
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Neurosurgery Peking University People's Hospital, Xicheng District Beijing China.
papers.authors_conclusion: Defining functionally validated astrocyte states and developing biomarker-guided, stage-adaptive therapies may enable more precise intervention in neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases.
papers.ai_note: 主题为神经科学/神经炎症，不属于胸部肿瘤或胸外科范畴；六类胸部肿瘤分类均不契合，category=advanced 仅为形式归类。叙述性综述未报告系统检索、纳入排除标准或定量合成，无法评估方法学严谨性；结论为未来方向性表述，缺乏原始数据支持。
papers.reason: 与胸外科和胸部肿瘤临床判断无关，不能影响手术患者选择、结节风险判断、围术期决策或胸部肿瘤科研设计；仅可作为神经炎症基础背景阅读。
papers.abstract_en: Astrocytes have emerged as central regulators of neuroinflammation, extending far beyond their traditional roles as structural and metabolic support cells. In neurological disorders, astrocytes undergo reactive remodeling that encompasses morphological, transcriptional, metabolic, and functional changes. Rather than fitting into a fixed A1/A2 dichotomy, reactive astrocytes exist along a disease-, region-, and stage-dependent continuum shaped by local pathology and intercellular crosstalk. This review summarizes how astrocytes contribute to neuroinflammatory processes in Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Huntington's disease, central nervous system injury, infection, multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, and autism spectrum disorder. We highlight convergent mechanisms, including cytokine and chemokine release, complement activation, glutamate and ion homeostasis disruption, oxidative stress, metabolic reprogramming, and blood-brain barrier regulation, while emphasizing disease-specific astrocytic programs. We further discuss astrocyte interactions with microglia, neurons, oligodendrocytes, endothelial cells, and peripheral immune cells, as well as key regulatory pathways, epigenetic remodeling, and lipid-dependent metabolic signaling. Finally, we evaluate current and emerging astrocyte-targeted therapeutic strategies, including metabolic modulation, receptor targeting, gene editing, nanodelivery, and gut-brain axis interventions. Defining functionally validated astrocyte states and developing biomarker-guided, stage-adaptive therapies may enable more precise intervention in neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases.

papers.authors: Buttle B, Verdon D, Sheppard HM

papers.ai_note: 本文为细胞免疫治疗工程化技术综述，与胸部肿瘤临床诊疗无直接关联，归入肿瘤类别仅为形式适配；摘要未说明文献检索策略、纳入/排除标准及“cross-study normalisation”的具体换算方法，存在选择性引用与跨研究可比性不明的风险；对rAAV“一致最高插入率”与非病毒cssDNA“前景可期”的表述未给出量化证据，结论口径偏乐观。
papers.reason: 为细胞治疗工程化（大片段敲入）的技术瓶颈提供背景梳理，可作为胸部肿瘤相关T细胞/工程化免疫治疗研究设计时的技术选型参考，但不直接影响胸外科或胸部肿瘤临床决策。
papers.abstract_en: Large insert gene editing in ex vivo, primary human T cells represents an important approach for engineering next-generation cellular immunotherapies. While CRISPR-based editing is well-established for small genetic modifications, large insert knock-in remains a technical bottleneck. This review examines current strategies for achieving efficient, precise and safe integration of large genetic elements. We compare delivery methods for CRISPR components, highlighting electroporation of Cas9 ribonucleoproteins as the most efficient but often cytotoxic approach; emerging alternatives such as cell-penetrating peptides and lipid nanoparticles offer improved cell viability at the expense of editing efficiency. The influence of genomic locus selection, guide RNA design and chromatin context on editing outcomes, as well as the role of homology-directed repair (HDR) template design is evaluated. Various template formats-including linear double- and single-stranded DNA, plasmids, circular single-stranded (css) DNA and recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV)-are assessed for their efficiency, toxicity and risk of off-target integration. Where possible, cross-study normalisation is used to enable meaningful comparisons. rAAV templates consistently achieve the highest insertion rates but come with concerns regarding cost, size limitations and insertional mutagenesis, whereas non-viral approaches such as cssDNA templates show promise. Additionally, we review the use of small-molecule modulators to enhance HDR efficiency, noting trade-offs between improved insertion rates and potential genomic instability. Overall, successful large insert editing requires balancing of editing efficiency, cell viability and genomic safety considerations. Continued optimisation of delivery systems, template design and repair pathway modulation will be critical for advancing scalable and clinically viable T-cell therapies.

papers.abstract_en: Lactate, once regarded merely as the terminal product of glycolysis, is now recognised as a pivotal immunometabolic regulator that actively shapes inflammatory responses. However, accumulating evidence reveals an apparent paradox that lactate can either amplify immune activation or promote inflammation resolution depending on the biological context. The mechanisms underlying this functional duality remain incompletely understood, limiting the development of effective lactate-targeted therapies. In this review, we propose that lactate functions as a context-dependent immunometabolic rheostat whose Yin-Yang properties are determined by the integration of four key factors: lactate concentration, cellular identity, disease stage and inflammatory microenvironment. We summarise how lactate regulates immune responses through coordinated control of metabolic reprogramming, intercellular lactate shuttling, receptor-mediated signalling, intracellular sensing, and protein lactylation, thereby orchestrating the activation and resolution of inflammation. We further discuss the cell-specific actions of lactate across endothelial cells, macrophages, fibroblast-like synoviocytes, neutrophils, and lymphocytes, highlighting how these mechanisms collectively remodel the inflammatory microenvironment. Beyond mechanistic insights, we examine evidence from representative inflammatory disease models, including rheumatoid arthritis, sepsis, and atherosclerosis, and evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies targeting lactate production, transport, sensing and metabolism. Rather than advocating indiscriminate lactate inhibition, current evidence supports context-specific modulation of lactate signalling according to disease stage and immune landscape.

papers.abstract_en: T-complex protein 1 (TCP1) encodes the TCP1α subunit, one of eight subunits of the chaperonin containing TCP1 ring complex (TRiC). Heterozygous TCP1 variants cause autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by developmental delay or intellectual disability, seizures, pyramidal or cerebellar signs, and brain malformations, particularly polymicrogyria. However, the reported clinical spectrum remains limited. We report a 4-year-old girl with global developmental delay, speech and motor delay, behavioral dysregulation, microcephaly, hypotonia with core weakness, and a previously unreported heterozygous likely pathogenic TCP1 variant, c.1392delT (p.A465Qfs*3). This frameshift variant is located in exon 11, truncates the final 16.5% of the protein, is predicted to undergo nonsense-mediated decay, and is absent from gnomAD. Biological parental testing was unavailable, precluding determination of variant inheritance. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated an absent septum pellucidum with mild bilateral frontal sulcation/gyration asymmetry without polymicrogyria; the optic nerves and pituitary were normal. No seizures were documented through age 4 years. Additional findings included bicuspid aortic valve with mild aortic insufficiency, asthma, severe eczema/atopy, and multiple food allergies. This case suggests that the molecular and neuroimaging spectrum of TCP1-related neurodevelopmental disorder may be broader than previously recognized; however, a causal association between TCP1 and absent septum pellucidum cannot be established from a single case. The relationship of the cardiac and atopic findings to TCP1 remains uncertain. Additional cases and functional studies are needed to clarify genotype-phenotype relationships.

papers.abstract_en: The World Health Organization and the National Advisory Committee on Immunization now recommend a single-dose HPV vaccine schedule for most immunocompetent adolescents. As Canadian jurisdictions transition to a single-dose schedule, we apply a social and behavioral science lens and draw on lessons from previous vaccine schedule changes and international experience to identify potential challenges and opportunities associated with this transition. Key implementation considerations include maintaining public confidence through transparent communication about the rationale for the schedule change, ensuring healthcare providers, immunizers, and parents are adequately prepared to support the transition, and promoting equitable access through robust catch-up programs and targeted outreach initiatives. Attention to these factors will be critical to supporting successful implementation of single-dose HPV vaccination programs in Canada.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: In locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (LA-ESCC), neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NCIT) plus high-quality surgery (R0 resection with systematic lymphadenectomy >19 nodes) is a promising strategy. However, the value of adjuvant immunotherapy remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between postoperative adjuvant immunotherapy and survival outcomes in a multicenter cohort. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study enrolled LA-ESCC patients receiving NCIT from eight high-volume Chinese centers between 2019 and 2023. After screening for high-quality surgery, propensity score matching (PSM) balanced characteristics between the two groups: NCIT plus surgery (NCIT+S) and NCIT plus surgery followed by adjuvant immunotherapy (NCIT+S+ICI). The primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS). A prognostic framework based on major pathological response (MPR) and postoperative pathological N stage (ypN) was constructed to refine patient selection. RESULTS: Among 724 patients with a median follow-up of 40.3 months, 3-year OS and DFS rates were 73.0% and 67.7%, respectively. After PSM, adjuvant immunotherapy significantly improved DFS (77.1% vs 65.8%, log-rank P=0.037), but not OS (83.4% vs 69.4%, log-rank P=0.058). Multivariate analysis identified ypN, MPR, and postoperative adjuvant immunotherapy as independent prognostic factors for DFS. Stratification by MPR and ypN status showed that DFS benefit from adjuvant immunotherapy was restricted to the non-MPR/ypN+ subgroup (HR=0.339; 95% CI: 0.173-0.662; log-rank P<0.001), with a significant treatment-by-subgroup interaction (P for interaction=0.025). CONCLUSIONS: Among LA-ESCC patients receiving NCIT and high-quality surgery, adjuvant immunotherapy significantly improves 3-year DFS in the non-MPR/ypN+ subgroup, with no significant benefit in other subgroups.

papers.title_zh: 基于机器学习构建肺癌肺切除与食管癌食管切除术后不良事件质量保证模型：9家医院多中心建模与内部验证

papers.authors: Ishwaran H, Blackstone EH
papers.affiliation_highlight: Division of Biostatistics, Cleveland Clinic, Cleveland, Ohio.
papers.results: 共分析16,430例肺切除与3,068例食管切除；肺切除71个、食管切除63个术前变量中分别有35个与29个被识别为7个结局模型的重要预测因子。Out-of-bag几何均值：肺切除0.588–0.713，食管切除0.517–0.649；out-of-bag校准仅覆盖“适度的概率范围”。肺切除手术死亡率方面，逐一排除各焦点医院后，各医院间对比保持稳定
papers.authors_conclusion: 使用当代机器学习，已初步建立肺癌肺切除与食管癌食管切除术后不良事件模型，为外科医生、患者及医院/医院系统提供患者风险评估工具并可用于指导普通胸外科质量改进举措
papers.ai_note: 全文核心性能指标仅以“out-of-bag几何均值”呈现（0.588–0.713、0.517–0.649），未报告区分度（AUC/C统计量）或其置信区间，指标含义与临床可用阈值无法判断；校准仅描述为覆盖“适度概率范围”，缺校准斜率/截距等数据；验证完全为内部（out-of-bag）与医院留出，无独立外部队列或前瞻性验证；7个模型对应多项终点，摘要未给出各单项/复合结局的事件数与定义，存在复合终点掩盖单项表现的可能；“医院间风险因素量级不同”与“对比稳定”仅做定性描述，未给数值；结论口径“提供风险评估工具”超出摘要所示证据强度。

pico.p: 9家医院、7个医院系统内因癌症行肺切除16,430例与食管切除3,068例的患者
pico.ic: 以术前信息（肺切除71个、食管切除63个候选变量）为基础，采用随机森林分位数分类（针对不平衡数据）加无模型变量重要性筛选，构建5个单项结局模型与2个复合结局模型；以out-of-bag预测作正则化估计与内部验证，并行医院留出/留一分析评估机构基准稳定性；无外部对照干预组

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To develop quality assurance models for adverse procedural events after lung resection and esophagectomy for cancer. METHODS: Using procedural outcomes after 16,430 lung resections and 3,068 esophagectomies for cancer at 9 hospitals in 7 hospital systems, we developed 5 individual and 2 composite outcome models from preoperative information. Random forest quantile classification for imbalanced data with model-free variable priority screening identified predictors. Out-of-bag prediction provided regularized estimates and internal validation. Hospital-holdout analysis assessed institutional benchmark stability. RESULTS: Of 71 lung resection and 63 esophagectomy preoperative variables, 35 and 29, respectively, were identified as important predictors across the 7 outcome models. These included demographics, advanced cancer, organ dysfunction, higher acuity, and planned surgical approach and resection extent. Out-of-bag calibration covered a modest range of probabilities. Out-of-bag geometric mean ranged from 0.588 to 0.713 for lung resection and 0.517 to 0.649 for esophagectomy. Continuous risk factors, particularly pulmonary function, provided high-importance information content, with complex dependency and interaction structure among predictors. Risk-factor magnitude differed among hospitals, as did their risk-adjusted outcomes according to patient risk as determined by counterfactual inference within a framework of virtual twins. For lung resection operative mortality, hospital-specific contrasts were stable when each focal hospital was excluded from the aggregate benchmark. CONCLUSIONS: Using contemporary machine learning, initial models for adverse procedural events after lung resection and esophagectomy for cancer have been developed. They provide surgeons, their patients, and hospital and hospital systems tools for patient risk assessment and for informing quality improvement initiatives in general thoracic surgery.

papers.abstract_en: Endocytosis regulates receptor trafficking and signaling, yet its role in colorectal cancer (CRC) remains unclear. We analyzed transcriptomic data from 15,025 CRC tumors to evaluate gene expression in clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME) and the endosomal sorting complexes required for transport (ESCRT) pathway. Pathway-level signatures were compared across consensus molecular subtypes (CMS) and examined in relation to oncogenic signaling programs, while individual endocytosis-related genes were evaluated for associations with clinical outcomes in an independent randomized trial cohort. Expression of CME and ESCRT pathways varied by CMS, with the highest expression in CMS4 and the lowest in CMS3. Endocytosis signatures correlated with multiple oncogenic signaling pathways, including MAPK, TGF-β, WNT, PI3K, NOTCH, and angiogenesis, suggesting broad links between endocytic activity and tumor biology. In the randomized phase III CALGB/SWOG 80405 trial, low expression of AP2M1-a core adaptor in the CME complex-was significantly associated with longer overall survival and progression-free survival in patients treated with anti-EGFR agents, but not in those receiving anti-VEGF agents. These findings suggest that endocytic trafficking may be associated with oncogenic signaling and differential therapeutic benefit in patients with metastatic CRC. The endocytosis pathway reflects biologically relevant heterogeneity in CRC and may help guide therapeutic stratification.

papers.abstract_en: Gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma (GEAC) remains a highly aggressive malignancy with limited effective targeted therapies. Cyclin-dependent kinase 9 (CDK9), a key regulator of transcriptional elongation, has been implicated in oncogenic processes across multiple cancer types; however, its functional role and therapeutic potential in GEAC remain poorly defined. In this study, we systematically investigated CDK9 expression, function, and therapeutic targeting in GEAC, with particular emphasis on its interaction with the YAP/TEAD signaling axis. Immunohistochemical analysis of primary GEAC tumors and patient-derived xenografts revealed elevated CDK9 expression, which correlated with poor patient survival. Mechanistic studies using immunofluorescence and co-immunoprecipitation demonstrated a reciprocal regulatory interaction between CDK9 and YAP1, promoting transcriptional programs associated with tumor progression and radiation resistance. We developed novel CDK9-targeting proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) and identified YX0597 as a potent CDK9 degrader. YX0597 effectively suppressed RNAP II Ser2 phosphorylation (RNAP II P-S2) and downregulated oncogenic drivers, including MCL-1. Functionally, CDK9 degradation markedly inhibited GEAC cell proliferation, invasion, and tumor sphere formation, with enhanced efficacy in radiation-resistant cells. Integrated RNA sequencing and ATAC sequencing revealed that CDK9 degradation increased chromatin accessibility, reactivated epigenetically silenced genes, and profoundly suppressed YAP/TEAD transcriptional activity. These coordinated transcriptional and epigenetic alterations disrupted oncogenic homeostasis, resulting in broad cytotoxicity. Importantly, co-targeting CDK9 and YAP/TEAD signaling produced strong synergistic antitumor effects in vitro and in vivo. Collectively, our findings identify CDK9 as a critical oncogenic driver in GEAC and highlight CDK9 degradation, particularly in combination with YAP/TEAD inhibition, as a promising therapeutic strategy for refractory GEAC.

papers.abstract_en: While immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized treatment of the patients with aero-upper digestive squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs), including esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC), only a subset of patients benefit from ICIs, therefore entailing exploration of the mechanisms to regulate treatment responsiveness. POLE, as a subunit of DNA polymerase ε, possesses 3'-5' proofreading activity, and its mutations have been associated with favourable response to ICIs in several solid tumors. However, post-translational modification (PTM) of POLE and its impact on the therapeutic efficacy of ICIs are unknown. Here, this study demonstrates that ubiquitin-like protein 3 (Ubl3), whose expression is markedly downregulated in SCCs, covalently binds to Pole, reduces nuclear Pole levels, triggers DNA damage, and activates cGAS-STING signaling pathway. Notably, Ubl3 modification of Pole significantly primes the local immune microenvironment to mitigate the growth of murine aero-upper digestive SCC cells and boost the efficacy of αPD-1 treatment in vivo. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis further revealed that UBL3 expression is positively correlated with better clinical outcomes in a cohort of ESCC patients receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy combined with αPD-1. Together, our findings unravel UBL3 modification as a novel PTM mechanism governing subcellular location of POLE and its influence on immunotherapy responsiveness, thus making UBL3 modification as a promising immunomodulatory approach to enhance immunotherapy efficacy in patients with aero-upper digestive SCCs.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: At the final analysis of KEYNOTE-966 (median follow-up 25·6 months), pembrolizumab plus gemcitabine and cisplatin (pembrolizumab group) versus placebo plus gemcitabine and cisplatin (placebo group) provided a statistically significant, clinically meaningful improvement in overall survival without any new safety signals in participants with advanced biliary tract cancer. We report results from a median study follow-up of 36·6 months (∼3 years). METHODS: In the randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 KEYNOTE-966 trial conducted at 175 medical centres worldwide, eligible participants aged ≥18 years with previously untreated advanced biliary tract cancer were randomly assigned (1:1) to pembrolizumab 200 mg or placebo intravenously every 3 weeks plus gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 and cisplatin 25 mg/m2 intravenously on days 1 and 8 of every 3-week cycle. Randomisation was done using a central interactive voice-response system and stratified by geographical region, disease status, and site of origin in block sizes of four. The primary endpoint of overall survival was evaluated in the intention-to-treat population (all participants randomly assigned to a treatment). Safety was evaluated in the as-treated population, comprising all participants who received at least one dose of study treatment. As the primary endpoint was met at the final analysis, updated data are reported without p values. This study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04003636. FINDINGS: Between Oct 4, 2019, and June 8, 2021, 1069 participants were randomly assigned to the pembrolizumab group (n = 533) or the placebo group (n = 536). Median follow-up at data cutoff (Nov 14, 2023) was 36·6 months (IQR 32·7-41·4). The hazard ratio for overall survival was 0·86 (95% CI, 0·75-0·98) with pembrolizumab versus placebo; estimated 36-month overall survival rates were 13% (95% CI, 11-17) in the pembrolizumab group and 11% (95% CI, 8-14) in the placebo group. Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 370 (70%) of 529 participants in the pembrolizumab group and 367 (69%) of 534 participants in the placebo group. No new treatment-related deaths occurred since the final analysis. INTERPRETATION: With extended follow-up, the survival benefit of pembrolizumab plus gemcitabine and cisplatin observed at the final analysis persists with approximately 3 years of follow-up, with no new safety signals among participants with previously untreated metastatic or unresectable biliary tract cancer. FUNDING: Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC, a subsidiary of Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway, NJ, USA.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Brain metastasis (BM) is a devastating complication of breast cancer (BC) with a poor prognosis. Early identification of high-risk patients is essential but currently lacks accurate predictive tools. This study aimed to develop a stable machine learning model for predicting BM in a large, diverse patient population. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 186,351 primary BC patients from the SEER program, the National Cancer Database, and a multi-center Chinese cohort. Patients were split into training and validation sets. Candidate predictors included demographic, clinicopathological, biomarker, and treatment-related variables, including surgery, chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, neoadjuvant therapy, and radiotherapy. LASSO regression was used for feature selection. Nine machine learning models were developed and compared using area under the curve (AUC) and decision curve analysis. The optimal model was deployed as an online tool. RESULTS: Among 186,351 patients, 2,982 (1.6%) developed BM. In baseline comparisons, patients who developed BM more frequently exhibited advanced disease characteristics and different treatment patterns, likely reflecting more aggressive disease presentation. Key predictors retained in the final parsimonious model included AJCC N/M/T stage, age, and surgery status. The LASSO-regularized Logistic Regression model achieved superior discrimination in the validation set, with an AUC of 0.907 (95% CI: 0.857-0.958). The model demonstrated good calibration, clinical net benefit, and interpretability, with SHAP analysis confirming the contribution of each retained predictor to individual risk estimates. Survival analysis confirmed the poor prognosis associated with BM (p < 0.001). An interactive online tool was developed for real-time risk estimation. CONCLUSION: We developed and internally validated a accurate, clinically translatable model for predicting BM in BC using over 186,000 patients from North American and Asian cohorts. This web-based tool can assist clinicians in identifying high-risk individuals, enabling personalized management and potentially improving patient outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status (ECOG-PS) is central to cancer care planning and prognostication. Whether ECOG-PS also carries prognostic value in the setting of primary thromboprophylaxis for cancer-associated venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains unknown. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of ECOG-PS on clinical outcomes in ambulatory patients with cancer initiating chemotherapy. METHODS: This was a post-hoc analysis of the AVERT randomized controlled trial that evaluated apixaban (2.5 mg twice daily) for thromboprophylaxis in patients at intermediate-to-high VTE risk. Multivariable survival models assessed the association between ECOG-PS (0-1 versus 2-3) and the composite primary outcome of VTE or clinically relevant bleeding (CRB), as well as its individual components and all-cause mortality, over 180 days. RESULTS: Of 428 patients included, 368 (86.0%) and 60 (14.0%) had an ECOG-PS of 0-1 and 2-3, respectively. The primary composite outcome occurred in 12.8% (n = 47) in those with ECOG 0-1 and 18.3% (n = 11) with ECOG-PS 2-3 (6-month cumulative incidence: 13.0% [95% CI: 9.8%-16.7%] versus 19.9% [95% CI: 10.5%-31.4%], respectively). Worse performance status was associated with higher risks for the composite outcome (aHR: 1.76; 95% CI: 1.14-2.72; p = 0.011), CRB (aHR: 1.58; 95%CI: 1.53-1.63; p < 0.0001), and all-cause mortality (aHR: 5.77; 95% CI: 4.98-6.67; p < 0.0001). In exploratory treatment-effect analyses, apixaban reduced VTE risk across ECOG-PS strata, including among participants with ECOG-PS 2-3, without clear evidence of excess CRB in this subgroup. CONCLUSIONS: ECOG-PS predicts VTE-related outcomes in ambulatory patients with cancer and may inform individualized, value-based shared decision-making regarding anticoagulant thromboprophylaxis.

papers.abstract_en: Patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) have an unmet need for new therapies that improve survival. In this phase II trial, patients received ociperlimab and tislelizumab (A) or placebo and tislelizumab (B) (NCT04732494). The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) assessed by the investigator per RECIST v1.1. A total of 125 patients were randomized to A (N = 62) and B (N = 63). The primary endpoint was not met, with an ORR (95% confidence interval [CI]) assessed by the investigator of 30.6% (19.6-43.7) for A and 20.6% (11.5-32.7) for B (stratified risk difference: 9.9% [95% CI - 5.4 to 25.3]; stratified 2-sided p = 0.2114). At the final analysis, median OS (95% CI) was 10.2 (7.9-19.5) months for A and 9.3 (6.4-14.8) months for B (stratified HR [95% CI]: 0.92 [0.58-1.45]). A total of 25.8% (16/62) and 20.6% (13/63) of patients in A and B, respectively, experienced grade ≥3 treatment-related treatment-emergent adverse events. Exploratory biomarker analyses showed that patients with an inflamed tumor microenvironment, shown by the enriched expression of natural killer (NK) cells, T cells, macrophages, dendritic cells, and B-cell signatures, and NK cell signature enrichment, may benefit from ociperlimab plus tislelizumab. Adding ociperlimab to tislelizumab did not provide significant efficacy improvement in recurrent/metastatic second-line ESCC; the addition of ociperlimab to tislelizumab was generally well-tolerated. Trial registration: Clinicaltrials.gov: NCT04732494.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: The tumor suppressor TP53 is the most frequently mutated gene in human cancer, and drugs targeting specific mutant p53 proteins have been developed. Rezatapopt, which reactivates the Y220C p53 protein, was recently evaluated in the Phase I PYNNACLE trial in patients with solid tumors, with promising results. The trial did not enrol any non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cases, and little is known about the clinicopathological characteristics and genetic profile of the TP53 Y220C NSCLC patients. METHODS: In this multicenter, European Thoracic Oncology Platform-sponsored study, we retrospectively collected data from NSCLC patients from several European institutions with Next Generation Sequencing data available. RESULTS: The study included 28,244 NSCLC patients. We found that 195 (0.7%) harbored the TP53 Y220C mutation, a prevalence higher than the average in solid tumors (0.4%). Half of these TP53 Y220C NSCLC patients did not carry any known drivers. No significant association was observed between the TP53 Y220C and gender, smoking status, histology or stage. However, the mutation was significantly more prevalent in EGFR-mutant than EGFR-wild-type tumors (1.7% vs. 0.7%; p=0.029). Finally, 17.0% of Y220C patients carried a second mutation in TP53. CONCLUSIONS: The TP53 Y220C has a frequency similar to other low abundance, actionable alterations in NSCLC. Patients with NSCLC should be screened and included in future trials of Y220C reactivators. Co-mutations in TP53 should also be analyzed, since they might be associated with intrinsic resistance.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Fontan patients are considered high risk for heart transplantation (HT) owing to their complex anatomy, multiple prior chest entries, and universal Fontan-associated liver disease (FALD). The impact of FALD and other preoperative factors remains, however, uncertain. OBJECTIVES: We sought to identify factors associated with 90-day mortality after isolated HT in adults with Fontan circulation, with particular focus on the relationship between liver-related parameters and post-transplant outcomes. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of all adult Fontan patients undergoing isolated HT was conducted. Factors associated with 90-day mortality were assessed using appropriate univariate analyses and penalized multivariable logistic regression. ROC analysis was used to derive liver size cut-offs and compare the discriminative performance of selected variables. A descriptive analysis of adult Fontan patients undergoing combined heart-liver transplantation (CHLT) was also performed for contextual comparison. RESULTS: Thirty-seven patients (mean age 30 years) underwent isolated HT; 19% (n=8) died within 90 days. Factors associated with increased 90-day mortality were >4 previous chest entries, major perioperative bleeding, and small liver size [total liver volume (TLV) ≤1366 mL, total liver volume indexed to body surface area (TLVi) <786 mL/m2 and liver transverse dimension (LTD) <21 cm]. Multiple chest veno-venous collaterals, >4 previous chest entries, and small liver were strongly associated with bleeding and subsequent fatal complications including sepsis, graft dysfunction, and bowel ischaemia. Within the study period, five other patients had undergone CHLT. All had biopsy confirmed advanced liver disease with features of clinically significant portal hypertension or hepatocellular carcinoma. One patient died within 90 days following prolonged cardiopulmonary bypass, major bleeding, graft dysfunction and sepsis, culminating in multiorgan failure. CONCLUSIONS: In Fontan patients undergoing isolated HT, >4 previous chest entries, major bleeding, and small liver volume were associated with increased 90-day mortality. Objective liver metrics (TLV ≤1366 mL, TLVi <786 mL/m2, TLD <21 cm) may provide adjunctive risk stratification for Fontan patients considered for isolated HT; however, these measures and proposed thresholds remain exploratory and require external validation. CHLT is a viable option, although non-liver related transplant risk factors may similarly influence outcomes. Detailed liver assessment and management at experienced, high-volume congenital transplant centres are important to optimizing outcomes in this complex population.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung-protective ventilation is essential in the management of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), but current approaches are limited by the heterogeneity of lung pathology and a lack of individualized strategies. Patient-specific computational models may overcome these limitations by providing predictive and physiologically interpretable insights into global and regional lung behavior. METHODS: Ten mechanically ventilated patients with ARDS were evaluated in a monocentric prospective pilot study. A predefined study protocol included ventilatory maneuvers with systematic changes in ventilator mode, tidal volume, positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), and driving pressure. For each patient, a personalized, regionally resolved physics-based computational lung model was generated and calibrated to reproduce the individual respiratory system mechanics. Model predictions of tidal volume, airway and transpulmonary pressures, end-expiratory lung volume (EELV), and electrical impedance tomography (EIT)-derived regional ventilation distribution were simulated for different PEEP levels and evaluated against clinically assessed reference values. Model predictions were compared to clinical data using Pearson correlation coefficients (r), root mean square error (RMSE), and Bland-Altman analyses. RESULTS: A strong agreement was observed between simulated and clinical data for tidal volumes (r = 0.925, p < 0.001, RMSE = 0.053 l) and driving pressures (r = 0.940, p < 0.001, RMSE = 1.328 mbar) across all PEEP levels. At initial PEEP level, a high image correlation (r > 0.8) was found between measured and simulated regional ventilation in five of seven patients where EIT data were available. CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study demonstrates the capability of the individualized, regionally resolved physics-based computational lung model to reproduce patient-specific respiratory mechanics and key features of regional ventilation patterns in ARDS. The strong agreement between simulated and measured data supports the potential of this approach to estimate the physiological response to ventilator adjustments and lays the groundwork for future studies integrating computational modeling into clinical decision-making. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Registered at the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00017151, https://drks.de/search/en/trial/DRKS00017151 ) at 12th April 2019.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Watchful waiting (WW) for inguinal hernia has been established as a safe strategy for selected patients. However, this approach relies on regular long-term follow-up and adherence rates to WW are poorly characterized. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed including patients with inguinal hernia enrolled in a WW surveillance protocol between May 2013 and May 2026. Follow-up visits were scheduled every 6 months during the first year and annually thereafter. Demographic, clinical, and long-term adherence to surveillance protocols were analyzed Patients who were lost to follow-up were contacted via a structured questionnaire to update their clinical status and identify causes for discontinuing protocol. RESULTS: A total of 400 patients were included in the WW protocol. Overall follow-up adherence was low, with 240 patients (60.0%) failing to maintain scheduled surveillance at the end of this study. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated a progressive drop out of the protocol over time. Younger age was an independent factor associated with follow-up discontinuation. Patients younger than 30 years demonstrated the highest rate of surveillance discontinuation (92.9%), compared with 63.6% among patients aged 30-50 years and 56.4% among patients older than 50 years (p = 0.015). Seventy-seven (32%) responded to the survey; the most frequent causes for discontinuation were the absence of symptoms and the lack of awareness of recommended follow-up intervals (36% and 27%, respectively). Eleven patients (14.1%) had an elective hernia repair at another institution. No emergency surgery was identified among patients who remained under institutional follow-up or among those successfully contacted after surveillance discontinuation. CONCLUSIONS: Watchful waiting appears to remain an acceptable management strategy for selected patients with asymptomatic or oligosymptomatic inguinal hernia. However, long-term adherence to surveillance beyond 2 years is low, posing a significant limitation to sustained WW management.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Intraoperative indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence cholangiography has been linked to fewer conversions to open surgery in emergency cholecystectomy, but it adds cost, and evidence for its effect on conversion and operative time is graded moderate to low even by the consensus statement recommending routine use. We asked whether preoperative C-reactive protein (CRP), a marker of surgical difficulty and conversion risk, identifies patients in whom ICG's benefit is greatest. METHODS: Prospective cohort of 221 patients undergoing emergency laparoscopic cholecystectomy for acute cholecystitis, stratified by ICG use (85 ICG vs 136 conventional). We tested the interaction between CRP and ICG use on conversion using Firth penalized logistic regression, and on operative time, length of stay, and complications using linear/logistic regression with a log-CRP sensitivity analysis. We compared conversion rates across CRP tertiles and calculated a CRP-stratified estimated absolute risk reduction (ARR) and number needed to treat (NNT). RESULTS: Conversion occurred only in the conventional arm (12/136, 8.8%; 0/85 ICG), rising from 0 to 15.4% across CRP tertiles. The formal CRP×ICG interaction for conversion was not significant (Firth model, p = 0.878), reflecting the absence of ICG-arm events; the ARR associated with ICG use rose from not estimable to 9.8 points (95% CI 3.9-22.5; NNT≈10) in the middle tertile and 15.4 points (95% CI 8.0-27.5; NNT 6.5) in the highest. The interaction was significant for operative time (p = 0.045), strengthening under a log-CRP sensitivity model (p = 0.001), with CRP-related lengthening of surgery markedly smaller in the ICG arm. CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, ICG's clinical benefit was not uniform across the CRP range. The CRP×ICG interaction reached significance for operative time; for conversion, the pattern was consistent and clinically plausible but not statistically significant, and should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. A CRP-informed strategy for prioritising ICG may be worth testing prospectively.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lower rectal gastrointestinal stromal tumors (rGISTs) pose a surgical challenge, as complete resection must be balanced against anorectal function preservation. Transanal local excision (taLE) may offer a less invasive alternative to transabdominal laparoscopic radical resection (tlRR), but comparative evidence, particularly for larger tumors, is limited. METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study of patients with primary lower rGIST (lower tumor margin ≤ 5 cm from the anal verge; tumor size ≥ 2 cm and < 7 cm) undergoing taLE or tlRR (April 2015-April 2023). Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) balanced baseline characteristics, and doubly robust models adjusted residual imbalance. Perioperative outcomes, recurrence-free survival (RFS), and a prespecified ≥ 5 cm subgroup analysis were evaluated. RESULTS: Among 101 patients (taLE, n = 74; tlRR, n = 27; median follow-up, 40 months), IPTW-adjusted analyses showed significantly reduced surgical burden with taLE: shorter operative time (- 118.4 min, P < 0.001), lower postoperative pain (- 2.5, P < 0.001), earlier drain removal (- 5.1 days, P = 0.008), no permanent stoma (0/74 vs. 5/27), and lower odds of temporary stoma (OR 0.05, P < 0.001) and reoperation (OR 0.02, P = 0.009). These advantages remained largely consistent in the ≥ 5 cm subgroup. Only four recurrences occurred, with no significant RFS difference (log-rank P = 0.43); power was limited. CONCLUSIONS: taLE was associated with substantially reduced surgical burden in selected patients with lower rGIST, and no significant difference in recurrence-free survival was observed during available follow-up. However, with only four events, the study was underpowered to establish oncologic equivalence. The taLE-based organ-preserving pathway may represent a promising option pending confirmation in larger cohorts.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lateral pancreaticojejunostomy (LPJ) is the treatment of choice in patients with symptomatic wide-duct chronic pancreatitis and a normal-size pancreatic head. Adequate pain control in the first days after LPJ via laparotomy is often challenging in these patients due to opioid tolerance resulting from chronic opioid use. Although a robotic approach may improve short-term outcome, comparative multicenter data on robotic versus open LPJ are lacking. METHODS: This nationwide multicenter retrospective cohort study included consecutive adults who underwent robotic or open LPJ for symptomatic wide-duct chronic pancreatitis in the Netherlands (2010-2025). Primary outcomes were hospital stay and major complications (Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher). RESULTS: Overall, 133 patients undergoing LPJ were included, of whom 36 (27%) robotic and 97 (73%) open LPJ. The robotic LPJ conversion rate was 0% (0/36). In the overall cohort, 90-day mortality was 0% (0/133) and median hospital stay was 2 days shorter after robotic LPJ (5 [IQR, 4-7] vs 7 [6-10] days; P < 0.001) compared with open LPJ, while the rate of major complications did not differ significantly between groups (36.1% [13/36] vs 26.8% [26/97]; P = 0.405). Blood loss was less with robotic LPJ (100 [IQR, 50-100] vs 300 [125-500] mL; P < 0.001), whereas operative time was comparable (275 [IQR 180-330] vs 232 [188-276] minutes; P = 0.210), and the rate of postoperative pancreatic fistula (POPF) grade B/C was higher (22.2% [8/36] vs 7.2% [7/97]; P = 0.034). The main findings of the overall cohort remained broadly consistent after propensity score matching. CONCLUSIONS: In this early nationwide experience, robotic LPJ was associated with shorter hospital stay compared with open LPJ. Although operative time and major complications did not differ significantly between groups, POPF occurred more frequently after robotic LPJ. The potential benefits of robotic LPJ and the possible learning curve effect should be further assessed in randomized trials in experienced centers.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the long-term efficacy and safety of bilateral R2 sympathetic surgery for CFH, to characterize the 10-year longitudinal trajectory of postoperative CH and recurrence, and to identify clinically accessible predictors of CH and postoperative satisfaction that may assist in preoperative risk communication. Preliminary nomograms were developed and internally validated using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration plots, sensitivity, and specificity. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 127 patients who underwent bilateral R2 sympathetic surgery for CFH between April 2013 and April 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. Baseline characteristics, operative details, and follow-up outcomes were extracted from medical records and structured telephone interviews. Predictive features were selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Cox proportional hazards and multivariate logistic regression models were subsequently applied to identify independent predictors of CH and satisfaction, respectively. Nomograms were developed and internally validated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots, sensitivity, and specificity. RESULTS: All patients achieved immediate resolution of craniofacial sweating, accompanied by a significant postoperative heart rate reduction (84.8 ± 11.68 → 72.17 ± 7.54 bpm, P < 0.001). Severe CH (grade IV) developed in 70.1% of patients, predominantly involving the thoracoabdominal (84.3%) and thigh (54.3%) regions. Cox regression identified preoperative heart rate > 79.5 bpm (HR = 2.46, 95% CI 1.61-3.75, P = 0.0002) and sympathetic clamping (HR = 5.69, 95% CI 3.03-10.67, P = 0.001) as independent risk factors for severe CH. Logistic regression showed that lower preoperative thoracoabdominal sweating was associated with higher postoperative satisfaction (OR = 0.05, 95% CI 0.01-0.23, P = 0.001). The nomograms demonstrated adequate discrimination and calibration. CONCLUSION: Bilateral R2 sympathetic surgery achieves rapid and durable relief of craniofacial hyperhidrosis with sustained high satisfaction over 10 years. Beyond confirming efficacy, the extended follow-up uniquely demonstrates that CH severity stabilizes within the first postoperative year and does not worsen over time-a critical finding for patient reassurance. Preoperative resting heart rate > 79.5 bpm and the use of sympathetic clamping independently predict severe CH, whereas lower baseline thoracoabdominal sweating predicts superior satisfaction. Although the proposed nomograms require external validation before routine adoption, they offer a practical, individualized reference for preoperative risk communication and, combined with the intraoperative choice of electrocautery, support a dual-phase strategy for optimizing surgical outcomes in CFH patients.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Neurofilament light chain (NfL) is an established biomarker for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). However, it remains unclear whether biomarkers reflecting amyloid-β metabolism (Aβ), tau (phosphorylated tau, pTau), and astrogliosis (glial fibrillary acidic protein, GFAP) can complement NfL in clinical applications. It is also unclear how Alzheimer's disease (AD) co-pathology affects disease progression in ALS. METHODS: We studied 264 patients with ALS and 164 disease-control participants, analysing baseline cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) NfL, Aβ peptides, pTau181, pTau217, and GFAP. A two-step diagnostic strategy was examined in individuals with intermediate NfL values, using machine-learning models. Prognostic associations were evaluated using linear mixed-effects and Cox models adjusted for established predictors; survival was additionally examined in pooled analyses including an external ALS cohort (n = 153). FINDINGS: Patients with ALS exhibited higher CSF NfL, Aβ38, Aβ40, Aβ42, pTau181, and pTau217 than controls, even within Aβ-negative subgroups. NfL discriminated ALS from controls with an AUC of 0.85 (0.82-0.88), which increased to 0.90 (0.88-0.92) in machine-learning models incorporating additional biomarkers. The machine-learning models maintained a high positive predictive value (0.90) for classifying cases with intermediate NfL values. Significant Aβ × NfL interactions were observed for longitudinal functional decline, and pooled survival analyses showed stronger associations between NfL and survival in the Aβ-positive ALS subgroup (14%) than in the Aβ-negative ALS subgroup (HR 4.02 [2.17-7.45] vs 1.62 [1.36-1.92]). INTERPRETATION: Multiple biomarker assessments can reduce misclassification of individuals with intermediate NfL values. CSF Aβ positivity modified the association between baseline NfL and disease progression. Personalised diagnosis and prognosis based on fine-grained co-pathology evaluation may enhance clinical management of ALS. FUNDING: This study was primarily supported by JST SPRING (JPMJSP2125). A complete list of funding organisations is provided in Acknowledgements.

papers.abstract_en: The use of medical real-world data is constrained by fragmented data infrastructures and the absence of tools integrating longitudinal clinical with molecular data at scale. Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), the most common monogenic cause of kidney failure, exemplifies this gap given its phenotypic complexity and the need for individualized treatment decisions. We present MEDA-PKD (MEdical DAta translation service of Polycystic Kidney Disease), an interactive, near-real-time analytics platform that integrates clinical routine with research data from the German AD(H)PKD Tolvaptan Registry (NCT02497521, DRKS00008910) into a harmonized database ( https://doi.org/10.18716/adpkd_registry ). MEDA-PKD provides automated near-real-time analysis and dynamic visualization, replacing traditional static approaches to clinical cohorts. As of March 2026, MEDA-PKD visualized data from 1735 patients (mean follow-up 796 days). eGFR slope analysis of data from patients initiating tolvaptan therapy (332 patients) demonstrates the platform's capacity to evaluate real-world therapeutic impact in real-time. Other tabs include family history, medication, lifestyle, quality of life and a wide array of lab values (20,894 entries). Besides, MEDA-PKD integrates proteomics data and allows for secure individual patient-level data access. MEDA-PKD represents a paradigm shift by transforming static cohort data into a living, actionable knowledge resource in ADPKD and will serve as a template for other diseases.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Surgical site infections (SSIs) are common after emergency laparotomy and are associated with substantial morbidity, prolonged recovery, and increased health care costs. Negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) has been increasingly used prophylactically on closed incisions in high-risk surgical patients; however, evidence supporting its effectiveness after emergency laparotomy remains heterogeneous. This updated systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to reassess the effectiveness of NPWT compared with standard postoperative dressings for the prevention of SSI and other wound-related complications following emergency laparotomy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the Cochrane Handbook and PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for studies published from April 2, 2022, to December 10, 2025, updating a prior review. Randomized clinical trials and comparative observational studies evaluating NPWT versus standard dressings in adult patients undergoing emergency laparotomy were included. The primary outcome was SSI. Secondary outcomes included superficial and deep SSI, wound dehiscence, seroma, hematoma, and length of hospital stay. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I, and certainty of evidence was evaluated with GRADE. RESULTS: Twenty-three studies involving 5371 patients were included, of whom 2528 received NPWT. NPWT was associated with a significantly lower risk of SSI compared with standard dressings (risk ratio, 0.53; 95% CI 0.41-0.68), with moderate to substantial heterogeneity (I² = 68%). NPWT was also associated with reductions in superficial and deep SSI, seroma formation, and wound dehiscence, but not with organ/space SSI, hematoma, or length of hospital stay. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent direction of effect. Funnel plot asymmetry and a significant Egger test suggested small-study effects. CONCLUSION: Among patients undergoing emergency laparotomy, prophylactic NPWT applied to closed incisions was associated with a lower risk of SSI and several wound-related complications compared with standard postoperative dressings. However, the certainty of evidence remains very low due to heterogeneity, risk of bias, and small-study effects, highlighting the need for large pragmatic multicenter randomized trials to better define the magnitude of benefit and optimal patient selection.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: To investigate the preventive effects of personalized positioning management on hypoxemia during sedated endoscopic examination in elderly patients with esophageal cancer (EC). METHODS: A retrospective observational study was conducted. We retrospectively reviewed the medical records of elderly patients with esophageal cancer who underwent sedated gastroscopy between January 2023 and June 2024. Patients who received personalized positioning management were assigned to the intervention group (n = 67), while those who underwent conventional left lateral decubitus positioning were assigned to the control group (n = 67). The incidence of hypoxemia, lowest peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO₂), severe hypoxemic events, examination time, sedative dosage, comfort scores, and incidence of adverse events were compared between the two groups. Binary logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with hypoxemia. RESULTS: In the intervention group, the incidence of hypoxemia was significantly lower; the lowest SpO₂ was distinctly higher; and the incidences of severe hypoxemia and hypoxemic events requiring intervention were lower. Personalized positioning management was identified as an independent protective factor against hypoxemia. A higher American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status classification (Class III) was an independent risk factor for hypoxemia. The intervention group had a shorter examination time, lower propofol dosage, higher comfort scores, and a lower incidence of adverse events. CONCLUSION: Personalized positioning management effectively reduces both the incidence and severity of hypoxemia during sedated endoscopic examination in elderly patients with EC. This strategy demonstrates high clinical safety and feasibility.

papers.abstract_en: Tumor heterogeneity is a universal feature of cancer and may arise as early as precancer stages during lung adenocarcinoma evolution, yet the emergence of aggressive transcriptional programs remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated spatial transcriptomics with single-cell RNA sequencing to characterize inter- and intratumoral heterogeneity across hyperplasia, adenoma, and invasive adenocarcinoma (IAC) in a genetically engineered mouse model (129S4/Sv KrasLSL-G12D/+). Disease progression was accompanied by coordinated remodeling of epithelial, stromal, and immune compartments, along with dynamic changes in proliferation, immune response, and metabolic pathways. Notably, lesions of the same histological stage exhibited substantial transcriptional heterogeneity. By quantifying dedifferentiation states, we identified a subset of adenomas that had already diverged toward highly proliferative and metabolically active programs despite lacking invasive features. These lesions were further marked by early chromosome 6 amplification, whose corresponding human ortholog signature recapitulated aggressive proliferation-associated programs in early-stage human lung adenocarcinoma. Spatial analyses further revealed pronounced intratumoral heterogeneity within IAC, with tumor core regions showing increased proliferation and metabolism but reduced immune signaling compared to peripheral regions. In addition, immune checkpoint gene expression in T cells was transiently elevated at the hyperplasia stage, suggesting early immune modulation prior to overt malignancy. Together, these findings indicate that aggressive transcriptional divergence can emerge early during lung adenocarcinoma evolution and that spatial organization critically shapes tumor and immune programs before and after invasion.

papers.abstract_en: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) replace selected scalar weights or fixed activations with learnable univariate edge functions. We conducted a controlled retrospective evidence reconstruction and update of Crossref, Europe PMC, arXiv, and OpenAlex, supplemented by local full texts and citation tracking, for studies published from January 2024 to February 2026. After report-level screening and version consolidation, 138 independent medical-imaging studies met explicitly defined medical-imaging eligibility criteria (127 direct imaging inputs; 11 image-derived representations). Studies were classified by primary KAN placement - backbone, bottleneck/token, physics-informed or implicit representation, or task-specific head - and evaluated for task, modality, comparator, reported result, and evidence of a KAN-specific contribution. None met the strictest contribution-evidence standard of a complete resource-controlled factorial comparison; 48 provided moderate, 46 weak/compound, and 44 insufficient evidence for the independent KAN contribution. Whole-model results were favorable in 68 studies, mixed or trade-off in 30, unfavorable or without incremental gain in 4, and indeterminate or not comparable in 36; these labels do not isolate the effect of KAN. External validation, calibration, repeated-run stability, and deployment metrics were inconsistently reported. The evidence supports KAN chiefly as a task-dependent module for controlled testing within established convolutional, Transformer, state-space, or physics-informed pipelines, rather than as a generally superior replacement. Priorities include matched ablations, function-stability analysis, external-center evaluation, and standardized resource reporting.

papers.abstract_en: Squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs) develop from the stratified epithelia of the esophagus, head and neck, lung, and skin, providing a tractable model to investigate how altered epithelial fields progress toward invasive cancer. Across SCC subtypes, evolution often begins before overt malignancy, with age- and exposure-associated mutant clones expanding within histologically normal epithelia. As lesions advance, early driver selection becomes coupled to copy number alterations, chromosomal instability, and epigenetic remodeling, whereas later stages are shaped by branching diversification, cellular plasticity, and regionally constrained selection. Despite tissue-specific differences, several recurrent principles emerge, including clonal expansion within mutated normal fields, transition bottlenecks marked by genome-scale instability, and the spatial organization of subclonal architecture and invasive-front states. In this review, we synthesize recent progress in the temporal ordering and spatial patterning of SCC evolution and discuss how genetic alterations, epigenetic remodeling, and tissue ecology jointly drive disease progression. We further highlight the implications for early interception, biomarker development, immune evasion, and evolution-informed prevention and therapy.

papers.abstract_en: Phage defense systems in bacteria exhibit high degrees of modularity, with sensing, signal transmission, and effector enzymes frequently exchanged among phage defense gene clusters. In this study, we capitalize on this modularity to discover phage defense systems by searching for defense-associated modules in new gene contexts across Pseudomonas aeruginosa genomes. This approach reveals a large and interconnected network of modular components distributed across diverse gene clusters. From over 500 candidate defense systems, we select five for experimental testing and validate three: Dionysus, a TerB-encoding system that interferes with early phage infection (EPI) vesicle formation by jumbo phages; Ophion, a radical S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM)-containing system that blocks progression from the EPI vesicle to the nucleus stage during jumbo phage infection; and Hercules, a tightly regulated restriction-modification (RM)-like system. Collectively, we demonstrate that leveraging the modular architecture of phage defense systems is an effective approach to their discovery.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Orofacial clefts, particularly cleft palate, are among the most common congenital anomalies, imposing substantial functional impairment and psychosocial burden on affected individuals. Emerging evidence implicates epigenetic modifications, especially histone lysine methylation, as critical regulators of embryonic development, yet their precise roles in palatogenesis remain poorly defined. The H3K4 methyltransferase complexes, which require the core subunit ASH2L for full enzymatic activity, govern transcriptional activation during development; however, whether ASH2L-mediated H3K4me3 deposition contributes to palatal morphogenesis is unknown. RESULTS: Here, we show that conditional deletion of Ash2l in Six2-positive palatal mesenchymal cells results in complete cleft palate in mice. Multi-omics analyses (RNA-seq and CUT&Tag-seq) reveal that Ash2l loss causes genome-wide reduction of H3K4me3 enrichment at key developmental genes, most notably Wnt5b, leading to their transcriptional downregulation. Functionally, Ash2l deficiency impairs proliferation and osteogenic differentiation of palatal mesenchymal cells, resulting in stunted palatal shelf growth and disrupted osteogenesis. Pharmacological activation of WNT signaling downstream of Wnt5b partially rescues these cellular defects, confirming the functional relevance of this axis. CONCLUSION: These findings establish ASH2L-mediated H3K4me3 as a critical epigenetic regulator of palatal development through WNT5B modulation, and identify potential therapeutic targets for cleft palate.

papers.abstract_en: Mycobacterium abscessus (Mab) is a rapidly growing non-tuberculous mycobacterium that causes opportunistic infections and exhibits extensive intrinsic antibiotic resistance. The proline-glutamate (PE) and proline-proline-glutamate (PPE) protein families are mycobacteria-specific virulence factors implicated in immune modulation, antigenic variation, and persistence. While Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) harbors approximately 170 PE/PPE members, the repertoire of PE/PPE genes in Mab remains largely uncharacterized. Here, we performed a genome-wide survey of PE/PPE genes in Mab ATCC 19,977 and identified 18 candidate family members, representing a relatively small fraction of the genome compared with slow-growing mycobacteria. Most predicted proteins harbor canonical PE or PPE domains and display acidic physicochemical properties. Phylogenetic analysis resolved the proteins into three subfamilies: PE, PPE, and PE-PPE, revealing moderate structural diversity but limited family expansion. Motif and gene structure analyses supported the evolutionary conservation. Notably, no PE_polymorphic GC-rich repetitive sequence (PE_PGRS) or PPE_major polymorphic tandem repeat (PPE_MPTR) members were detected, suggesting lineage-specific genomic reduction relative to other pathogenic mycobacteria. AlphaFold predictions revealed conserved N-terminal folds and variable C-terminal regions, which may contribute to functional diversification. Subcellular localization predictions indicated that most proteins are extracellular. Synteny analysis revealed no detectable collinearity among these genes. Transcriptomic analyses revealed condition-dependent expression of PE/PPE genes during amoeba and macrophage infection and under artificial sputum medium and metal ion stress, suggesting roles in environmental adaptation and host interaction. This study provides the first systematic overview of PE/PPE gene repertoire in Mab and lays the groundwork for elucidating their roles in intracellular survival, host interaction, and antimicrobial resistance.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Addressing tumor heterogeneity in breast cancer research is crucial, given the distinct subtypes like triple-negative, luminal A/B, and HER2, requiring precise differentiation for effective treatment. This study introduces a non-invasive method by analyzing post-translationally modified proteins in plasma extracellular vesicles, which play a role in immune regulation and intercellular communication. Examining modifications like phosphorylation, acetylation and glycosylation in extracellular vesicles provides insights into breast cancer dynamics. One hundred and one plasma samples from luminal A/B breast cancer, triple-negative breast cancer and healthy individuals underwent discovery and validation experiments. RESULT: The study identified over 28,000 unique non-modified peptides, 5,000 phosphopeptides, 680 acetyl peptides and 1,300 glycopeptides that are successfully characterized. Bioinformatics analyses revealed significant overexpression of 815 non-modified proteins, 3,958 phosphopeptides, 352 acetyl peptides and 895 glycopeptides in luminal A/B breast cancer or triple-negative breast cancer subtypes. Phosphorylated and glycosylated PD-L1 peptides emerge as potential markers for breast cancer, regardless of subtype. Aligning the findings with literature and PAM50 gene signatures highlights markers correlated with lower survival rates. The study also reports 123 scheduled parallel reaction monitoring analyses, leveraging machine learning to pinpoint a panel of specific modification sites with high accuracy for subtype differentiation. CONCLUSIONS: This research reveals diagnostic markers and enhances understanding of the molecular landscape, contributing to more effective and personalized breast cancer diagnostics and treatments.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Breast milk (BM) is a complex biological system that not only delivers essential nutrition to the baby, but is also a rich collection of microorganisms, including bacteria, viruses and fungi. Dominated by bacteriophages and eukaryotic viruses, the BM virome plays a role in shaping the infant gut microbiome composition, influencing immune development and long-term health outcomes. Emerging research confirms the vertical transmission of bacteriophages from the mother to her infant via breastfeeding, and the shared viral taxa suggest functional roles in modulating bacterial populations and maintaining gut homeostasis. Disruptions in this early life virome, driven by factors such as maternal health, mode of delivery, and geographic location, have been linked to dysbiosis and disease susceptibility for conditions ranging from inflammatory bowel disease to metabolic disorders. METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in NCBI/PUBMED and the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) using the keywords "Milk virome," "Milk phage," "Milk phageome," and "Milk metagenome". After applying our inclusion and exclusion criteria, two studies remained. This comparative analysis explores the composition and diversity of the BM virome across two geographically distinct cohorts-Turkey and the United States-revealing significant differences in viral diversity and composition. RESULTS: The Turkish cohort exhibited a significantly higher viral richness and unique taxonomic distributions compared to the USA group. Notably, bacteriophage families like Myoviridae, Siphoviridae, and Podoviridae were shown to be abundant in both populations. The Turkish BM virome featured a higher prevalence of plant- and insect-derived viruses (e.g. Partitiviridae, Tospoviridae), likely tied to dietary or regional agricultural practices. CONCLUSIONS: Despite limitations related to sample size and methodological variability, this study emphasizes how dietary habits, environmental exposures, and geographic location may shape the breast milk virome. Further research integrating longitudinal data from a multi-ethnic population, cohorts is essential to fully harness the diagnostic and therapeutic potential of the human milk virome.

papers.abstract_en: The etiology of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) remains unknown, and therapeutic interventions are currently restricted. The activation of lung fibroblasts and the focal adhesion kinase (FAK) signaling pathway are crucial to the pathogenesis of IPF, yet the exact molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Our study shows that the deleted in lymphocytic leukemia 2 (DLEU2) is elevated in the peripheral blood of patients with IPF, as well as in the lung tissues of mice with pulmonary fibrosis. Functional assays revealed that overexpression of DLEU2 facilitated fibrogenesis, whereas its suppression attenuated lung fibrosis in vivo and impeded fibroblast activation in vitro, predominantly through the regulation of FAK phosphorylation. Mechanistically, our findings reveal that DLEU2 regulates lung fibroblast activation by targeting miR-29a-3p. Conversely, inhibition of miR-29a-3p reversed the anti-fibrotic effects observed upon DLEU2 knockdown. Furthermore, DLEU2 was shown to directly interact with FAK, enhancing its phosphorylation and thereby facilitating fibrogenesis; inhibition of FAK phosphorylation counteracted the pro-fibrotic effects induced by DLEU2 overexpression. Taken together, these findings clarify the function of DLEU2 in facilitating FAK phosphorylation via its interactions with miR-29a-3p and FAK. The findings of this study suggest that DLEU2 may serve as a novel diagnostic biomarker and a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of IPF.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Tumor-associated macrophages in colorectal cancer predominantly exhibit an immunosuppressive M2 phenotype that contributes to tumor progression and resistance to immune checkpoint inhibition. Repolarizing M2 macrophages toward a proinflammatory M1 phenotype represents a promising immunotherapeutic strategy. While interferon-γ promotes M1 macrophage activation, the effect of combining interferon-γ with granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor remains underexplored. METHODS: THP-1-derived M2-like macrophages were treated with interferon-γ (0-500 ng/mL) and granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (0-1,000 ng/mL) in a dose-matrix experiment (n = 4). M1 and M2 markers and programmed cell death-ligand 1 were quantified by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction at 24 hours. Secreted interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-α, and interleukin-10 were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. HT-29 colorectal cancer cells were treated with macrophage-conditioned media and assessed for E-cadherin, N-cadherin, vimentin, and Ki-67. Statistical analyses included t tests and analysis of variance. RESULTS: Interferon-γ strongly induced M1 gene expression, whereas granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor alone demonstrated modest effects. Combined interferon-γ (50 ng/mL) and granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (500 ng/mL) amplified interleukin-6, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 10, and tumor necrosis factor-α gene expression 5.4-fold, 2.9-fold, and 3.1-fold, respectively, beyond interferon-γ alone. Two-way analysis of variance showed no significant interaction, suggesting additive rather than synergistic enhancement. Combination treatment increased the secretion of interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor-α and reduced interleukin-10. Conditioned media from combination-treated macrophages increased E-cadherin and reduced N-cadherin, vimentin, and Ki-67 in HT-29 cells. CONCLUSION: Granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor augments interferon-γ-driven proinflammatory macrophage responses with protein-level changes and functional effects on colorectal cancer cells. The resulting macrophage secretome was associated with a less mesenchymal, less proliferative colorectal cancer-cell phenotype. Concurrent programmed cell death-ligand 1 upregulation provides a preclinical rationale for evaluating cytokine-mediated macrophage reprogramming in combination with programmed cell death protein 1/programmed cell death-ligand 1 checkpoint blockade in colorectal cancer.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Older adults present unique challenges in emergency general surgery (EGS) due to increased comorbidities and frailty. While minimally invasive surgery (MIS), including laparoscopic (lap) and robotic techniques, reduces perioperative morbidity, the role of minimally invasive EGS in geriatric patients remains unclear. This study compares outcomes for geriatric EGS patients following robotic, lap, and open procedures. We hypothesize that MIS approaches would improve perioperative outcomes in geriatric patients. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of the ACS-NSQIP database (2022-2023) including patients ≥65 years undergoing emergent or urgent intra-abdominal surgery. Operative approach was categorized as robotic, lap, or open. The primary outcome was severe complication, and secondary outcomes included length of stay (LOS), discharge disposition, and readmission. RESULTS: 58,940 patients were included: 1832 robotic, 30,137 lap, and 26,971 open. With robotic vs lap and open, operative time was shortest (82.5 vs 110 vs 96 min, p < 0.001), conversion to open was less frequent (6.2 vs 12.9%, p < 0.001), and LOS was shorter (4 vs 4 vs 8 days, p < 0.001). Readmission and reoperation were lowest following MIS (9.2 vs 7.9 vs 9.8%, and 3.7 vs 3.3% vs 7.6%, both p < 0.001). After propensity matching, robotic patients had higher ASA scores and more transfusions but lower rates of sepsis (2.6 vs 6.5%) and mortality (2.3 vs 2.7%) compared to the lap group (p < 0.001). Multivariable regression demonstrated decreased risk of severe complications for patients who underwent robotic surgery (p = 0.025) with no difference in operative time or LOS, and patients were more likely to be discharged home. CONCLUSIONS: Robotic EGS in geriatric patients is associated with fewer severe complications, lower conversion rates, shorter LOS, and favorable discharge disposition.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Diverse representation in clinical research is essential for equitable healthcare. Despite mandates from organizations like the NIH and ICMJE, race and gender remain underreported in surgical research, raising concerns about the generalizability of findings. This study examines demographic reporting trends in minimally invasive surgery (MIS) and advanced endoscopy publications before and after the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic. METHODS: A systematic review of Surgical Endoscopy, Journal of Robotic Surgery, and Surgical Innovation was conducted, analyzing articles published between January 1, 2018, and December 31, 2023. 472 studies were included. For each study, study type, journal, date, geographic origin, and reported demographic data were recorded. Reporting rates across time periods (pre- vs. post-March 2020), region of origin, study design, and journal were analyzed via Chi-square, Fisher's exact tests, and Cochran-Armitage trend tests. RESULTS: Of the 472 studies, 61.2% were randomized controlled trials, with geographic representation from Asia (37.7%), Europe (34.8%), and North America (22.3%). Only 21 North American studies (20 U.S., 1 Canada) reported race; no studies from Asia or Europe did so. Among U.S. studies, race reporting did not differ significantly pre- vs. post-COVID (22.2% vs. 21.8%; p = 0.25), nor did gender reporting (p = 0.07). Regional differences in U.S. race reporting were significant (p = 0.003), with the Midwest having the lowest rate. Post-2020, gender reporting was significantly higher in Asia (94.9%) compared to Europe (84.7%) and North America (80.9%) (p = 0.005). CONCLUSIONS: Demographics remain underreported in MIS and advanced endoscopy research, particularly outside North America. Despite increased attention to health equity during the COVID-19 pandemic, reporting practices have not significantly improved. Broader adoption of standardized demographic reporting is needed to ensure evidence-based surgical care for all populations.
