papers.abstract_en: Stimulation of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) that couple to Gi/o leads to the activation of G protein-activated inward rectifier K+ (GIRK) channels and membrane hyperpolarization in excitable cells. GIRK channel availability can determine the success of optogenetic silencing strategies based on Gi/o-coupled GPCRs. To selectively enhance Gi/o-mediated GIRK currents, we created expression cassettes that coupled the activity of a GIRK subunit to the light-activated Gi/o-coupled GPCRs Opn4L (an opsin also known as melanopsin), longwave-sensitive opsin Opn1, parapinopsin, or Opn7b. We used the GIRK1 F137S mutant because of its fast activation, generation of large currents, and formation of homomeric channels, which reduced the size of the expression cassette. We demonstrated that light-mediated activation of GIRK1F137S through the opsins induced robust GIRK currents in HEK293 cells, cardiomyocytes, and cerebellar Purkinje neurons. Moreover, coupling GIRK1F137S activation to the promiscuous Opn4L changed the net effect of G protein signaling from Gq/11-mediated excitation to Gi/o-mediated inhibition in cerebellar Purkinje neurons and cardiomyocytes. Thus, our tools optimize the use of GIRK activity in the optogenetic control of the Gi/o pathway in excitable cells.

papers.abstract_en: m5C, an important RNA modification, is closely associated with breast cancer; however, their causal relationship is unknown. We examined the relationship between m5C regulation and breast cancer. Genome-wide association study breast cancer data and expression quantitative trait loci of m5C regulatory factor genes in blood were collected. We explored the causal relationship among m5C regulatory genes, breast cancer susceptibility, and prognosis through Mendelian randomization. Single-cell RNA sequencing data from peripheral blood mononuclear cells of patients with breast cancer and healthy controls were used to determine the differential expression of key genes among different cellular subpopulations. The effects of these genes on specific cellular subpopulations were further explored in single-cell RNAseq data from primary breast cancer using cellular communication, metabolic and cellular function analyses and validated the findings using flow cytometry. We validated the prognostic value of specific cellular subpopulations expressing key genes and assessed the impact of antitumor immunity using spatial transcriptomics, bulk transcriptomics, and immunofluorescence analysis of tissue microarray (120 patients). Mendelian randomization analysis indicated that the expression of the m5C writer tRNA aspartate methyltransferase 1 (TRDMT1) in blood was associated with breast cancer prognosis. TRDMT1 expression in T cells was decreased in patients with breast cancer. TRDMT1 was closely related to T-cell function. Moreover, it may modulate the antitumor immune effects of CD8+ T cells by influencing cellular communication and metabolism, impacting the prognosis and immunotherapeutic response of patients with breast cancer. We confirmed the immunotherapy predict value and prognostic value of measuring TRDMT1 levels in CD8+ T cells, provided insights into enhancing CD8+ T-cell function, and identified potential targets to improve breast cancer prognosis and immunotherapy. Our research may help guide breast cancer treatment decisions and provide a prognostic evaluation option for future breast cancer treatment.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Perforation peritonitis is one of the most common surgical emergencies encountered in clinical practice and is associated with considerable morbidity and mortality. Prognostic scoring systems are important for predicting outcomes, guiding management strategies and facilitating surgical audits. The Mannheim Peritonitis Index (MPI) is a widely used intraoperative scoring system, while the Mansoura Scoring System (MSS) is a newer model based on preoperative inflammatory parameters. The aim of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of MPI and MSS in predicting mortality and postoperative complications in patients with perforation peritonitis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A prospective observational cohort study was conducted in the Department of Surgery at Jawaharlal Nehru Medical College, Aligarh Muslim University. A total of 200 patients diagnosed with perforation peritonitis and undergoing surgical intervention were included. MPI and MSS scores were calculated for all patients. Patients were followed up for 30 days postoperatively to evaluate outcomes including mortality, postoperative complications and hospital stay. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 29. Diagnostic performance of the scoring systems was evaluated using Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. RESULTS: The mean age of patients ranged widely, with the highest proportion belonging to the 31-40 year age group. Males constituted 69.5% of the study population. The ileum was the most common site of perforation (56.5%), followed by gastric perforation (15%). Higher MPI and MSS scores were significantly associated with increased postoperative morbidity and mortality. MPI demonstrated higher specificity in predicting mortality, whereas MSS showed comparable sensitivity and allowed earlier preoperative risk assessment. CONCLUSION: Both MPI and MSS are effective prognostic tools for predicting outcomes in perforation peritonitis. While MPI has a better discriminatory ability for predicting mortality due to its incorporation of intraoperative findings, MSS offers the advantage of early preoperative risk stratification using simple laboratory parameters.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: We assessed contemporaneous changes in gastric adenocarcinoma incidence, presentation, registry-recorded treatment, and survival. METHODS: Two complementary analyses used Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) 17 data. Incidence during 2000-2023 was analyzed using Joinpoint regression. A clinical cohort diagnosed during 2004-2023 at prespecified stomach subsites (C16.1-C16.6, C16.8, and C16.9) was compared across four periods. Surgery trends were decomposed into stage-composition and within-stage components. Outcomes included overall survival (OS), cause-specific survival (CSS), and 36-month restricted mean survival time (RMST); adjusted Cox models separately summarized associations over 0-60 months. RESULTS: The clinical cohort comprised 66,391 tumor records from 66,025 patients. Incidence declined during 2000-2019 (annual percent change, -1.32%; 95% CI, -1.61% to -1.08%) and increased during 2019-2023 (4.96%; 95% CI, 2.51-9.91%). Comparing 2004-2008 with 2019-2023, distant-stage disease increased from 36.1% to 43.0%, whereas surgery among records with known surgery status decreased from 51.9% to 36.3%. Stage-composition change represented 25.7% of the surgery decline. Recorded chemotherapy increased from 35.7% to 54.4%. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) is a frequent and clinically relevant complication in patients with lymphoma treated with anthracyclines. Early identification of subclinical myocardial injury is critical to prevent progression to overt heart failure and to avoid chemotherapy dose reductions that may compromise oncologic outcomes. We aimed to evaluate the role of cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) with T1 mapping and feature-tracking myocardial strain, in comparison with transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) and circulating biomarkers, for the early detection of CTRCD in lymphoma patients receiving anthracycline-based chemotherapy. METHODS: In this prospective, single-center observational study, forty-nine adult patients with lymphoma scheduled for anthracycline-based chemotherapy underwent serial assessment of high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT), NT-proBNP, TTE, and CMR at baseline (visit 0), after the third chemotherapy cycle (visit 1), and at chemotherapy completion (visit 2). TTE was repeated at 12-month follow-up (visit 3). CMR included cine imaging, T1 mapping with extracellular volume (ECV) quantification, late gadolinium enhancement, and feature-tracking strain analysis (global longitudinal [GLS], circumferential [GCS], and radial [GRS] strain). CTRCD was defined and graded according to the 2022 ESC Cardio-Oncology Guidelines. RESULTS: The median age of patients was 46 (29.5-62) years; 53.1% were female. The mean cumulative doxorubicin dose was 295 ± 57 mg/m². hs-cTnT levels increased progressively from baseline (0.006 ± 0.005 ng/mL) to visit 2 (0.022 ± 0.016 ng/mL; p < 0.001), while NT-proBNP did not change significantly (p = 0.086). TTE showed a significant decline in LVEF by the Simpson method (62.92 ± 5.61% to 60.23 ± 5.41%; p = 0.037) and progressive worsening of GLS (- 19.84 ± 2.35% to - 18.31 ± 2.73%; p = 0.001). CMR-derived LVEF also declined (61.98 ± 6.08% to 57.34 ± 7.29%; p < 0.001), accompanied by significant deterioration of GLS, GCS, and GRS (p < 0.001 for all). CTRCD was identified in 7 patients (14.9%) by CMR and 5 (10.6%) by TTE (p = 0.625), with substantial agreement between modalities (κ = 0.619; p < 0.001). A relative GLS decline > 15% was observed by CMR in 34.1% of patients at visit 1 and 43.9% at visit 2, exceeding the corresponding TTE-detected rates (15.2% and 18.6%). CONCLUSIONS: CMR-derived strain identified myocardial functional abnormalities during anthracycline therapy. Whether these abnormalities represent earlier manifestations of clinically relevant cardiotoxicity requires confirmation in larger prospective studies with longer follow-up.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Complicated disease affects a substantial proportion of pediatric Crohn's disease (CD) patients and leads to surgery. A subset of children requires intestinal resection shortly after diagnosis. Several risk factors for surgery are known; however, the predictors of these early resections have not been well defined. We aimed to characterize this patient group and identify risk factors associated with early intestinal resections. METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of patients under 18 y diagnosed with CD between 2010 and 2019, based on the Hungarian Pediatric inflammatory bowel disease Registry. We compared those patients who underwent intestinal resection within 6 mo after diagnosis (very early surgery group, VES) with those who did not require resection within 6 mo. Descriptive statistics and logistic regressions were used for the analysis. RESULTS: Out of 1040 newly diagnosed pediatric CD patients, 27 (2.6%) underwent intestinal resection within 6 mo of diagnosis. The mean age of the two groups did not significantly differ. The proportion of females was significantly higher in the VES group (63.0% versus 42.3%, P = 0.03). Multivariate analysis identified abdominal pain without diarrhea (odds ratio [OR]: 5.59; P = 0.02) and higher pediatric CD activity index (OR: 1.05; P = 0.02) as risk factors for VES. Diagnostic delay (OR: 0.99; P = 0.74) and perianal involvement (OR 2.84; P = 0.12) were not predictive for VES. CONCLUSIONS: VES is rare in pediatric CD, with a possible female predominance. Higher pediatric CD activity index at diagnosis indicates greater risk for early surgery.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) counts respiratory events but not the depth or duration of accompanying desaturation. We examined AHI-ODI discordance (AHI minus oxygen desaturation index, ODI) and its associations with daytime symptom burden and prevalent cardiometabolic comorbidity. METHODS: Single-center retrospective cross-sectional study of 200 adults with OSA (January 2023-January 2025). Five indices (AHI, ODI, mean SpO2, T90 and AHI-ODI discordance) were examined; excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS; Epworth Sleepiness Scale ≥ 11) was the primary outcome. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, BMI and an AHI-ODI × sex interaction. RESULTS: The cohort was 77.5% male, median age 57 years (48.8-64.2). For EDS, AHI-ODI discordance showed the numerically highest AUC (0.639, p < 0.001), followed by T90 (0.627), and mean SpO2 and ODI (0.609 each); AHI was not significant (0.546, p = 0.264). No pairwise difference was significant. AHI-ODI discordance remained independently associated with EDS after adjustment (OR 1.04 per event/h, 95% CI 1.01-1.07, p = 0.008), with no significant sex interaction. Among secondary outcomes, T90 showed the highest AUCs for diabetes mellitus (0.644) and hypertension (0.615), and mean SpO2 for heart failure (0.608). No index discriminated against previous stroke or atrial fibrillation. CONCLUSIONS: AHI-ODI discordance was independently, but only modestly, associated with EDS, whereas oxygenation indices were related to prevalent cardiometabolic comorbidity. The discrimination was insufficient, and all reported cut-offs are exploratory. AHI-ODI discordance is not a measure of sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To evaluate the overall safety of stent placement for malignant superior or inferior vena cava (SVC/IVC) syndrome by assessing adverse events in a nationwide multicenter population. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Japanese Diagnosis Procedure Combination nationwide inpatient database. Patients who underwent stent placement for malignant superior or inferior vena cava (SVC/IVC) syndrome between April 2019 and March 2023 were included. The primary endpoint was the overall incidence of adverse events, which were identified using International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision codes. Secondary evaluations included patient characteristics, underlying malignancies, therapeutic interventions, 7-day mortality after stent placement, 30-day in-hospital mortality after admission, and comparisons between the SVC and IVC groups. RESULTS: This nationwide study included 301 patients from 137 hospitals, of whom 187 underwent SVC stenting, and 114 underwent IVC stenting. Overall, 34 adverse events occurred in 32 patients (10.6%). Red blood cell transfusion was required in 10 patients (3.3%), but no invasive treatment, including embolization, was required. Seven-day mortality after stenting was 5.0%, and 30-day in-hospital mortality after admission was 11.6%. In comparisons between the SVC and IVC groups, respiratory failure was more common after SVC stenting, whereas other adverse events and mortality were comparable between groups. Lung tumors predominated in SVC cases and liver tumors in IVC cases; multiple stents were used more frequently in IVC cases. CONCLUSION: Stent placement for malignant vena cava obstruction demonstrated an overall complication rate of 10.6% with no serious adverse events requiring invasive intervention.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary carcinoids generally have favorable outcomes after surgery, but postoperative recurrence differs substantially by histological subtype. Existing guidance recognizes atypical histology and nodal involvement as adverse features, yet a focused quantitative synthesis of the magnitude and consistency of this association remains limited. METHODS: MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, and Embase were searched from inception to July 12, 2026 for surgical cohorts reporting postoperative recurrence. Two reviewers independently screened titles and abstracts and assessed full-text eligibility, with disagreements resolved by consensus. The primary meta-analysis emphasized the risk ratio (RR) of observed recurrence in atypical versus typical carcinoids using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood and modified Hartung-Knapp intervals; odds ratios (ORs) and risk differences were complementary measures. Time-defined recurrence, adjusted prognostic factors, and anatomical patterns were synthesized separately because of incompatible outcome definitions and effect measures. RESULTS: Eighteen reports were included in the review, 11 contributed structured quantitative evidence, and 7 independent comparative cohorts entered the primary meta-analysis. Among 1074 resected tumors, recurrence occurred in 24 of 816 typical carcinoids and 51 of 258 atypical carcinoids. The pooled RR of observed recurrence was 6.57 (95% CI, 3.65-11.84), with a complementary OR of 8.08 (95% CI, 4.20-15.53). No statistical heterogeneity was detected (I2 = 0%), but this result was interpreted cautiously because only seven studies were available and clinically important differences in follow-up, staging, pathological review, and surveillance remained. Leave-one-out RR estimates ranged from 5.77 to 7.48. Time-defined evidence suggested recurrence of approximately 18%-25% by 5 years and 29%-32% by 10 years in atypical tumors, whereas node-negative typical tumors generally remained below 5% at 10 years, although late events occurred. Nodal involvement, advanced pT category, and larger tumor size were adverse prognostic features. CONCLUSION: Observed recurrence after resection was substantially more frequent in atypical than in typical pulmonary carcinoids. Histology and nodal status provide a clinically useful basis for postoperative risk stratification, but the available evidence does not establish the optimal surveillance modality, interval, or duration.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Evidence concerning gastrointestinal cancer risk after eosinophilic oesophagitis (EoE) diagnosis is limited. AIMS: To examine the association between EoE and incident gastrointestinal cancer in a population-based cohort. METHODS: Using nationwide Danish health registries, we identified all patients diagnosed with EoE between 1997 and 2024, using a validated algorithm. We computed standardised incidence ratios (SIRs) for gastrointestinal cancers overall and site-specific cancers compared with the general population. To distinguish short-term diagnostic activity from longer-term risk, we stratified analyses by < 1 and ≥ 1 year after EoE diagnosis. Secondary analyses examined oesophageal cancer incidence among EoE patients with coexisting Barrett's oesophagus (BE). RESULTS: Among 9115 EoE patients, 170 developed gastrointestinal cancers. During the first year after EoE diagnosis, the SIR was 2.83 (95% confidence interval: 2.10-3.74). Beyond 1 year, the overall SIR attenuated (1.03 [0.85-1.23]) but remained elevated for oesophageal cancer (2.40 [1.42-3.79]) and hepatocellular carcinoma (2.05 [0.98-3.77]). Among patients who developed oesophageal cancer ≥ 1 year after EoE diagnosis (n = 18), most had prior BE. The SIR for oesophageal cancer was 5.44 (2.90-9.31) among patients with both EoE and BE and 4.84 (4.36-5.37) among patients with BE alone. SIR for patients with EoE alone could not be reported due to the low number of cancer cases. CONCLUSIONS: One year after EoE diagnosis, oesophageal cancer and hepatocellular carcinoma rates remained elevated. Most oesophageal cancers occurred in patients with prior BE, suggesting that the association between EoE and oesophageal cancer may be mediated largely through BE.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: In Germany, inpatient hospital and rehabilitation facilities are two main settings for the delivery of cancer care. Epidemiology and demography are major forces that influence the need for care in these settings. This article examines the extent to which cancer incidence is associated with the use of inpatient and rehabilitative care. METHODS: Population-based estimates of cancer incidence and survival came from the German Center for Cancer Registry Data. Statistical data on inpatient and rehabilitative care came from the Federal Statistical Office. Analyses included annual numbers and rates of hospitalizations and rehabilitation cases, and joinpoint regression models of these cases in relation to incident case numbers covering the period 2003-2016. To calculate the ratio of rehabilitation cases to incident cases, the number of incident cases was adjusted for 1-year survival. RESULTS: The number of incident cancers increased from 2003 to 2016 (women: +9.6%; men: +7.0), whereas the difference in inpatient cases was far smaller (women -0.4%; men +4.5%). In 2016, there were 2.46 inpatient cases per incident case for women and 2.72 for men. This indicator varied: 1.87 for breast cancer (women only) and 3.33 for lung cancer (women and men). The estimated number of 1-year cancer survivors was 180,000 women and 185,900 men in 2016. The number of estimated cases in oncological rehabilitation per 100 1-year survivors among women increased from 59.2 (2003) to 65.2 (2010) and then decreased to 57.2 (2016). There was also an initial increase among men, from 50.8 (2003) to 51.5 (2008) and a subsequent decline to 46.9 (2016). CONCLUSIONS: Inpatient cases far exceed incident cases, which may reflect multiple hospitalizations for diagnostics and therapy of primary or recurring disease. The time trends of inpatient cases differ greatly from those of incident cases. This could be due to structural changes in the German health care system, such as possible shifts of services from the inpatient to the outpatient care sector. Regarding rehabilitation, the change in the trend of utilization has not been previously reported. Whether the ratio of rehabilitation cases to incidence indicates underuse of rehabilitative services cannot be assessed solely on the basis of the analyzed data.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To map the landscape of death anxiety regarding its conceptualization, prevalence, correlates, and management within both patients and caregivers. METHOD: We systematically searched PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Web of Science, Ovid Medline, Cochrane Library, CNKI and Wanfang from their inception to 5 January, 2026. This scoping review was conducted following the framework of Arksey and O'Malley and was reported in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Following the screening of abstracts and full-text articles, data were extracted and synthesized using an inductive thematic analysis. RESULTS: A total of 54 studies were included. Death anxiety is multidimensional, involving fear of one's own death and loss, with varied measurement tools. Contributing factors are demographic, disease-related, psychosocial, and relational. Consequences include psychological distress, reduced quality of life, and compromised caregiving or decisions. Individual therapies like Managing Cancer and Living Meaningfully are effective for patients, but integrated dyadic interventions are scarce. CONCLUSIONS: This scoping review demonstrates that death anxiety in advanced cancer is a multidimensional and relational phenomenon influencing both patients and caregivers. Recognizing death anxiety as a shared emotional burden highlights the need to move beyond individual-based interventions toward integrated dyadic approaches that address death anxiety. Embedding death anxiety management within holistic care models may enhance emotional adaptation and end-of-life quality. Continued research should refine theoretical frameworks and develop evidence-based strategies to mitigate the reciprocal impact of death anxiety across cancer patient-caregiver dyads.

papers.abstract_en: Intestinal fibrosis is a major complication of Crohn's disease, for which targeted therapies remain unavailable. Fibrosis is defined by excess matrix deposition, which may result from inadequate phagocytic clearance, yet how phagocytosis shifts here is unclear. Using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, we identify fibrosis-associated CD47hi fibroblasts coupled to SIRPAhi macrophages in fibrotic regions. Cell-cell communication analyses and neutralizing-antibody experiments identify interleukin-1β as a mediator of their crosstalk, forming a profibrotic niche characterized by phagocytic evasion. Genetic disruption of fibroblast Cd47 or macrophage Sirpa enhances fibroblast clearance and attenuates fibrosis. Mechanistically, checkpoint disruption reprograms macrophages toward an NRF2-associated pro-phagocytic state, linking enhanced clearance to the antifibrotic response. Furthermore, therapeutic antibody blockade of this checkpoint attenuates intestinal fibrosis in mouse models with schedule-dependent efficacy. Collectively, these findings support CD47-mediated phagocytic evasion as a key pathogenic mechanism in intestinal fibrosis and identify CD47-SIRPα blockade as a promising therapeutic target.

papers.abstract_en: Over the past few decades, the emergence of immunotherapy and single-target drugs has brought new promise to the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Yet the high heterogeneity of NSCLC leads to both primary and acquired resistance that neither sequential monotherapy nor empirical combinations can effectively overcome. In contrast to the conventional coadministration of two separate monoclonal antibodies, bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) feature a series of molecular engineering designs that confer inherent synergistic antitumor effects. We propose that a network pharmacology perspective can be adopted to understand the application of BsAbs in NSCLC and to guide their subsequent development.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Following Pennsylvania's motorcycle helmet law repeal, motorcycle collision (MCC) rates were fixed; however, injuries increased. We investigated post-repeal injury severity. We hypothesized helmeted (H) motorcyclists would have better outcomes than unhelmeted (UH) motorcyclists and outcomes would worsen post repeal. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed (7/1/1998-7/1/2023) MCC patients in the Pennsylvania Trauma Outcome Study database. We compared H and UH patients and Pre- and Post-repeal data (Pre:1998-2002; Post:2003-2023). Adolescent and geriatric subgroup analyses were performed. RESULTS: We included 36,943 patients: UH:14,069 and H:22,874. UH had higher ISS (p < 0.001), more severe head injuries (p < 0.001), and greater mortality (p < 0.001). Mortality was higher in UH geriatric motorcyclists (p < 0.001) and similar in adolescents (p = 0.129). Despite decreased helmet use post-repeal, ISS (p = 0.003), severe head injuries (p < 0.001) and mortality (p = 0.021) decreased. CONCLUSIONS: Overall, 62% of motorcyclists wore helmets. Although helmet use decreased post-repeal, outcomes were comparable. Decreased helmet use leaves motorists vulnerable to head injuries and worse outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Clinoid process pneumatization is a critical anatomical variation that influences surgical exposure and complication risks in skull base approaches. This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the pneumatization patterns of the anterior (ACP), middle (MCP), and posterior clinoid processes (PCP) and to determine the effects of age, sex, and nasal septal deviation (NSD) parameters, specifically angle severity and laterality, on these aeration patterns. METHODS: Computed tomography images of 250 adults (125 females, 125 males; aged 18-70 years) were retrospectively evaluated. Pneumatization patterns of the ACP and PCP were classified using a four-type grading system (Type 0-III). In addition, the presence of the MCP and its pneumatization status were evaluated. NSD was evaluated for laterality and angle severity (mild:<9°, moderate:9°-15°, severe:>15°). Statistical associations were assessed using chi-square tests and multivariate regression models. RESULTS: Type 0 (no pneumatization) predominated across all processes (ACP:81.8%, MCP:82.4%, PCP:82.6%), while Type III (total pneumatization) was rare (ACP:2.0%, PCP:2.2%). While univariate analysis showed age-related associations across all regions, multivariate logistic regression identified an independent association between age and ACP pneumatization, with younger individuals (18-34 years) exhibiting lower degrees of aeration (p < 0.01). Male sex was independently associated with bilateral MCP pneumatization (OR:3.016, p < 0.001) and right PCP pneumatization (OR:2.234, p = 0.032). Severe NSD angle (> 15°) was strongly associated with bilateral PCP pneumatization (p < 0.001) and higher-grade ACP aeration (p < 0.01). Furthermore, MCP presence showed strong ipsilateral clustering with ACP and PCP pneumatization patterns (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Clinoid process pneumatization demonstrates distinct anatomical associations with NSD angle severity, age, and sex. A severe NSD angle (> 15°) showed the strongest independent association with higher-grade pneumatization, particularly in the ACP and PCP, whereas NSD laterality was not independently associated with pneumatization. These findings support the inclusion of NSD angle severity in the radiological assessment of patients undergoing preoperative skull base CT, especially when extensive clinoid pneumatization may influence surgical planning.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pneumothorax is consistently reported as the most prevalent complication of computed tomography-guided transthoracic needle biopsy. While most cases of pneumothorax resolve with conservative management strategies, some cases are linked to a more protracted clinical trajectory necessitating active intervention. However, few reports have described the clinical and procedural determinants of prolonged hospitalization after post-biopsy pneumothorax. METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 1,457 CT-guided TTNB procedures performed at a tertiary referral center between January 2021 and December 2025. The incidence of post-biopsy pneumothorax was 20.5%. Among 82 patients with prolonged hospitalization due to pneumothorax, their management strategies were categorized into two groups: (1) high-concentration oxygen therapy (n = 54) and (2) invasive interventions, including percutaneous catheter drainage (PCD) or chest tube insertion (n = 28). Logistic regression models with backward selection were used to identify predictive factors for prolonged hospitalization. RESULTS: Among the 82 patients with prolonged hospitalization due to pneumothorax, the median age was 75 years and 75.6% were male. In multivariable analysis, a lower diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) was independently associated with prolonged hospitalization (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.980; P = 0.004). In the high-concentration oxygen group, lower DLCO (aOR, 0.974; P = 0.007) and a trans-fissural needle route (aOR, 3.968; P = 0.028) were independently associated with prolonged hospitalization. Conversely, in the PCD/chest tube group, reduced forced expiratory volume in 1 s was independently associated with prolonged hospitalization (aOR, 0.961; P = 0.002). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with post-biopsy pneumothorax, impaired pulmonary function may be linked to a prolonged clinical course. Incorporating these pre-procedural physiological markers may facilitate improved risk stratification and optimized hospital resource allocation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The optimal duration of abdominal drainage and bed rest after laparoscopic appendectomy (LA) remains uncertain. This study investigated whether these modifiable factors are associated with residual intra-abdominal infection (RII) and prolonged length of hospital stay (LOS). OBJECTIVE: To retrospectively analyze the risk factors for RII and prolonged LOS following LA and clarify the impact of abdominal drainage time and bed rest duration on postoperative recovery. METHODS: This retrospective study included 478 adults who underwent LA for acute appendicitis (2017-2020). Patients were followed weekly for 4 weeks. RII was defined as a composite endpoint occurring between postoperative day 5 and 4 weeks. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with RII and prolonged LOS (≥5 days). Subgroup analyses were exploratory due to small sample sizes. RESULTS: RII occurred in 59 patients (12.3%). In the overall cohort, independent factors for RII were complicated appendicitis (OR 4.35), drainage ≥36 h (OR 3.69), bed rest ≥24 h (OR 3.27), and Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) ≥6.64 (OR 3.18) (all P<0.05). Drainage <36 h was not associated with increased risk. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested drainage ≥36 h as the only factor for RII in uncomplicated appendicitis (OR 7.47), while bed rest ≥24 h (OR 7.21), elevated White blood cell count (WBC) (OR 4.65), and NLR (OR 6.02) were associated in complicated appendicitis. For prolonged LOS (198 events), independent factors were surgical complications (OR 6.14) and drainage ≥36 h (OR 4.74). Exploratory subgroup analyses showed surgical complications and drainage ≥36 h were significant in uncomplicated appendicitis, while only surgical complications remained in complicated appendicitis. CONCLUSION: Prolonged drainage (≥36 h) and bed rest (≥24 h) were associated with increased RII in the overall cohort; however, sensitivity analysis revealed variability in effect estimates, underscoring the need for cautious interpretation. Subgroup findings are exploratory and require confirmation. Prolonged drainage and surgical complications were associated with longer LOS. Drainage <36 h appeared safe. These findings suggest potential benefits of avoiding routine drainage, early drain removal, and early mobilization, but require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Neck dissection and adequate lymph node yield (LNY) are important in the treatment of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Cervical lymph nodes represent the primary sites for T-cell priming; however, the impact of LNY on the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) remains unclear. METHODS: A total of 120 patients with HNSCC who relapsed after surgical resection and subsequently received ICIs were included. The association of LNY, neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression with ICI outcomes were evaluated. RESULTS: Among 120 patients, 31 underwent unilateral, 82 bilateral, and 7 no neck dissection. The median LNY was 26 (mean, 29.9; range, 0-145). PD-L1 expression was evaluated in 80 patients, 69 of whom had combined positive score ≥ 1. The low-LNY group had a higher overall response rate to ICI than the high-LNY group (42.9% vs. 16.9%, P = 0.003). Patients with high LNY had inferior PFS (median, 1.3 vs. 5.9 months; P < 0.001) and OS (median, 9.7 vs. 21.1 months; P = 0.007) compared with those with low LNY. In multivariable analysis, high LNY and high NLR were independent predictors of poor survival, whereas PD-L1 expression was not. Among patients with PD-L1-positive tumors, those with high NLR had inferior survivals compared with those with low NLR. CONCLUSIONS: Extensive lymphatic ablation, as reflected by high LNY, may be associated with diminished ICI efficacy in relapsed HNSCC. These findings suggest that LNY warrants further investigation as a potential biomarker for ICI outcomes in patients with post-surgical recurrent HNSCC.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: The aim was to explore head and neck cancer (HNC) survivors' experiences of barriers to follow-up care and rehabilitation in Norway 3-5 years after treatment. METHODS: This descriptive qualitative study involved 12 individual interviews with Norwegian HNC survivors. Data were analysed using inductive semantic thematic analysis. Haggerty's continuity-of-care framework subsequently informed the interpretation of findings in relation to informational continuity (the use of information to connect care), relational continuity (ongoing patient-provider relationships), and management continuity (coordinated and consistent care across providers). RESULTS: Four themes emerged: (1) limited continuity due to difficult access to services and frequent personnel changes, leading to fragmented care and insufficient follow-up; (2) challenges in information flow and communication, including complex and poorly tailored information, speech barriers, and increasing reliance on self-management; (3) inadequate coordination across care levels, with unclear responsibilities and limited collaboration, particularly during transitions to primary care; and (4) structural barriers affecting access, including limited availability of specialised services, financial burden, and challenges navigating digital systems. CONCLUSION: HNC survivors face substantial barriers to continuity in follow-up and rehabilitation, which may be particularly pronounced in rural areas. Targeted strategies to improve coordination, accessibility, and integration within and across healthcare services are needed to promote equitable, holistic, and long-term support for survivors with complex needs.

papers.abstract_en: Four-dimensional computed tomography (4DCT) is routinely used in radiotherapy simulation to evaluate respiration-induced tumor motion, but the motion information is often reviewed visually rather than captured as structured, phase-resolved data. We developed and evaluated M4DTrack, a DICOM-based imaging-informatics workflow for user-supervised 4DCT lung tumor motion analysis and structured, exportable three-dimensional center-of-mass (CoM) motion reporting. M4DTrack imports phase-resolved DICOM CT images, groups images by respiratory phase, displays linked axial/coronal/sagittal views, supports crosshair-based tumor localization and HU inspection, and applies seed or linked 3D-box initialization with sequential phase-to-phase HU-volume propagation. An 8-case lower-lobe lung 4DCT dataset (80 respiratory phases) was analyzed. Directional amplitudes, 3D vector amplitude, maximum phase-wise displacement, and agreement with independent ITV-GTV reference amplitudes were quantified. HU-weighted CoM amplitudes were 2.44 ± 1.44 mm, 2.64 ± 1.37 mm, and 6.04 ± 2.48 mm in X, Y, and Z patient-coordinate directions, respectively. Mean 3D vector amplitude was 7.26 ± 2.50 mm, and mean maximum phase-wise 3D displacement was 6.20 ± 2.10 mm. Biases versus ITV-GTV reference amplitudes were 0.01, - 0.84, and 0.23 mm for X, Y, and Z, respectively, with a 3D vector amplitude bias of - 0.29 mm. M4DTrack provides a user-supervised imaging-informatics bridge between qualitative 4DCT cine review and structured quantitative motion documentation. The pilot results support feasibility for generating exportable, phase-resolved tumor-motion metrics while preserving user-supervised review of 4DCT artifacts, HU-capture uncertainty, adjacent anatomy, and differences between CoM-based and extent-based measurements.

papers.abstract_en: Accurate pulmonary nodule detection in computed tomography (CT) remains challenging because small- and low-contrast nodules may resemble vessels and other anatomical structures on individual axial slices. We propose 3D-DDN Faster R-CNN, a multi-slice detection framework that incorporates structured local axial context into a two-stage detector. The five-slice interactive blending (5-SIB) strategy organizes five consecutive CT slices as an ordered contextual group and preserves slice-specific feature streams extracted by a shared two-dimensional backbone. The cross-slice feature fusion (CSFF) module applies slice-wise spatial self-attention at shallow feature levels and learnable cross-slice aggregation at deep feature and region-of-interest levels. The dynamic displacement constraint (DDC) models proposal displacement across adjacent slices using a positive-sample regression loss and a margin-based negative-sample contrastive loss, while a class-weighted focal loss alleviates foreground-background imbalance. The model was evaluated on a private hospital dataset, LIDC-IDRI, and LNDb using patient-level data partitions. On the private hospital dataset, 3D-DDN achieved an average precision at an IoU threshold of 0.5 (AP0.5) of 75.80% ± 1.05%, a sensitivity of 89.33% ± 1.91%, and a competition performance metric (CPM) of 91.20% ± 1.50%. The corresponding AP0.5 values on LIDC-IDRI and LNDb were 66.27% ± 0.45% and 48.20% ± 0.30%, respectively. Ablation experiments showed that direct five-slice stacking degraded performance, whereas structured feature fusion and displacement supervision recovered the performance loss and improved the overall detection profile. These results indicate that ordered cross-slice representation, hierarchical feature fusion, and proposal-displacement supervision provide complementary mechanisms for incorporating local three-dimensional context.

papers.abstract_en: Medical imaging data are increasingly used for benchmarking, quality improvement, research, and artificial intelligence applications. However, the lack of consistent metadata characterization limits the reliability and scalability of such analyses. Existing standards provide syntactic interoperability but often fail to capture the semantic clinical context and workflow details necessary for secondary uses such as AI development and radiation safety assessment, affecting the utility for reproducible profiling of imaging examinations across institutions. In this work, we describe key gaps in current approaches to imaging data standardization. These include syntactic interoperability without semantic equivalence, limited representation of clinically relevant context, inconsistent definitions of radiology procedures across institutions, and the absence of mechanisms to systematically profile imaging examinations for analysis. These limitations make it difficult to compare imaging practices, aggregate datasets, and interpret results across sites. To address these challenges, we have devised an ontology framework, the Operational Ontology for Radiology (OOR), that models the radiology study workflow from ordering through interpretation using explicitly defined entities, relationships, and annotated data properties. A CT-focused implementation of the framework was then formed, including 34 classes, 15 object properties, and 156 data properties in this present formation. The framework was deployed in a demonstrative use case scenario to illustrate the utility of OOR in drawing more clinically relevant radiation dose aggregates from clinical CT data. The work demonstrates that OOR provides both a structured representation of imaging data and a foundation for more transparent data aggregation, scalable secondary analysis, and reproducible characterization of imaging practices across institutions.

papers.abstract_en: To develop and validate a compact, locally deployable MedGemma-based model converting unstructured Turkish spine MRI reports into structured six-field output. In this retrospective single-institution study, 5210 lumbar and 5017 cervical Turkish spine MRI reports were used to fine-tune MedGemma 4B IT with QLoRA. Silver-standard labels from a proprietary large language model served as training targets and as the reference for automated fidelity analyses, but not as the clinical reference standard. Evaluation comprised multi-reader validation of 180 authentic reports interleaved with 20 adversarial cases, a second round in which the readers scored the silver labels themselves, and comparison on the full held-out set against a rule-based baseline, the non-fine-tuned base model, and a much larger model. Every output was valid, schema-conformant JSON, and the grouped acceptance rate was 100% (95% CI 97.9-100), though one reader judged negative-finding lists incomplete in 57.8% of reports. On the full held-out set (1025 reports), fine-tuning increased agreement with the silver-label impression from 17.7% to 67.1% and urgent-flag sensitivity against the silver reference from 18.8% to 62.5% (both p < .001); the larger non-fine-tuned model reached 27.5% and 50.0%, and a rule-based baseline 99.0% on body region. papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Perineural invasion (PNI) is a high-risk feature of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and is associated with aggressive behavior and poor outcomes. The biological programs associated with PNI in PDAC remain incompletely characterized. METHODS: PDAC patients in The Cancer Genome Atlas were stratified by PNI status. Gene set enrichment analysis using Hallmark gene sets was performed to characterize transcriptomic differences between PNI-positive and PNI-negative tumors. Established immune, proliferative, and genomic annotations curated from prior The Cancer Genome Atlas analyses were used for downstream comparisons. RESULTS: A total of 101 PNI-positive and 26 PNI-negative tumors were identified. PNI was associated with higher grade (P < 0.05). Gene set enrichment analysis demonstrated enrichment of multiple gene sets in PNI-positive tumors, including pathways related to cell proliferation (G2M checkpoint, mTORC1 signaling, E2F targets, MYC targets, and mitotic spindle), immune signaling (tumor necrosis factor-α signaling via NF-κB, interferon-α, and γ responses), and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Yet, no differences were observed in measures of tumor proliferation, aggressiveness, mutational burden, immune response, or immune cell infiltration within the tumor microenvironment. In contrast, EMT enrichment was supported by concordant biological features, including increased infiltration of mesenchymal cells and elevated expression of EMT-associated genes in PNI-positive tumors. CONCLUSIONS: PNI-positive PDAC demonstrate enrichment of EMT-related transcriptional programs with concordant microenvironmental and gene-level support.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Appendicitis diagnosis relies heavily on medical imaging procedure studies; however, a definite diagnosis is obtained through histological assessment. Understanding the imaging characteristics and their relation to various histological phases enhance the quality of treatment recommendations. This study analyzed imaging characteristics of acute appendicitis in relation to its histological severity. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted using data from a third-level hospital. Appendectomy specimens from patients with prior computed tomography (CT) scans or ultrasound (US) imaging were included. Histological stages were categorized into simple, suppurative, abscessed, and perforated phases, depending the presence of edema, vascular congestion, neutrophilic infiltrate into the muscular layer, microabscess formation, mucosal ulceration, purulent exudate, macroscopic pus, and perforation with transmural inflammation. Imaging features as fat stranding, presence of free fluid, contrast enhancement within the appendix, appendicolith detection, reactive lymph nodes in the vicinity, appendix diameter itself, increased echogenicity, and detecting heightened perfusion via Doppler imaging were compared across these stages. RESULTS: Among 760 patients included (51.4% women, mean age 30.1 ± 5.3), 196 (25.8%) had CT scans and 361 (47.5%) had US. CT confirmed appendicitis in 59.2% of cases, yielded a negative result in 19.4%, and provided an inconclusive diagnosis in 21.4% of cases, commonly identifying fat stranding, free liquid, and contrast enhancement. US diagnosed appendicitis in 67.6% of cases, whereas 32.4% were reported as negative, with findings including increased echogenicity, Doppler perfusion, appendix identification, and free liquid in the right parietocolic gutter. All imaging characteristics were less prevalent in early stages compared to advanced stages, with a higher negativity rate in earlier stages. CONCLUSIONS: Imaging findings are associated with the histopathological severity of appendicitis. Increased histopathological severity is associated with greater frequency of CT and US findings. These relations suggest the potential for managing appendicitis based on the histological phase suspected from imaging findings. Further research is warranted.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: The United States Preventative Task Force recommends initiating colorectal cancer (CRC) screening at age 45, but screening rates among 45-49 y-olds has been lower than older age groups. Reasons for low screening rates among younger individuals are not clear. METHODS: Using Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data from 2022 to 2024, we investigated factors associated with CRC screening among adults aged 45-49; stratified analyses were conducted among the insured and uninsured. We characterized preventative care behaviors including seeking primary care, time since last checkup, and completion of other age-appropriate cancer screening. RESULTS: Of 50,132 individuals, 21,566 (42.6%) underwent CRC screening. Those with primary care physicians had higher odds of screening (odds ratio = 1.71; 95% confidence interval = 1.47-1.98, ref: no primary care physician), but increasing time since one's last visit was associated with decreasing odds of screening at all time intervals (5+ y ago: odds ratio = 0.29; 95% confidence interval = 0.23-0.38, ref: <1 y). CRC screening was completed in only 41.3% of women who had mammograms and 48% who were screened for cervical cancer. CONCLUSIONS: Uptake of CRC screening lags in adults aged 45-49, with differences in socioeconomic factors and preventative care utilization. A majority of eligible but unscreened individuals accessed other age-appropriate cancer screening tests, directing focus to patient- and provider-specific factors as potential targets for intervention.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Patient education is essential for older adults with cancer and their caregivers to support understanding of diagnosis and treatment. However, the evidence describing patient education interventions has not been comprehensively mapped. Our objective was to characterize the features, delivery approaches, and outcomes of patient education interventions developed for older adults with cancer and/or their caregivers across any study design, and to identify gaps in the evidence. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A scoping review was conducted using the Arksey and O'Malley framework and reported according to the PRISMA-ScR guideline. MEDLINE, EMBASE, EMCARE, CENTRAL, PsycINFO, and Scopus were searched on January 23, 2025. Studies published from 2000 onward were included if they evaluated healthcare professional-delivered patient education. RESULTS: From 26,898 records screened, 93 studies met inclusion criteria. Most interventions were delivered pre-treatment (n = 63), with surgery the most common context (n = 31). Common aims included side-effect prevention (n = 32) and supporting treatment decision-making (n = 26). Caregiver involvement was limited. Outcomes were clustered into 20 domains. Frequent reported domains were satisfaction/acceptability (52 occurrences) and knowledge/understanding (46 occurrences), while caregiver outcomes and clinical endpoints were rarely assessed. DISCUSSION: Patient education interventions generally improved knowledge and satisfaction, but evidence for clinical or system-level impacts remains limited. Key gaps include minimal integration of geriatric assessment, limited adaptation for cognitive impairment, sparse caregiver-specific outcomes, and inconsistent reporting of unintended effects. Future research should better integrate caregiver needs and geriatric principles into patient education design.

papers.abstract_en: Vestibular schwannomas (VS) are benign neoplasms of the VIII cranial nerve; they account for 6-8% of all intracranial tumors and about 80% of tumors of the cerebellopontine angle. Cystic forms of VS may be particularly dangerous, as they demonstrate faster growth and worse postoperative outcomes. In this study, we performed proteomic analysis of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples obtained from patients with solid and cystic forms of VS, as well as cyst fluid from patients with cystic VS. CSF samples from patients with hemifacial spasm were used as controls. Mass spectrometric (MS) analysis resulted in identification of 816 proteins in all samples and 111 proteins were upregulated in samples obtained from VS patients compared to the control group. The upregulated proteins belonged to the groups of components and regulators of the complement system, proteins associated with glucose and lipid metabolism. MS analysis of CSF obtained from patients with cystic and solid forms of VS resulted in identification of two proteomic clusters enriched in proteins associated with the development of the nervous system, cell adhesion, and myelination processes. The data obtained suggest the involvement of these biological processes in the pathogenesis of cystic VS. SIGNIFICANCE: This study provides a comprehensive proteomic characterization of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and cyst fluid from patients with solid and cystic vestibular schwannomas (VS), offering valuable insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying these tumors. Our discovery that complement system components and regulators are consistently upregulated in CSF and cyst fluid from VS patients, along with proteins involved in lipid metabolism, points to a potential mechanism of blood-brain barrier disruption and cyst formation, which is particularly relevant given the more aggressive clinical course of cystic VS. These findings not only contribute to understanding of VS pathogenesis but also suggest candidate protein targets for future diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic strategies, particularly for the more challenging cystic form of the disease.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Postoperative anaesthesia visits after inpatient procedures guarantee a comprehensive assessment of the patient's status. As the number of outpatient surgical cases in hospitals increases, more patients are recovering at home. Telemedicine may provide an efficient and effective link between anaesthesiologists and patients at home without restricting their freedom and self-determination. METHODS: After an initial acceptance survey, a single-arm, observational pilot study piloted an optional postoperative anaesthesia visit for patients undergoing outpatient surgery under general anaesthesia. RESULTS: Of the 300 people initially surveyed in the initial acceptance survey, nearly two-thirds (62.0%) expressed interest in using videochats to contact an anaesthesiologist after discharge. One hundred patients (n = 100) were included in the subsequent observational pilot study. The offer of an optional postoperative visit was used by 65 participants (n = 65, 65%). Videochats were considered a reliable tool for communicating medical issues and perceived as superior to telephone calls. The use of PROM questionnaires was considered meaningful by more than 80% of participants. Sixty-two of the sixty-five participants considered the postoperative anaesthesia visit a useful and beneficial part of the treatment and recovery process. CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative anaesthesia visits via videochat combined with PROM questionnaires after outpatient surgery were successfully piloted and consistently perceived positively by participants. Telemedicine-assisted postoperative anaesthesia visits may be a feasible component of patient-centred care in settings with limited resources. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Reduced exercise capacity, measured by the 6-min walk distance (6MWD), is a critical prognostic factor in interstitial lung disease (ILD). However, conventional physiological markers often fail to identify early functional decline. We aimed to evaluate whether the foot-to-foot lower-limb phase angle (F-F PhA), a non-invasive surrogate marker of muscle quality, predicts reduced exercise capacity better than traditional muscle mass and pulmonary function indices. METHODS: In this retrospective study of 68 patients with ILD, F-F PhA was measured using bioelectrical impedance analysis, and erector spinae muscle area (ESM_CSA) via computed tomography. Reduced exercise capacity was defined as 6MWD < 450 m. Multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age and pulmonary function (%DLCO or %FVC), with internal validation performed via 1000-resample bootstrapping. RESULTS: In multivariable analysis, F-F PhA was independently associated with a 6MWD < 450 m when adjusted for age and %DLCO (OR: 0.228, 95% CI: 0.088-0.591, p = 0.002; bootstrap p = 0.005) or %FVC (OR: 0.213, 95% CI: 0.091-0.496, p = 0.001; bootstrap p = 0.001). ROC analysis showed F-F PhA had the highest discriminative accuracy (AUC: 0.802), outperforming %DLCO (AUC: 0.729) and ESM_CSA (AUC: 0.701). Combining age, %DLCO, and F-F PhA achieved the highest performance (AUC: 0.833). CONCLUSIONS: F-F PhA serves as a robust, independent indicator for predicting reduced exercise capacity in ILD, outperforming conventional muscle mass. As a non-invasive tool, F-F PhA complements established functional tests in screening for early physical decline.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: In 2015 the World Health Assembly (WHO), based on recommendations by the Lancet Commission on Global Surgery, passed resolution (68:15) on strengthening emergency and essential surgical care and anesthesia as a component of universal health coverage. However, children's surgery was not adequately represented and in response, the Global Initiative for Children's Surgery (GICS) published the Optimal Resources for Children's Surgical Care (OReCS) in 2019 providing insight into procedures which should be performed at different facility types. OReCS 2 addresses a gap in both policy and published literature to further define surgical conditions and procedural capabilities by hospital level. METHODS: We performed a review of the literature to identify procedures routinely performed in a variety of settings. We then used an iterative Delphi like approach to identify specialty-specific procedures and nursing skills by hospital level. Participation was open to all members of GICS with representation from 21 working groups and more than 50 low-middle income countries (LMICs) and high-income countries (HICs). Data on essential procedures were collected for twelve specialty groups. Modifications of the recommendations provided by the working groups were made by the executive board based on firsthand knowledge of capabilities at lower-level facilities where subspecialists have less experience. Final recommendations were made based on greater than 75% agreement by respondents and review of the executive board of GICS. RESULTS: Procedures performed at health centers were limited to those not requiring anesthesia or sedation and were largely identified to help triage and stabilize patients for transfer to higher level care. Similarly, first level hospital procedures focused on stabilization and transfer to referral level hospitals for most specialties. Alternatively, specialties such as ophthalmology and dental surgery have identified definitive procedures for lower-level facilities. Procedures performed at the National Children's Hospital level include those requiring specialty providers and equipment such as transplantation, repair of congenital heart disease, and reconstructive surgery for complex trauma, congenital anomalies, and burns. CONCLUSIONS: This updated version of OReCS provides specific examples of procedural capabilities for twelve subspecialties at the health center, first, second, third, and referral level hospitals in LMICs. Whereas the list is not meant to be all inclusive, it provides a framework within which to define the minimum essential material resources, equipment, and personnel by hospital level.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs) are associated with increased cardiovascular risk, but surgical outcomes in the modern era of immunosuppressive therapy remain unclear. We evaluated early and late outcomes after cardiac and thoracic aortic surgery in patients with IMIDs, focusing on the impact of glucocorticoids and disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs). METHODS: A total of 140 patients with IMIDs who underwent cardiac or thoracic aortic surgery between 2008 and 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. The primary endpoints were in-hospital mortality and long-term overall survival. RESULTS: Median age was 70 [61-76] years, and 62% were women. Rheumatoid arthritis was the most common IMID (36%). Prednisolone and DMARDs were used in 68% and 33% of patients, respectively. Procedures included valve (43%), ischemic (26%), and thoracic aortic surgery (23%). In-hospital mortality was 4.3%. During a median follow-up of 5.9 years (93% completeness), overall survival was 91% at 1 year, 87% at 3 years, 78% at 5 years, and 62% at 10 years, respectively. Outcomes did not differ by a surgical category or IMID subtype. Glucocorticoid use was independently associated with worse late survival (HR, 2.91; 95% CI, 1.01-8.41; p = 0.048), whereas DMARD use showed a trend toward improved survival (HR 0.46; 95% CI, 0.19-1.09; p = 0.08). Notably, a dose-dependent relationship was observed, with high-dose prednisolone (≥ 5 mg/day) showing significantly worse survival compared with low-dose (< 5 mg/day) or no glucocorticoid use (p = 0.004). Diabetes mellitus and preoperative anemia were also independent predictors of late mortality. CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac surgery in patients with IMIDs provides acceptable early outcomes but suboptimal long-term survival. Glucocorticoid use was associated with worse late survival, with a dose-dependent relationship, whereas DMARD use showed a nonsignificant trend toward better survival, underscoring the importance of optimized immunosuppressive management.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The previously published Optimal Resources for Children's Surgical Care (OReCS) addressed disparities in access to high-quality children's surgery in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) with an emphasis on physical and human resources. Data from high-income countries (HICs) show a clear advantage in outcomes when there is an investment in quality improvement (QI) programs. In-hospital adverse events, many of which are avoidable through implementation of quality improvement programs, contribute disproportionately to morbidity in LMICs. The objective of this document is to make recommendations for quality improvement programming at the hospital level. METHODS: We performed a systematic review of the literature to identify quality improvement programming appropriate for a variety of healthcare settings. We then used an iterative Delphi like approach to rank specific quality improvement programs by hospital level according to the DCP3 and WHO classification systems. Participation was open to all members of the Global Initiative for Children's Surgery (GICS) with representation from 21 working groups and 50 LMICs and HICs. Final recommendations were made based on greater than 75% agreement by respondents and review by the GICS executive board. RESULTS: After three rounds of an iterative Delphi like approach, it is recommended that facilities of all levels, participate in a minimum of local data collection and review and establish an antibiotic stewardship program. Recommendations increased by the complexity of work done at each hospital level with the addition of surgical safety checklists, and protocols for multiple domains including the operating room, radiology, and transfusion medicine at first level hospitals. Surgical quality improvement committees and routine mortality and serious event review processes should be implemented at second level hospitals and above. At the National Children's Hospital level, program recommendations mirror those of most HICs, including continuous data collection and monitoring, multidisciplinary review boards, morbidity and mortality conferences and more. CONCLUSION: Quality improvement is defined in the literature as a systematic, data driven approach to improve outcomes and safety of healthcare delivery. Despite significant barriers in data collection, we recommend a minimum level of quality improvement programming and standardization of care for facilities of various levels.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: By preserving spontaneous breathing and avoiding mechanical ventilation, Non-intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery may attenuate perioperative inflammatory responses and promote early mobilization, thereby influencing the risk of venous thromboembolism. However, whether the risk of postoperative venous thromboembolism differs between Non-intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery and conventional Intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery remains unclear due to a lack of definitive evidence. We hypothesized that patients undergoing Non-intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery would have a lower risk of postoperative venous thromboembolism. METHODS: A single-center retrospective study was conducted. Patients with lung cancer who underwent video-assisted thoracoscopic lung surgery at the Department of Cardiothoracic Surgery, Jinhua Central Hospital between March 2025 and July 2025 were enrolled and, based on the anesthetic approach, divided into the Non-intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery group (n = 25) and the Intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery group (n = 30). The primary outcome was the risk of venous thromboembolism, as assessed by thrombotic complications, postoperative coagulation parameters, time to early postoperative ambulation, time to first flatus, and time to first defecation. RESULTS: No perioperative venous thromboembolic complications occurred in either group. Regarding coagulation parameters, the D-dimer level in the Non-intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery group was 0.30 (0.04, 0.70) µg/L, which was significantly lower than 0.77 (0.34, 1.46) µg/L in the I-VATS group (P = 0.006). There were no statistically significant differences in prothrombin time (PT) or activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) between the two groups (P > 0.05). The time to early postoperative ambulation was significantly shorter in the Non-intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery group [0 (0, 0) days] than in the Intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery group [1 (1, 1) days] (P < 0.001). The time to first flatus and defecation was 1 (1, 1) day in the Non-intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery group, significantly shorter than 2 (2, 3) days in the Intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery group (P < 0.001). Furthermore, the Non-intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery group exhibited a significantly attenuated elevation in the inflammatory marker (leukocyte count: 2.24 ± 0.39 × 10⁹/L) compared with the Intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery group (5.82 ± 0.60 × 10⁹/L). CONCLUSIONS: Non-intubated video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery may reduce the risk of venous thromboembolism through several mechanisms: maintaining negative intrathoracic pressure generated by spontaneous breathing, lowering the risk of elevated intra-abdominal pressure, and facilitating early mobilization - all of which enhance venous return; substituting general anesthesia with combined regional anesthesia; and avoiding muscle relaxants, thereby attenuating surgery-induced hypercoagulability and preserving endothelial function.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths worldwide. The mortality rate can be reduced through the development of novel therapeutic drugs for lung cancer. In this study, we developed nanoparticles (NPs) consisting of polyethylene glycol (PEG)-cloaked mesoporous polydopamine (MP) loaded with indocyanine green (IG) and talazoparib (TZ), designed to combine therapies for lung cancer. MP NPs were synthesized and surface-capped with methoxypolyethylene glycol amine. PEG2K-MP and PEG5K-MP NPs were analyzed using dynamic light scattering, scanning electron microscopy, and transmission electron microscopy. PEG2K-MP@IG&TZ and PEG5K-MP@IG&TZ NPs were developed using the solvent diffusion technique to co-load IG and TZ. The reduction in drug-feeding ratios led to a decrease in the amount of drug loaded and an increase in the encapsulation efficiency. PEG2K-MP@IG&TZ and PEG5K-MP@IG&TZ NPs, which showed excellent drug loading efficiency (IG: 9.9 ± 0.4% and 9.1 ± 0.2%; TZ: 6.8 ± 0.3% and 6.5 ± 0.2%), were chosen for further investigation. The hydrodynamic sizes ranged from 200 to 300 nm. These nanoparticles exhibited improved stability of IG in water, near-infrared laser-stimulated release of TZ, effective photothermal activity, excellent biocompatibility, and increased cellular uptake. These two nanoparticles demonstrated a stronger anticancer effect on lung cancer A549 cells than the combination of IG and TZ when irradiated with 808 nm light in vitro. Fluorescence microscopy revealed that PEG5K-MP@IG&TZ NPs efficiently triggered apoptosis in A549 cells. This study presents an innovative and efficient method for combination therapy against lung cancer cells.

papers.abstract_en: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), the most common subtype of lung cancer, is associated with substantial global mortality. Nuclear receptor coactivator 5 (NCOA5) has been implicated in several malignancies; however, its functional role and regulatory mechanisms in LUAD remain largely unknown. In this study, NCOA5 expression was evaluated in 94 paired LUAD and adjacent tissues using immunohistochemistry, RT-PCR, and Western blotting. Functional analyses were conducted using shRNA knockdown, CRISPR-mediated knockout, and overexpression models to assess the effects of NCOA5 on LUAD cell proliferation, migration, invasion, apoptosis, cell cycle progression, and organoid formation. Xenograft models were used to validate tumorigenicity in vivo. IP-MS and co-immunoprecipitation identified NCOA5-interacting proteins, while ChIP-seq and dual-luciferase assays interrogated downstream transcriptional regulation. NCOA5 was significantly upregulated in LUAD tissues and associated with advanced stage, poor differentiation, and reduced overall survival, serving as an independent prognostic factor (P < .040). NCOA5 knockdown inhibited LUAD cell proliferation, migration, invasion, induced G0/G1 arrest, promoted apoptosis, reduced organoid formation, and suppressed xenograft growth, whereas NCOA5 overexpression produced the opposite effects. Among 39 candidate interacting proteins identified by IP-MS, ZCCHC3 was validated as a direct NCOA5-binding partner. ZCCHC3 depletion phenocopied NCOA5 loss and reversed NCOA5-induced proliferation, migration, invasion, and colony formation, supporting a functional NCOA5-ZCCHC3 interaction. ChIP-seq analysis identified fibroblast growth factor 22 (FGF22) as a direct transcriptional target of NCOA5. FGF22 was markedly downregulated in LUAD tissues and higher FGF22 expression was associated with improved patient survival. NCOA5 suppressed FGF22 transcription, while NCOA5 inhibition increased FGF22 expression. Functionally, FGF22 knockdown enhanced LUAD aggressiveness, whereas FGF22 restoration abrogated the oncogenic effects of NCOA5 in vitro and in vivo. Collectively, these findings identify a previously unrecognized NCOA5-ZCCHC3/FGF22 axis that drives LUAD progression and provide new mechanistic insight into the role of NCOA5 in LUAD biology.

papers.abstract_en: Radiation-induced lung injury (RILI) is a common dose-limiting toxicity after radiotherapy for lung cancer, but the immunological mechanisms contributing to RILI pathogenesis remain poorly understood. Here we analyze a RILI mouse model using high-dose, restricted-field irradiation to the left lung. Flow cytometry and cytokine profiling analysis of innate lymphoid cells (ILC) reveals a radiation-induced shift from lung-resident type 2 ILCs (ILC2) toward pro-inflammatory type 1 ILCs (ILC1). Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis of mouse lung ILC populations after radiation suggests that type I interferon (IFN) promotes radiation-induced ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity. In vitro, IFN-β stimulation of mouse ILC2s leads to increased expression of the ILC1 markers T-bet and IFN-γ, while IFN-β stimulation of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells increases the ILC1-to-ILC2 ratio. In vivo, inhibition of type I IFN signaling attenuates lung damage after irradiation in our RILI model. Thus, our findings indicate that radiation-induced type I IFN induces ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity to contribute to RILI pathogenesis, and suggest that targeting type I IFN signaling may be a therapeutic strategy to mitigate radiation-induced lung injury.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Tumor proximity to the left brachiocephalic vein (LBCV) may affect vascular exposure and dissection during the subxiphoid approach (SXA). We investigated the association between tumor-LBCV distance and operative time in patients undergoing subxiphoid robot-assisted or video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery for thymoma. METHODS: Consecutive patients who underwent minimally invasive SXA for thymoma between 2019 and 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. The shortest tumor-LBCV distance (d-LBCV) was measured on preoperative computed tomography. Associations of d-LBCV and tumor size with operative time were evaluated using correlation, interaction, and multivariable linear regression analyses. RESULTS: Among 64 patients with clinical Stage I thymoma without radiological evidence of vascular invasion, 45 and 19 underwent robot- and video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery, respectively. Overall, shorter d-LBCV (r = -0.357, p = 0.0037) and larger tumor size (r = 0.328, p = 0.0082) were correlated with longer operative time. In multivariable analysis adjusting for tumor size, surgical platform, and surgical procedure, shorter d-LBCV remained significantly associated with longer operative time (regression coefficient, -7.62 min per 10-mm increase; 95% CI, -13.21 to -2.03; p = 0.008). Surgical procedure was also significantly associated with operative time, whereas tumor size and surgical platform were not. Although platform-specific analyses showed different association patterns, interaction analyses showed no significant differences between RATS and VATS for tumor size or d-LBCV. CONCLUSION: Shorter d-LBCV was independently associated with longer operative time during minimally invasive SXA for thymoma, despite adjustment for tumor size, surgical platform, and surgical procedure. d-LBCV may provide useful anatomical information for preoperative planning; although further validation is required.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To inform lung cancer screening (LCS) in primary care settings, the study assessed providers' knowledge, attitudes, and practices around LCS and recommended implementation strategies. METHODS: The online survey was administered from May-August 2025 among primary care providers in Georgia, USA. We ran descriptive analyses for all data and linear regression for predictors of greater knowledge. RESULTS: Providers (N = 112) had an average knowledge score of 3.72/5 (SD = 1.11). Physicians (N = 73) scored significantly higher than nurses/nurse practitioners (β = -1.0, 95% CI: -1.6, -0.44). Overall, participants viewed LCS positively, and about 45% reported offering LCS at their facility while 50% reported referring patients to LCS programs. Most (75.5%) had strategies to follow-up with patients who screened positive, but few (22.6%) offered tobacco cessation services. Top barriers were cost, lack of patient knowledge/interest, and transportation; cost assistance, patient education materials, and patient navigation were the top facilitators. Providers (N = 86) identified 'Distributing patient educational materials' and 'Reminding clinicians' as highly feasible and important implementation strategies. CONCLUSIONS: While most providers had sufficient knowledge, positive perceptions, and high availability of LCS services, few engage in patient education or offer smoking cessation resources. Patient education and clinician reminders may be beneficial implementation strategies for primary care-based LCS.

papers.abstract_en: Precise, reversible control of transgene expression is essential for safe and durable gene therapy, yet current inducible systems remain difficult to translate in vivo due to large size, limited induction duration, and dependence on immunogenic regulators. Here, we present the adaptamer (adenosine deaminases acting on RNA [ADAR]-modulatable aptamer), a compact (<120 base pair) RNA switch that couples FDA-approved small-molecule-responsive aptamers with endogenous ADAR-mediated RNA editing to regulate expression. Ligand binding stabilizes a double-stranded RNA structure that recruits ADAR to convert a stop codon into a sense codon, restoring downstream protein translation. This cleavage-free, post-transcriptional mechanism enables precise, small-molecule-dependent modulation without exogenous protein machinery. We demonstrate that adaptamers are highly functional across multiple cell lines, including human T cells. In mice, adeno-associated virus (AAV)-delivered adaptamer-controlled FGF21 expression induced metabolic remodeling, reversing obesity and hepatic steatosis. This minimal, programmable system offers a clinically compatible approach for tunable genetic medicines and safe deployment of pleiotropic and dose-limited proteins.

papers.abstract_en: Many E3 ubiquitin ligases recognize degrons located at protein termini, but the paucity of bona fide substrates of N-degron and C-degron pathways hampers our understanding of their physiological significance. Devising an expression screening strategy to assess the effect of C-terminal "capping" on the stability of thousands of human proteins, we systematically identify substrates harboring C-degrons. Interrogating one leading candidate, ZMYND19, we characterize a C-degron pathway governed via the C-terminal to LisH (CTLH) E3 ligase complex subunit Muskelin. Cell-to-cell variability in ZMYND19 stability uncovered conditional regulation, with CTLH-mediated degradation impaired by TNF-α stimulation but enhanced by mTOR inhibition. Parallel genetic and proteomic screens identified angio-associated migratory protein (AAMP) and apoptosis-enhancing nuclease (AEN) as additional substrates of the CTLHMuskelin C-degron pathway, leading us to define an essential role for AAMP in ribosome maturation through chaperone activity toward uL16. Altogether, these data define a C-degron pathway connecting conditional regulation of the CTLH E3 ligase complex to ribosome biogenesis.

papers.abstract_en: With the increase in the diagnosis rate of small pulmonary nodules, the segmentectomy has been increasingly used in clinical practice worldwide. However, for the segmentectomy, the confirmation of intersegmental plane has always puzzled many thoracic surgeons. This paper described a new method, named artery-based Inflation-deflation method, used to confirm the intersegmental border under video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery. After only dividing the targeted segment artery and preserving the targeted segmental veins and bronchi, the intersegmental plane was successfully generated by this novel Inflation-deflation method. Compared with other current methods, this new technique had some advantages including the smaller airway damage, easier to determine the intersegmental plane, the higher fault-tolerant rate and easy to operate without any additional devices. And a further clinical study should be carried out to verify the feasibility and applicability of this new technique.

papers.authors: Liu N, Wang X, Zhang W, Kan Y, Petrovna BM, Wang Z, Kong X, Wang J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Breast Surgical Oncology, National Cancer Center, National Clinical Research Center for Cancer, Cancer Hos…
