papers.abstract_en: Immunochemotherapy (ICT) is a critical treatment for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (LA-ESCC), yet predicting individual response remains challenging. We developed a three-channel 3D deep learning framework integrating tumor habitat analysis for predicting ICT response. In this multicenter retrospective study of 277 patients, voxel-level clustering of pretreatment CT images segmented tumors into habitat subregions reflecting microenvironmental heterogeneity. A ResNet-50 model incorporating habitat maps, cropped tumor images, and ROI masks achieved an AUC of 0.927 (95% CI, 0.850-0.951) in the independent external test cohort, compared with 0.869 for habitat radiomics (DeLong p = 0.343). SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified texture features, particularly gray-level co-occurrence matrix correlation in habitat 3, as the primary contributors. This framework provides a noninvasive approach for predicting ICT response in LA-ESCC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Osimertinib is the standard first-line therapy for epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but outcomes remain heterogeneous. This meta-analysis evaluated baseline clinical and molecular prognostic factors associated with poorer outcomes in this setting. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched through 20 May 2026. Eligible studies included patients with EGFR-mutated advanced, recurrent, or metastatic NSCLC receiving first-line osimertinib with extractable prognostic data. The primary outcome was progression-free survival or real-world progression-free survival (PFS/rwPFS); overall survival or real-world overall survival (OS/rwOS) was secondary. Hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled using random-effects models. RESULTS: Eighteen studies involving 4,070 first-line osimertinib-treated patients were included. TP53 mutation was associated with shorter PFS/rwPFS (HR 1.65, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.15-2.37) and worse OS/rwOS (HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.14-2.12). EGFR L858R, versus exon 19 deletion, was associated with shorter PFS/rwPFS (HR 1.62, 95% CI 1.39-1.90) and worse OS/rwOS (HR 1.63, 95% CI 1.40-1.88), with consistent estimates across sensitivity analyses. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status ≥ 2, central nervous system/brain metastasis, and liver metastasis were associated with poorer outcomes. The OS/rwOS association for liver metastasis was sensitive to alternative estimate selection. Evidence for bone metastasis and programmed death-ligand 1 expression was less robust. CONCLUSIONS: Evidence-tier assessment identified EGFR L858R, ECOG PS ≥ 2, and CNS/brain metastasis as high-certainty adverse prognostic factors. Liver metastasis was supported by moderate certainty for PFS/rwPFS but lower certainty for OS/rwOS. TP53 mutation, PD-L1 expression, and bone metastasis were lower-certainty or exploratory findings. These findings support future integrated prognostic models, but do not establish criteria for selecting intensified first-line therapy over osimertinib monotherapy.

papers.authors: Sakiyama K, Serapio A, Ye M, Nowroozi A, Bondarenko M, Wu YF, Qi K, Liu J et al.
papers.authors_conclusion: 规划器-执行器式多模态智能体系统能可靠回答LCS相关的患者个体化问题；其较高的工具调用与自我调节表现显示其有潜力成为LCS项目中安全有效的数字化沟通辅助工具。
papers.ai_note: ①问题为模拟生成而非真实患者提问，未验证真实语境下的提问分布与误解模式；②“自我调节准确率”以LLM-as-a-judge判定，缺少医师金标准对照，属循环式评价风险；③工具调用分母694与699题不一致，5题缺失原因未说明；④“100条回答×4名医师”与结果中228/172的分母关系需读者自行推断，报告口径不清；⑤仅报告“全 reader 满分5.0”这一严苛但粗糙的比例，未给均值/分布或失败案例的错误类型分析；⑥无与基线模型、检索式问答或人工护士/医师回答的对照；⑦单中心回顾性数据，无真实随访依从性等临床结局。

pico.p: 某三级学术医院116份肺癌筛查（LCS）CT报告及图像；基于此生成699个模拟患者问题（分为可回答与应转诊医生两类）；医师阅片评分子集为4名医师×100条回答
pico.ic: 干预：基于大语言模型的多智能体（planner+executor）多模态智能体系统，用于回答LCS CT结果相关问题；对照：无对照组，仅以工具调用准确率、自我调节准确率（LLM-as-a-judge）及医师评分（临床准确性、患者可理解性）为评价指标

papers.reason: 为肺癌筛查结果沟通类AI工具提供了可复用的评价框架（工具调用、越界问题转诊、医师多维评分），可作为后续真实患者场景研究与数字沟通工具对照设计的基线；但尚不足以改变当前筛查随访或患者沟通的临床路径。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Accurate patient understanding of lung cancer screening (LCS) results is critical for engagement and follow-up adherence, given the currently low screening uptake. While artificial intelligence (AI) systems show promise in facilitating patient communication, its effective use in clinical settings requires appropriate invocation of imaging tools and self-regulation by deferring certain questions to physicians. To this end, we developed and evaluated a planner-executor style multimodal agentic system to answer simulated patient questions about LCS CT results. METHODS: This retrospective study utilized 116 LCS CT reports and images collected from a tertiary academic hospital. The system employed a multi-agent architecture (planner and executor) to mimic clinical reasoning. We developed a large language model (LLM)-based question generation framework to prepare a comprehensive set of 699 simulated patient questions, categorized as answerable and defer-to-doctor to assess self-regulation. Performance was evaluated on tool-calling, self-regulation accuracy (ability to correctly defer out-of-scope questions to a human provider) assessed by LLM-as-a-judge, and clinical quality assessed by a reader performance study with four physicians evaluating a subset of 100 responses. RESULTS: The system demonstrated high overall tool-calling accuracy of 93.1% (646/694; 95% CI: 91.2%, 95.0%) and self-regulation accuracy of 92.6% (462/499; 90.2%, 94.8%). For answerable questions, the percentage of responses receiving perfect 5.0 scores across all readers included 78.9% (180/228) for clinical accuracy (inter-rater agreement: Gwet's AC2=0.92), and 73.2% (167/228) for patient understandability (0.86). For defer-to-doctor questions, the percentage of responses included 77.3% (133/172) for clinical accuracy (0.80) and 70.3% (121/172) for patient understandability (0.78). CONCLUSIONS: The planner-executor style multi-modal agentic system reliably answers patient-specific questions about LCS. Its high tool-calling and self-regulation performance demonstrates its potential as a safe and effective digital communication facilitator in LCS programs.

papers.authors: Makarov V, Baimukhametov E, Yessentayeva S, Oljaev S, Arybzhanov D
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Multidisciplinary Surgery, National Research Oncology Centre, Astana, Republic of Kazakhstan.
papers.results: VATS术后死亡率0%（0% versus 5.8% for thoracotomy）；I期中位总生存65.3 versus 67.7个月（p=0.768）；II期75.8 versus 48.8个月（p=0.003）；III期方向相似但未达统计学显著（摘要未给出数值）；探索性模型测试准确度0.39–0.48。
papers.authors_conclusion: In this unadjusted retrospective cohort, VATS was associated with lower perioperative mortality, and at stage II with longer overall survival. Given the retrospective design and baseline imbalances, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective, adjusted studies before informing surgical indications.
papers.ai_note: 未预设单一主要终点，按分期进行多重亚组比较且未校正多重性，II期p=0.003属亚组内结果；VATS组更多为女性、腺癌、I期，适应证偏倚（confounding by indication）未通过校正处理，0%与5.8%的围手术期死亡率未给出组样本量与置信区间；III期“方向相似但未达显著”未报告效应量与P值，存在选择性叙述空间；机器学习部分作者已自认准确度低不可临床使用，但摘要仍以“random forest performing best”呈现排序。

pico.p: 2014–2018年间接受手术治疗的255例非小细胞肺癌患者（回顾性队列）
pico.ic: 干预：电视辅助胸腔镜手术（VATS）；对照：开胸手术（thoracotomy）；非随机分组、基线不平衡、比较未做校正

papers.reason: 为早期NSCLC手术路径（VATS vs 开胸）的生存获益讨论提供未校正的真实世界对照基线，并明确提示II期获益仅为假说，可用于设计需校正混杂的前瞻性或注册队列研究；同时示范了探索性ML模型在样本量不足时不可外推的边界。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: This study retrospectively compared outcomes of minimally invasive and open surgical approaches for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in a cohort of 255 patients operated on between 2014 and 2018. A machine-learning analysis was performed as an exploratory, hypothesis-generating component. METHOD: Survival was analysed by disease stage using Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests. Because the groups were not randomised and were imbalanced at baseline, comparisons are unadjusted and should be interpreted as associations. Exploratory predictive models were developed using five machine-learning algorithms (random forest performing best), with feature contributions interpreted using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP). Missing values were handled by multiple imputation, continuous variables were standardised, and correlated features were excluded. RESULTS: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) was used more frequently for adenocarcinoma, in women, and at stage I, with zero postoperative mortality (0% versus 5.8% for thoracotomy). At stage I, there were no differences in median overall survival (65.3 versus 67.7 months; p=0.768); at stage II, VATS was associated with longer survival (75.8 versus 48.8 months; p=0.003); at stage III, a similar direction did not reach significance. Recurrent predictors in the exploratory models were coronary artery disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, intervention volume, tumour histology, and vascular invasion; however, test accuracy remained low (0.39-0.48), precluding clinical use. SHAP analysis highlighted resection completeness, lack of conversion, and tumour morphology. CONCLUSIONS: In this unadjusted retrospective cohort, VATS was associated with lower perioperative mortality, and at stage II with longer overall survival. Given the retrospective design and baseline imbalances, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective, adjusted studies before informing surgical indications.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lower income is consistently associated with poorer survival after disease diagnosis, even in countries with universal healthcare such as Sweden. While income-related survival differences have been documented for specific conditions, comparative evidence across a range of disease categories with long-term follow-up is lacking. We quantify income-related differences in survival across 100 disease categories focussing on leading non-communicable diseases (NCDs). METHODS: All individuals aged 16-95 years registered in Sweden between 2001 and 2023 were followed from first diagnosis until death or the end of 2023. By disease category cohort, individuals were matched to five general population controls (no prior diagnosis of that category) on birth year, sex, and income quartile. Flexible parametric models were used to estimate standardised survival curves for diagnosed individuals and their matched controls. FINDINGS: For all 100 disease categories, estimated 10-year survival was lower for the lowest income quartile (Q1) than higher quartiles. For 37 conditions, the Q1 vs Q4 10-year survival gap exceeded 10 percentage points; the largest gaps were for other pharynx cancer (10-year survival 34.2% [95% CI 32.5-35.7] in Q1 vs 58.2% [56.3-60.1] in Q4), larynx cancer, mouth cancer, COPD, and endocarditis. Income-related survival disparities accounted for 6.2 million (95% CI 5.9-6.6 million) person-years of survival loss within 10 years of diagnosis across all cohorts compared to a high-income survival counterfactual, with cardiovascular diseases accounting for the largest share for Q1 (1.3 million). Survival loss after diagnosis relative to undiagnosed controls was significantly greater for Q1 compared to Q4 for 73 of 100 conditions. INTERPRETATION: Substantial income-related disparities in survival persist in Sweden across all the most prevalent NCDs. Policies addressing income inequality alongside targeted disease-specific interventions are likely required to reduce income disparities in survival. FUNDING: Swedish Research Council for Health, Working Life and Welfare.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: In cutaneous oncology, radiotherapy use is largely based on retrospective studies, institutional experience, and expert consensus, with limited high-level evidence to guide practice. We summarize randomized controlled trials in cutaneous radiation oncology and identify gaps in contemporary treatment warranting additional study. METHODS AND MATERIALS: We searched Ovid MEDLINE ALL, Embase.com, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials for randomized controlled trials of radiotherapy for cutaneous malignancies: basal cell carcinoma (BCC), squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), melanoma, and Merkel cell carcinoma. Outcomes of interest included recurrence, survival, toxicity and cosmesis. Study inclusion required approval by three authors, with discrepancies resolved by an additional author. RESULTS: Thirteen trials entailing fewer than 2500 patients were identified, with only four studies published in the last decade. Three BCC studies compared radiotherapy with other treatments, while two additional BCC studies and one mixed BCC/SCC study compared dose-fractionation regimens. One SCC study evaluated adjuvant radiotherapy versus chemoradiotherapy. Among five melanoma trials, four evaluated adjuvant radiotherapy, including one for the primary tumor site and three for the regional nodal basin, and one compared definitive radiotherapy with topical imiquimod for unresectable melanoma in situ. One Merkel cell carcinoma trial evaluated lymph node basin radiotherapy. CONCLUSIONS: Randomized trials of radiotherapy for cutaneous malignancies are limited, small and heterogeneous, relative to the frequency of these diseases and clinical trials of other therapeutic interventions. Modern randomized trials are needed to bridge these gaps.

pico.ic: 干预：APEX机器学习框架（整合H3K4me3/H3K36me3定位信息与基因体片段周期性的单基因表达推断）；对照：现有血浆来源表达推断方法（头对头比较）

papers.reason: 为液体活检从“突变/甲基化检测”扩展到“肿瘤转录状态无创推断”提供了方法学基线与对照框架，对判断血浆cfDNA能否替代组织RNA用于亚型分型与靶点/疗效标志物（如NECTIN4、SCLC靶点）选择具有参考价值，同时可作为后续胸部肿瘤液体活检队列设计的benchmark参照。
papers.abstract_en: Tumor phenotype and therapeutic vulnerability are shaped by dynamic transcriptional states that are not captured by genetic profiling alone and are difficult to monitor longitudinally. Existing plasma-based approaches have largely been developed using samples with high circulating tumor DNA fractions, evaluated across expression quantiles rather than individual genes, and rarely benchmarked head-to-head. Using timepoint-matched plasma epigenomes and tumor transcriptomes, we identify biologically grounded relationships between circulating chromatin, fragmentation, and transcription. H3K4me3 and H3K36me3 encode distinct positional information reflecting promoter activity and transcriptional elongation, while gene-body fragment periodicity predicts expression. We integrate these relationships into APEX, a machine-learning framework for genome-wide single-gene expression inference. Across 559 plasma samples spanning 24 cancer types and clinically relevant tumor fractions, APEX outperforms existing approaches for individual-gene inference, resolves pancreatic cancer transcriptional subtypes, tracks therapeutic targets in small-cell lung cancer, and identifies NECTIN4 expression as a biomarker of response to enfortumab vedotin in urothelial cancer.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: For patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) for lung cancer or other pulmonary lesions, effective one-lung ventilation (OLV) is essential to provide surgical exposure. Bronchial blockers (BBs) are increasingly used for OLV, but the optimal management of their vent port to accelerate lung collapse remains unclear. METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, controlled trial, 75 patients were allocated to three groups (n = 25 each): Group 1-BB with vent port closed; Group 2 (control)-BB with vent port open; Group 3-BB with the disconnection technique. Primary outcome was the time to complete lung collapse, which was scored according to the video clips obtained during the operation. Secondary outcomes included intraoperative hypoxemia, blood gas analysis, blocker malposition, perioperative complications, and surgeon satisfaction. RESULTS: A total of 72 patients were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis, with 24 patients in each group. Median time to complete lung collapse was 15 min (95% CI: 10-15) in Groups 1 and 3 but was not reached in Group 2 (15/24, 62.5% had not achieved complete collapse by 30 min). In an exploratory 30-min restricted mean survival time (RMST), complete collapse occurred on average 14.17 min earlier in Group 1 (95% CI: 11.10-17.23) and 12.50 min earlier in Group 3 (95% CI: 9.62-15.38) than in Group 2, with no difference between Groups 1 and 3 (1.67 min, 95% CI: -1.85 to 5.19); time-averaged hazard ratios were consistent (Group 1 vs. 2, 9.80 [4.22-22.73]; Group 3 vs. 2, 7.63 [3.36-17.31]; Group 1 vs. 3, 1.20 [0.67-2.16]). However, there was no statistically significant difference observed between the vent port closure technique and the disconnection technique regarding the time required for complete lung collapse. papers.abstract_en: Two randomized trials, CALGB 140503 and JCOG0802, established segmentectomy as an oncologically acceptable alternative to lobectomy for small, peripheral, clinically node-negative non-small cell lung cancer. Both reached that conclusion under a protocol-enforced condition that is rarely emphasized when their results are applied in practice: nodal status had to be verified intraoperatively against a defined anatomic standard. CALGB 140503 required frozen-section confirmation of N0 status at two mediastinal stations and one major hilar node before randomization, whereas JCOG0802 mandated systematic or selective dissection of N1 and N2 stations in both arms and explicitly disallowed sampling as a substitute. This review examines whether that nodal rigor is reproduced, or even reported, once segmentectomy leaves the trial setting. National data indicate that it is not. Segmentectomy accounts for 4.4% of resections for clinical stage I to IIA disease, and only 12.6% of segmentectomy cases met all three Commission on Cancer quality measures, with adherence concentrated in academic and higher-volume programs. Retrospective series consistently report lower nodal upstaging after segmentectomy than after lobectomy, but the difference is driven by N1 rather than N2 stations and tracks the smaller nodal footprint of the operation, so a lower upstaging rate cannot by itself distinguish less disease from less looking. Anatomic mapping data indicate that exhaustive intersegmental dissection is unnecessary, whereas reliable hilar and mediastinal sampling is not. Across the wider literature, adequate nodal evaluation is defined inconsistently and reported at a granularity too coarse for readers to verify compliance, a two-axis problem that we characterize here for the segmentectomy literature specifically. Robotic assistance increases the number of nodal stations harvested relative to video-assisted surgery but has not been shown to improve risk-adjusted detection of occult disease. We propose a seven-point minimum standard, anchored on station-based rather than count-based adequacy, for segmentectomy performed outside a clinical trial.

papers.abstract_en: Red blood cells (RBCs) modulate host inflammatory responses by scavenging mitochondrial and pathogen DNA. However, how RBC surface properties govern the capture of tumor-derived DNA remains poorly understood. We show that RBCs tether and retain tumor-derived DNA on their surface, forming a distinct circulating pool of RBC-bound tumor DNA (rtDNA). Desialylation increased DNA capture in a Toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9)-dependent manner, identifying RBC surface sialylation and TLR9 as regulators of DNA binding. In mice bearing lung cancer xenografts, rtDNA was detected in all animals and its abundance correlated with tumor burden, whereas tumor DNA was undetectable in matched plasma samples. In patients with lung cancer, the majority of detected mutant tumor DNA was associated with RBCs rather than plasma, and RBC-derived mutations were concordant with molecular alterations identified in matched tumor tissue. Collectively, these findings establish the RBC surface as a tunable site of tumor DNA capture and retention and challenge the plasma-centric paradigm of liquid biopsy by identifying a distinct cellular reservoir of tumor-derived genetic material.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) features a poor prognosis and unclear pathogenesis, and the role of R-loops, key regulators of genome stability, has not been systematically characterized in this disease. METHODS: Transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing data of ESCC were integrated with published R-loop-related genes (RLRGs) to construct an RLRG scoring system. The associations between the RLRG score and prognosis, tumor immune microenvironment, and tumor stemness were analyzed via multiple bioinformatics algorithms. The expression of core genes was verified using reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), Western Blot, immunohistochemistry, and immunofluorescence. RESULTS: Seven key RLRGs related to the prognosis of the ESCC patients were identified, among which three core genes-BRIX1, CHEK1, and NUP155-were significantly upregulated in ESCC tissues compared with controls, as confirmed by both bioinformatic analysis and experimental validation. Notably, BRIX1, CHEK1, and NUP155 were co-enriched in DNA replication, pyrimidine metabolism, RNA degradation, and MYC target pathways, which are closely linked to R-loop biology and suggest potential crosstalk between these genes and R-loop regulatory networks. Meanwhile, the low RLRGs score group exhibited significantly worse overall survival but displayed a more active yet dysfunctional immune microenvironment. Single-cell analysis identified SquamousEpithelium cells as the key cell type with the highest RLRG scores across five independent algorithms. Malignant SquamousEpithelium cells with high RLRG scores showed enhanced stemness and activation of pathways including JAK-STAT, hypoxia, and DNA repair. CONCLUSION: This study provided the first systematic characterization of the R-loop landscape in ESCC, suggests that SquamousEpithelium cells may play a key role in R-loop-associated progression and are identified as potential prognostic biomarkers with possible therapeutic relevance that requires functional validation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is highly prevalent and frequently undiagnosed, despite liver fibrosis being the strongest predictor of liver-related morbidity and mortality. We aimed to quantify Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index-based fibrosis risk and to evaluate guideline-recommended follow-up-FIB-4 documentation, confirmatory testing, and specialist referral-in a large US cohort. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of electronic health record data from the US All of Us Research Program. Among adults aged 35 years or older with sufficient laboratory data, FIB-4 scores were calculated from routinely captured biomarkers, classified as low (<1.3), indeterminate (1.3-2.67; 2.0-2.67 if aged ≥65 years), or high risk (>2.67), and described across sociodemographic and metabolic subgroups; associations with incident major adverse liver outcomes (MALO) were assessed with Cox proportional-hazards regression. We examined FIB-4 documentation, confirmatory testing, and specialty referrals within 365 days of the index FIB-4 date. FINDINGS: Among 136,004 participants (mean age 60.8 years [SD 13.5]; 79,365 [58.4%] female; 81,420 [59.9%] White, 21,779 [16.0%] Hispanic or Latino, 20,076 [14.8%] Black), 26,971 (19.8%, 95% CI 19.6-20.0) had indeterminate and 11,217 (8.2%, 8.1-8.4) high FIB-4-based fibrosis risk. Elevated risk was more frequent with cardiovascular disease (41.7% vs 25.6%), hypertension (30.7% vs 23.4%), and type 2 diabetes (29.7% vs 27.4%), rising from 25.6% with no metabolic comorbidities to 36.6% with four. FIB-4 documentation was rare, and fewer than 1% of high-risk participants underwent confirmatory testing or referral; referral was low across risk categories (0.19% high, 0.19% indeterminate, 0.25% low risk). MALO occurred in 1308 (11.7%) high-risk vs 830 (0.8%) low-risk participants (adjusted hazard ratio 19.68, 95% CI 17.88-21.67). INTERPRETATION: Routinely collected laboratory data identify substantial liver fibrosis risk in this volunteer US cohort, yet guideline-recommended follow-up is uncommon. Implementation strategies such as automated risk calculation and reflex-based testing pathways could reduce missed opportunities for earlier diagnosis and intervention. FUNDING: No specific funding was received for this study.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Smoking is the primary cause of lung cancer, the leading cause of cancer-related mortality in Norway. To inform disease modeling and tobacco control policies, including lung cancer screening, we estimated sex-specific, birth-cohort smoking behaviors among Norwegians born between 1950 and 2000 using national survey data. METHODS: We analyzed nationally representative cross-sectional survey data from 1978 to 2024 (n = 78,282) to reconstruct smoking trends and smoking intensity in Norway. We used a previously established Age-Period-Cohort modeling framework to estimate cohort-specific prevalence of daily ever-smoking, probabilities of smoking initiation and cessation, prevalence of daily current-smoking, and average cigarettes smoked per day (CPD). Analyses were conducted separately by sex assigned at birth for cohorts born between 1950 and 2000. FINDINGS: Daily ever-smoking prevalence peaked in the 1950 birth cohort, reaching 70% (90% CI 66%-91%) among males and 66% (90% CI 55%-89%) among females, alongside similar peaks in smoking initiation probabilities, 13% (90% CI 12%-24%) for males and 12% (90% CI 10%-23%) for females. Smoking cessation probabilities increased with age within each birth cohort, rising from approximately 0% to 5% over 40 years in earlier cohorts, compared with an increase from about 5% to 15% over 20 years from the 1965 birth cohort onward. Smoking intensity peaked at 15 CPD among males and 12 CPD among females. Although smoking intensity declined in both sexes after the 1975 birth cohort, it remained higher among males, with peak model-estimated CPD decreasing from approximately 13.5 to 10 cigarettes in males and from 11.5 to 7.5 cigarettes in females between the 1980 and 2000 birth cohorts. INTERPRETATION: Smoking behavior in Norway has changed across generations, with declining smoking initiation rates, increased smoking cessation, and lower cigarettes per day. Understanding these trends provides essential inputs to inform tobacco control and lung cancer prevention policies in Norway. FUNDING: Norwegian Cancer Society, National Cancer Institute of the National Institutes of Health, U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Childhood socioeconomic position (SEP) influences later health, but how inequalities persist into early older age and operate through adult SEP remains unclear. Quantifying these pathways is important for identifying opportunities to reduce health inequalities over the life course. We therefore used an interventional causal mediation framework to quantify the contribution of four distinct dimensions of adult SEP to childhood socioeconomic inequalities in self-reported and objective health outcomes in early older age. METHODS: We analysed data from the 1958 British Birth Cohort collected at birth, ages 33 and 55, and the most recent sweep, when participants were aged 60-66 years. Sample sizes ranged from 4014 to 8363 depending on the outcome. We examined the extent to which four dimensions of adult SEP - adult occupational class, education, housing tenure, and income - mediated associations between childhood SEP, measured by paternal occupational class at birth, and self-rated health (SRH), C-reactive protein (CRP), cholesterol ratio, glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), and NT-proBNP. FINDINGS: Among men, occupational class mediated 39% of the association with poorer SRH (indirect effect RR 0.90, 95%: CI 0.86-0.95), and education mediated 27% (0.93, 0.90-0.96). Among women, mediation was smaller and most evident via education (10%; 0.95, 0.91-0.98) and housing tenure (6%; 0.97, 0.94-0.99). Mediation was limited for CRP and minimal for cholesterol ratio, HbA1c, and NT-proBNP. INTERPRETATION: Improving adult SEP could reduce, but is unlikely to eliminate, early older-age health inequalities associated with childhood SEP, highlighting the importance of interventions across the life course. FUNDING: UK Economic and Social Research Council.

papers.abstract_en: IntroductionZenocutuzumab-zbco is the first approved therapy for NRG1 fusion-positive cancer, indicated for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), and cholangiocarcinoma (CCA). At the pivotal analyses, overall survival (OS) was unreported for NSCLC and PDAC, whereas a later publication reported observed OS and progression-free survival (PFS) for CCA. Cost-effectiveness was evaluated from a US payer perspective.MethodsA three-state partitioned survival model estimated incremental costs and quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs) over 5 years. For NSCLC and PDAC, OS was modeled as a threshold variable across prespecified scenarios, with an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) per scenario. For CCA, OS and PFS were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves and used directly, with a base-case ICER and extrapolation sensitivity. The wholesale acquisition cost was $24,155.46/infusion. Probabilistic, one-way, and threshold analyses were performed.ResultsFor NSCLC and PDAC, ICERs ranged from approximately $665,000 (PDAC, OS 18 months) to $2.79 million per QALY (NSCLC, OS 10 months). For CCA, using observed data, the base-case ICER was approximately $397,000 per QALY (extrapolation range $349,000-$430,000). No indication was cost-effective at $150,000 or $200,000 per QALY. Drug acquisition cost, comparator OS, and utilities were the dominant drivers. Cost-effectiveness required acquisition-cost reductions of 60% to 91%.ConclusionsAt its current price, zenocutuzumab is not cost-effective for any approved indication, whether OS is unobserved (NSCLC, PDAC) or observed (CCA). Cost-effectiveness is achievable only through substantial price reduction. NSCLC and PDAC findings are conditional on the prespecified OS scenarios; CCA findings rest on observed survival with extrapolation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is highly heterogeneous, leading to limited drug effectiveness and resistance. Antibody therapies offer limited benefits due to low response rates. Multispecific antibodies, targeting multiple tumor antigens and natural killer (NK)-cell receptors, may overcome these challenges, but their effectiveness in ESCC therapy is not yet understood. METHODS: Transcriptome sequencing and database analysis were performed on samples from patients with ESCC to identify tumor antigens. Multispecific antibodies were designed to target tumor antigens and NK-cell surface markers. Fast protein liquid chromatography and surface plasmon resonance were applied for quality control of antibodies. Using multiple ESCC cell lines and NK cells from different donors, flow cytometry was performed to assess NK cell cytotoxicity and activation. Immunofluorescence assays were used to confirm colocalization. Transcriptome sequencing, flow cytometry and western blots were performed to explore molecular mechanisms. Subcutaneous and metastatic xenograft tumor models were established to evaluate the in vivo antitumor efficacy of antibodies combined with adoptive transfer of NK cells. RESULTS: The expression of EGFR was consistently highly expressed in all ESCC samples, while MET was specifically upregulated in recurrent ESCC, whereas the database also validated two antigens overexpression in tumor tissues. Antibodies were successfully engineered for multiple antigens binding. The tetraspecific antibodies significantly enhanced NK-cell cytotoxicity by up to 30% against ESCC and paclitaxel-resistant cell lines compared with the NK-only group in vitro. Transcriptomic analysis and experimental validation revealed that antibodies triggered immune activation pathways and increased the expression of tumor necrosis factor-α, interferon-γ, and granzyme B in NK cells, but also induced NK cell exhaustion. In vivo, tetraspecific antibodies combined with NK cell infusions exerted superior antitumor efficacy, with an 82.3% tumor volume reduction in the early-stage model and 65.7% in the advanced-stage model compared with controls. The therapeutic efficacy was also observed in the metastatic tumor model. Meanwhile, the combination therapy was well tolerated, with enhanced NK cell infiltration in tumor tissues. CONCLUSIONS: We developed tetraspecific antibodies to effectively bridge ESCC cells and NK cells. The antibodies have the potential to enhance the antitumor activity of NK cells against ESCC. This study supports the clinical translation of tetraspecific antibodies for NK cell-based immunotherapy for ESCC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) has greatly expanded the identification of rare germline variants in hereditary cancer predisposition. However, the interpretation of variants of uncertain significance (VUS), particularly in novel candidate genes, remains a major challenge in lung cancer genetics. OBJECTIVE: To functionally characterize selected germline variants identified by WES in patients with familial or suspected hereditary lung cancer and provide evidence for their prioritization. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Three splicing variants in HGS, CDK12, and CEACAM5 genes were investigated by RT-PCR and Sanger sequencing to assess their effect on splicing. Candidate missense variants were analyzed through protein-protein interaction network analysis, gene expression profiling, and structure-based computational modeling to evaluate their potential impact on protein stability and molecular interactions. RESULTS: RNA analysis confirmed that the CDK12 variant produced the previously reported in-frame one amino acid deletion, whereas the HGS variant activated a cryptic splice acceptor site, resulting in an in-frame deletion affecting a region containing a known ubiquitination site. No aberrant splicing was detected for CEACAM5. Network analyses highlighted convergence of three candidate genes (ERBB3, MAP2K1 and RASA2) on receptor tyrosine kinase signaling and the RAS/MAPK pathway. Structural analyses predicted local perturbations affecting membrane interactions, residue interaction networks, or protein stability for variants in the three previous genes and in USP4, supporting their functional relevance. CONCLUSIONS: Integrating RNA-based functional assays with network and structural analyses provides a practical framework for interpreting and prioritizing rare germline VUS identified by WES, supporting the identification of candidate lung cancer susceptibility genes and improving genetic risk assessment.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: HIV prevalence in prisons is three times higher than in the general community, and ongoing transmission risks highlight the importance of prevention, including pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP). We evaluated the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of prison-based PrEP programs in four US states. METHODS: We developed a dynamic compartmental model simulating HIV transmission in both general and incarcerated populations, instantiated for four representative US states (standardized population of five million people). We assessed five strategies involving PrEP for specific risk groups in prison compared to the status quo of no PrEP. We assumed 25% uptake among eligible individuals for 20 years. We estimated total lifetime costs (in 2024 USD) and quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), discounted at 3% annually, incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs), and HIV infections averted from a healthcare sector perspective. FINDINGS: In Washington, New York, and Georgia, providing PrEP to 25% of people who inject drugs (PWID) in prison prevented 12%-14% of new infections in incarcerated people, and 0.01%-0.02% of new infections in the community, and was cost-saving compared to no PrEP. Expanding eligibility to all high-risk persons (PWID and men who have sex with men (MSM)) prevented more infections and cost less than $60,000 per QALY gained compared to more restrictive policies. In California, where the epidemic is concentrated among MSM rather than PWID, providing PrEP to only MSM costs $32,000 per QALY gained. INTERPRETATION: Prison-based PrEP programs can be cost-saving or cost-effective, averting infections within and outside the prison system. These findings support expanding access to PrEP in prisons, with implementation and funding decisions guided by local HIV epidemiology. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Oropouche virus (OROV) is transmitted by the biting midge Culicoides paraensis. Historically, it was restricted to small outbreaks in the Amazon region. Since 2023, genomic reassortment and human-environment interactions facilitated its geographic expansion, including into urban areas. We estimate the OROV attack rate and identify factors associated with infection in an urban area outside the Amazon. METHODS: A randomised cross-sectional serosurvey in the urban area of Baturité, Brazil. Households were selected using stratified probability sampling proportional to census tract population; one resident per household was randomly chosen. Participants completed a questionnaire, and serum samples were tested for OROV IgM using MAC-ELISA. Associations were estimated using prevalence ratios (PR) with 95% confidence intervals from Poisson regression with robust variance. Spatial clustering of seropositives was assessed using kernel density and nearest-neighbours. FINDINGS: Of 392 participants, 212 were seropositive (54·0%). Most infections were asymptomatic/oligosymptomatic (72·6%-154/212). Living near rivers (PR = 1·80; 95% CI: 1·20-2·50) and working from home (PR = 1·70; 95% CI: 1·30-2·30) were associated with higher prevalence of infection. Clustering of seropositivity was found in census tracts close to cultivated and forested areas, and in central urban neighbourhoods. INTERPRETATION: We show large-scale urban OROV transmission, with attack rates exceeding 50%. The high proportion of infections among low mobility individuals suggests peridomestic transmission and vector adaptation to urban microenvironments. Results highlight the need to incorporate OROV into routine surveillance, outbreak preparedness, and differential diagnoses of acute febrile illnesses. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: International guidelines recommend sterile water for endoscopic irrigation despite limited evidence. Single-use plastic sterile water bottles generate substantial costs, greenhouse gas emissions, and microplastics. We sought to estimate whether replacing sterile water with potable tap water for endoscopic irrigation affected clinical outcomes. METHODS: This quasi-experimental study involved an interrupted time series design at a multi-campus tertiary care academic health system (The Ottawa Hospital, Canada). All adults undergoing esophagogastroduodenoscopy, colonoscopy, flexible sigmoidoscopy, enteroscopy, ileoscopy, or pouchoscopy between February 2024 and August 2025 were included. A system-wide switch to tap water took place on February 10, 2025. The primary outcome was a composite of emergency department visits, unplanned admissions, or deaths within 7 days post-procedure. Infectious complications within 30 days constituted secondary endpoints. Data were obtained from validated institutional databases. Segmented regression modeled the weekly outcome proportion to estimate the step change post-implementation, with a non-inferiority margin of <0.5% absolute risk increase. FINDINGS: A total of 29,522 procedures were performed on 29,423 patients (18,863 pre-implementation; 10,560 post-implementation). Patient and procedural characteristics were comparable. The weekly proportion experiencing the primary outcome was 1.6% in both phases. The post-implementation step change was -0.40% (95% confidence interval [CI] -1.16 to 0.35), with the upper boundary of the 95% CI below the pre-specified non-inferiority margin of 0.5%. Results were similar for infectious complications (step change -0.23%, 95% CI -0.75 to 0.29). INTERPRETATION: Potable tap water was non-inferior to sterile water for endoscopic irrigation with respect to clinical outcomes. These findings provide an evidence base for revising current guideline recommendations that mandate sterile water for endoscopic irrigation. FUNDING: This project was supported by the 2024 Canadian Society of Colorectal Surgeons Research Operating Grant.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Dengue (DENV), chikungunya (CHIKV), and Oropouche (OROV) viruses co-circulate in Brazil and present with overlapping acute febrile syndromes, complicating clinical differentiation. Comparative data integrating clinical phenotyping and viral load dynamics across these arboviruses are limited. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study using linked surveillance and laboratory databases from Espírito Santo State, Brazil (2024-2025). We aimed to compare DENV, CHIKV, and OROV infections and to explore their virological correlates. Cycle threshold (Ct) values, used as a relative semi-quantitative proxy for viral RNA levels, were analysed within each virus to characterise temporal dynamics and clinical expression. Multinomial logistic regression identified clinical features associated with arboviral infection; associations between Ct values and clinical domain scores were assessed using multivariable linear regression adjusted for age, sex, and time since symptom onset. FINDINGS: Among 10,793 cases (4058 DENV, 2508 CHIKV, 4227 OROV), Oropouche affected older individuals (median age 49 years, interquartile range [IQR] 43-56) and was characterised by near-universal fever (97·8%), headache (96·2%), and intense arthralgia (86·4%), with fewer gastrointestinal and mucocutaneous manifestations. After adjustment for age, sex, and time since symptom onset, increased odds of arthritis (OR 5·22, 95% CI 4·08-6·68) and rash (OR 2·39, 95% CI 1·83-3·12) were observed for CHIKV versus OROV. Conversely, nausea (OR 2·98, 95% CI 2·52-3·53), vomiting (OR 2·54, 95% CI 2·01-3·21), and retro-orbital pain (OR 8·00, 95% CI 6·69-9·56) were positively associated with DENV versus OROV. Dengue and chikungunya showed progressive Ct increases over time, consistent with viral decay. Oropouche displayed a non-monotonic, with lower Ct values and higher systemic and musculoskeletal domain scores after adjustment for age, sex, and time since symptom onset. INTERPRETATION: The distinct clinical and temporal patterns identified provide descriptive foundations that may inform future development of diagnostic algorithms and sampling strategies, pending formal predictive validation. FUNDING: This study was partially funded by the Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa e Inovação do Espírito Santo (FAPES), with additional institutional support from the Brazilian Ministry of Health and the Government of the State of Espírito Santo.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: In patients with acute stroke, early withholding or withdrawal of life-sustaining therapies is associated with an increased risk of death. We used practice variation across nine European countries to assess whether this relation may be causal. METHODS: We performed a post hoc analysis of the PREvention of Complications to Improve OUtcome in elderly patients with acute Stroke (PRECIOUS) trial, a randomised clinical trial of metoclopramide, paracetamol, and/or ceftriaxone started within 24 h of symptom onset in older patients with acute ischaemic stroke or intracerebral haemorrhage (ISRCTN82217627). The frequency of early treatment restrictions, defined as those installed within 24 h after randomisation, was calculated per participating country and their relation with the primary outcome 'death at 90 days' was estimated through: 1) adjustment for confounders with regression analysis with inverse-propensity score reweighting; and 2) comparing patients enrolled in countries with and without early restrictions, adjusted for confounders with regression analysis. FINDINGS: Of 1493 patients enrolled in PRECIOUS between 2016 and 2022, 1451/1493 (97%) were included in this analysis, of whom 276/1451 (19%) had an early treatment restriction. The rate of these restrictions ranged from 0% to 48% across the participating countries. Patients with restrictions were more likely to die within 90 days (inverse propensity-weighted odds ratio (OR) 3.39; 95% CI 2.71-4.25). However, there was no difference in the rate of death at 90 days between countries with and those without restrictions (21.3% vs 23.5%, adjusted OR 1.39; 95% CI 0.8-2.39). INTERPRETATION: The use of treatment restrictions early after stroke varied widely across Europe. Although restrictions were independently associated with an increased rate of death, the comparison of death rates between countries with and those without such restrictions provides no indication that this relation is causal. papers.abstract_en: The rare HOXB13 G84E variant is one of few established high-risk prostate cancer (PrCa) variants, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms by which it drives tumor development remain unknown. Prostate tumors from six heterozygous G84E variant carriers and 18 non-carriers (wild-type) were examined using the Human AmpliSeq Transcriptome Gene Expression Panel, and proteomes were generated by mass spectrometry (SWATH). We identified a 799-gene expression profile and a 75-protein expression profile in G84E-positive tumors when compared with wild-type tumors. Cluster analysis revealed a top-ranked 23 protein profile, which mapped to lipogenesis pathways. Integration of transcriptome and proteome data revealed overlapping differential expression of three genes (NCLN, NFIB, and VASN), two of which have an established link to lipid metabolic pathways. Examination of publicly available transcriptome data from 493 primary PrCa tumors from the The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)   tumors revealed 52 tumors with a similar differential expression profile for these three genes. Herein, an innovative proteogenomic approach was used to map molecular changes unique to HOXB13 perturbation in prostate tumors, revealing upregulation of genes in the steroid metabolic, lipid biosynthesis, and fatty acid metabolic pathways.

papers.abstract_en: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a progressive cerebrovascular disease linked to immune dysregulation, yet T-cell metabolic reprogramming and regulatory T-cell (Treg) function remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated multi-omics approaches, including mass cytometry, single-cell RNA sequencing, bulk RNA sequencing, metabolomics, and flow cytometry to characterize T-cell metabolic alterations and Treg dysfunction in MMD, uncovering a key metabolic-immune axis. Compared with healthy controls, MMD patients showed chronic immune activation and broad suppression of amino acid, glycolytic, and fatty acid metabolic pathways. Although Tregs were aberrantly expanded, they displayed metabolic inflexibility, together with impaired intercellular communication. Single-cell transcriptomics indicated Treg-to-Th17 conversion, while flow cytometry confirmed increased IL-17A+ cells within the CD4+FOXP3+ compartment. Besides, these dysfunctional Tregs correlated with advanced Suzuki stages, ischemic stroke, and posterior cerebral artery involvement. Bulk transcriptomic and serum metabolomic analyses further confirmed coordinated immune activation and metabolic suppression at the gene, protein, pathway, and metabolite levels. These findings define a metabolic-immune axis in MMD in which metabolically constrained, functionally unstable Tregs may contribute to neuroinflammation and vascular remodeling, suggesting that restoring Treg metabolic fitness could represent a therapeutic strategy.

papers.abstract_en: Cerebral cavernous malformations (CCMs), which frequently predispose patients to strokes or seizures, primarily arise from endothelial specific loss-of-function mutations in the CCM genes, and occasionally accompanied by gain-of-function mutations in PIK3CA and MAP3K3. While the Hippo pathway is a well-established regulator of tissue homeostasis, its emerging relevance in vascular pathology particularly its precise role in CCM pathogenesis remains poorly understood. In this study, we demonstrate that CCM gene deficiency suppresses endothelial Hippo signaling, as evidenced by diminished LATS activity, alongside concomitant elevation of YAP expression and nuclear translocation in both human and mouse CCM lesions. Notably, endothelial-specific deletion of Yap mitigates CCM lesion formation, reinforces endothelial junctions, enhances inflammatory resistance, and decreases KLF4 protein levels in a CCM mouse model. Conversely, intracranial Adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated inhibition of LATS or activation of YAP promoted CCMs formation under Ccm2 deficiency. Mechanistically, under the dual coordination of negative regulation by LATS and positive regulation by MAP3K3, YAP orchestrates KLF4 transcriptional activity and protein stability. This is achieved through a direct interaction with KLF4 that shields it from β-TrCP-mediated proteasomal degradation, thereby driving CCM progression. Collectively, our findings unveil a novel dimension to Hippo pathway regulation and underscore YAP as a pivotal driver of CCM pathogenesis.

papers.abstract_en: Optimal patient selection for consolidative metastasis-directed radiotherapy (MDRT) after chemoimmunotherapy (CIT) remains uncertain in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) with exclusive distant metastasis, defined as distant metastasis without synchronous locoregional recurrence. This study was aimed at estimating the survival benefit of MDRT and identifying patients most likely to benefit. A total of 1083 patients from two independent centers were analyzed using a target trial emulation with cloning, artificial censoring, and inverse probability of censoring weighting. The emulation estimated a 4.2-month gain in 3-year progression-free survival (PFS) restricted mean survival time with the MDRT strategy (95% CI: 2.4-5.9; bootstrap p < 0.001). Eight survival machine-learning algorithms were developed and compared, among which the gradient boosting machine achieved 3-year PFS AUROCs of 0.875 in internal validation and 0.877 in geographical external validation. Heterogeneous treatment effects were further estimated using a T-learner framework across risk groups defined by recursive partitioning analysis. In the external cohort, model-estimated 3-year absolute risk reductions with MDRT were 21.6%, 14.7%, and 5.7% in intermediate-, low-, and high-risk groups, respectively. The framework was subsequently implemented as a web-based clinical decision-support system. These findings support individualized selection of consolidative MDRT after CIT and provide a practical framework for multidisciplinary decision-making.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Functional assays can assist individualised selection of treatment regimens by evaluating the ex vivo response of tumour cells to anticancer therapeutics. However, the two major strategies used to assess responses to targeted drugs, target-based profiling and phenotypic profiling, have inherent limitations. Target-based profiling does not directly capture downstream cell-fate outcomes, whereas phenotypic profiling provides limited mechanistic information on drug action. METHODS: Live-cell fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) microscopy was used to integrate the interaction between EGFRL858R and GRB2 with cellular phenotypic features, thereby predicting the efficacy of EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) at the single-cell level. RESULTS: The target-based drug score (T-score), derived from the interaction between EGFRL858R and GRB2 in living cells co-expressing CFP-EGFRL858R and YFP-GRB2, enabled evaluation of the on-target activity of EGFR-TKIs against EGFRL858R. The phenotype drug score (P-score), constructed from cellular phenotype features, characterised the phenotypic responses induced by EGFR-TKIs. The TP-score, integrating the T- and P-scores, accurately predicted the efficacy of EGFR-TKIs. In living H3255 cells, the TP-score of osimertinib (OSI) was higher than that of gefitinib (GEF). Notably, in H3255 cell-derived xenograft (CDX) mouse models, OSI showed superior in vivo antitumour efficacy compared with GEF. Furthermore, live-cell TP scoring revealed that primary tumour cells from a patient with NSCLC did not respond to OSI, a finding consistent with the absence of actionable EGFR mutations in this patient. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates the clinical feasibility of predicting EGFR-TKI efficacy by integrating EGFRL858R-GRB2 interactions with cellular phenotypic features in single living cells.

papers.abstract_en: UNLABELLED: Cancer cachexia is a debilitating wasting syndrome associated with involuntary weight loss, reduced appetite and food intake, adipose and muscle atrophy, and systemic inflammation with induction of a myriad of candidate cachexia factors. Using a multi-omic approach in a genetically engineered mouse model of lung cancer cachexia, we found that early circulating metabolic alterations preceded overt weight loss. Although both cachexia and fasting are characterized by a reduction in food intake, we show that the systemic metabolic changes in cachexia are distinct, indicating a lack of induction in the normal protective response to negative energy balance during cachexia. Cancer cachexia causes profound hepatic reprogramming, and activation of inflammatory programs, alongside muscle atrophy and elevation of circulating cytokines. However, targeting individual candidate cachectic factors such as IL-6, TNF-α, GDF15, CCL2, LIF, and IL17A failed to rescue weight loss or prolong survival. In contrast, caloric restriction initiated prior to tumor induction elicited a program of protection during tumor progression that attenuated multi-tissue inflammatory and catabolic transcriptional responses, preserved lean mass, and prolonged survival. Together, these findings suggest that metabolic preconditioning broadly dampens systemic inflammation and delays the onset and progression of cancer cachexia. HIGHLIGHTS: Despite both fasting and cachexia involve reduced nutrient intake, the metabolic alterations are distinct.Cachexia induces a systemic inflammatory response.Single targeting of implicated cachectic factors fails to rescue weight loss or survival in cancer cachexia.Caloric restriction pre-conditioning to enforce the protective response to nutrient limitation attenuates cachexia.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary resection is a primary treatment for patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer, but removal of lung tissue can result in significant changes in postoperative pulmonary function and patient recovery. This review examines changes in pulmonary function tests (PFTs) and patient-reported outcomes following lung resection, with consideration of differences among surgical procedures and postoperative timepoints. Across studies, pulmonary function demonstrated its greatest decline during the early postoperative period, followed by gradual improvement during subsequent follow-up. However, pulmonary function generally remained below preoperative values, with the magnitude of decline influenced by the extent of lung tissue removed. Patients undergoing lobectomy or pneumonectomy generally experienced greater postoperative reductions than those undergoing sublobar procedures, although outcomes also varied according to the lobe and number of segments resected. Patient-reported outcomes, including dyspnea, pain, physical function, and quality of life, similarly worsened during early recovery but generally improved over time, with some measures returning to baseline. Preoperative pulmonary function, particularly DLCO, remains important for assessing a patient's ability to tolerate resection, while postoperative oxygen requirements are influenced by pulmonary function, patient characteristics, and postoperative complications. Additionally, decreased physical activity after surgery was associated with non-recovery of DLCO. Overall, postoperative pulmonary function follows a pattern of early decline followed by gradual recovery, although complete return to baseline is uncommon. These findings emphasize the importance of evaluating both pulmonary function and patient-reported outcomes when considering the consequences of pulmonary resection.

papers.abstract_en: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has become a biomarker-driven disease, yet durable control remains limited by therapeutic resistance, metabolic heterogeneity, and incomplete predictors of response. Cuproptosis, a copper-dependent form of regulated cell death linked to mitochondrial respiration and lipoylated TCA-cycle proteins, offers a potential metabolic layer for patient stratification. However, the current NSCLC literature is dominated by cuproptosis-related gene scores, lncRNA models, and immune-association signatures. These studies are useful for hypothesis generation but rarely demonstrate copper flux, FDX1 dependence, lipoylated DLAT/DLST engagement, iron-sulfur cluster protein loss, or pathway-specific pharmacodynamics. We therefore organize the NSCLC literature using a mechanistic evidence matrix that separates transcriptomic association, copper-access enrichment, mitochondrial-dependence evidence, canonical target engagement, and clinical pharmacodynamic confirmation. Rather than proposing a new molecular subtype or diagnostic label, we conceptualize cuproptosis susceptibility as a continuous, mechanism-based construct defined by copper access, TCA/OXPHOS dependence, lipoylated substrate burden, detoxification capacity, and immune context. This framework reframes cuproptosis from universal copper toxicity to a conditional therapeutic vulnerability. Its clinical value will depend on biomarker-enriched trials with pharmacodynamic confirmation rather than retrospective gene signatures alone.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Multiple myeloma (MM) frequently causes osteolytic bone disease and skeletal symptoms. Proteasome inhibitors (PIs) are central to MM treatment and in routine practice, PI-based therapy is preferentially selected for patients with more active or symptomatic disease. Hereby, PIs may also exert bone-modulating effects beyond their antimyeloma activity. Whether these biological effects are reflected in patient-reported outcomes or skeletal symptoms during routine care remains unclear. METHODS: We prospectively enrolled 209 patients with MM during routine interdisciplinary follow-up and stratified them by current PI-based versus non-PI-based treatment status. Sixty-nine patients were reassessed after at least 6 months. Patient-reported outcomes and skeletal symptoms were evaluated using multivariable regression and sensitivity analyses addressing baseline imbalances and treatment selection. RESULTS: Seventy-eight patients (37%) were currently receiving PI-based treatment. In adjusted analyses, current PI-based treatment status was not associated with Quality of Life (β = -0.08, 95% CI -0.45 to 0.29; p = 0.662), health-related status (β = -0.06, 95% CI -0.42 to 0.30; p = 0.740), bone pain (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.48 to 1.74; p = 0.791), or prevalent osteolytic lesions (OR 1.26, 95% CI 0.53 to 2.96; p = 0.601). QoL and health-related status remained comparable during follow-up. MM-related bone pain was numerically more frequent among patients currently receiving PI-based treatment (46% vs. 33%), although the association did not reach statistical significance after multivariable adjustment (OR 1.80, 95% CI 0.93 to 3.48; p = 0.081). CONCLUSIONS: In this prospective real-world cohort, current PI-based treatment status was not associated with measurable differences in global patient-reported outcomes, overall bone pain, or prevalent osteolytic lesions compared with non-PI-based treatment. MM-related bone pain was numerically more frequent among patients currently receiving PI-based treatment, although the association did not reach statistical significance after multivariable adjustment. These findings provide a real-world description of patient-reported and skeletal outcomes according to current treatment status but do not establish whether the biological effects of proteasome inhibitors on bone remodeling translate into clinically meaningful patient-reported or structural skeletal benefits.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Clinically important deterioration (CID) has been used to assess chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) progression by time-to-first-event analysis. However, this does not reveal the clinical importance of the CID components. The win ratio may provide a complementary assessment by comparing outcomes according to a prespecified hierarchy. We reanalysed data from the Tie-COPD studywith win ratio to assess the overall treatment benefit associated with tiotropium in patients with mild-to-moderate COPD. METHODS: In this exploratory post hoc study, the unmatched win ratio method was applied to the outcomes observed in the Tie-COPD study comparing 18 µg tiotropium with placebo in patients with mild-to-moderate COPD over 24 months. CID was defined as an occurrence of moderate-to-severe exacerbation, an increase of ≥2 units in COPD Assessment Test (CAT) score or a decrease of ≥100 mL in the forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1). We evaluated the win ratio across all possible hierarchies of CID components. Exploratory inverse-probability-of-censoring weighted (IPCW), and covariate-adjusted IPCW (CovIPCW) analyses were performed to account for censoring. Subgroup analyses were performed with stratification by sex, smoking status, Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease stage, CAT score and modified Medical Research Council score at baseline. RESULTS: Of the 841 randomised patients, 771 were included in the full analysis set (tiotropium=388; placebo=383). With the clinical hierarchy of CID defined by FEV1, exacerbation and CAT, the win ratio was 2.26 (95% CI 1.87 to 2.73, p<0.001), and the net benefit was 0.35 (95% CI 0.27 to 0.44, p<0.001). Win ratios were greater than 1 across all hierarchies, subgroups and censoring-adjusted analyses. No treatment-by-subgroup interaction was detected (all p for interaction >0.05). CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory post hoc analysis, tiotropium was associated with a greater overall treatment benefit than placebo in patients with mild-to-moderate COPD. This benefit was also observed in patients with mild disease or fewer respiratory symptoms. The direction of the findings was consistent across alternative CID hierarchies and censoring-adjusted analyses. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT01455129.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: As cancer survival improves, cardiovascular disease (CVD) has emerged as a major competing cause of death. However, population-level evidence on the burden of pre-existing and post-cancer CVD remains limited. This study aims to quantify pre-existing and post-cancer newly documented major CVD and their association with mortality outcomes among people with cancer. METHODS: Major CVD was identified using linked hospital records among 344,336 adults registered with primary invasive cancer in the New South Wales Cancer Registry from 2006 to 2016. The cohort was followed up until 31 December 2021. Fine-Grey modelling estimated sub-distributional hazard ratios (sHR) for cancer and cardiovascular mortality, and Cox proportional hazard modelling estimated hazard ratio for mortality from any cause across 20 common cancers. RESULTS: Overall, 18% (n = 62,675) of participants had pre-existing CVD within 5 years before cancer diagnosis, varying by age (3% for age < 50 vs. 40% for ≥ 80). Of those without pre-existing CVD (n = 281,661), 27% (n = 76,924) had post-cancer newly documented CVD, with the highest age-standardised incidence rates in pancreatic cancer (716 per 10,000 person-years), followed by lung (657). The median follow-up period was 6.8 years with an interquartile range: 2.1-10.3 The sHR of pre-existing CVD for cancer mortality ranged from 0.99 (95% CI: 0.85-1.13) in cancer of kidney to 1.81 (95% CI = 1.71-1.91) in lymphoma, and for cardiovascular mortality, 1.98 (1.78-2.18) in lymphoma to 4.74 (4.39-5.09) in pancreatic cancer. The sHR of post-cancer newly documented CVD for cancer mortality, ranging from 0.87 (95% CI: 0.69-1.05) in liver cancer to 2.33 (95% CI = 2.04-2.62) in cervical cancer and cardiovascular mortality, ranging from 1.45 (95% CI: 1.18-1.72) in myeloma to 3.39 (95% CI = 2.90-3.88) in liver cancer. CONCLUSION: CVD is prevalent both before and after cancer diagnosis, with strong relations to increased cancer, cardiovascular and all-cause mortality. Population-based strategies to strengthen holistic survivorship care and address key risk factors are essential to improve both cancer and cardiovascular outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the relationship between the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) and prognosis in patients with oesophageal cancer undergoing radiotherapy, and to evaluate the incremental prognostic value of combining SII with clinical TNM stage. METHOD: A retrospective analysis was performed on 159 patients with locally advanced oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma who received radiotherapy. The optimal cut-off value for pre-radiotherapy SII was determined using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, and patients were stratified into low- and high-SII groups accordingly. Univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses were employed to identify independent prognostic factors. The predictive performance of SII alone, TNM stage alone, and their combination was compared. Primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). RESULTS: The optimal pre-radiotherapy SII cut-off was 506.63. SII showed a tendency to increase during the course of radiotherapy. Short-term efficacy in the low-SII group was significantly better than that in the high-SII group (p = 0.042). Significant differences were observed between the two groups in 1-year, 3-year, and 5-year OS and PFS rates (all p < 0.05). Multivariate Cox regression analysis identified tumour location, TNM stage, gross tumour volume, and pre-radiotherapy SII as independent prognostic factors (all p < 0.05). The area under the curve (AUC) for the combination of SII and TNM stage in predicting survival was significantly larger than that of SII or TNM stage alone. The combined SII-TNM model demonstrated superior predictive performance compared with either parameter individually (both p < 0.05). CONCLUSION: Pre-radiotherapy SII serves as an independent prognostic factor in oesophageal cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy, with higher SII values associated with poorer survival outcomes. Integrating SII with TNM stage provides enhanced predictive accuracy for prognosis in this patient population.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Somatic alterations in the RAS-RAF-MAPK and PI3K pathways are key in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet their distribution, co-occurrence patterns, and clinical significance remain incompletely defined. We characterized RAS/MAPK- and PI3K-pathway alterations in a large cohort and assessed their prognostic implications. METHODS: We analyzed whole-exome sequencing data from 1243 paired samples from patients with CRC. Somatic variants in KRAS, NRAS, HRAS, BRAF, and PIK3CA were analyzed to quantify frequencies, codon-level distributions, and co-occurrence patterns. Descriptive somatic mutation status and demographic and clinical characteristics were evaluated using chi-square or Fisher exact tests, and associations with overall survival (OS) were evaluated using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: Any RAS-family mutation was detected in 507 tumors (40.8%); KRAS, NRAS, and HRAS mutations occurred in 35.3%, 5.4%, and 0.6%, respectively. BRAF V600E was detected in 85 tumors (6.8%), PIK3CA in 221 (17.8%), and KRAS G12C in 38 (3.1%). KRAS codon 12 was the dominant RAS hotspot. KRAS-PIK3CA co-mutations occurred in 126 tumors (10.1% overall; 28.7% of KRAS-mutant tumors), whereas KRAS-BRAF and KRAS-NRAS co-mutations were uncommon, consistent with MAPK pathway mutual exclusivity. RAS-mutant tumors were enriched in right-sided and microsatellite-stable disease (p < 0.001 for both). KRAS, BRAF V600E, and PIK3CA mutation frequencies were higher in right-sided than left-sided tumors. In unadjusted analyses, Hispanic patients had lower KRAS, BRAF V600E, and PIK3CA mutation frequencies than non-Hispanic patients. After adjustment for age, sex, tumor location, and MSI status, the associations with KRAS and PIK3CA were attenuated, whereas the lower frequency of BRAF V600E among Hispanic patients persisted (p < 0.01). Mutation status was not significantly associated with 5-year overall survival. CONCLUSIONS: RAS/MAPK and PI3K pathway alterations in CRC varied primarily by tumor subtype and molecular context, with clinically relevant co-mutation patterns and a targetable KRAS G12C subset. These findings may support future clinical trials targeting the BRAF-RAS axis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) shows marked heterogeneity in its immune microenvironment, which may contribute to differences in disease-free survival (DFS) and clinical outcome. Although current LUAD classifications are largely based on genomic or transcriptomic features, immune subtypes defined directly from bulk proteomic data remain poorly characterized. Here, we used an immune-cell proteomic reference matrix to investigate proteome-defined immune states in LUAD and to identify prognostically relevant immune subtypes. METHODS: A quantitative human immune-cell proteomic reference matrix was integrated with LUAD tumor proteomic profiles. The reference matrix covered seven major immune lineages and 26 immune-cell states. The discovery cohort included 101 LUAD tumor proteomes with matched clinical information. After gene symbol matching and normalization, proteome-defined immune-cell state signals were estimated for each sample using non-negative constrained regression. These signals were then used for unsupervised subtype identification and DFS analysis. An independent Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC)-LUAD cohort was used for validation, with subtype analysis performed at the immune-cell marker protein module level. RESULTS: The immune-cell reference matrix contained 8400 quantified proteins, and 2381 proteins were retained for modeling. Based on 26 proteome-defined immune-cell state signals, LUAD samples separated into two immune proteomic subtypes. In the discovery cohort, Subtype 2 had significantly worse DFS than Subtype 1 (log-rank p = 0.0047; HR = 2.09, 95% CI 1.24-3.54). In the Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC)-LUAD validation cohort, marker protein module-based analysis again identified two subtypes with distinct DFS outcomes. The high-risk Subtype 2 showed higher Granulocyte and Myeloid/DC modules, whereas the low-risk Subtype 1 showed higher B cell, T cell, and NK-cell modules. Subtype 2 was associated with shorter DFS in the validation cohort (log-rank p = 0.0061; HR = 3.45, 95% CI: 1.35-8.82), and this association remained significant after adjustment for age, sex, and stage. CONCLUSIONS: Proteomic immune profiling identified two prognostically distinct immune subtypes in LUAD. The poor-DFS subtype was characterized by increased myeloid/granulocyte-related protein modules, whereas the favorable-DFS subtype showed stronger B cell-, T cell-, and NK cell-related signals. These findings support the use of bulk tumor proteomics to characterize clinically relevant immune heterogeneity in LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Evidence on the prevalence, trajectory, and predictors of cancer-related cognitive impairment (CRCI) in newly diagnosed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients remains limited, particularly regarding the role of physical activity patterns. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of CRCI, assess changes in objective and subjective cognitive functions, and identify predictors of CRCI, focusing on physical activity trajectories among patients newly diagnosed with NSCLC in Hong Kong. METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted with 327 NSCLC patients newly diagnosed within 4 weeks. Cognitive function was objectively assessed using the HK-MoCA 5-Minute Protocol and subjectively measured using the FACT-Cog scale at baseline and monthly for six months. Physical activity patterns were analyzed through group-based trajectory modelling. Multivariate logistic regression identified predictors of CRCI, adjusting for demographic and clinical factors. RESULTS: The prevalence of objective CRCI ranged from 17.5% to 29.1% over the 6-month period, with 24.1% affected at 6 months. Three distinct physical activity trajectories emerged: consistently low (43.1%), consistently high (11.9%), and declining from high to moderate activity (45%). Both consistently high and declining physical activity trajectories were associated with a significantly reduced CRCI risk (93.8% and 85.9% lower risk, respectively) compared to the consistently low activity group. Consistently high physical activity trajectories were also correlated with better objective and subjective cognitive performance. Additional predictors of CRCI included lower baseline perceived cognitive function and self-efficacy for exercise. CONCLUSION: This study provides novel evidence that physical activity trajectories are associated with CRCI in newly diagnosed lung cancer patients.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer screening (LCS) remains underutilized, with 18% uptake nationally, despite established evidence-based guidelines, particularly among women who engage with preventive care through breast cancer screening (BCS). We characterized baseline LCS uptake and its correlates among women receiving BCS at two participating hospitals. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using six years of electronic health record data (October 2019-November 2025) from Barnes-Jewish West County Hospital and Christian Hospital. Women aged 50-80 with any documented smoking history were included. The primary outcome was LCS uptake, defined as evidence of at least one low-dose computed tomography scan. We conducted multivariable logistic regression models and assessed for effect modification by race and area deprivation using likelihood ratio tests. Results Of 9,686 women with smoking history, 3,209 (33.1%) had received at least one LCS. Pack-year documentation status (AOR 2.90; 95% CI: 2.63, 3.19), tobacco cessation medication use (AOR 2.21; 95% CI: 1.98, 2.48), and current smoking (AOR 1.84; 95% CI: 1.64, 2.07) were the factors most strongly associated with uptake. Non-Hispanic Black women had lower adjusted odds of obtaining LCS compared to non-Hispanic White women (AOR 0.87; 95% CI: 0.78, 0.98); estimates in the smaller pack-year subgroups were similar in direction but imprecise. Alcohol use was associated with lower odds of LCS uptake (0.81, 95% CI: 0.73, 0.89). Effect modification by race and area deprivation were not significant. Conclusions Baseline LCS uptake exceeded the national average; however, racial disparities were observed. Completeness of smoking history documentation, tobacco cessation medication use, and current smoking status were strongly associated with LCS uptake. These findings highlight the need for strategies to improve smoking history documentation and promote tobacco cessation efforts in cancer screening programs and establish the baseline against which the Pink & Pearl program, a co-located breast and lung cancer screening initiative at these sites, will be evaluated.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The 8th American Joint Committee on Cancer postneoadjuvant pathologic stage grouping is the current standard for risk stratification after neoadjuvant therapy and esophagectomy. However, its prognostic ordering may be unstable in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, particularly across intermediate stage groups. METHODS: Patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma who underwent neoadjuvant therapy followed by esophagectomy at two centers were retrospectively identified. The West China Hospital cohort was used for development, and the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University cohort was used for external validation. Recursive partitioning analysis using routine ypT and ypN categories was applied to develop a revised stage grouping. Prognostic ordering, model fit, and discrimination were compared with the 8th American Joint Committee on Cancer postneoadjuvant stage grouping. RESULTS: Among 1486 patients, 872 were included in the development cohort and 614 in the validation cohort. The revised system grouped patients into 5 prognostic categories and restored an ordered survival gradient in both cohorts, whereas the current American Joint Committee on Cancer stage showed survival overlap and inversion between stages II and IIIA. The revised system showed higher linear trend chi-square and likelihood ratio chi-square values and lower Akaike information criterion values in both cohorts. Concordance index and time-dependent area under the curve values were comparable between the two systems. CONCLUSIONS: The revised ypT/ypN-based stage grouping improved prognostic ordering and model fit in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, while maintaining comparable discrimination. This approach may support postoperative risk stratification after neoadjuvant therapy and esophagectomy.
