papers.abstract_en: Epigenetic age, influenced by environmental factors like smoking, predicts mortality in general populations but remains under-explored in early-stage lung cancer. We analyzed blood DNA methylation from 75 Boston Lung Cancer Study participants with early-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), of whom 63 died during follow-up. Epigenetic age acceleration (EAA) was estimated using Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, and GrimAge2 clocks and assessed using Cox models and random survival forests (RSFs). Across clocks, EAA significantly predicted survival in early-stage NSCLC. GrimAge2 EAA achieved the highest predictive accuracy (C index = 0.73±0.04) and emerged as the dominant predictor of survival among RSF models (variable importance = 5.7%), surpassing smoking and age. GrimAge2 EAA showed a non-linear association with mortality in which current smokers had >10% higher predicted mortality risk than former or never smokers at equivalent EAA, a pattern confirmed in Kaplan-Meier analyses. GrimAge2 EAA is a promising biomarker for personalizing risk stratification alongside traditional clinical factors.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Garsorasib (D-1553) is an orally administered selective KRAS G12C inhibitor. We report results from group 1 of the phase 1b D1553-101 study assessing garsorasib plus pembrolizumab and platinum-based chemotherapy in participants with KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic NSCLC. METHODS: Eligible participants had locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with KRAS G12C mutation and were candidates for pembrolizumab plus platinum-based chemotherapy. Participants received garsorasib 600 mg once daily or twice daily combined with pembrolizumab 200 mg once every 3 weeks plus 4 to 6 cycles of cisplatin or carboplatin and pemetrexed (nonsquamous histology) or carboplatin and paclitaxel (squamous histology). The primary end points were safety and the incidence of dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs). RESULTS: As of February 24, 2024, 17 participants received garsorasib 600 mg once daily (n = 10) or twice daily (n = 7) combined with pembrolizumab plus platinum-based chemotherapy. Overall, 94% of participants experienced grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events (AEs), and 88% had a dose reduction or interruption due to treatment-related AEs. One participant in the twice-daily group experienced a DLT of grade 2 diarrhea; no other DLTs occurred. Among all participants, the objective response rate was 59%, and the median progression-free survival was 7.4 months. CONCLUSION: In participants with KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC, despite an encouraging signal of efficacy, the incidence of treatment-related AEs with garsorasib plus pembrolizumab and platinum-based chemotherapy was high, and participants frequently had dose modifications or interruptions due to treatment-related AEs. Based on these findings, the study did not proceed to phase 2. CLINICALTRIALSGOV IDENTIFIER: NCT04585035.

papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) provide durable tumor control in some patients, but resistance can develop through tumor-intrinsic and microenvironmental mechanisms. This narrative review examines the metabolic and immune conditions under which ferroptosis may enhance ICI responsiveness or resensitize selected ICI-refractory tumors. Radiotherapy (RT) increases oxidizable phospholipids and can repress SLC7A11, the light-chain component of system xc-. ICI-activated CD8+ T cells provide convergent interferon-γ signaling. Tumors can resist this pressure through GPX4, FSP1-CoQ10, mitochondrial DHODH, NRF2-dependent programs, and iron-export pathways. Recent preclinical studies have tested RT with ferroptosis-directed interventions and ICIs. These studies include functional evidence of ferroptosis dependence in radioresistant lung cancer and resensitization of LKB1-deficient, primarily ICI-refractory tumors. The findings support a preclinical rationale for combination therapy, although their causal strength varies. Reversal of clinically defined acquired ICI resistance remains unestablished, and the clinical RT-ICI studies reviewed here did not measure ferroptosis in patients. The immune effects also vary by cell type. Tumor-cell ferroptosis may support immunity, whereas lipid peroxidation in CD8+ T cells, dendritic cells, or polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells can impair antitumor responses. Translation will require functional validation, cell-resolved biomarkers, achievable drug exposures, and evaluation of RT dose, fractionation, and sequence alongside normal-tissue and immune-cell safety.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) has evolved dramatically over the past decade with the advent of widespread genetic testing, immunotherapy, and targeted therapies. Treatments directed against epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and other driver mutations have reduced toxicity and improved efficacy for selected patients. CASE PRESENTATION: We present a 59-year-old man with metastatic NSCLC harboring coexisting EGFR, BRCA1, and RNA-binding motif protein 10 (RBM10) mutations and high programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression. A BRCA2 mutation was later detected on peripheral blood testing. The patient presented with a debilitating stroke that included dysphagia and hemiparesis. During his course of care, he received osimertinib, after which EGFR and RBM10 variant allele frequencies (VAFs) increased on peripheral blood testing. He also received immunotherapy and olaparib. Despite high response rates reported in the literature, he did not respond to these agents. He had a response to chemotherapy but tolerated it poorly. Ultimately, given the lack of durable response and his inability to tolerate chemotherapy, the patient opted for palliative care. DISCUSSION: Patients with actionable targets such as EGFR, BRCA1/2, or elevated PD-L1 generally have superior outcomes with targeted and combination therapy compared with patients who lack targetable options. However, coexisting mutations can interact and provide escape mechanisms. The lack of response in our patient is consistent with studies showing reduced efficacy of EGFR-directed therapy in the presence of RBM10 loss-of-function (LOF) alterations. Further research in patients with multiple concurrent mutations is needed to improve treatment options for this group.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Oncogenic KRAS mutations drive 25-30% of western lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) cases, however the mechanisms that restrain tumor progression remain poorly defined. N-Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein (N-WASP) regulates actin cytoskeleton dynamics and epithelial architecture, but its role in KRAS-driven lung tumorigenesis is unclear. METHODS: We generated a conditional N-WASP knockout in KRASG12D-driven lung adenocarcinoma mice (N-WASPLKO/KRASG12D) using Sftpc-CreERT2, and assessed N-WASP knockdown A549 cells (A549KD) in 3D culture for tumor burden, ERK signaling, transcriptomic changes, and E-cadherin expression. RESULTS: Conditional deletion of N-WASP in type II alveolar cells (N-WASPLKO) markedly increased tumor number and size in KRASG12D mice. The tumors isolated from these mice retained strong pro-surfactant protein C expression, confirming alveolar epithelial origin and predominantly adopted a solid growth pattern, indicative of disrupted epithelial organization. Mechanistically, N-WASP loss enhanced KRAS-driven ERK1/2 activation in lung tissue, consistent with increased mitogenic signaling. In A549 cells, N-WASP deficiency disrupted cytoskeletal architecture, promoted proliferation, and impaired cell-cell adhesion, recapitulating in vivo tumor phenotypes. A kinase inhibitor screen identified Rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK) activity as a driver of this hyperproliferative phenotype, with ROCK inhibition normalizing proliferation in N-WASP-deficient cells, linking elevated Rho/ROCK signaling to the increased ERK1/2 activation observed upon N-WASP loss. Transcriptomic profiling of N-WASP-deficient lungs revealed coordinated upregulation of genes regulating proliferation, cytoskeletal remodeling, and tumor-promoting pathways, alongside downregulation of epithelial differentiation and adhesion programs. CONCLUSION: These results establish N-WASP as a critical suppressor of KRAS-driven lung adenocarcinoma, linking cytoskeletal integrity to oncogenic signaling and transcriptional regulation. Our findings highlight the interplay between actin dynamics, epithelial architecture, and KRAS signaling, suggesting that targeting N-WASP dependent pathways could modulate lung cancer aggressiveness and offer novel therapeutic opportunities.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Cisplatin has been a standard chemotherapeutic agent for advanced non-small cell lung cancer for decades. Conventionally administered intravenously, it undergoes systemic distribution, exposing both tumour and healthy tissues to the drug. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle injection of cisplatin is emerging as a potential intratumoural drug delivery (ITDD) strategy. However, rigorous preclinical research is needed before ITDD can be more widely adopted. METHODS: We used our experimentally induced ovine pulmonary adenocarcinoma (OPA) model, generated by Jaagsiekte sheep retrovirus (JSRV) infection, to evaluate transthoracic and transbronchial ITDD techniques. We compared systemic platinum exposure following intravenous cisplatin delivery with that following intratumoural cisplatin administration. Both non-recovery and recovery studies were conducted in a total of eight sheep. RESULTS: ITDD techniques were successfully developed and performed in three tumour bearing sheep during non-recovery procedures. To provide a reference for systemic platinum exposure, intravenous cisplatin was administered to three JSRV-infected sheep that did not develop OPA. Intravenous administration produced a rapid plasma platinum peak followed by a rapid decline. ITDD resulted in preferential platinum deposition within targeted lung tumours while producing substantially lower systemic platinum exposure compared with intravenous administration. Intratumoural cisplatin delivery was also evaluated in a recovery procedure using a single sheep, comparing single-site and fractionated administration over a 28-day period, with tumour biopsies confirming lesion presence before treatment. Following ITDD, tumour volumes were observed to decrease over the study period. The recovery experiments demonstrated the feasibility of repeated tumour biopsies, intratumoural injections, longitudinal CT monitoring and recovery anaesthesia using the OPA model. DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this is the first report of direct intratumoural cisplatin administration into ovine lung tumours. This study also provides proof-of-concept that this clinically relevant large animal lung cancer model can serve as a translational platform for evaluating intratumoural therapeutic delivery strategies relevant to human lung cancer.

papers.results: 早期启动相对延迟启动每例患者多获得0.56个QALY（95% UI 0.32-0.83），增量成本为-US$43,902.94（95% UI -US$147,096.29 至 US$61,615.86），ICER为-US$78,398.11/QALY；在US$50,000/QALY的支付意愿阈值下，平均INMB为US$71,902.94（95% UI -US$36,663.51 至 US$176,658.91），90.6%的模拟中早期启动为优选策略。

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) are standard first-line therapy for psoriatic arthritis (PsA). Observational studies suggest earlier initiation is associated with superior minimal disease activity (MDA) attainment, yet the economic and health implications of treatment timing remain uncertain. This cost-utility analysis evaluated the cost-effectiveness of early versus delayed DMARD initiation in DMARD-naive adults with PsA from a U.S. payer perspective. METHODS: We built a cohort state-transition (Markov) model (monthly cycles, 15-year horizon) from published data (2000-2025). Patients initiated a DMARD under two strategies: early (≤1 year post-diagnosis) and delayed initiation (>1 year). Patients remained in the pre-treatment state for six months prior to response assignment, then transitioned among complete response (sustained MDA), partial response (non-sustained MDA), non-response, no treatment, and death. Primary outcomes included the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) and incremental net monetary benefit (INMB). Uncertainty intervals (UIs) were derived from probabilistic sensitivity analyses. FINDINGS: Early DMARD initiation provided an additional 0.56 (95% UI, 0.32-0.83) QALYs at an incremental cost of -US$43,902.94 (95% UI, -US$147,096.29 to US$61,615.86) per patient relative to delayed initiation, yielding a favourable ICER (-US$78,398.11/QALY). At a willingness-to-pay threshold of US$50,000/QALY, mean INMB was US$71,902.94 (95% UI, -US$36,663.51 to US$176,658.91), with early initiation preferred in 90.6% of simulations. INTERPRETATION: Early DMARD initiation was associated with improved long-term health outcomes at reduced costs, suggesting timely DMARD initiation may represent a high-value strategy. Given the observational basis of the key treatment-timing input, findings support disease-duration stratified analyses of existing phase III trials and further characterization of access delays. FUNDING: None.

papers.abstract_en: This study elucidates the distinct roles of Wrap53 isoforms (1α/1β) in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) radiosensitivity through integrated bioinformatics and functional analyses. Bioinformatics revealed Wrap53-associated enrichment in DNA repair and p53 pathways, with TCGA data linking its expression to prognosis and chemotherapy response. Functional studies demonstrated isoform- and p53 context-dependent effects: In p53-wild type A549 cells, Wrap53-1α silencing upregulated p53, enhanced radiosensitivity through Bax/Bcl-2-mediated apoptosis, and impaired DNA repair through RAD51 recombinase (RAD51)/Breast cancer susceptibility gene 1 (BRCA1) regulation. Conversely, in p53-mutant H1975 cells, silencing either Wrap53-1α or Wrap53-1β individually increased colony formation. Wrap53-1α was found to modulate post-radiation G2/M arrest through cyclin-dependent kinase 1 (CDK1) regulation, with effects contingent on p53 status. Importantly, Wrap53 expression correlated with differential chemosensitivity. High Wrap53 tumors showed increased cisplatin sensitivity but resistance to docetaxel, while low-expressing tumors were resistant to paclitaxel and vinca alkaloids. Our findings reveal a previously unappreciated inverse correlation between Wrap53-1α and p53 in LUAD cells and establish a molecular network where Wrap53 isoforms and p53 status collectively determine LUAD radiosensitivity.

papers.results: 识别出 11 个稳健的膳食-癌症关联：AHEI-2010 与 DASH 与结直肠癌风险呈负相关；AHEI-2010、aMED、CDAI、DASH 及反向 E-DII 与肾癌风险呈负相关；AHEI-2010、aMED 及反向 E-DII 与肺癌风险呈负相关；反向 E-DII 与较低总体癌症风险相关；DRLCD 无稳健关联。总体人群中 HR 最低者为 DASH（结直肠癌）、反向 E-DII（肾癌）、AHEI-2010（肺癌）；高 PRS 组中为 DASH（结直肠癌）、AHEI-2010（肾癌）、反向 E-DII（肺癌）。但 bootstrap 两两比较均无统计学显著性。

papers.ai_note: 摘要通篇未给出任何 HR、95%CI 或 P 值，仅以“稳健关联”定性表述，稳健性的判定标准（校正层级、滞后年限一致性阈值）未交代；6 种指数×多癌种存在大量多重比较，11 个“稳健关联”如何控制假阳性不明；主要分析定义（逐步校正+滞后敏感性）与探索性分析边界模糊，肺癌相关结果属探索性分析却与主要结果并列呈现；bootstrap 两两比较阴性后仍列举“最低 HR”排序，存在以排序替代统计检验的选择性强调风险；膳食暴露依赖 24 小时回顾自报，测量误差与残余混杂不可忽略。

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Previous studies on diet and cancer have mainly examined individual dietary indices in relation to specific cancer outcomes, limiting direct comparison across dietary patterns. A unified population with consistent adjustment and standardized dietary-index scales is needed to explore whether different dietary patterns show different statistical associations with each specific cancer outcome. METHODS: We included 118,056 cancer-free UK Biobank participants with at least two valid 24-h dietary assessments. Six predefined dietary indices were evaluated: DRLCD, aMED, AHEI-2010, DASH, CDAI, and E-DII. All indices were standardized to enable direct comparison. Progressively adjusted Cox regression models and 1-, 3-, and 5-year lagged sensitivity analyses were used as the primary analysis to identify the most stable diet-cancer outcome pairs. In the exploratory analysis, after excluding potential non-linear associations, standardized dietary indices were compared for colorectal, kidney, and lung cancers in the overall population and high genetic risk group to compare the direction and magnitude of associations across dietary patterns for each cancer outcome. RESULTS: Eleven robust diet-cancer associations were identified. AHEI-2010 and DASH were inversely associated with colorectal cancer; AHEI-2010, aMED, CDAI, DASH, and reversed E-DII were inversely associated with kidney cancer; AHEI-2010, aMED, and reversed E-DII were inversely associated with lung cancer; and reversed E-DII was associated with lower overall cancer risk. DRLCD showed no robust association. In cross-index comparisons, the lowest HRs in the overall population were for DASH (colorectal cancer), reversed E-DII (kidney cancer), and AHEI-2010 (lung cancer); in the higher PRS group, they were for DASH (colorectal cancer), AHEI-2010 (kidney cancer), and reversed E-DII (lung cancer). However, bootstrap pairwise comparisons were not statistically significant, suggesting directional trends, not evidence of superiority. CONCLUSION: We identified significant and stable diet-cancer risk associations and observed differences in the direction or magnitude of associations across dietary indices. Because bootstrap pairwise comparisons were not statistically significant, these findings should be interpreted as directional trends and hypothesis-generating, not as evidence of a definitively optimal dietary strategy or dietary superiority.

papers.authors: Rychalsky K, Luon D, Tracchia J
papers.affiliation_highlight: Smilow Cancer Hospital at Yale New Haven Hospital, New Haven, CT, USA.
papers.authors_conclusion: Tebentafusp and tarlatamab have established proof of concept for BTCE therapy in solid tumors, bridging the gap from hematologic malignancies. This class of therapy represents a promising platform for expanding applications across tumor types. Continued advances in target selection and strategies to overcome the tumor microenvironment and T-cell evasion barriers are expected to further expand the role of BTCEs in solid tumors.

papers.abstract_en: ObjectiveTo review the mechanism of action, clinical efficacy, safety considerations and future development of bispecific T-cell engagers (BTCEs) in solid tumors.Data sourcesA literature search was conducted using PubMed for clinical trials leading to FDA approvals and major oncology conference proceedings through February 2026. Major ongoing clinical trials were identified through a search of clinicaltrials.gov. Search terms included "bispecific T-cell engager," "BiTE," "solid tumors," "tarlatamab," and "tebentafusp." Prescribing information was also evaluated.Data summaryBTCEs are antibodies designed to redirect cytotoxic T-cells toward tumor cells through binding of CD3 and tumor-associated antigens. FDA approvals of tebentafusp for HLA-A*02:01-positive metastatic uveal melanoma and tarlatamab for extensive stage small cell lung cancer have established utility of BTCE therapy in solid malignancies, with improved outcomes over conventional chemotherapy and immunotherapy. BTCEs have unique toxicities, such as cytokine release syndrome, that must be monitored and treated appropriately. Ongoing investigations are evaluating novel targets, optimized molecular constructs to overcome development challenges, including toxicity and tumor microenvironment barriers, as well as combination treatment strategies to improve the efficacy of BTCEs in solid tumors.ConclusionsTebentafusp and tarlatamab have established proof of concept for BTCE therapy in solid tumors, bridging the gap from hematologic malignancies. This class of therapy represents a promising platform for expanding applications across tumor types. Continued advances in target selection and strategies to overcome the tumor microenvironment and T-cell evasion barriers are expected to further expand the role of BTCEs in solid tumors.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Mediastinal epidermoid cysts are exceptionally rare benign lesions, particularly in the anterior mediastinum. Their nonspecific clinical and radiological features may resemble other anterior mediastinal masses, including thymic lesions and mature cystic teratomas, making preoperative diagnosis challenging. CASE PRESENTATION: A 35-year-old man with no relevant medical or surgical history presented with a 2-month history of retrosternal chest pain. Clinical examination and cardiac evaluation were unremarkable. Chest radiography demonstrated mediastinal widening, while contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed a well-defined anterior mediastinal mass measuring approximately 7 × 5 × 3 cm. CT-guided biopsy and fluid aspiration initially suggested a mature cystic teratoma without immature or malignant elements. The patient underwent complete excision using a three-port video-assisted thoracoscopic approach. Intraoperatively, the cyst was densely adherent to the pericardium and contained thick purulent material. Hair-like material and firm cartilage-like areas were observed grossly but were not confirmed histologically. Culture of the cyst contents yielded Staphylococcus aureus. Histopathological examination demonstrated a squamous epithelial lining with chronic inflammation, granulation tissue, and fibrosis, confirming an infected mediastinal epidermoid cyst. The discrepancy between the initial cytological impression and the final histopathological diagnosis highlights the limitations of imaging and needle biopsy in evaluating rare cystic mediastinal lesions. CONCLUSION: Complete surgical excision provides both definitive diagnosis and effective treatment. Epidermoid cysts should be considered in the differential diagnosis of cystic anterior mediastinal masses. Video-assisted thoracoscopic excision may be feasible in carefully selected patients, even in the presence of dense pericardial adhesions.

papers.abstract_en: ALK rearrangements are uncommon in lung squamous cell carcinoma, and neoadjuvant ALK inhibition remains investigational. We report a 52-year-old never-smoking female with stage IIIB ALK-positive squamous cell carcinoma treated with neoadjuvant lorlatinib for 12 weeks. Serial imaging demonstrated a 61% reduction in tumor size with nodal regression. The patient subsequently underwent a uniportal video-assisted thoracoscopic (uVATS) lobectomy, and final pathology revealed a complete pathological response (pCR) of the primary tumor. This case highlights the feasibility and safety of minimally invasive anatomical lung resection following neoadjuvant lorlatinib despite treatment-related hilar fibrosis and vascular-bronchial adhesions.

papers.abstract_en: Thymic cysts are uncommon benign lesions of the anterior mediastinum and are frequently detected incidentally on imaging studies. Microscopic thymoma and microthymoma are extremely rare microscopic thymic epithelial proliferations that are usually identified only by histopathological examination. Their relationship to thymic cysts and to each other remains poorly understood. A 54-year-old woman was referred to our institution after an anterior mediastinal lesion was incidentally detected on routine chest computed tomography (CT). Magnetic resonance imaging and fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/CT findings were consistent with a thymic cyst. Robot-assisted thoracoscopic resection of the cyst with the adjacent thymic tissue was performed for definitive diagnosis and treatment. Histopathological examination revealed a unilocular thymic cyst accompanied by two incidental microscopic thymic epithelial lesions within the adjacent thymic tissue: a 0.6-mm microscopic thymoma and a 2.0-mm Type A microthymoma. Based on their characteristic size and histological features, both lesions were diagnosed without additional immunohistochemical analysis. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient remains free of recurrence 18 months after surgery. To our knowledge, the coexistence of microscopic thymoma and Type A microthymoma adjacent to a thymic cyst is exceptionally rare. The close proximity and similar histological features of these lesions suggest that they may represent different stages within a continuous morphological spectrum of microscopic thymic epithelial proliferations rather than entirely distinct entities. Furthermore, this case highlights the potential value of careful pathological examination of thymic tissue adjacent to resected thymic cysts for detecting occult microscopic epithelial lesions and improving pathological assessment.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Thoracic SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated tumor (SMARCA4-UT) is a recently recognized, rare, and highly aggressive malignancy. No standard treatment has been established for unresectable disease, and the prognosis is generally poor. These tumors often grow rapidly, and bulky masses can cause clinically significant symptoms. CASE PRESENTATION: A 52-year-old man with a history of heavy smoking presented with chest and back pain. Imaging revealed a large mediastinal mass. A CT-guided biopsy demonstrated an undifferentiated neoplasm with complete loss of BRG1 (SMARCA4) expression, a high proliferative index (Ki-67 labeling index, 80%), and no evidence of specific lineage differentiation, findings consistent with SMARCA4-UT. Subsequent comprehensive genomic profiling revealed a SMARCA4 nonsense mutation and a high tumor mutational burden. The tumor was clinically unresectable and showed rapid progression, resulting in severe dyspnea and syncope due to marked extrinsic airway compression. Because a high-grade sarcoma was initially suspected before the final diagnosis of SMARCA4-UT was established, first-line doxorubicin plus ifosfamide (AI) therapy was administered, resulting in rapid symptomatic relief and a partial response. However, after three cycles of AI therapy, the disease progressed clinically with a left adrenal metastasis. Subsequent treatment with the immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) atezolizumab plus carboplatin and paclitaxel showed no objective response, and the patient died 6 months after the initiation of systemic therapy. CONCLUSION: This case suggests that doxorubicin plus ifosfamide may provide rapid but transient tumor shrinkage and symptomatic improvement in thoracic SMARCA4-UT with airway obstruction. This regimen may be considered when urgent tumor reduction is required to relieve impending airway compromise. However, early diagnosis may also be important because first-line ICI-containing regimens have been associated with improved clinical outcomes in thoracic SMARCA4-UT.

papers.title_zh: 人工智能在医学影像中的应用综述：印度视角下的放射诊断现状、AI素养缺口与本地化验证需求
papers.title_en: Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging: A Review of Radiodiagnosis in Indian Perspectives.
papers.authors: Das E, Mondal R, Dhor A, Basu T
papers.affiliation_highlight: Maulana Azad Medical CollegeNew DelhiIndia.
papers.authors_conclusion: AI literacy is no longer optional: the radiologist's role is not threatened by AI but transformed by it—from film reader to AI-augmented clinical imaging physician capable of extending world-class diagnostic care to underserved populations across India and globally.
papers.ai_note: 叙述性综述，摘要未见系统检索策略、纳入排除标准、文献筛选流程或偏倚风险评估，无法判断证据覆盖是否完整、是否存在选择性引用。摘要核心为立场性论述与背景统计（950件FDA清关器械、约75%属放射领域、<30%放射科医师能批判性评价AI研究、<20%接受过正式AI培训、放射科医师与人口比1:50,000对比WHO建议1:10,000、印度占全球TB负担26%），这些数字均未标注来源与年份，属背景引用而非研究结果，不宜作为证据引用。表述上“validated-and in controlled settings superior-performance”将外部验证与受控条件下的优越性并置，易被读作临床效能已确立；对肺结节检测等应用的落地限制、假阳性/工作流影响与前瞻性对照证据未在摘要中交代。摘要亦未说明利益冲突与本综述的方法学质量，需回到全文核实检索时限与引用结构。
papers.reason: 为胸部影像AI（肺结节检测等）的临床引入提供一个宏观背景：提示器械清关数量与真实世界验证、使用者判读能力之间存在落差，可用于论证AI工具上线前需本地化验证与使用者培训；但作为叙述性综述，不能作为疗效或诊断准确性证据引用。
papers.abstract_en: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become the most transformative development in radiology since digital imaging, with deep learning algorithms demonstrating validated-and in controlled settings superior-performance across pulmonary nodule detection, breast cancer screening, tuberculosis (TB) triage, acute stroke identification, and glioma segmentation. Over 950 AI/machine learning-enabled medical devices have received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration as of 2024, ∼75% within radiology, yet a consequential knowledge gap persists: fewer than 30% of practising radiologists can critically evaluate an AI study and fewer than 20% have received formal AI training. This review addresses that gap by providing a clinically accessible account of core AI concepts, major neural network architectures-including convolutional neural networks, U-Net, generative adversarial networks, vision transformers, and foundation models-the complete model development and validation workflow, and validated clinical applications across all major imaging modalities. We give dedicated attention to the Indian context, where an acute radiologist deficit of 1:50,000 against the World Health Organization-recommended ratio of 1:10,000, a 26% share of the global TB burden, and heterogeneous imaging infrastructure make AI both urgently necessary and uniquely demanding of local validation; we discuss the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, federated learning, and the domestic ecosystem of Qure.ai, Niramai, and Sigtuple as structural enablers, as well as algorithmic bias, explainability, and regulatory frameworks. We conclude that AI literacy is no longer optional: the radiologist's role is not threatened by AI but transformed by it-from film reader to AI-augmented clinical imaging physician capable of extending world-class diagnostic care to underserved populations across India and globally.

papers.abstract_en: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a highly aggressive malignant tumor which suffers from poor prognosis and limited therapeutic remedies. As a physiologically-oriented radiotherapy and highly tumor-specific modality, boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) shows great potential for the treatment of ESCC. Since efficacy of BNCT is critically restricted to boron drugs, novel boron agents with satisfactory boron load and intracellular uptake are highly demanded. Herein, we developed a novel albumin/BSH-conjugated nanoparticle (BSH@Alb) as a safe and effective boron agent. It resulted BSH@Alb displayed uniform particle size, high encapsulation efficiency (93.1 ± 0.39%), loading capacity (15.52 ± 0.41%) and good stability in different solution (water, PBS and plasma). Collectively, BSH@Alb significantly enhanced intracellular boron accumulation and showed acceptable cytocompatibility in comparison with prototype BSH, supporting its potential value for BNCT therapy as a promising boron-delivery candidate.

papers.abstract_en: Breast cancer and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) are most prevalent forms of malignancies worldwide and are associated with BRCA2 variants. While BRCA2 pathogenic variants are well established in breast cancer, their transcriptional consequences in lung adenocarcinoma remain poorly characterized, and no study has directly compared the shared differentially expressed gene (DEG) signature between BRCA2-variant metastatic breast cancer and BRCA2-variant LUAD. In this study, we used an integrative bioinformatics approach to identify and characterize this shared transcriptomic profile using publicly available TCGA and GEO datasets accessed via cBioPortal. Top dysregulated genes were subjected to protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis using STRING and Cytoscape (CytoHubba, MCC algorithm), functional enrichment through Metascape and survival analysis through UALCAN, with disease associations validated against the DISEASES database. SERPINA1, PIGR, FGG and FCGBP were identified as candidate hub genes, common in both types of malignancies. The breast cancer gene set was associated with impaired BRCA2-RAD51-mediated homologous recombination, and the lung dataset had strong signatures of alveolar type 2 (AT2) cells and signatures specific to lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). SERPINA1 and PIGR were significant markers in breast cancer and FGG was significant marker in LUAD. The findings identify a partially overlapping epithelial transcriptional profile associated with BRCA2-variant breast and lung tumor datasets. However, these observations represent associations within BRCA2-altered cohorts and do not establish that BRCA2 dysfunction directly drives the identified transcriptional changes. SERPINA1, PIGR, FGG, and FCGBP therefore represent candidate tissue-dependent biomarkers requiring independent validation.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Choroidal metastases may cause substantial visual impairment in patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although local ocular treatments are frequently considered, targeted systemic therapy may provide effective control in tumors harboring actionable mutations. We report the rapid regression of a choroidal metastasis following first-line osimertinib therapy in a patient with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated NSCLC. CASE PRESENTATION: A 59-year-old man with metastatic EGFR-mutated NSCLC presented with progressive visual decline in the left eye. Ophthalmic examination revealed a peripapillary choroidal lesion associated with serous retinal detachment. Optical coherence tomography demonstrated subretinal fluid, consistent with a choroidal metastasis. First-line osimertinib therapy had been initiated 12 days before presentation at our clinic. An early reduction in subretinal fluid was observed during follow-up, followed by complete resolution at the 2-month follow-up. This was accompanied by regression of the choroidal lesion and improvement in visual function. No local ocular treatment was required. CONCLUSION: First-line osimertinib may induce rapid regression of choroidal metastases in patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC. In selected cases, an early response to systemic targeted therapy may allow local ocular treatment to be avoided.

papers.abstract_en: The individual incidences of lung cancer and cardiovascular disease in the elderly population mean that there is a strong likelihood of both occurring simultaneously. Common practice for severe aortic stenosis (AS) would be surgical aortic valve replacement (AVR), unless deemed high-risk for this surgical procedure. Age and lung cancer both increase a patient's surgical risk; hence, the less invasive transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) to manage valve disease ahead of lung resection for lung cancer is an acceptable alternative after assessing other factors such as procedural risk, comorbidities, and prognosis. We present the case of an 82-year-old female patient who underwent a TAVI seven months before lung resection for an incidental diagnosis of lung cancer with staging T1b N0 M0. Postoperatively, she was treated for atrial fibrillation and lung collapse, then discharged after resolution of these complications on the eighth day after surgery, and remained well at follow-up three months later. This case report explores a situation when this sequence of interventions was appropriate due to increased surgical risk in the elderly population.

papers.abstract_en: Cardiac tamponade is a life-threatening emergency classically associated with Beck's triad of hypotension, muffled heart sounds, and elevated jugular venous pressure; however, incomplete or atypical presentations may delay diagnosis. We report the case of a previously healthy 28-year-old woman who presented with progressive dyspnoea, pleuritic chest pain, orthopnoea, peripheral oedema, fever, and fatigue. Examination revealed mild tachycardia, soft heart sounds, reduced basal air entry, and ankle oedema, while the patient remained normotensive. Initial investigations demonstrated cardiomegaly with pleural effusions on chest radiograph, low-voltage QRS complexes on electrocardiogram, and markedly raised inflammatory markers. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography identified a large anterior mediastinal mass encasing the great vessels, a significant pericardial effusion with features of cardiac tamponade, and bilateral pleural effusions. Emergency pericardiocentesis resulted in immediate clinical improvement. Histopathological analysis confirmed high-grade B-cell lymphoma, most consistent with primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma. The patient was treated with immunochemotherapy, achieving complete metabolic remission on end-of-treatment PET-CT. This case highlights the importance of recognising atypical presentations of cardiac tamponade and considering mediastinal malignancy in young patients presenting with unexplained cardiorespiratory symptoms.

papers.abstract_en: Endothelial dysfunction-induced platelet activation contributes to thrombosis in major cardiovascular diseases. Endothelial cells sense hemodynamic shear stress via the mechanosensitive ion channel Piezo1, which determines their physiological functions. However, the downstream transcriptional pathways of Piezo1 linking mechanical force to endothelial function remain incompletely defined. Here, nuclear receptor subfamily 4 group A member 1 (NR4A1) is identified as an endothelial mechanosensitive transcription factor induced by Piezo1 that modulates platelet activation and thrombosis. Mechanistically, shear stress is shown to activate Piezo1, resulting in calcium influx and the subsequent activation of protein kinase C δ (PKCδ), which activates extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) to induce NR4A1 transcription. NR4A1 then upregulates prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2 (PTGS2) expression, leading to the increased production of prostacyclin and inhibition of platelet activation and thrombosis. In vivo, mice with endothelial cell-specific deletion of Nr4a1 exhibit greater thrombus weights and faster occlusion. These data establish the Piezo1/Ca2+/PKCδ/ERK/NR4A1/PTGS2 signaling cascade as a critical endothelial mechanotransduction pathway that senses physiological shear force to transcriptionally promote an antithrombotic state.

papers.abstract_en: This study investigated the biochemical mechanisms by which rosmarinic acid (RA), a natural polyphenol, sensitizes A549 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cells to mild hyperthermia (43°C). A549 cells were treated with RA (100 or 200 μM) and exposed to mild hyperthermia (43°C, 30 min), after which we performed a comprehensive analysis of cell viability, clonogenic potential, and migratory recovery. The molecular underpinnings were explored through flow cytometry for reactive oxygen species (ROS) and cell cycle progression, together with western blotting for MAPK signaling (JNK, ERK), apoptosis-related proteins (Bcl-xL, survivin, caspases), and the heat-shock response (HSP27, 70, 90, and HSF1). Our results show that the combination of RA and hyperthermia impaired cell proliferation and migration while promoting S-phase accumulation and apoptosis. At the biochemical level, combined RA and hyperthermia increased intracellular ROS beyond the level produced by either treatment alone. This rise in ROS occurred alongside an altered p-JNK/total JNK profile and caspase activation-associated apoptosis. Importantly, RA suppressed the canonical heat-shock response, lowering the p-HSF1/total HSF1 ratio and reducing the expression of the molecular chaperones HSP27, 70, and 90. Pretreatment with N-acetylcysteine (NAC) attenuated the observed ROS, Annexin V, and immunoblot changes, consistent with a contribution of redox imbalance to this sensitization process. In conclusion, RA enhanced hyperthermia-induced oxidative stress and suppressed the HSF1-HSP axis in A549 cells, providing a rationale for its further preclinical evaluation as a biochemical adjuvant in hyperthermic lung cancer therapy.

papers.abstract_en: Therapeutic mRNA vaccines are a clinically validated cancer immunotherapy platform using in vitro transcribed mRNA encoding tumor antigens to induce durable anti-tumor immunity. Advances in mRNA engineering, lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery, and immunomodulatory combinations have propelled this approach from preclinical models to randomized trials with survival benefit. This review systematically examines vaccine efficacy through an antigen-delivery-immunomodulation tripartite framework. We trace the evolution from shared tumor-associated antigens to personalized neoantigens identified by computational pipelines, discuss ionizable lipid chemistry and LNP formulation for controlled tissue tropism and transfection, and analyze the bidirectional crosstalk between vaccine components and innate immune sensing that shapes adaptive T cell responses. Clinical evidence across melanoma, pancreatic cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, and other solid tumors is critically evaluated, alongside combination strategies-checkpoint blockade, oncolytic virotherapy, and adoptive cell therapy to overcome TME resistance. Persistent challenges include optimal neoantigen selection, standardized immune monitoring, and predictive biomarkers. We conclude that future research should prioritize systematic optimization of the tripartite design through multi-antigen targeting, tissue-specific delivery engineering, and rational combination immunotherapy, aiming to establish mRNA cancer vaccines as a standard-of-care modality.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Superficial pharyngeal cancers are frequently missed during routine endoscopy and remain challenging to diagnose, even with image advances such as digital chromoendoscopy. Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) has emerged as a minimally invasive, organ-preserving, therapeutic option. Pharyngeal ESD, however, requires awareness of specific anatomical and technical considerations, including narrower working space, thinner pharyngeal wall, proximity to vascular and neural structures, and the risk of airway impairment during the procedure. METHODS: A 71-year-old male patient had previously undergone subtotal esophagectomy for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). On follow-up endoscopy, after examination of the oral cavity and pharynx, a subtle flat lesion with minimal erythema was identified on the posterior wall of the oropharynx, extending distally to the hypopharynx and right piriform sinus, mildly brownish on virtual chromoendoscopy with preserved loop-like vessels. Biopsy confirmed high-grade dysplasia, and ESD was performed. RESULTS: Histopathology confirmed in situ SCC with free margins. The patient recovered uneventfully and was discharged after 2 days. Endoscopic follow-up revealed cicatricial retraction, and the patient remained asymptomatic. CONCLUSIONS: Careful inspection of the oral cavity and pharynx should be incorporated into routine endoscopy in patients at high risk for SCC, because early detection may allow curative treatment with minimally invasive endoscopic technique.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Dedifferentiated liposarcoma (DDLPS), a rare disease with limited research, exhibits resistance to radiotherapy and chemotherapy. Few reports have analyzed the tumor microenvironment of retroperitoneal undifferentiated liposarcoma using single-cell sequencing. METHODS: Single-cell analysis of three retroperitoneal DDLPS cases characterized the cellular and immune microenvironment. RESULTS: Our findings reveal significant heterogeneity among malignant cells in DDLPS, with chromosome 6 deletions being prevalent across malignant cell subpopulations and potentially linked to reduced immunogenicity based on pathway analyses. Notably, the coexistence of CD8 + T cell exhaustion and cytotoxicity reflects a continuum of exhaustion transition. Moreover, we identify a C3 + malignant cell subpopulation with ECM remodeling, angiogenesis, and activated complement pathway. Further exploration suggested that C3 + malignant cells may recruit IL2RA+ regulatory T cells and SPP1 + macrophages through the C3-C3aR1 axis. CONCLUSION: Our findings provide new insights into the application of immunotherapy in sarcoma.

papers.abstract_en: The 4-nitroquinoline-1-oxide (4NQO) model closely recapitulates oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) progression but is limited by cumulative toxicity in conventional protocols. This study aimed to develop a modified 4NQO regimen with defined carcinogen-free intervals and evaluate the chemopreventive potential of black tea-derived polyphenols. C57BL/6 mice were subjected to conventional and modified 4NQO regimens (50 and 100 ppm). Tumour incidence, multiplicity, and volume were assessed alongside histopathology. Systemic toxicity was monitored using body weight, fluid intake, and serum biochemistry. Chemoprevention was evaluated using thearubigins and decaffeinated extracts (1.5% and 10%) administered during pre- and concurrent intervention phases. Molecular analyses included western blotting and qualitative immunohistochemistry. The modified regimen improved body weight maintenance without compromising tumour incidence or progression. No significant differences in tumour burden were observed between the 50 and 100 ppm groups. Histopathological analysis confirmed the presence of lesions across the disease spectrum in all carcinogen-treated groups. In chemoprevention studies, tumour incidence remained unchanged; however, the 10% decaffeinated extract significantly reduced tumour volume, while thearubigins showed a non-significant trend. Molecular analyses revealed no statistically significant differences, though directional changes were observed. The modified protocol enables defined intervention windows, addressing limitations of continuous carcinogen exposure, and the reduction in tumour volume without changes in incidence suggests an effect on tumour progression rather than initiation. Collectively, the modified 4NQO model provides a robust platform for stage-specific chemoprevention evaluation, with black tea polyphenols, particularly decaffeinated extracts, demonstrating modest progression-modulating effects that warrant further investigation.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer is known to have a very high incidence and mortality rate. Trans-cinnamic acid (tCA) is a phenolic compound found in various fruits and vegetables and is known to have many effects such as antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory and anticancer. In this study, molecular docking analysis was performed to predict the binding affinities of tCA toward apoptosis- and ER stress-related target proteins. The effects of tCA on proliferation, apoptosis and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress gene expression, colony forming ability, total antioxidant status (TAS) and total oxidant status (TOS) in A549 human lung cancer cells were investigated. Cell proliferation and, expression levels of genes associated with apoptosis and ER stress determined using XTT and qRT-PCR, respectively. ELISA test was used for TAS, TOS and caspase-3 levels. Molecular docking analysis predicted favorable binding affinities of tCA toward the investigated target proteins. The IC50 value of tCA in A549 cells was found to be 2.59 mM at 48 h. Treatment with tCA significantly increased the expression of apoptosis genes including BAX, CASP3, CASP7, CASP8, CASP9, CYCS, and FADD. Among the ER stress-associated genes analyzed, only PERK and CHOP showed significant upregulation following tCA treatment, while no significant changes were observed in the remaining ER stress-related genes. Furthermore, tCA treatment caused a decrease in TAS level but an increase in TOS level. tCA suppressed the ability to form colonies in A549 cells according to the colony assay. In conclusion, tCA inhibited proliferation and colony formation, modulated selected apoptosis- and ER stress-related genes, and altered oxidative stress parameters in A549 cells. These in vitro findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the potential anticancer activity of tCA; however, further protein-level, functional, and in vivo studies are required to confirm the underlying mechanisms and therapeutic potential. The image outlines a study evaluating the anticancer effects of trans-cinnamic acid (tCA) on A549 lung cancer cells. Molecular docking analysis showed tCA has potential binding affinity to target proteins. In cell experiments, the IC50 of tCA was 2.59 mM at 48 h, determined by an XTT test. Treatment with tCA reduced TAS and caspase-3 levels while increasing TOS. RNA isolation and cDNA synthesis were followed by quantitative RT-PCR analysis, indicating that tCA may induce upregulation of ER stress and apoptotic markers in A549 cells. A colony assay demonstrated that tCA suppressed colony formation in these cells. ELISA assays for TAS, TOS, and caspase-3 were also performed as part of the analysis.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Recent advances in direct rat sarcoma (RAS) inhibition and downstream pathway targeting have created novel therapeutic strategies which can be utilized in gynecologic oncology. This review examines RAS biology, lessons learned from other malignancies, and emerging strategies for gynecological malignancies. RECENT FINDINGS: KRAS G12C inhibitors in lung cancer established the clinical feasibility of direct RAS targeting, while colorectal cancer studies demonstrated the importance of lineage-specific combinations. KRAS G12D inhibitors, targeted protein degraders, and multiselective RAS(ON) inhibitors represent the next frontier in RAS inhibition, expanding therapeutic options across both gynecologic and nongynecologic tumors. In recurrent low-grade serous ovarian cancer, therapeutic advances have centered on inhibiting the downstream RAS-mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK)-extracellular signal-regulated kinase signaling pathway using MEK or combined RAF/MEK and focal adhesion kinase inhibitors, rather than direct RAS inhibition, demonstrating encouraging clinical responses, leading to accelerated approval for KRAS-mutant disease. SUMMARY: RAS-pathway directed therapy requires consideration of tumor lineage, specific alleles, and functional pathway dependence. Although clinical progress in gynecologic oncology is most relevant in low-grade serous ovarian cancer, emerging non-G12C therapies warrant further evaluation across gynecologic malignancies. Novel combinations and integrated biomarkers will be necessary to improve patient selection and overcome therapeutic resistance.

papers.abstract_en: Pituitary metastases are uncommon, and most cases originate from breast or lung cancer. Tumor-to-tumor metastasis, in which one neoplasm metastasizes into another, is particularly rare in the sellar region. We report a 66-year-old man with metastatic sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma treated with modified FOLFOX6 (5-fluorouracil, L-leucovorin, and oxaliplatin) plus panitumumab; extracranial disease was controlled, whereas a sellar mass initially suspected as a pituitary adenoma slowly enlarged over 2 years. Endocrine testing showed anterior hypopituitarism without arginine vasopressin deficiency. Endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery was performed for continued enlargement and diagnostic uncertainty. Histopathology demonstrated a gonadotroph pituitary adenoma infiltrated by colorectal adenocarcinoma, with extensive intermingling of the 2 components rather than discrete nests, favoring tumor-to-tumor metastasis over a collision tumor. The metastatic component consisted of viable tumor cells without necrosis or convincing treatment effect despite prolonged chemotherapy. This case underscores that metastatic tumor within a pituitary adenoma may enlarge despite favorable systemic therapy outcomes. Metastasis should therefore remain a key differential diagnosis for a sellar mass radiologically suggestive of a pituitary adenoma.

papers.abstract_en: Neurodegenerative diseases are a growing cause of disability worldwide, particularly as populations age. Although these disorders differ in etiology and clinical presentation, advances in genetics, neuropathology, and biomarker research have identified shared disturbances in protein homeostasis, mitochondrial function, and immune regulation. These processes may contribute to selective neuronal vulnerability and neural circuit dysfunction. These findings are refining disease classification and diagnosis, yet effective disease-modifying therapies remain limited. Disease-specific abnormalities remain essential to clinical interpretation and treatment selection. Existing reviews often focus on individual disorders or isolated mechanisms, leaving the links between shared biology and disease-specific phenotypes insufficiently clear. We synthesize evidence on the epidemiology, risk factors, classification, and pathophysiology of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Huntington's disease, frontotemporal dementia, Friedreich's ataxia, and multiple sclerosis. We compare their clinical manifestations and diagnostic approaches, including the evolving role of biomarkers, and critically assess established and emerging therapies. By distinguishing shared mechanisms from disease-specific abnormalities, we identify key translational gaps and explore how common biological disturbances may lead to distinct clinical trajectories. This cross-disease perspective may inform diagnostic reasoning, treatment development, and future comparative research.

papers.abstract_en: MRI is a reference-standard modality for an expanding range of clinical questions, yet it remains among the most unevenly distributed technologies in medicine. Portable low- and ultra-low-field MRI, compact permanent-magnet systems that operate without cryogens or need for in-room radiofrequency shielding, have been proposed as a means of extending imaging to settings where fixed scanners are unavailable or cannot be reached safely. A growing evidence base indicates that these systems can address a defined set of high-value clinical questions, including the detection of intracerebral hemorrhage and large ischemic infarcts, the assessment of hydrocephalus, and the monitoring of critically ill patients at the bedside. This article synthesises the technical basis, clinical applications, and equity implications of portable MRI and argues that the technology's equity impact depends less on the device than on how it is implemented and financed. Consistent with the inverse-equity hypothesis, an imaging technology introduced without deliberate design tends to reach advantaged populations first, and may transiently widen the disparities it is intended to reduce. Drawing on implementation science, change management, and financial reasoning, this article reframes portable MRI as a socio-technical intervention whose equitable benefit depends on the coordinated design of three domains: (1) device capability, (2) implementation and organizational change, and (3) sustainable financing matched to local context. The Canadian setting, including remote and Indigenous communities, is used to illustrate both the opportunity and the conditions required to realize the benefits of portable MRI. A deployment framework is proposed to support radiology leaders and health systems.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To identify patients who may benefit from an interstitial brachytherapy boost in the era of hypofractionation and widespread use of simultaneous integrated boost. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Between 1984 and 2025, 112 articles were identified through a narrative search of the PubMed, MEDLINE, and Cochrane databases using the keywords "breast cancer", "boost", "interstitial brachytherapy", and "interventional radiotherapy". Two main areas were addressed: an update on risk factors and patient selection, and a review of boost techniques, with an emphasis on interstitial brachytherapy and comparisons with other techniques. Based on this evidence, we formulated recommendations on the role of brachytherapy boost in contemporary breast cancer (BC) treatment. RESULTS: Based on the available literature, the addition of a boost should be strongly recommended for patients aged <40 years, patients with positive margins, and patients aged <50 years with at least one of the following features: high-grade disease, extensive intraductal carcinoma, and/or a triple-negative phenotype. In other scenarios, including residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, a balanced shared decision should be made. Interstitial brachytherapy allows delivery of a high radiation dose to the target volume while significantly reducing the dose received by adjacent organs at risk. CONCLUSION: The use of brachytherapy as a boost has declined, particularly since the introduction of integrated and ultra-hypofractionated regimens. In the current era of breast cancer treatment, we suggest that brachytherapy remains a valuable option for selected high-risk patients because it enables dose escalation tailored to the risk volume while sparing surrounding organs at risk.

papers.abstract_en: The two earthquakes that recently struck the northern coast of Venezuela will deepen a health crisis that has troubled the country for twenty years. They have exposed how weak its health infrastructure is, how scarce medicines are, how little epidemiological surveillance remains, and how long investment has been lacking. The humanitarian health crisis in Venezuela did not arise from armed conflict, as it has elsewhere. Its roots lie in decades of authoritarian rule and institutional decay, which have eroded public health capacity, research infrastructure, vaccination coverage and the control of infectious diseases in general. Because these weaknesses have accumulated, the earthquakes may well turn into an even graver humanitarian emergency. Recovery that lasts will not be secured by short-term international aid alone. It will require the rebuilding of accountable institutions able to govern transparently and to apply equitable health policies, so that the health system can regain its resilience.

papers.abstract_en: Wild emmer wheat (Triticum turgidum ssp. dicoccoides, BBAA), the wild progenitor of cultivated tetraploid and hexaploid wheats, provides an important reference for investigating centromere reorganization during polyploidization and domestication. Here we generated a near-complete genome assembly of wild emmer wheat, including centromeric regions for all 14 centromeres. Comparative analyses with cultivated tetraploid and hexaploid wheats revealed extensive variation in centromere-associated sequences and centromere-proximal structure, as well as distinct subgenome-associated patterns in the A and B subgenomes. The A subgenome was characterized by positional shifts and sequence turnover of CRW-rich centromere-derived blocks, whereas the B subgenome showed reduced CentT566 satellite abundance accompanied by localized retention or expansion on specific chromosomes. These results provide a high-resolution tetraploid wheat reference and reveal subgenome-associated patterns of centromere remodeling during wheat polyploid evolution.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pediatric obesity is a major global public health challenge, associated with increased risk for numerous sequelae, persistence into adulthood, and growing economic burden. STARKIDS is a stepwise, tailored, e-health-enhanced, family-focused intervention in primary care. It integrates nutritional counseling targeting dietary energy density reduction, physical activity promotion, behavioral strategies, and psychosocial support. METHODS: We tested whether STARKIDS improves weight development and quality of life (QoL) compared with usual care. A cluster-randomized controlled trial was conducted in pediatric/family practices enrolling children/adolescents with overweight/obesity. Practices were stratified and block-randomized (no blinding) to STARKIDS or one-time counseling (optimized treatment-as-usual, TAU-O). Outcomes were assessed at baseline, 12, and 18 months. Primary outcomes were changes in BMI z-scores and QoL. Trial registration: DRKS00022813. FINDINGS: 89 practices were cluster-randomized (44 intervention, 45 TAU-O). Between April 2022 and July 2023, 379 families were assigned to STARKIDS and 232 to TAU-O. 343 and 216 families were included into the intention-to-treat analysis. After 12 months, 114 (33%) participants in the STARKIDS group and 47 (22%) in the TAU-O group achieved a BMI z-score reduction ≥0.2 (risk difference = 0.11, 95% CI 0.03, 0.20, p = 0.0256). After 18 months, no group differences in BMI z-score reductions were found (p = 0.6940). No significant differences in QoL were observed between study arms at either time point among adolescents. Among parents/guardians, a statistically significant between-group difference was observed at 18 months (-2.10, 95% CI -4.13 to -0.06; p = 0.044), though not considered clinically meaningful. No treatment-related serious adverse events were reported. INTERPRETATION: STARKIDS improved BMI z-score over 12 months with effects comparable to more intensive programs. The German Federal Joint Committee recommended transferring step 1 into routine care for children/adolescents with obesity. Effects were not sustained at 18 months, indicating a need for adaptations including additional contact hours to reinforce achieved outcomes, followed by a gradual reduction. FUNDING: Innovation Committee of the German Joint Federal Committee (G-BA).

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The triplet combination of hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC), a tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), and a programmed cell death-1 (PD-1) inhibitor has emerged as a highly promising strategy for unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC). This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the efficacy and safety of this triple-therapy compared with the dual-therapy of a TKI plus a PD-1 inhibitor. METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for randomized controlled trials or comparative cohort studies that assessed HAIC plus a TKI and a PD-1 inhibitor (H-T-P) versus a TKI plus a PD-1 inhibitor (T-P) for uHCC. The primary endpoints were overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR), and disease control rate (DCR). The secondary endpoint was treatment-related adverse events (AEs). A random-effects model was employed to pool data, calculating hazard ratios (HRs) or relative risks (RRs) with their 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: A total of 12 studies involving 2,386 patients with uHCC were included. Compared with T-P dual therapy, the H-T-P triple therapy was associated with significantly improved OS (HR, 0.51; 95%CI, 0.47-0.56; P < 0.001) and PFS (HR, 0.59; 95%CI, 0.51-0.68; P < 0.001). Furthermore, the H-T-P group demonstrated a significantly higher ORR (RR, 1.97; 95%CI, 1.73-2.24; P < 0.001) and DCR (RR, 1.19; 95%CI, 1.11-1.28; P < 0.001). Regarding safety, while no significant difference was observed in the overall incidence of all-grade AEs (P = 0.238), the incidence of grade ≥3 AEs was significantly higher in the triple-therapy arm (RR, 1.29; 95%CI, 1.13-1.48; P = 0.004), consisting primarily of manageable hepatotoxicity and hematologic toxicities. CONCLUSION: Our findings indicate that for patients with uHCC, the H-T-P triple-therapy regimen is superior to dual therapy in terms of survival benefits and tumor response. The associated increase in severe toxicity is considered predictable and clinically manageable. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251113276.

papers.abstract_en: For more than two millennia, Archimedean screws have been used for water pumping and, more recently, as turbines in hydroelectric power stations[1]. Their helical-blade structure, essential to their function, is also found in chiral molecules and nanostructures, where injected electric current has been proposed to generate torque-mediated rotation[2,3]. Here, we present a torque-driven molecular machine with a rotor actuated by electric current and conductance enhanced by its rotation. Suspending a helicene molecule between two electrode tips, we show that an applied voltage induces cyclic molecular motion with 100% directional preference that can be inverted by the voltage's polarity. Above a voltage threshold, the current through the rotating molecule is significantly enhanced, and the enhancement onset is tuned by stretching or compressing the helical molecule. Such effects were absent in previous helical molecular junctions, likely due to structural and operational differences[4-6]. Calculations show that molecular rotation by current-induced forces explains both the observed cyclic motion and current enhancement. This mechanism predicts a transition from stepwise to continuous rotation at a threshold voltage, yielding a current increase as rotation allows adopting highly conducting configurations not accessible at rest. Our work introduces a prototype for a new class of torque-driven molecular machines with perfect rotor unidirectionality and significant current modulation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: A recent population-based cohort study of Seoul residents in South Korea reported increased incidence of several cancers within one year of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. We examined whether a short-term, population-level change in cancer incidence trends was detectable at the national vaccination rollout, using a design that does not compare vaccinated with unvaccinated individuals. METHODS: We conducted an interrupted time series analysis of Korea National Health Insurance Service data for 36,024,394 individuals born between 1955 and 2004, covering February 2011 to September 2025 (176 months). The intervention point was August 2021, when cumulative first-dose coverage exceeded 50%. Monthly incidence of 13 cancer categories defined by ICD-10 code ranges and of four site-specific cancers (stomach, colorectum, lung and prostate) was compared with counterfactual forecasts from ARIMA/SARIMA models, and segmented regression estimated immediate level and trend changes (significance threshold P < 0.01). The placement of the intervention point was varied from 0 to 18 months, and the resulting estimates were compared with those obtained at 30 placebo points in the pre-pandemic period. RESULTS: Overall, 89.3% of the population received at least one dose. No immediate level change (relative risk 0.923-1.072) or trend change (0.995-1.005) reached significance for any of the 13 categories, and none reached significance for the four site-specific cancers. Across the lag grid, 2.0% of estimates met the threshold, compared with 4.1% at placebo points. The 99% confidence limits excluded immediate increases larger than 8.9% to 23.0% across the 13 categories and 8.1% to 23.4% across the four site-specific cancers. CONCLUSIONS: The national SARS-CoV-2 vaccination rollout in South Korea was not accompanied by a detectable short-term, population-level change in cancer incidence trends over the 50 months that followed. papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Patients with PD-L1-negative non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) often exhibit inherent PD-1 inhibitor resistance, leading to poor monotherapy efficacy and unfavorable clinical outcomes. Notably, no effective stratification biomarkers are currently available to overcome this resistance. Thus, this study aimed to reverse PD-1 inhibitor resistance in PD-L1-negative NSCLC by identifying novel predictive biomarkers and developing effective targeted immunotherapeutic regimens. METHODS: Pleural effusion-derived organoids (PEOs) were established and validated from driver gene wild-type, PD-L1-negative NSCLC patients. Four treatment groups were set: control, anti-PD-1 monotherapy (Toripalimab), anti-CD73 monotherapy (Uliledlimab), and anti-PD-1 + anti-CD73 combination (Toripalimab + Uliledlimab). ATP assay was used to detect tumor cell viability. Spearman's rank correlation analysis was applied to evaluate the association between CD73 expression and tumor inhibition rates. Flow cytometry was employed to measure T cell activation markers. Enzyme-linked Immunospot assay was used to detect IFN-γ and TNF-α secretion. RESULTS: PEO models recapitulated the biological features of primary pleural effusion. Toripalimab monotherapy showed no antitumor efficacy in PD-L1-negative subgroup regardless of CD73 expression levels, whereas Toripalimab + Uliledlimab combination significantly reversed PD-1 inhibitor resistance in CD73-high PD-L1-negative NSCLC patients. Furthermore, a significant positive correlation was observed between CD73 expression levels and tumor inhibition rates. CONCLUSION: This study validates CD73 as a potential predictive biomarker for stratifying PD-L1-negative NSCLC patients and establishes anti-PD-1+ anti-CD73 combination regimen that effectively reverses PD-1 inhibitor resistance in CD73-high PD-L1-negative NSCLC patients.

papers.reason: 启发式模式收录（未接入语言模型精评）：按期刊层级与研究类型自动入选。
papers.abstract_en: Urothelial carcinoma is a common urinary malignancy with high incidence, recurrence, and mortality. Early diagnosis is pivotal for improving patient outcomes. Current standards have important limitations: cystoscopy, although the cornerstone of diagnosis and surveillance, is invasive and costly, while cytology has limited sensitivity for low-grade or early-stage lesions. Urine, as a liquid biopsy, offers a non-invasive and repeatable approach for sampling urogenital pathology, with the potential for longitudinal monitoring through serial collection. The review covers urinary multi-omics biomarkers, including cfDNA/methylation, miRNAs, extracellular vesicles (EVs), and proteomic/metabolomic signatures. We summarize their performance in early detection, staging, and postoperative monitoring. Integrated multi-analyte models, including true multi-omics assays and multiplex single-omics panels, generally outperform single biomarkers, with some panels achieving >90% sensitivity and >95% specificity in prospective cohorts. Despite progress, several challenges remain: standardization, large-scale prospective validation, and regulatory/reimbursement barriers. We conclude that urinary multi-omics diagnostics are promising complementary tools that may optimize surveillance and risk stratification. Still, limited prospective validation, lack of standardization, and the persistent risk of false-negative results constrain adoption. On current evidence, they are not positioned to replace cystoscopy, which remains the cornerstone of diagnosis and surveillance, particularly in non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC). However, their most realistic and immediate clinical role is as a triage tool to optimize the selective use of cystoscopy-particularly for risk-stratifying patients with hematuria, adjudicating equivocal cytology, and potentially reducing the frequency of invasive surveillance in low-risk NMIBC patients.

papers.abstract_en: Genetic tests for lung cancer, such as the Oncomine Dx Target Test (ODxTT), are essential for patient management, and require RNA and DNA of sufficient quality and quantity from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) samples. ODxTT fails due to poor nucleic acid preservation. Although enhancing the penetration of formalin into tissues improves nucleic acid preservation, the clinical utility of negative-pressure fixation methods remains unclear. Therefore, we investigated whether the negative-pressure fixation method using a vacuum fixation device improves ODxTT success rates and the quality of nucleic acids in FFPE samples from lung and other cancers, and examined the underlying mechanisms. The ODxTT success rate was higher with the negative-pressure fixation method than with the conventional method (96.5% vs. 81.2%), accompanied by increased RNA quality and yield; however, no marked differences were observed in DNA. RNA deteriorated more rapidly than DNA in resected mouse liver tissues, indicating that RNA is more labile than DNA during cold ischemia. Furthermore, in FFPE samples from colon, pancreatic, and prostate cancers, negative-pressure fixation consistently improved RNA DV200. These results indicate that the negative-pressure fixation method improves ODxTT success by accelerating formalin penetration, which may suppress RNase-mediated RNA degradation and preserve RNA quality.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Timely and accurate characterization of breast lesions into different pathological classes through noninvasive imaging techniques is crucial for early cancer diagnosis and effective patient management. This study aims to develop a novel, explainable attention-based deep network to analyze radiomic patterns for predicting heterogeneous breast cancer types using ultrasound imaging. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A multicentric retrospective dataset comprises brightness-mode ultrasound images of breast tissue collected across five different centers/databases. A total of 3256 images, having biopsy-proven 2068 benign and 1188 malignant lesions, were analyzed. A lightweight and computationally scalable network, WinDWS-SwinNet, is developed for binary and multipathology breast cancer classification. An optimized image preprocessing algorithm is proposed to enhance ultrasound radiomic features, thereby improving data generalizability and diagnostic accuracy. RESULTS: The WinDWS-SwinNet architecture demonstrated superior performance in breast cancer classification, achieving an area under the curve of 0.96, an overall test accuracy of 95.79%, and robust class-wise results with 95.11% precision and 98.51% sensitivity for benign tumors and 97.13% precision and 90.86% sensitivity for malignant tumors. For multipathology classification, the model achieved a test accuracy of 93%, with class-wise accuracies ranging from 94% to 99.5%. External validation on the independent unseen dataset resulted in an accuracy of 95.36%, highlighting the robustness and generalizability of the proposed model beyond the training data. CONCLUSION: The developed methodology shows promising results in characterizing breast lesions into pathological subtypes noninvasively, effectively mimicking real-world diagnostic workflows, thereby supporting radiologists in reducing diagnostic uncertainty and enhancing confidence in clinical decision-making.

papers.abstract_en: How PTEN function is impaired in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) without detectable genomic alterations remains unresolved. We investigated whether the long isoform of fatty acid-binding protein 6 (FABP6L) contributes to this process. Analyses that distinguished FABP6 isoforms identified FABP6L as the principal tumour-upregulated variant, whereas the short isoform, FABP6S, did not show a comparable increase. SHOX2 depletion preferentially reduced FABP6L expression. Biochemical experiments linked FABP6L to increased association between PTEN and the E3 ligase WWP2, enhanced PTEN polyubiquitination, and reduced PTEN protein stability. These changes were accompanied by increased AKT/mTOR signalling. Gain- and loss-of-function experiments supported a growth-promoting role for FABP6L in cultured ccRCC cells and xenografts, while genetic rescue experiments indicated a major contribution of PTEN to the signalling and growth phenotypes. In preclinical models with reduced everolimus sensitivity, FABP6L depletion increased PTEN abundance and enhanced the response to mTOR inhibition. The findings support an isoform-specific mechanism connecting FABP6L to PTEN turnover and ccRCC growth. They also provide a basis for investigating FABP6L-directed approaches to improve everolimus response, although their clinical relevance requires further validation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: People who inject drugs (PWID) may engage in sexual behaviours that increase their HIV and hepatitis C virus (HCV) risk, including sex work and male-with-male sexual activity. We undertook a global systematic review to assess whether PWID who engage in these behaviours have higher HIV and HCV acquisition risks. METHODS: In this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched MEDLINE, Embase, and PsycINFO for studies among PWID published between 01/01/2000 and 09/06/2026 that included estimates of the association between male-with-male sex or sex work and our primary outcomes of HIV or HCV incidence. Studies that estimated incidence by longitudinally re-testing people at risk of infection or by using assays for recent infection were eligible for inclusion. We also contacted authors for unpublished estimates. We pooled estimates using random-effects meta-analysis. We used I2 to assess heterogeneity, and we used Egger's test to assess publication asymmetry. This review is registered with Prospero (CRD42020220884). FINDINGS: We included 57 studies comprising 164 estimates. Among men, recent male-with-male sex was associated with higher HIV acquisition (pooled incidence rate ratio (IRR):2.35; 95% CI: 1.51-3.66; I2: 51%).) but not HCV (IRR: 1.28; 95% CI: 0.95-1.72; I2: 21%). Recent sex work had a 1.72-fold (95% CI: 1.30-2.28; I2: 65%) and 1.59-fold (95% CI: 1.29-1.96; I2: 60%) higher HIV and HCV acquisition risk among all PWID, respectively. When stratified, sex work was associated with higher HIV acquisition among women (IRR: 2.30; 95% CI: 1.44-3.68; I2: 68%) but not men (IRR: 1.43; 95% CI: 0.92-2.22; I2: 51%), and was associated with HCV acquisition among men (IRR: 1.51; 95% CI: 1.22-1.87; I2: 0%), but not women (IRR: 1.26; 95% CI: 0.90-1.77; I2: 55%). For lifetime behaviours, only male-with-male sex was associated with HIV acquisition (IRR: 2.44; 95% CI: 1.18-5.02; I2 = 87%). Results from Egger's tests did not provide evidence of asymmetry bias for our pooled estimates, while I2 measures suggested considerable heterogeneity for many outcomes. INTERPRETATION: PWID who also engage in sex work or male-with-male sex were found to have higher HIV or HCV acquisition risks. Future research should aim to understand the mechanisms driving these associations. papers.abstract_en: UNLABELLED: Digital technology is a ubiquitous part of adolescent life, yet progress in understanding its implications for health and development is constrained by the lack of standardised, developmentally appropriate measurement tools. This systematized scoping review, conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, identifies and evaluates instruments used to measure adolescent digital technology use between 2014 and December 14 2025. Searches in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science yielded 533 peer-reviewed studies, from which 135 validated measurement instruments were identified. We extracted data on instrument characteristics and conducted a secondary search to evaluate psychometric properties using adapted COSMIN criteria. Most tools relied on self-reported frequency or duration of use, with 63% designed to detect problematic behaviours-such as social media addiction or gaming disorder-often using adult-derived clinical criteria. Fewer than 2% of instruments assessed positive or developmentally beneficial use. Tools frequently lacked adolescent-specific content, cultural adaptation, and validation across sociodemographic subgroups, and objective or multi-method measures were rare. Current measurement practices are heavily risk-focused and often insufficiently tailored to adolescents' developmental and sociocultural contexts. This review lays the foundation for WHO's efforts to develop more balanced, psychometrically robust, and culturally sensitive approaches to measuring adolescent digital technology use.
