papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: There is growing evidence on the positive effects of the arts and arts therapies for mental health (MH) outcomes. This review aims to fill a research gap by establishing the evidence on the effects of arts-based interventions on selected MH outcomes for children and young people (CYP). METHODS: Our systematic review and meta-analysis included randomised controlled trials with CYP aged 5-24 years receiving any type of arts-based intervention. Five databases (CINAHL, Embase.com, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, and Web of Science) were searched for studies published between 1/1/2005 and 18/5/2025. Two reviewers independently screened all records and assessed risk-of-bias using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB2) and certainty using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE). Data were initially extracted using the AI-assisted review tool Elicit and independently verified by two reviewers. All data were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis, and effect estimates for MH outcomes are summarised as Standardised Mean Differences (SMD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Heterogeneity was assessed using the I 2 statistic, with pre-specified subgroup and sensitivity analyses conducted to explore possible sources of inconsistency. This study is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251015352). FINDINGS: One hundred trials across 29 countries involving CYP aged 5-24 years with a range of health conditions, alongside healthy populations, were included in this review. Based on studies with some concerns or high risk-of-bias, arts-based interventions were found to reduce individuals' depression (1.06 SMD lower [95% CI 0.45-1.67, n = 1655, I 2 = 97%]), anxiety (0.75 SMD lower [95% CI 0.57-0.94, n = 3898, I 2 = 87%]), and increase individuals' wellbeing (0.53 SMD higher [95% CI 0.26-0.80, n = 538, I 2 = 49%]) and quality of life (0.54 SMD higher [95% CI 0.25-0.83, n = 441, I 2 = 53%]) on average post-intervention. Certainty of results relating to wellbeing and quality of life was low due to imprecision and concerns about risk of bias, and very low for depression and anxiety due to additional inconsistency associated with high heterogeneity. Findings relating to anxiety were further supported by biomarker data (blood pressure and heart rate) with moderate certainty. INTERPRETATION: This systematic review provides a comprehensive synthesis of evidence from randomised controlled trials assessing the effects of a wide variety arts-based interventions on the mental health of CYP. Although the strength of any conclusions is limited by heterogeneity, imprecision and bias of the studies assessed, average effects were similar to those typically reported for established non-arts-based psychosocial interventions, including talking therapies. These findings advance our understanding of arts-based therapeutic strategies for CYP's MH. Further high-quality trials, with larger sample sizes and standardised outcome measures and timepoints, are needed to improve the certainty of evidence in this area. FUNDING: UKRI.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The suicide mortality rate is a key global indicator for monitoring progress toward improved mental health and well-being under the Sustainable Development Goals, and the World Health Organization Comprehensive Mental Health Action Plan has set an explicit suicide-specific target of reducing the age-standardized suicide mortality rate by one-third by 2030 (with a baseline year of 2015). This study assessed temporal trends in suicide mortality and suicide methods in the Region of the Americas using average annual percent change (AAPC) for the period 2015-2021. METHODS: Age-standardized and age group-specific suicide mortality rates (per 100,000 population) for the region, subregions, and by country for 2000-2021, and proportion of suicides by method by country, overall and by sex for 2015-2021, were obtained from the World Health Organization Global Health Estimates and the Pan American Health Organization Regional Mortality Database, respectively. In this population-based time-series analysis, AAPC was estimated using joinpoint regression analyses. The AAPCs for suicide mortality rates between 2015 and 2021 were compared with the compound annual reduction required to achieve a one-third reduction by 2030 (-2·67%). FINDINGS: The regional age-standardized suicide mortality rate increased by 1·05% (95% CI: 0·85%, 1·26%; p ≤ 0·0001) annually on average between 2015 and 2021, driven by males (AAPC: 0·99%, 95% CI: 0·81%, 1·17%; p ≤ 0·0001), as the rate among females remained relatively stable during this period (AAPC: 0·02%, 95% CI: -1·38%, 1·45%; p = 0·97). Only 10 countries (30·3%; out of 33) showed significant declines exceeding the 2·67% annual reduction needed to achieve the one-third reduction target by 2030. Across countries, the distribution of recorded suicide methods shifted over time, with increases in the proportion of suicides involving hanging and decreases in the proportions involving firearms and poisoning. INTERPRETATION: Suicide mortality in the region is rising, and the target of a one-third reduction by 2030 is unlikely to be met regionally; however, progress varies considerably across countries, with 10 (30·3%) making substantial progress toward the target. Urgent, coordinated action is needed in the countries with high and increasing suicide mortality rates, combining evidence-based means restriction strategies with broader upstream interventions that address social, economic and health-system determinants of suicide risk. FUNDING: None.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Ultra-high dose rate (UHDR) radiotherapy has shown significant promise in reducing normal tissue toxicities with equivalent tumour control compared to conventional (CONV) dose rates termed the FLASH effect. In this study, we compared radiation-induced lung injury and changes in the pulmonary circulation following localised right lung irradiation at UHDR and CONV exposures using photons. METHODS: Acute and late pulmonary radiation responses were assessed in pneumonitis (C3H/NeJ) and fibrosis prone (C57BL/6) mice. 18 Gy was delivered to the right lung at CONV (0.05 Gy/s), FLASH (76.2 Gy/s) and FLASH split dose (FSD, average 2.6 Gy/s) exposures. Early responses (72 h and 4 weeks after irradiation) were investigated by immunohistochemistry (Ly6G, F4/80), fluorescence staining (EdU) and serum profiling (cytokines and lipid peroxidation assays). Fibrosis was assessed at 30 weeks after irradiation by cone-beam CT (CBCT) analysis and quantification of collagen, senescence (p21) and TGF-β levels. Changes in pulmonary vasculature and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) was assessed in C57BL/6 mice at 30 weeks to characterise changes in pulmonary circulation associated with pulmonary hypertension (PH). RESULTS: At early timepoints, UHDR exposures led to reduced immune cell infiltration (neutrophils and macrophages) and tissue damage in comparison to CONV and FSD groups. Serum analysis supported FLASH sparing with decreased levels of markers associated with chronic inflammation and increased markers of tissue repair in comparison to CONV and FSD groups. At 30 weeks after irradiation at a UHDR, the lung parenchyma was structurally similar to controls (p = 0.33) with minimal collagen deposition supported by CBCT tissue density analysis. In contrast, CONV and FSD animals showed significant collagen deposition (p < 0.01) with thickened alveolar septa and reduced alveolar air spaces. UHDR exposures significantly reduced functional and histological metrics of PH (p < 0.05) compared to CONV. CONCLUSIONS: UHDR photons significantly reduce radiation-induced pneumonitis and fibrosis with secondary effects on the pulmonary circulation sparing PH.

papers.abstract_en: Combined heart-lung transplantation remains a rare but essential therapy for selected patients with end-stage cardiopulmonary disease that cannot be addressed by isolated heart or lung transplantation. Modern donor allocation, increasing recipient acuity, donation after circulatory death, and longer transport distances have made graft preservation a critical determinant of whether scarce en bloc grafts can be used safely. Unlike isolated organs, the intact heart-lung bloc presents competing preservation requirements: the heart and lungs differ in ischemic tolerance, optimal storage temperature, perfusate chemistry, airway management, and tolerance of pressure and volume during recovery. Across conventional static cold storage, controlled hypothermic transport, regulated airway-pressure devices, 10°C storage, and emerging donation after circulatory death recovery pathways, this review integrates contemporary approaches for donation after brain death and donation after circulatory death while distinguishing direct en bloc evidence from single-organ extrapolation. The evidence base remains observational and constrained by procedural rarity. Future progress will require multicenter preservation-specific data collection and graft-specific systems that treat the heart-lung bloc as an integrated physiologic unit rather than as two isolated organs transported together.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Cranial radiotherapy (RT) and pyrotinib both demonstrate efficacy in HER2-positive breast cancer brain metastases (BCBM); however, the optimal sequencing of these modalities remains to be established. We evaluated survival across treatment sequences within a real-world cohort. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, two-centre study included 101 patients with HER2-positive BCBM treated with cranial RT plus pyrotinib (June 2018-July 2025). Based on treatment sequence, patients were categorized into: concurrent RT and pyrotinib (Group A, n = 41); RT after intracranial progression on pyrotinib (Group B, n = 38); and pyrotinib upon progression following RT (Group C, n = 22). The primary endpoint was CNS-PFS. Survival outcomes were assessed via Kaplan-Meier estimation and Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: At a median follow-up of 43.3 months, 63 patients (62.4%) had died and 70 (69.3%) experienced CNS-PFS events. Median CNS-PFS was 14.8 months (95% CI 10.68-19.92) overall, and 14.3, 15.0, and 21.4 months in groups A, B, and C, respectively (P = 0.252); median OS was 36.0 months (95% CI 28.0-39.7) overall, and 33.0, 35.4, and 42.0 months in groups A, B, and C, respectively (P = 0.281). Focal cranial RT was independently associated with longer OS (HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.34-0.94; P = 0.028). Any-grade adverse events occurred in 100 of 101 patients (99.0%); grade ≥ 3 events occurred in 2.4%, 7.9%, and 4.5% of groups A, B, and C, respectively (all P > 0.05), and radiation necrosis occurred in 7 patients (6.9%). An exploratory threshold of RT initiated >3.9 months before pyrotinib (OS 49.9 vs 29.8 months; HR 0.31, 95% CI 0.11-0.91; P = 0.025) did not withstand internal validation. CONCLUSIONS: Treatment sequence did not significantly affect OS or CNS-PFS. Focal cranial RT was independently associated with longer survival, and toxicity was manageable. The proposed timing threshold is hypothesis-generating and warrants prospective validation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Curative-intent management of locally recurrent rectal cancer (LRRC) generally comprises neoadjuvant therapy and surgery. In patients with unresectable LRRC, where surgical intervention is not feasible, management is limited to non-operative bimodality therapy with systemic therapy and radiotherapy. Evidence guiding the optimisation of non-operative management remains limited. In this context, the therapeutic goal is to achieve prolonged local control while minimising treatment-related adverse events and preserving quality of life. Radiotherapy dose escalation has been proposed as a potential strategy to achieve this balance. However, its feasibility and safety in the non-operative management of unresectable LRRC have not yet been established. As such, this study aims to evaluate the feasibility and safety of this radiotherapeutic approach, and to determine its impact on both symptom control and oncological outcomes. METHODS: This prospective, multicentre, single-arm feasibility study will enrol 30 patients with unresectable or inoperable LRRC without distant metastases, or with (oligo)metastatic disease not requiring immediate systemic therapy. Previously irradiated patients will undergo reirradiation with stereotactic body radiotherapy (re-SBRT; 5 × 9 Gy) when feasible, or, alternatively hyperfractionated chemo-reirradiation (50.4 Gy in 1.2 Gy twice-daily fractions with concurrent capecitabine). Radiotherapy-naïve patients will receive chemoradiotherapy with a simultaneous integrated boost (25 × 2.6 Gy, EQD2Gyα/β=5Gy of 71 Gy with concurrent capecitabine). [1] The primary endpoint is treatment regimen feasibility, defined as grade ≥ 3 acute radiotherapy-related adverse events (CTCAE version 5.0) occurring in no more than seven patients (23%). Secondary endpoints include late adverse events, quality of life and symptom control, and 1- and 3-year progression-free survival, disease-free survival, and overall survival. DISCUSSION: This protocol describes the STEP-UP study, which will determine the feasibility of radiotherapy dose escalation in unresectable LRRC. If feasible and safe, this approach could provide an effective treatment intensification strategy to improve local control and symptom burden in patients with unresectable LRRC, addressing a major unmet clinical need. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lymph node (LN) involvement is a critical determinant of staging and prognosis in Wilms tumor (WT). However, conventional binary nodal staging (positive vs. negative) is often compromised by significant variability in surgical lymph node sampling. The lymph node ratio (LNR), which integrates metastatic burden and sampling adequacy, has emerged as a potential prognostic alternative. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether LNR serves as an independent predictor of survival outcomes in children with WT. METHODS: A systematic query of PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), and ClinicalTrials.gov was executed, covering the period from their earliest records through May 10, 2026. Retrospective cohort studies reporting hazard ratios (HRs) or risk ratios (RRs) for survival outcomes based on LNR in children with WT were included. Overall survival (OS) was the primary outcome; 5-year, 10-year, and 20-year OS were secondary outcomes. Prespecified subgroup analyses were performed by LNR cutoff (≥0.40 vs. <0.40). RESULTS: Six retrospective cohort studies involving 4,190 patients met the inclusion criteria. High LNR was significantly associated with poorer overall survival (HR = 2.10; 95% CI: 1.67-2.64). This prognostic significance persisted across secondary outcomes, including 5-year OS (RR = 1.14; 95% CI: 1.11-1.17), 10-year OS (RR = 1.19; 95% CI: 1.15-1.23), and 20-year OS (RR = 1.14; 95% CI: 1.10-1.19). Subgroup analysis revealed no significant interaction based on the LNR cutoff (P = 0.74). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness and stability of the pooled findings. CONCLUSIONS: Higher LNR appears to be associated with poorer overall survival in children with WT and may serve as a useful prognostic indicator. By accounting for both nodal disease burden and surgical effort, LNR may provide additional prognostic information beyond conventional nodal status. While LNR represents a valuable adjunct for individualized treatment decisions, prospective studies are required to establish standardized clinical cut-offs and integrate LNR into formal risk-adapted protocols. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261396220.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: The modern management of locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) involves sequential radiotherapy and chemotherapy, termed Total Neoadjuvant Therapy (TNT). Although TNT significantly improves tumour regression and achieves complete response rates of approximately 30 %, treatment efficacy remains limited in part by tumour-intrinsic resistance to apoptosis. We therefore sought to investigate the effects of radiotherapy on TNFα-associated apoptotic signalling in rectal cancer and evaluate whether inhibition of Inhibitor of Apoptosis Proteins (IAPs) could enhance treatment response. METHODS: Transcriptomic profiling was performed on rectal tumour biopsies obtained before and after two weeks of neoadjuvant radiotherapy (n = 42). Gene Set Enrichment Analysis was used to identify pathways altered following radiotherapy. The clinically relevant IAP antagonist, tolinapant, was evaluated in rectal cancer models to assess effects on cIAP1/2 degradation, radiation- and chemotherapy-induced apoptosis, and formation of 5-fluorouracil (5FU)-induced drug-tolerant persister (DTP) cells. Mechanistic studies were performed in the presence of TNFα, and in vivo efficacy was assessed in SW837 xenograft models. RESULTS: Radiotherapy induced robust upregulation of TNFα/TNFR1 signalling and apoptosis-associated gene sets. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis confirmed enrichment of both "TNFα signalling via NFκB" and "Apoptosis" pathways. Upregulation of TNF, TNFRSF1A, RIPK1, TRADD, and CFLAR (FLIP) was observed alongside downregulation of DIABLO, suggesting that radiotherapy primes tumours for TNFα-mediated apoptosis but that elevated antiapoptotic signalling may suppress this response. Tolinapant degraded cIAP1/2 and significantly enhanced radiation-induced apoptosis in rectal cancer models. Co-treatment with TNFα further amplified apoptosis through a caspase-8-dependent mechanism. The combination of tolinapant and radiation was well-tolerated in vivo and reduced SW837 xenograft tumour volume compared to radiation alone; however, this difference did not meet statistical significance. Tolinapant also potentiated chemotherapy-induced apoptosis and prevented the emergence of 5FU-induced DTP rectal cancer cells. CONCLUSION: These findings identify TNFα-associated apoptotic signalling as a potential radiation-induced vulnerability in rectal cancer and provide a mechanistic rationale for combining radiotherapy with IAP antagonists. Tolinapant also enhanced apoptosis induced by chemotherapy whilst suppressing drug-tolerant persisters, supporting further investigation of IAP antagonism as a strategy to improve TNT efficacy in the neoadjuvant management of rectal cancer.

papers.abstract_en: Ferroptosis is a regulated form of cell death driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation and has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in nonsmall cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the specific mechanisms by which nonsmall cell lung cancer cells evade ferroptosis remain to be further elucidated. We conducted integrative transcriptomic analyses of published NSCLC datasets to identify ubiquitin-specific proteases (USPs) potentially involved in the regulation of ferroptosis. Multiple USP proteins were screened and their prognostic significance evaluated, ultimately selecting USP5 for functional studies in two lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) cell lines and patient-derived LUAD organoids. Following treatment with the ferroptosis inducer erastin, survival rates and metastatic capacity were assessed. Ferroptosis was evaluated by measuring established ferroptotic markers and examining mitochondrial ultrastructure. Protein interactions were investigated using mass spectrometry, immunoprecipitation, and GST pull-down assays. USP5 was significantly upregulated in LUAD tissues and correlated with poor patient prognosis. Functional experiments demonstrated that USP5 suppresses ferroptosis in LUAD cells treated with erastin, thereby promoting cell survival, proliferation, and invasiveness. Mechanistically, USP5 directly binds to and deubiquitinates GPX3, a key antioxidant enzyme, to enhance its stability. Rescue experiments confirmed that GPX3 is a functional mediator of USP5's ferroptosis-inhibitory role. These findings are further supported in patient-derived LUAD organoids. Our study identifies USP5 as a critical suppressor of ferroptosis in LUAD through its stabilization of GPX3, revealing a novel USP5-GPX3 regulatory axis that enables tumor resistance to oxidative stress. Targeting this pathway may represent a promising therapeutic strategy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to investigate the associations of senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)-related genes with the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) and clinical outcomes in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and to develop and evaluate a prognostic signature for risk stratification and exploratory treatment-response prediction. METHODS: Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) was conducted to identify distinct molecular subtypes. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), Random Forest, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) were utilized to identify core prognostic SASP genes. The expression patterns of selected SASP-related genes were explored using multi-omics datasets, LUAD cell lines, and clinical specimens. RESULTS: Cluster 1 was associated with significantly shorter overall survival (OS), enhanced senescence pathway activity, and computationally inferred immunosuppressive and immune-exclusion features. Five intracellular SASP regulators-ANGPTL4, CDKN2A, H2AX, MMP1, and CCL20-were selected through machine learning to construct the SASP Protein Regulator Score (SASP-PRS). A high SASP-PRS was associated with the activation of senescence/SASP and cell-cycle pathways, suppression of antitumor immune signatures, and distinct immune-checkpoint and chemokine expression profiles. A higher SASP-PRS was also associated with advanced disease stage, poorer OS, predicted lower responsiveness to immunotherapy, lower predicted sensitivity to erlotinib, and higher predicted sensitivity to selected chemotherapeutic agents. The nomogram incorporating the SASP-PRS demonstrated discriminatory ability and calibration for predicting 1-, 3-, and 5-year OS in the analyzed LUAD cohorts. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that SASP-related gene-expression patterns are associated with LUAD molecular subtypes, senescence signaling, computationally inferred immune features, and treatment-related outcomes. The SASP-PRS may serve as a potential biomarker for prognostic stratification in LUAD. However, its utility for treatment-response assessment remains exploratory. Prospective external validation and functional studies are required to establish its clinical applicability and clarify the mechanisms linking SASP-related networks to the LUAD immune microenvironment.

papers.abstract_en: Advanced recurrent gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) after prolonged tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) exposure requires integration of surgical oncology, molecular reassessment, and continuous systemic therapy. We report a 72-year-old man with a 21-year history of gastric GIST who underwent initial resection in 2005, resection of recurrent disease in 2009, and long-term imatinib therapy. After years of apparent disease stability, he independently reduced imatinib and had a prolonged surveillance gap before recurrence was detected in 2024. Following tumor rupture and short-interval progression on sunitinib and regorafenib, he received ripretinib. In January 2026, clinically necessary maximal cytoreductive surgery was performed for bulky recurrent peritoneal disease with bleeding, anemia, abdominal-wall involvement, high risk of re-rupture, and invasion or close involvement of the right colon. Pathology confirmed recurrent high-risk spindle-cell GIST. Postoperative next-generation sequencing identified a founding KIT exon 11 deletion and a secondary KIT exon 17 p.Asn822Tyr activation-loop mutation; ripretinib was resumed after recovery of oral intake. Three-month CT showed recurrent peritoneal tumors, while a right hepatic subcapsular low-enhancement nodule was favored to represent post-ablation change. This case illustrates that surgery in resistant recurrent GIST may be necessary for local complication control and tissue acquisition, but even after maximal macroscopic cytoreduction, durable management depends on continuous genotype-informed systemic therapy and close surveillance.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Sexual behavior, sexually transmitted infections (STIs), and viral markers have been investigated in relation to prostate cancer, but heterogeneous exposure definitions and ascertainment methods complicate interpretation. We synthesized observational evidence separately across biologically and methodologically distinct exposure domains. METHODS: We followed PRISMA 2020 and searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase.com, and Web of Science Core Collection from inception through 27 May 2026. Eligible studies were comparative observational studies evaluating sexual behavior-related exposures, STI history or serology, or viral markers in relation to prostate cancer. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed for sufficiently comparable estimates. Risk of bias was assessed using Newcastle-Ottawa Scale domains, supplemented by design-specific epidemiological considerations. GRADE was used as a post-registration evidence-certainty assessment. RESULTS: Of 121 reports assessed for eligibility, 57 primary observational reports were included after final eligibility reconciliation. Twenty-five reports entered at least one pooled model and three additional reports appeared only in descriptive forest plots. For tissue- or PCR-based HPV detection, the observed pooled association was OR 3.01 (95% CI 1.97-4.61; I²=36.2%; prediction interval 1.15-7.91; 13 studies). HPV16 and HPV18 tissue/PCR subtype estimates were also elevated, whereas HPV serology showed no clear association. Estimates for Trichomonas vaginalis serology and history-based STI exposure were imprecise or heterogeneous, and sexual-behavior exposures were too heterogeneous for pooling. Certainty was very low across all evaluated exposure domains. CONCLUSIONS: Tissue- or PCR-based HPV detection was more frequent among prostate cancer cases in the available comparative studies, but the evidence is very uncertain because of risk of bias, limited temporal clarity, sampling and comparator differences, and other methodological limitations. These findings should not be interpreted as establishing an etiologic or causal effect and do not support prostate-cancer prevention recommendations based on HPV vaccination, STI screening, or sexual-behavior modification. papers.abstract_en: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly expanding across gynecologic oncology, but most applications remain focused on image interpretation and retrospective prediction rather than direct support of treatment decisions. This review examines how AI is progressing from imaging biomarkers toward multimodal decision-support systems that integrate radiologic, pathologic, molecular, and clinical information. We summarize current applications in ovarian, endometrial, and cervical cancers, with particular attention to preoperative risk stratification, surgical planning, radiotherapy, systemic treatment selection, treatment-response prediction, and multidisciplinary decision-making. Multimodal approaches are especially promising because they reflect the way clinical decisions are made and may provide greater value than models based on a single data source. However, the current evidence remains dominated by retrospective and often single-center studies, with limited external and prospective validation. Data heterogeneity, domain shift, incomplete multimodal datasets, bias, workflow integration, regulatory requirements, and model monitoring remain important barriers to routine implementation. We therefore outline a stepwise pathway for clinical translation, from robust multicenter validation and prospective human-AI evaluation to clinical-impact studies and post-deployment monitoring. The next phase of AI in gynecologic oncology should prioritize clinically meaningful decisions and measurable patient or workflow benefit rather than incremental gains in predictive performance alone.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Long-term head and neck cancer survivors are few, but always exposed to a risk of mandibular osteoradionecrosis (ORN) despite the use of appropriate dose-volume constraints in today's radiotherapy. Here, ORN development is approached from another look, in an attempt to explain its complexity. DEFINITIONS: Early ORN is best defined by length of the mucosal defect (<2 teeth long) and radiological assessment of the depth of areas of bone resorption (lysis below the level of the inferior alveolar canal) in the radiotherapy volume. Technical improvements have greatly reduced the incidence of ORN, but a lifelong risk remains and requires long-term follow-up. CAUSAL FACTORS: Pathogenic hypotheses have evolved over time from the "radiation-trauma-infection" triad to the 3H theory of "hypoxia-hypocellularity-hypovascularity", and then radiation-induced fibro-atrophy of the bone. ORN is a dynamic process combining interacting causal factors that worsen each other over time: (a) radiation-induced fibro-atrophy of the bone and its related radiotherapy technical parameters; (b) periodontal disease/dental trauma and their related questions on optimal timing of pre- or post-radiotherapy extractions and how many teeth; (c) infection/oral microbiota and their related mechanically inaccessible bone sequestra (residual bacteria); (d) vascular factors from capillary network destruction to artery stenosis of irradiated branches and the carotid trunk. CONCLUSION: Symptomatic medical care focusing on comorbidity parameters and devitalized tissue removal is not sufficient to protect patients against ORN. These new insights should help to treat early ORN through concomitant control of these causal factors and best dental care.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Dual immune checkpoint inhibition (DICI) is an established first-line treatment for metastatic NSCLC. Whether the addition of chemotherapy provides an incremental survival benefit beyond DICI alone remains unclear. METHODS: We performed a systematic review and reconstructed individual patient data meta-analysis of trials evaluating first-line DICI and DICI plus chemotherapy (DICI-CT) in metastatic NSCLC. Data were reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves. Overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards and time-varying models. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted according to PD-L1 expression, histology, and STK11 or KEAP1 mutational status. RESULTS: Four trials comprising 1654 patients were included (699 receiving DICI-CT and 955 receiving DICI). Median OS was similar between the groups (15.4 versus 15.0 mo, hazard ratio = 0.93, 95% confidence interval: 0.81-1.08). Proportional hazards assumptions were violated, and time-varying analyses suggested modest late survival differences favoring DICI, with higher 5-year OS (19.4% versus 17.1%) and progression-free survival (10.5% versus 8.2%). In STK11-mutated tumors, DICI-CT was associated with a limited early survival benefit that was not sustained over time. No clear differences were observed in KEAP1-mutated tumors. CONCLUSIONS: The addition of chemotherapy to DICI was not associated with improved survival in an unselected population of patients with metastatic NSCLC. These findings support an individualized approach to the use of chemotherapy in combination with DICI.

papers.abstract_en: FLASH radiotherapy (FLASH-RT) has rapidly emerged as a promising approach to widen the therapeutic window through differential sparing of normal tissue. However, despite substantial experimental activity, uncertainties remain regarding the magnitude, reproducibility, and determinants of the FLASH effect. This work reviews common pitfalls and sources of ambiguity in the acquisition and interpretation of preclinical FLASH data to support clinical application. In particular, the widespread use of fixed single-dose study designs, over-reliance on differential endpoint-based metrics, and limited quantification of effect size may obscure the true magnitude and clinical relevance of observed effects. Moreover, small dose-modifying effects are highly susceptible to experimental and biological variability, including dosimetric uncertainties, endpoint sensitivity, and environmental factors such as oxygenation. Heterogeneity in experimental protocols and endpoints further complicates cross-study comparisons. Addressing these challenges through improved quantitative characterisation, harmonised methodologies, and transparent reporting will be essential to enable robust interpretation and support the clinical translation of FLASH-RT.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Recovery after video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS) can involve pain, fatigue, distress, and reduced confidence in rehabilitation activities. OBJECTIVES: Guided by conservation of resources theory, this study examined associations between resilience and cancer-related self-care self-efficacy measured during early postoperative recovery, the indirect roles of social support and negative emotion, and whether social support moderated the resilience-self-efficacy association. DESIGN: A cross-sectional study. SETTINGS: One tertiary Grade A cancer hospital in South China. PARTICIPANTS: A convenience sample of 225 adults with primary lung cancer who underwent elective VATS was assessed on postoperative days 3 to 5 before discharge. METHODS: Participants completed a sociodemographic/clinical questionnaire and validated Chinese versions of the social support, cancer self-care self-efficacy, resilience, and negative emotion scales. Observed-variable serial mediation paths were estimated with 5000 bootstrap resamples; moderation was examined with a resilience by social support interaction. RESULTS: Resilience was positively associated with self-efficacy (B = 2.080, 95% CI 1.826 to 2.334). The indirect associations through social support (B = 0.118, 95% CI 0.024 to 0.212), negative emotion (B = 0.084, 95% CI 0.004 to 0.164), and both variables sequentially (B = 0.018, 95% CI 0.004 to 0.032) were statistically significant. The resilience by social support interaction was also significant (beta = 0.083, p = 0.010). CONCLUSIONS: In this early postoperative sample, resilience, social support, negative emotion, and self-efficacy showed patterns consistent with the proposed resource-based model. Nursing strategies that assess and support these resources should be tested in longitudinal and interventional studies.

papers.abstract_en: Pericardial effusion has infectious, inflammatory, neoplastic, traumatic, cardiac, vascular, and idiopathic causes. When effusion accumulates rapidly enough to compromise ventricular filling, cardiac tamponade develops and becomes a life-threatening emergency requiring urgent drainage, a procedure conventionally performed by a cardiologist or cardiothoracic surgeon and rarely available on site at rural or resource-limited hospitals. Malignant pericardial effusion is most often attributed to lung and breast carcinoma, while lymphoma is the leading hematologic cause. Tamponade as the presenting feature of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, however, is distinctly uncommon. We describe a 40-year-old man from a rural community in Nuevo León, Mexico, with three weeks of intermittent chest tightness, diaphoresis, unquantified fever, and approximately 7 kg of unintentional weight loss, followed by progressive exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. He presented to a rural hospital with jugular venous distension, muffled heart sounds, and lower-limb edema, without pulsus paradoxus. Echocardiography demonstrated a severe pericardial effusion measuring up to 4.6 cm with tamponade physiology. With no cardiologist on site and hemodynamic collapse imminent, an internist performed pericardiocentesis under real-time telemedicine guidance from a cardiologist, draining serosanguineous fluid whose biochemical profile suggested tumor involvement. Contrast-enhanced chest computed tomography at the referral center revealed a 14.4 × 11.8 × 11.3 cm anterior mediastinal mass with necrotic areas. Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery allowed pericardial window creation and tumor biopsy, which established a CD20-positive primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma (PMBCL). Chemotherapy with R-CHOEP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, etoposide, and prednisone) was initiated, with resolution of hemodynamic instability and no recurrence of tamponade during the reported follow-up. This case illustrates that malignancy warrants early consideration in unexplained tamponade and that real-time telemedicine guidance may allow a non-specialist physician to undertake a life-saving bedside procedure where specialist care is otherwise unavailable, an approach that merits further evaluation in rural and underserved settings.

papers.abstract_en: Pleural effusion in children is most frequently associated with infectious diseases, particularly parapneumonic effusion. Recurrent or unexplained pleural effusion, however, should prompt consideration of less common etiologies, including autoimmune disease, tuberculosis, chylothorax, cardiac and renal disease, and malignancy. We report the case of a 10-year-old boy with recurrent large right-sided pleural effusions requiring repeated drainage of more than 1,500 mL. An extensive diagnostic evaluation for rheumatologic and infectious causes was unrevealing. During the current admission, the patient had anorexia, weight loss, axillary lymphadenopathy, leukocytosis, and mild thrombocytopenia, without reported peripheral blood blasts. Chest computed tomography demonstrated a large right pleural collection, bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy, and prominent thymic tissue without a definite bulky anterior mediastinal mass. Pleural-fluid flow cytometry demonstrated an abnormal immature T-lineage lymphoblast population comprising approximately 99% of analyzed cells. Pleural biopsy showed tissue infiltration by atypical lymphoid cells morphologically resembling non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Subsequent bone marrow examination, performed after three days of methylprednisolone therapy, demonstrated diffuse blast infiltration with an immature T-cell immunophenotype and was diagnostic of T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Lymph-node biopsy showed lymphoproliferative disease, while lumbar puncture was normal. Pleural-fluid tuberculosis PCR and acid-fast bacilli testing were negative. This case emphasizes that recurrent pleural effusion may be an initial and predominant manifestation of T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, even in the absence of peripheral blood blasts or a typical mediastinal mass. Early pleural-fluid flow cytometry may facilitate diagnosis and prevent diagnostic delay.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Accumulating evidence suggests that aberrant HHLA2 expression is closely implicated not only in tumorigenesis, disease progression, and metastatic spread, but also in the intricate modulation of the tumor immune microenvironment. Nevertheless, the biological functions of HHLA2 and the molecular mechanisms underlying its action in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) remain unexplored. MATERIALS AND METHODS: HHLA2 expression was systematically assessed in LSCC tumor specimens and matched adjacent tissues using multiplex immunofluorescence (mIHC). The functional consequences of HHLA2 silencing in LSCC cells were evaluated through a series of in vitro assays, including CCK-8-based proliferation analysis, wound-healing (scratch) assays, and invasion assays. Transcriptomic sequencing integrated with public database mining was subsequently performed to identify key target genes potentially governed by HHLA2 in regulating LSCC biological behavior. Furthermore, Gene Ontology (GO), Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) and Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) pathway analyses were conducted to delineate the signaling networks and molecular pathways through which HHLA2 might exert its regulatory effects in LSCC. RESULTS: HHLA2 expression was significantly elevated in LSCC tumor tissues, and associated with poor prognosis in patients. Functional experiments revealed that suppression of HHLA2 leads to marked inhibition of LSCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, underscoring its essential role in sustaining malignant phenotypes. Mechanistically, we identified potassium channel tetrameric domain 12 (KCTD12) as a pivotal target of HHLA2 in mediating these oncogenic processes. Importantly, forced overexpression of KCTD12 effectively counterbalanced the inhibitory effects induced by HHLA2 depletion, thereby restoring proliferative, migratory, and invasive potential to LSCC cells. Furthermore, pathway enrichment analyses indicated that the TNF-NF-κB signalling pathway might serve as a key conduit through which HHLA2 orchestrated both tumor cell functions and immune regulatory mechanisms. The HHLA2-KCTD12 axis may regulate the phenotype of LSCC cells and reshape the tumor immune microenvironment through the TNF-NF-κB signaling pathway. CONCLUSIONS: HHLA2 enhanced the proliferative, migratory, and invasive capacities of LSCC cells and might contribute to immune microenvironment remodeling via modulation of TNF-NF-κB signaling through the HHLA2-KCTD12 axis.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To identify latent psychological resilience profiles in older patients after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) and examine their association with physical resilience. METHODS: A total of 300 patients with prostate cancer were recruited from a Class III Grade A hospital in Sichuan Province between December 2025 and May 2026. Assessments were conducted on postoperative day 3 using the general information questionnaire, Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale, and Physical Resilience Instrument for Older Adults. Latent profile analysis was performed using the total score on the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale. Generalized linear regression was used to analyze the relationship between psychological and physical resilience across categories among elderly patients after RARP. RESULTS: Three latent psychological resilience profiles were identified among older patients after RARP. Physical resilience scores differed among people with different psychological resilience. The results of generalized regression analysis showed that patients in different psychological resilience profiles of RARP patients were related to their physical resilience (P < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Older patients after RARP showed heterogeneous psychological resilience profiles, and profile membership was associated with physical resilience. Longitudinal and intervention studies are needed to determine the temporal direction and clinical utility of these profiles.

papers.title_zh: 欧盟学术性治疗优化研究的风险与负担适配监管框架：一篇政策观点文章（无原始数据）
papers.title_en: Academic treatment optimization studies in oncology and internal medicine: a risk- and burden-adapted regulatory framework for the European Union.
papers.authors: Berdel WE, Dreyling M, Schrappe M, Wanner C, Schmidt G
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medicine A, University Hospital Münster, Albert Schweitzer Campus 1, Münster 48149, Germany.
papers.authors_conclusion: 目标不是对学术临床研究去监管，而是风险相称的监管；针对学术治疗优化研究的风险适配框架可强化研究者发起的证据生成，尤其适用于商业激励有限的问题，并改善欧洲常规临床照护优化的证据基础。
papers.ai_note: 本文为立场性政策观点，无系统检索策略、无纳入排除标准、无数据或量化风险估计；OECD A/B1/B2 分类与“最小额外风险与负担”缺乏可操作判定阈值，核心概念（以“常规临床照护”而非说明书为参照）依赖各专科学会自定标准，可致执行异质性与放宽解释；作者群体为学术试验发起方与伦理委员，存在推动降低行政负担的立场倾向，文中“非去监管”的自我限定与实质简化审评路径之间的张力未被实证检验。
papers.reason: 为研究者发起的外科／肿瘤治疗优化类试验（如围手术期方案加减、序贯或降阶梯设计）在欧盟申办时的监管定位提供政策背景与论点参照，可用于理解此类研究合规成本与伦理审评逻辑，但不提供任何可直接改变临床决策的数据。
papers.abstract_en: Academic treatment optimization studies (TOS) play an important role in determining how established and emerging treatments should be combined, sequenced, intensified, de-intensified, or otherwise optimized in routine clinical care. Unlike commercial clinical trials, which primarily support the development and regulatory approval of new medicinal products, academic TOS frequently address questions for which commercial incentives are limited. Such studies therefore contribute directly to the evidence base underlying clinical guidelines and health-care standards. A substantial proportion of academic TOS involves authorized medicinal products used outside the strict wording of their marketing authorization (label), but within evidence-supported clinical practice. Current European clinical-trial regulation does not always adequately reflect the distinction between the label of a medicinal product and the incremental risk and burden introduced by a particular treatment optimization strategy. Increasing administrative and regulatory requirements disproportionately affect investigator-initiated multicentre studies with limited resources. This article presents a policy perspective derived from the experience of investigators, clinical researchers and ethics committee members involved in academic clinical trials. We propose a risk- and burden-adapted regulatory approach for eligible academic TOS. The relevant reference point for assessing proportionality should be normal clinical care rather than the label alone. Evidence-supported TOS involving authorized medicinal products, particularly studies corresponding to OECD categories A and B1, should be considered for a risk-proportionate regulatory pathway when the proposed intervention introduces minimal additional risk and burden compared with normal clinical care. Selected OECD B2 studies could potentially qualify where additional evidence and expert assessment demonstrate similarly low incremental risk. The assessment should be performed on a trial-specific basis. Relevant standards of routine care should be defined by the respective medical societies in the field. Ethics committees, supported by physicians experienced in the relevant disease area, should assess incremental risk and burden. Monitoring, oversight and reporting requirements should likewise be risk-proportionate and prospectively justified in the trial protocol. The objective is not deregulation of academic clinical research but risk-proportionate regulation. A risk-adapted framework for academic TOS could strengthen investigator-initiated evidence generation, particularly for questions with limited commercial incentives, and improve the evidence base for optimizing routine clinical care in Europe.

papers.title_zh: 帕博利珠单抗联合仑伐替尼治疗期间出现直接免疫荧光阴性的免疫检查点抑制剂相关大疱性类天疱疮：一例病例报告
papers.title_en: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Related Bullous Pemphigoid with Negative Direct Immunofluorescence during Pembrolizumab Plus Lenvatinib Therapy: A Case Report.
papers.authors: Seko A, Nagai S, Hino M, Takatsuji N, Shirane T, Iijima M, Hattori Y, Kurahashi T et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, National Hospital Organization Saitama Hospital, Saitama, Japan.
papers.results: 治疗38周（第9周期）出现躯干及四肢广泛紧张性大疱并硬腭糜烂；血清抗BP180抗体115.4 U/mL（参考值<9.0）；皮肤活检示表皮下水疱形成伴嗜酸性粒细胞丰富浸润；直接免疫荧光（DIF）阴性；仍按CTCAE v5.0诊断为3级ICI相关大疱性类天疱疮；泼尼松龙90 mg/日（约1 mg/kg）后临床迅速改善、抗体下降；帕博利珠单抗永久停用，7周后恢复仑伐替尼单药；因手足综合征需减量，未见BP复发。
papers.authors_conclusion: 在接受LP治疗出现紧张性大疱的患者中，即使DIF阴性也应考虑大疱性类天疱疮；对伴黏膜受累的重症病例，选择性停用帕博利珠单抗而继续仑伐替尼单药可能是合理的个体化策略；随着LP治疗在妇科肿瘤中扩大应用，皮肤科参与识别与多学科管理罕见皮肤irAE日益重要。
papers.ai_note: 单例报告，无对照与系统随访，无法评估该处理策略的获益归因（激素、停ICI、停/续TKI效应混杂）；DIF阴性而诊断成立，说明诊断依赖临床+血清学+病理，需排除获得性大疱性表皮松解症等其他表皮下大疱病，摘要未报告排除过程；结论中的“合理个体化策略”属经验外推，随访时长与抗体复查具体数值未给出；与胸部肿瘤的相关性仅来自ICI类药物共性，人群为子宫内膜癌，不涉及胸科结局。

pico.p: 53岁日本女性，FIGO IA期子宫内膜样癌，术后辅助紫杉醇-卡铂，30个月后腹膜复发，再挑战后进展并接受仑伐替尼+帕博利珠单抗治疗（n=1）
pico.ic: 仑伐替尼+帕博利珠单抗治疗期间发生皮肤irAE的处理：停用帕博利珠单抗、泼尼松龙90 mg/日（约1 mg/kg）、7周后恢复仑伐替尼单药并逐步减激素；无同期对照

papers.reason: 为胸部肿瘤常用的帕博利珠单抗相关罕见皮肤irAE（大疱性类天疱疮）的识别提供单例参照，尤其提示DIF阴性不能排除诊断；并示范“选择性停ICI、保留TKI”的个体化处理思路，可作为免疫治疗毒性管理宣教与病例对照讨论的素材，但不足以改变具体临床决策。
papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) is a rare but clinically significant cutaneous immune-related adverse event (irAE) of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. It is most often described during treatment of melanoma, lung cancer, and renal cell carcinoma, whereas reports in gynecologic oncology, and specifically during lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab (LP) therapy, remain scarce. CASE PRESENTATION: A 53-year-old Japanese woman with International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage IA endometrioid carcinoma underwent hysterectomy followed by adjuvant paclitaxel-carboplatin. Peritoneal recurrence occurred 30 months later. After paclitaxel-carboplatin rechallenge and subsequent progression, LP therapy was initiated. At 38 weeks (cycle 9), erythema progressed to widespread tense bullae on the trunk and extremities with hard-palate erosion. Serum anti-BP180 antibody was markedly elevated (115.4 U/mL; reference: <9.0). Skin biopsy showed subepidermal cleft formation with an eosinophil-rich infiltrate. Direct immunofluorescence (DIF) was negative; nevertheless, ICI-related BP (Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events [CTCAE] v5.0, grade 3) was diagnosed on the basis of clinical, serological, and histopathological findings. LP therapy was discontinued and prednisolone 90 mg/day (approximately 1 mg/kg) was started, achieving rapid clinical improvement and antibody decline. Pembrolizumab was permanently discontinued, and lenvatinib monotherapy was resumed 7 weeks later under tapering steroids. Dose reduction was required for hand-foot syndrome, but no BP recurrence has been observed. CONCLUSION: BP should be considered in patients who develop tense bullae during LP therapy, even when DIF is negative. In severe cases with mucosal involvement, selective discontinuation of pembrolizumab while continuing lenvatinib monotherapy may represent a reasonable individualized strategy. As LP therapy expands in gynecologic oncology, recognition and multidisciplinary management of rare cutaneous irAEs by dermatologists is increasingly important.

papers.title_zh: 欧洲下一代孕产妇疫苗：科学进展、监管准备与战略规划（系列综述）
papers.title_en: The next generation of maternal vaccines: scientific advances, regulatory readiness, and strategic planning in Europe.
papers.authors: Heath PT, Galiza EP, Salcedo PJ, Karafillakis E, Khalil A, Maertens K, Le Doare K, Jones CE et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Centre for Neonatal and Paediatric Infection and Vaccine Institute, City St George's, University of London, Cranmer Terr…
papers.authors_conclusion: Realising this potential will require integrated action across research, regulation, implementation, and communication.
papers.ai_note: 叙述性综述，未报告系统检索、纳入排除标准或证据分级；结论以政策建议为主，非临床疗效证据；摘要无主要终点或定量结果；主题非胸外科/胸部肿瘤，仅RSV等呼吸道病原体预防有边缘关联。

papers.abstract_en: With the recent approval of maternal RSV vaccines and late-phase trials underway for a GBS vaccine, Europe is entering a new era of maternal immunisation. Yet scientific progress is outpacing pregnancy-specific evidence and preparedness for equitable implementation. Pregnant women are often excluded from early vaccine trials, while national recommendations, surveillance and delivery vary across Europe, even after regulatory authorisation. Without coordinated planning, new maternal vaccines risk reproducing the delays and inequities seen with influenza, pertussis and COVID-19 vaccination. In this Review, we examine scientific advances in the next generation of maternal vaccines, including mRNA, protein conjugate, nanoparticle and combination approaches, and candidates against emerging and other priority pathogens. We discuss barriers to including pregnant women in trials, assess regulatory and pharmacovigilance readiness, and identify health-system and vaccine-confidence risks to equitable rollout. We offer strategic recommendations for Europe's maternal immunisation roadmap, from research investment to policy integration, provider education, and equity-centred planning. Realising this potential will require integrated action across research, regulation, implementation, and communication. This is the final paper in the Series on the future of maternal vaccination in Europe and synthesises its findings into a framework for Europe and beyond.

papers.authors: Mascherini J, Eid MK, Vanterpool G, Sucandy I
papers.affiliation_highlight: AdventHealth Tampa, Digestive Health Institute, Tampa, FL, United States.
papers.authors_conclusion: 现有证据一致提示，在筛选后的患者中，微创入路较开放手术失血更少、术后并发症更少、住院时间更短，同时肿瘤学结局相当；腹腔镜仍是最成熟的微创平台，机器人可能通过更好的灵活性、三维视野与缝合能力在复杂切除中提供技术优势；但现有证据多为回顾性，受选择偏倚与机构经验影响，平台选择应依据肿瘤解剖、肝功能、技术复杂度与中心经验个体化决定。

papers.reason: 为肝细胞癌外科平台选择（开放/腹腔镜/机器人）提供叙述性证据框架与场景化决策思路，可作为肝胆对比类研究立题与对照设计的背景参考；对胸部肿瘤临床判断无直接影响。
papers.abstract_en: Hepatocellular carcinoma remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide and frequently arises in the setting of chronic liver disease, cirrhosis, and portal hypertension. Liver resection represents a cornerstone of curative-intent treatment, but its role is uniquely influenced by the need to balance oncologic radicality with preservation of functional liver parenchyma. Over the last two decades, minimally invasive liver surgery has progressively expanded from selected laparoscopic minor resections to complex laparoscopic and robotic hepatectomies, challenging the historical dominance of open surgery. This narrative review critically examines the evolving roles of open, laparoscopic, and robotic liver resection for hepatocellular carcinoma, emphasizing patient selection, technical considerations, scenario-based platform choice, and comparative outcomes. Particular attention is given to hepatocellular carcinoma-specific challenges, including impaired liver function, clinically significant portal hypertension, future liver remnant adequacy, recurrence risk, and the need for parenchymal-sparing strategies. The review also discusses distinct clinical scenarios, including small solitary tumors, posterosuperior lesions, central or deeply located tumors, multifocal disease, and recurrent HCC. Current evidence consistently suggests that minimally invasive approaches are associated with reduced blood loss, fewer postoperative complications, and shorter hospital stay compared with open surgery, while maintaining comparable oncologic outcomes in selected patients. Laparoscopy remains the most established minimally invasive platform, whereas robotics may offer technical advantages in complex resections through improved dexterity, three-dimensional visualization, and enhanced suturing capability. However, available evidence remains largely retrospective and influenced by selection bias and institutional expertise. Platform selection should therefore be individualized according to tumor anatomy, liver function, technical complexity, and center experience, with the goal of maximizing oncologic benefit while minimizing functional liver loss.

papers.authors_conclusion: 研究确认 GSTP1 是一个衰老相关应激反应基因，为前列腺癌发病机制提供新视角，并显示针对衰老与免疫关联的治疗策略前景；该研究为在精准肿瘤学中利用衰老生物标志物提供了系统性框架，并突出 GSTP1 作为 PCa 临床转化 promising candidate 的价值。

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Prostate cancer (PCa) is a common malignancy of the male genitourinary system with high metastatic potential and poor clinical outcomes, for which effective biomarkers and therapeutic targets remain limited. METHODS: This study employed a multi-omics approach, integrating transcriptome profiles, age-related gene screening, and machine learning techniques, to analyze four GEO datasets, in order to identify key diagnostic biomarkers for prostate cancer (PCa). RESULTS: Differentially expressed aging-related genes were identified, with enrichment analyses revealing significant involvement in PCa. Using machine learning algorithms, a robust diagnostic model centered on GSTP1 was developed, demonstrating high predictive performance. GSTP1 depletion drove multiple oncogenic phenotypes, including enhanced proliferation, migration, invasion, and the inhibition of cellular aging and DNA damage, suggesting that GSTP1 may promote cellular senescence while restraining malignant progression. Furthermore, its expression correlated with distinct immunocyte profiles, highlighting a role in shaping the PCa immune landscape. DISCUSSION: Our findings confirm that GSTP1 functions as an aging-associated stress response gene, offering new perspectives on prostate cancer pathogenesis and showing promise for advancing therapeutic strategies that target both aging and immune associations. This study provides a comprehensive framework for leveraging aging biomarkers in precision oncology and highlights GSTP1 as a promising candidate for clinical translation in PCa management.

papers.abstract_en: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is often diagnosed after the opportunity for curative treatment has passed. Blood-based biomarkers offer opportunities for earlier detection and serial molecular assessment, but their value depends on the intended clinical use. This nonsystematic narrative review critically examines circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), circulating tumor cells, extracellular vesicles, circulating RNAs, proteins and multimodal panels, including models developed using artificial intelligence. We distinguish population screening, high-risk surveillance, diagnostic evaluation, molecular profiling, treatment monitoring and postoperative recurrence assessment. High discrimination in selected case-control cohorts does not establish performance in asymptomatic populations or clinical benefit. Differences in disease stage, comparator groups, sample handling and validation design preclude reliable ranking of biomarker classes using published area-under-the-curve values. ctDNA has a more established role in selected molecular-profiling situations than in early detection; postoperative detection and longitudinal changes provide prognostic information, but do not by themselves justify treatment modification. Multimodal assays require comparison with clinical assessment and CA19-9 at prespecified thresholds, external validation, calibration and evaluation of downstream harms and costs. This review presents an intended-use framework and a summary of representative prospective studies. Limitations include purposive, non-exhaustive evidence selection and the absence of formal risk-of-bias or certainty grading. Clinical translation requires reproducible assays and evidence that biomarker-informed decisions improve outcomes. Liquid biopsy should therefore be evaluated within defined clinical pathways alongside imaging, pathology and established molecular testing.
